title: Bound every in-process libpari call: cysignals alarm around ellcard, ellsea and ellorder, PariStall ends a pytest run at exit 124, planted stalls prove the bound fires
description:
CONTEXT. Three of five CI runs since 6c9a555 (33596453230, 33599198395, 33648051060) froze 5-15 minutes inside in-process libpari (ellsea once, ellcard twice, in self-test corpus evaluation) until the session deadline, and the same freeze reproduced on the build machine at load average 9 (main thread in src/cairn/pari.py ellsea under tests/integration/test_bsgs_selftest.py). The per-test watchdog was silent both times: neither pytest-timeout method can interrupt a C call. Bead cairn-ict holds the cause hypothesis (libpari's pthread pool, nbthreads = core count, under CPU contention) and the pin that would remove it; that pin moves the 60-bit vectors and is a separate decision. This bead is the bound: whatever the cause, a stalled in-process libpari call has to end the run loudly and within a fixed time instead of eating the deadline.

MEASURED (2026-09-02, session cairn-75, scratch probes, each child under an outer timeout):
- cysignals' alarm (cysignals 1.12.6, the signal layer cypari2 2.2.4 already runs every call under) interrupts a planted busy loop `while(1,)` at 1.009 s of a 1.0 s alarm and a planted thread-pool wait `parapply(x->while(1,),[1,2,3,4])` at 1.008 s; AlarmInterrupt derives from KeyboardInterrupt.
- After the busy-loop escape libpari is healthy: the 151-bit corpus ellcard returns the same value as before (1427247692705959881058262545272474300628281448, 0.54 s). After the pool escape the process is poisoned: the next libpari call segfaulted (rc 139) in two of three children, one child returned normally. The poison is nondeterministic, so the rule is no further libpari call in that process.
- A Python-level SIGALRM handler installed with signal.signal displaces cysignals' C handler; the busy loop then ran to the outer 30 s timeout with the alarm never delivered. signal.getsignal(SIGALRM) reads SIG_DFL (0) while cysignals owns the signal and the Python callable when Python does, so the wrapper can tell the two apart; signal.signal(SIGALRM, SIG_DFL) followed by cysignals.signals.init_cysignals() restores both tables (owner None, busy loop interrupted at 0.3 s).
- An alarm that fires while the main thread is in pure Python raises AlarmInterrupt at once (cysignals.signals.python_check_interrupt), so the arm/cancel pair must sit in try/finally.

WHAT. `src/cairn/pari.py`: `CALL_BOUND_S = 60.0`; `bounded(name, fn, *args, bound_s=None)` arms cysignals' alarm around the call, cancels it in finally, and converts AlarmInterrupt into `PariStall(name, bound_s, elapsed_s)`, a subclass of AlarmInterrupt (so of KeyboardInterrupt: an `except Exception` in a corpus loop cannot swallow it) whose message carries nbthreads, the load average and the Python thread count; the first stall is kept in module state and every later wrapper call raises `PariStall(..., earlier=first)` without touching libpari; `_alarm_owner()` reads Python's SIGALRM table and `bounded` raises `PariBoundUnavailable` under a Python handler rather than running unbounded. `ellcard`, `ellsea`, `ellorder` route through `bounded` and gain a keyword `bound_s`. `NBTHREADS` is read once at import. `src/cairn/cli.py`: a PariStall reaching main maps to exits.BACKEND with the message and `cairn doctor` as the next command; any other KeyboardInterrupt still propagates. `tests/_libpari_stall.py`: a `pytest_runtest_protocol` wrapper turns a PariStall escaping any phase of a test into `pytest.exit(..., returncode=124)` naming the nodeid, the deadline's code, so the run stops before the next test. `MAP.md` row 2 names the refusal; `CLAUDE.md` carries the working note; `scripts/check.sh` names the banner beside the deadline's.

The bound is 60 s because the largest legitimate in-process call, ellcard on the corpus's 151-bit curve, takes 0.57 s at 10 threads here and 0.65 s on the 3-vCPU runner, and one stall then costs 60 s of a 900 s CI deadline. Rejected: a subprocess boundary around the curve draw. It would leave the parent clean after a stall, but the in-process cypari2 path is what toy_curve is (the gp-vs-cypari2 agreement tests compare the two libraries from one seed), the stall also appears in selftest.py's corpus evaluation which is not a draw, and the alarm covers every wrapper call site with one mechanism. Rejected: pinning nbthreads here; that is cairn-ict's decision and it moves vectors.

TEST PLAN. tests/unit/test_pari_module.py: a planted busy loop through the real `ellcard` wrapper (the cypari2 instance stubbed to evaluate `while(1,)`) raises PariStall within the 0.5 s bound, the stall is a KeyboardInterrupt, the next wrapper call is refused without reaching the stub, and a direct ellcard afterwards returns the value from before the plant (this plant is the in-suite proof the handler chain is intact in the pytest process); the alarm is cancelled when a call returns (a 0.2 s bound, a 0.5 s Python sleep, no AlarmInterrupt); a Python SIGALRM handler makes the wrapper refuse before arming, and after the restore sequence the plant fires again; a child process plants the thread-pool wait under a 1 s bound and dies at exit 7 with the stall line on stdout in under 10 s (the poison stays in the child). tests/unit/test_libpari_stall_hook.py (pytester): a PariStall escaping a test or a fixture ends the inner session at exit 124 with the banner and the next test never runs; an ordinary KeyboardInterrupt keeps pytest's exit 2. tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py: a command raising PariStall exits BACKEND with the message; a plain KeyboardInterrupt propagates. Editing pari.py moves the toy_curve and instance_maker revisions, so their certificate and transcript goldens regenerate in the same attributed commit.

NO-CLAIM. Green proves a stalled call ends the run within the bound and that the process refuses to continue; it does not prove the CI stall's cause, does not remove it, and does not make libpari usable after an interrupted pool call. The first CI run after the push is the parity check for the bound; a run that ends with the stall banner is the bound working and finding 2 of cairn-ict still open.

## Architecture
- Approach: arm cysignals' alarm around each pool-using libpari call inside the existing wrappers in src/cairn/pari.py, convert the interrupt into a typed KeyboardInterrupt subclass that names the call and the host state, keep the first stall as module state so every later wrapper call refuses instantly, and let the test harness convert an escaping stall into a session exit at the deadline's code. The alternative, a subprocess boundary around the curve draw, was rejected because the in-process cypari2 path is the skill's definition and the stall also hits selftest.py's corpus evaluation.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/pari.py (run_gp's timeout and typed GpTimeout), tests/_session_deadline.py (a harness module imported by tests/conftest.py, exit 124)
- Touches: src/cairn/pari.py, src/cairn/cli.py, tests/_libpari_stall.py, tests/conftest.py, tests/unit/test_pari_module.py, tests/unit/test_libpari_stall_hook.py, tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py, pyproject.toml, typings/cysignals/__init__.pyi, typings/cysignals/alarm.pyi, typings/cysignals/signals.pyi, tests/goldens/toy_curve_certificate.golden, tests/goldens/toy_curve_selftest_transcript.golden, tests/goldens/instance_maker_certificate.golden, tests/goldens/instance_maker_selftest_transcript.golden, MAP.md, CLAUDE.md, scripts/check.sh
- ADRs: none; the operating rule is PLAN §12 (research software: a bound on every external call) and the CLAUDE.md working note carries the mechanism
- Data model impact: none
- Failure modes: (1) the alarm never fires because Python owns SIGALRM, observable: PariBoundUnavailable from the wrapper and test_a_python_sigalrm_handler_refuses_the_call_rather_than_running_it_unbounded; (2) the alarm fires but the process continues into a poisoned libpari, observable: the refusal message `libpari refused: ... after an earlier stall` and exit 124 from the harness before the next test; (3) the alarm outlives a call and fires in unrelated code, observable: test_the_bound_is_cancelled_when_the_call_returns.

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] cysignals' alarm interrupts an in-process libpari busy loop and a thread-pool wait at the armed second, and AlarmInterrupt derives from KeyboardInterrupt — source: scratch probes probe_alarm.py and the cysignals.alarm.AlarmInterrupt MRO, cysignals 1.12.6 (verified: 2026-09-02) (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R2] After a pool escape the next libpari call segfaults nondeterministically (2 of 3 children rc 139) — source: scratch probe probe_pool2.py (verified: 2026-09-02) (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R3] A Python SIGALRM handler displaces cysignals' handler and the alarm never interrupts a C call; signal.getsignal distinguishes the two owners; SIG_DFL then init_cysignals restores both — source: scratch probes probe_pool2.py (pyhandler), probe_reinstall.py, probe_restore.py (verified: 2026-09-02) (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R4] pytest re-raises KeyboardInterrupt subclasses through the runtest protocol and honors pytest.exit's returncode — source: _pytest/runner.py CallInfo.from_call reraise tuple and _pytest/main.py wrap_session, pytest 9.1.1 (documented: read in the venv) (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R5] The runner classifies a skill child that dies on a signal as STATUS_FAIL with stderr captured — source: src/cairn/runner.py status_for (verified: 2026-09-02, read) (Confidence: HIGH)
- Delegability: STATEABLE
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_pari_module.py tests/unit/test_libpari_stall_hook.py` green; the planted busy loop raises PariStall between 0.4 and 10 s of a 0.5 s bound and the child's pool-wait line reports under 10 s; command and output pasted.
- Positive: `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py -k stall` green: a command raising PariStall exits BACKEND (4) with `PariStall: libpari stall:` in the error and a plain KeyboardInterrupt propagates.
- Positive: the toy_curve and instance_maker certificate and transcript goldens regenerate under the new pari.py revision and their selftest files are green (`uv run pytest -q tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py tests/integration/test_instance_maker_selftest.py`); every other golden is byte-identical (sha256 before and after pasted).
- Positive: the first CI run after the push completes; if it ends with `libpari stall in`, the bound fired on the runner and that line, its nodeid and the load average from the message are pasted on cairn-ict.
- Planted negative: deleting `cancel_alarm()` from `bounded` makes test_the_bound_is_cancelled_when_the_call_returns fail; deleting the `_stall` check makes the refusal assertion fail; deleting the `_alarm_owner` check makes test_a_python_sigalrm_handler_refuses_the_call_rather_than_running_it_unbounded fail; deleting the hook's `pytest.exit` makes the pytester test's exit-124 assertion fail; each shown on a scratch copy with the tree restored byte-identical (sha256 compared).
- No-Claim: green proves a stalled in-process call ends the run within the bound and the process refuses to continue; it does not prove the CI stall's cause, does not remove it, and does not make libpari usable after an interrupted pool call.
- Test types: unit (wrapper, hook via pytester, CLI mapping), integration (skill selftest goldens), planted child process. Files: tests/unit/test_pari_module.py, tests/unit/test_libpari_stall_hook.py, tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py, tests/integration/test_toy_curve_selftest.py, tests/integration/test_instance_maker_selftest.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

title: Investigate CI suite runtime near the session deadline
description:
The CI suite approaches its session deadline. Run34211439340 on63ff58f reached62% and hit900 seconds without a final pytest summary. Run34203431106 completed3085 tests in798.27 seconds. The timeout stack is an observation, not an identified bottleneck. CopperRidge message381 authorizes a1080-second CI deadline inside the20-minute job ceiling and defers runtime investigation to daytime.

## Architecture
- Approach: measure the complete suite and the three observed slow integration tests on a pinned revision, then optimize only a reproduced cost center while preserving every positive and negative observable. Do not reduce sample counts, skip Lean execution, mock arithmetic or storage, or widen timeouts as the optimization. Whole-suite progress percentages are too coarse to identify individual root causes.
- Pattern-to-follow: scripts/check.sh and tests/integration/test_axiom_computation.py
- Touches: the measured cost center among tests/integration/test_axiom_computation.py, tests/integration/test_bsgs_selftest.py, tests/integration/test_lean_toolchain.py and their production callees; final ownership requires coordination.
- ADRs: none; records the measured choice on this bead before implementation.
- Data model impact: none expected; not authorized by this investigation.
- Failure modes: lost test depth detected by preserved planted negatives; misleading speedup detected by paired runs at the same source/toolchain; a deadline kill detected by the existing session watchdog with no green claim.

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] Run34203431106 reports test_real_axiom_matrix71.60s, test_twenty_fresh_forty_bit_instances_drawn_by_postcondition_are_recovered70.25s, and test_hello_theorem_builds_and_leanchecker_replays_it_from_empty52.26s. Source: https://github.com/jwross24/cairn/actions/runs/34203431106 (verified:2026-09-08, root retrieved full log and read duration rows; Confidence:HIGH).
- [R2] Run34211439340 hits the unchanged900-second deadline at62%; the final frame is test logging during an arbitrary-population property test. Source: https://github.com/jwross24/cairn/actions/runs/34211439340 (verified:2026-09-08, root retrieved terminal JSON and full log; Confidence:HIGH).
- [R3] The1080-second session deadline plus15-second backstop leaves105 seconds below the1200-second job ceiling before setup cost. Source: .github/workflows/ci.yml and tests/_session_deadline.py (verified:2026-09-08, full file reads; Confidence:HIGH). Setup cost consumes part of that margin and must be measured.
- Delegability: NEEDS-INVESTIGATION-TICKET. This is the investigation; no specific optimization is prescribed before measurement.

## Acceptance criteria
- Report pinned source, exact commands and full raw output for suite timing and the three named integration tests; no green claim for a partial run.
- Identify a measured cost center and demonstrate one bounded optimization with paired positive and planted-negative behavior, or record a measured no-optimization conclusion without claiming a speedup.
- Compare elapsed time to the1080-second deadline and1200-second job ceiling including setup, naming the remaining margin and runner limits.
- No-Claim: reducing suite runtime adds no mathematical evidence and cannot justify fewer samples, skipped tests, mocked systems or relaxed epistemic gates.

title: Harness: the evidence set is built from the same message grep the anomaly scan was fixed for
description:
The corrector fixes which commit the ANOMALY patterns judge. It does not reach the
EVIDENCE set, and the same message-grep defect lives there.

`gather-evidence.sh:39` sets COMMITS from `git log --all -F --grep="$ID"` and `:45`
builds TOUCHED_FILES from it, so any commit whose message cites a bead id donates its
files to that bead's evidence. `research/SESSION-PROMPTS.md` asks every session to cite
its beads in commit messages, so this fires routinely.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH cairn-fi7. TOUCHED_FILES is consumed at `:79-83` as the second
resolver for a path hint taken from the bead body, with a project-wide `rg --files`
fallback at `:94` behind it. Correcting it after the fact means re-running the hint
resolution, which is re-implementing the script rather than correcting its output. The
corrector cannot reach it without a sixth fork of the vendored skill, and cairn-exi's
standing choice is no sixth fork.

BOUNDED, not harmless. A hint has to substring-match a file from the foreign commit
before it matters, and the project-wide fallback would often resolve the same path
anyway. Nobody has measured how often the foreign match wins.

DONE WHEN
- A measurement over the closed beads of how often TOUCHED_FILES resolves a hint to a
  file that came from a commit the bead did not close, and what the fallback would have
  resolved instead. A count, not an impression.
- Either a cairn-owned correction that does not fork, or a recorded decision that the
  measured rate does not justify one.

comments.text:
CLOSED as a RECORDED DECISION: the measured rate does not justify a correction. No code
changed, and that is the finding rather than a shortfall.

THE MEASUREMENT, over all 37 closed beads, 0 skipped

  path hints                                          435

  resolved at :79-83 TOUCHED_FILES                     24
  resolved at :94 rg --files fallback                  12

  citations LOST if TOUCHED_FILES were deleted outright      1

The one differing case is the resolver doing the right thing. The hint `cairn/doctor/` names a
directory; the fallback's basename regex is anchored `/doctor/$` and matches no file, and
TOUCHED_FILES supplies `src/cairn/doctor/__init__.py`, which is genuinely that bead's artifact.
Deleting the resolver loses that citation and gains nothing.

WHY "FOREIGN" TURNS OUT NOT TO MEAN "ANOTHER BEAD"

All 21 foreign donors are the bead's OWN implementation commit, which is a different commit
from the one that flipped its status in `.beads/*.jsonl`. `scripts/closing_commit.py` is right
that the flip is the closing commit, and the file provenance is still the bead's own work.

Cross-bead contamination IS present in the commit set: `-F --grep` is a substring match, so
`cairn-m0-e0s.1` matches 54 commits because `.10`, `.11` and `.12` all contain it. It
contributed ZERO wrong resolutions, because in every such case the bead's own commit donated
the same file.

THE PROBE WAS SHOWN TO BE ABLE TO SEE THE DEFECT, which is what makes a low number evidence

`absence-is-not-evidence.md` says a zero has two indistinguishable causes. So the harmful shape
was constructed against the real corpus rather than assumed absent: with `cairn-m0-e0s.18`'s
real touched set, the hint `doctor/__init__.py` resolves via TOUCHED to
`src/cairn/doctor/__init__.py` (foreign) while the fallback would name
`src/cairn/skills/__init__.py` -- a different, wrong file. The instrument reports
TOUCHED / foreign / differs and fires. It found zero such instances in 435 real hints.

THE REPLAY WAS VALIDATED AGAINST THE REAL GATHERER'S OUTPUT

Every one of the 37 beads retains an `evidence.json` from the pass that targeted it. The
replay's citations were compared against those recorded citations: 37 agree, 0 disagree, 0
missing. Re-run independently by the session, with the same result. That is what licenses
reading this as a measurement of the historic runs rather than of today's tree.

THE DECISION

Do not correct. Of 435 hints, 24 are decided by TOUCHED_FILES, 21 are "foreign" by the
closing-commit test, none are foreign BEADS, and exactly 1 changes the outcome -- in the
resolver's favor. A cairn-owned corrector would have to re-run the whole hint resolution, which
is this bead's own stated reason the corrector could not reach it, to buy a strictly negative
delta. A sixth fork of the vendored skill is doubly unjustified and was never reached.

THE RESIDUAL RISK IS REAL AND UNREALIZED. The mechanism needs a hint whose substring hits a
foreign file BEFORE the correct one in `sort -u` order, in a tree with duplicated basenames.
This repo carries 35 duplicate `__init__.py` paths, so the mechanism is loaded and has not
fired. If the rate is ever worth re-measuring, the method is: replay `resolve_path_hint`'s four
branches in Python against each closed bead's `spec.json` hints, take the closing commit from
`scripts/closing_commit.py` rather than from `git log --grep`, and validate the replay against

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
CLOSED. The decision stands; the recipe it named does not, and the measurement that changed it
is the substance of this close.

WHAT WAS DECIDED, AND WHY IT SURVIVED

CI derives the bead store from the tracked JSONL through br, rather than each gate growing its
own parser of a format br owns. issues.jsonl is the tracked source of truth and beads.db is
derived, so a CI job deriving it is CI resembling a developer machine. Reading the JSONL
directly in each gate was rejected: it stops exercising the path a developer's br takes.

THE RECIPE THE BEAD NAMED IS NOT SUFFICIENT

`br sync --import-only` was recorded here as the documented recovery path. Measured on br
0.2.22 in a scratch workspace holding only the four tracked .beads files and no database:

  br show cairn-exi --json    exit 6   SYNC_CONFLICT
  br sync --import-only       exit 6   same refusal
  br init                     exit 6   same refusal

br refuses every storage open while a .beads directory carrying no database is in place.
Bisected across five probes: an empty pre-existing .beads/ is the trigger, and `br init` in a
directory with no .beads at all exits 0. So the CI step moves .beads aside, runs br init,
restores the four tracked files, then imports. Executed verbatim from the workflow text in a
scratch checkout built from `git archive HEAD .beads`: exit 0, 62 issues created, `br show`
resolving afterwards, and the four restored files byte-identical to HEAD by sha256.

THE DEFECT UNDERNEATH, WHICH IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE

A database that does not exist was reported as `sync_merge_pending_unknown` -- a pending merge
whose state could not be inspected. A file that is absent is not a conflict, and the
remediation offered was `br list --all`: check the id, for a problem that has nothing to do
with the id. That is an absence given the shape of a verdict, after cairn-8jm, cairn-a30 and
cairn-keq.

The message is br's and cairn does not own it. How cairn's gates react is cairn's.
scripts/br_lookup.py classifies a bead lookup into four conditions, each with its own message
and its own remediation, and a test asserts the four remediations are pairwise distinct:

  br-absent      br is not installed
  no-database    beads.db is derived; issues.jsonl is tracked, with the rebuild recipe
  unknown-bead   the id is not in the store
  unreadable     anything the allowlist does not recognize, which blocks

VERIFICATION, RE-EXECUTED BY THE SESSION

Six tests observed failing against the unfixed gates before the fix.
99 passed with a database present, and 99 passed from an empty mktemp -d cwd with no .beads
anywhere above it -- which is the CI condition, since cwd is what br walks up from.
scripts/check.sh 1958 passed, exit 0.
The planted negatives were re-run by the session AFTER the reformat the implementer's own
NO-CLAIM flagged as unmeasured: removing the ci.yml step kills 3, and neutering
br_lookup.unavailable() kills 8. All four files restored byte-identical.

Two pre-existing tests were repaired in passing: both reached a monkeypatched subprocess only
because a real database happened to exist.

NO-CLAIM

CI behavior after this change is inference. GitHub Actions was not run; what was executed is
the rebuild script's exact text in a macOS scratch checkout, with RUNNER_TEMP set to a temp
dir. The runner differs in ways not reproduced: a real actions/checkout tree, RUNNER_TEMP
semantics, and the br binary from the release tarball rather than the local one. The br
behaviors are measured on 0.2.22 on one machine, and why br refuses is inference from the
error text rather than from its source. CODE_CONDITIONS is an allowlist built from two
observed codes; another code meaning "no database" would land in `unreadable`, which blocks
rather than passes, so the failure is coarse rather than silent. Giving no-database the
warn-not-deny treatment in theater_patterns.py extends an existing documented decision and is
a judgment call this bead did not specify. Whether cairn-o25's br upgrade changes any of the
0.2.22 behaviors measured here is untested, and that bead owns it.

title: Investigate whether the Skeptic Lean projection needs the gate arm
description:
Investigate whether the Skeptic's Lean evidence projection needs the gate execution arm.

The W3 acceptance text explicitly permits only formal_statement_hash and verdict. The current projection therefore omits arm, while the container gate distinguishes dev-macos-fake-landrun from gold-linux-container. A dev-arm pass and a gold-arm pass can present the same projected fields. This is an interface-policy question, not an established epistemic failure. CopperRidge405 requests a separate daytime investigation; F1-F4 test gaps remain on cairn-m1-cqt.6.3.

## Architecture
- Approach: compare the existing two-field projection with the gate-owned arm taxonomy using two real stored gate-run bindings that differ only in arm. Determine whether any authorized Skeptic consumer must distinguish those cases. Keep the existing contract unless the investigation establishes a concrete consumer and the requirement owner approves a deliberate projection change; do not add fields solely because the audit noticed their absence.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/skeptic.py _lean_projection; tests/integration/test_skeptic_isolation.py test_lean_binding_is_statement_and_bundle_scoped.
- Touches: investigation evidence and the decision on this bead; any later implementation is scoped to skeptic.py and its named tests. No Lean, challenge, or gate-bundle edits are authorized by this investigation.
- ADRs: none for the investigation; PLAN.md section7 and the W3 acceptance text define the existing interface. Record the disposition here before proposing implementation.
- Data model impact: none in the investigation.
- Failure modes: a consumer treats a dev-arm result as gold evidence (observable: an executed consumer trace, not merely equal projection bytes); an extra field leaks forbidden proof data (observable: existing exact-projection and forbidden-read assertions fail); an unneeded contract change adds surface without a consumer (observable: no authorized reader branches on arm).

- Planted negative: a dev-arm result cannot acquire a gold-arm interpretation solely through the projection; demonstrate the claimed consumer behavior before proposing a fix. Existing forbidden-content refusals remain intact.

title: human_queue: the attestation binding is vacuous for every attested blocker with no clause
description:
FOUND BY the fresh-eyes audit on cairn-ifd, re-executed by me.

THE OBSERVATION. `human_queue._attestation_binding` (src/cairn/human_queue.py:209-221) has
two real clauses: a statement-target clause reaching `claims.verdict_mirrored`, and a
`nogo_review` clause reaching `nogo.mirrored`. Every other combination falls through to
`return None`, so the only remaining requirement is
`attest.attestation_record_matches`, which asks whether ANY record sits at that offset with
that digest. Any record in the log at any offset but 0 therefore clears the blocker.

MEASURED over `ATTESTED_BLOCKERS x TARGET_KINDS`, clearing each with a `fixture_waiver`
record whose text is unrelated to the item: 24 of 36 pairs cleared. The 12 that did not are
the `nogo_review` rows and the statement-target rows.

REACHABILITY, checked rather than assumed. Two sites in `src/` construct a
`human_queue.Item` with a blocker: `disagreement.py:134` (statement target) and
`nogo.py:218` (branch target). Both land on a bound clause, so no `src/` path reaches a
vacuous pair today. `cairn-ifd` additionally made an attestation record spendable once, so
a vacuous pair still cannot be cleared by a record already used elsewhere.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH CLOSING. `scrutiny.write_signoff` exists and enqueues no queue item.
The day it does, `expert_signoff` is an attested blocker with a target kind that has no
clause, so its clearing binds to nothing but "some record exists". The binding is empty
exactly where a new producer would first rely on it.

DONE WHEN `_attestation_binding` names a clause for every (attested blocker, target_kind)
pair it admits, or refuses the pair outright rather than falling through to `None`, and a
planted negative shows an unrelated record refused for a branch, rung and audit_cycle
target.

TEST PLAN. tests/integration/test_blocker_clearing_binding.py gains the matrix as a
parametrized planted negative beside the pairs already covered there.

title: Clarify Skeptic recipe input digest visibility
description:
Clarify whether Skeptic-readable recipe input digests satisfy the scoped-read contract.

The W3 interface allows recipes needed for reruns and refuses Solution/prover content and general input reads. Its non-Lean recipe projection is canonical recipe bytes; RECIPE.inputs is Map(STR, BLOBREF), so those bytes describe input references. The audit raises whether hashes and sizes are intended provenance or forbidden exposure. It provides source inspection, not an executed leak reproduction. CopperRidge405 requests this separate daytime investigation; the four W3 test gaps remain on cairn-m1-cqt.6.3.

## Architecture
- Approach: decode a real scoped non-Lean recipe projection and attempt to read each referenced blob through the same handle. Determine whether the reference values are needed by the writer's rerun validation and whether an authorized reader can use them to obtain forbidden content. Resolve digest visibility separately from content access; do not remove reproducibility identity or widen access to make a fixture pass.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/skeptic.py _non_lean_projection and _canonical_projection; src/cairn/keys.py RECIPE; tests/integration/test_skeptic_isolation.py test_snapshot_reads_filtered_records_and_refuses_forbidden_data.
- Touches: investigation evidence and disposition on this bead; any later projection change requires an explicit requirement decision and scoped tests. No Lean, challenge, or bundle changes are authorized here.
- ADRs: none for this investigation; PLAN.md sections3/7 and W3 acceptance define the provenance and read boundary. Record the disposition here before implementation.
- Data model impact: none in the investigation.
- Failure modes: a digest permits a forbidden read through an exposed capability (observable: successful read of an outside-scope blob); redaction breaks exact recipe binding for a fresh rerun (observable: existing real rerun fails or uses another recipe); a seeded string is reported as a real content leak (observable: probe lacks a real stored recipe/blob or reachable read path).

WHAT WAS WRONG, ESTABLISHED BY READING THE PRODUCER, NOT THE TABLE

The five items on cairn-m0-e0s.12's missing list are not unresolvable, they are unreachable.
gather-evidence.sh guards its per-test ripgrep with `[ "$NAME" != "primary" ]` where NAME is

minted bead states on its face which of its items were measured and which were not."

2. "An item with no expected_path_hints is either given them or reported as unresolvable
rather than missing."

3. "A decision, recorded, on whether the pre-commit path should run a real Phase 4, or

than report-only. A real Phase 4 is out of reach regardless: single-bead-audit.sh:152 writes

therefore no standing to mint debt from its own silence.

A fresh Opus /optimal-tests --audit found six confirmed defects. The worst was on this
bead's headline property: every assertion about the two subsection labels reached them
through constants imported from the subject, so the label text sat on both sides of the
comparison. Swapping the two constants' values, so every classification rendered under the
opposite heading, left all 29 tests green. Since remediate.sh copies the section verbatim,
an inverted label would have shipped an inverted claim into the exact artifact this tool

title: Harness: the bead database corrupted, and its cleanup debris blocks commits under a misleading message
description:
Two failures on the same surface, both hit while closing cairn-pwj.

ONE. THE BEAD DATABASE CORRUPTED DURING ORDINARY USE.

`br comments add` reported "Mutation succeeded, but automatic JSONL export failed", and
`br doctor` then found:

  sqlite.integrity_check   ERROR  database disk image is malformed: page 16 is referenced
                                  multiple times (freelist trunk[0] leaf[116];
                                  table `issues` root -> child[36])
  sqlite3.integrity_check  ERROR  Tree 2 page 2 cell 36: 2nd reference to page 16; wrong #
                                  of entries in eight indexes

No power loss, no kill, no concurrent writer beyond the session's own. It happened within
the hour after the binary moved from 0.2.10 to 0.5.3 and the database was rebuilt from
JSONL, and `br doctor` had run `fsqlite: applied migration repairs` on the way.

Recovery cost nothing, because the database is untracked derived state and `issues.jsonl`
was intact: 57 records parsed, db and JSONL in sync, the pwj close present. Moving the
family aside and `br sync --import-only` rebuilt it, integrity clean, JSONL byte-identical
at sha256 9dbc90c8. That is the documented path and it worked.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the cause. One occurrence, no reproduction, and three candidates
that this session cannot separate -- a 0.5.3 defect, damage inherited from the schema-10
database it replaced, or the interrupted write that produced the export failure. Recording
it as an observation rather than a diagnosis.

TWO. HOUSEKEEPING BLOCKS THE COMMIT GATE, AND THIS ONE RECURS.

`.githooks/pre-commit` runs the vendored beads hook, which runs `br doctor` and treats a
non-zero exit as a failed audit:

  ERROR: br doctor failed with exit code 1. Hand off to /fixing-beads-problems.
  [beads-hook] BLOCKED: one or more newly-closed beads failed quick audit (score < 700).

The message names a score, and no score was involved. The actual cause was

  WARN db.recovery_artifacts: Preserved recovery artifacts remain for this database family
                              (21 item(s))

which is a WARN about `.bak` files in `.beads/.br_recovery/`, a gitignored directory. Every
database rebuild and every `br doctor --repair` leaves more of them, so the count only
grows, and `br doctor --repair` reports "No errors detected; nothing to repair" for exactly
this finding. Clearing them by hand is what unblocked the commit, twice in one session.

So a commit that closes a bead can be refused for a pile of backup files, under a message
that says the bead scored below threshold. The diagnosis cost more than the fix both times.

DONE WHEN
- The beads hook's refusal distinguishes a failing AUDIT from a failing `br doctor`, and a
  doctor WARN does not read as a bead scoring below threshold. The message a reader gets
  should name what actually happened.
- A doctor finding that `--repair` declines to act on does not block a commit, or the hook
  says which finding blocked it and how to clear it.
- Recorded: whether `.br_recovery/` needs periodic clearing at all, and if so what clears
  it, since nothing currently does and the count grows monotonically.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
SECOND OCCURRENCE, and the export half now looks reproducible rather than incidental.

Closing cairn-o0l, a large `br comments add` again reported

  Warning: Mutation succeeded, but automatic JSONL export failed. ...
  Error: Database error: unable to open database file: '.../.beads/beads.db'

That is two for two on large comment bodies this session, roughly 8 KB each. Unlike the
first occurrence the database was NOT corrupt: `sqlite.integrity_check` and
`sqlite3.integrity_check` both read OK immediately afterward, the comment was present in the
database, and a manual `br sync --flush-only` exported cleanly.

So the two failures separate into two findings rather than one:

  the EXPORT failing on a large comment write  -- reproducible, benign, recovered by a
                                                  manual flush
  the DATABASE corrupting                      -- once, cause unestablished, recovered by
                                                  rebuilding from JSONL

The first is what the operator hits every time; the second may or may not share its cause.
A write path that reports "unable to open database file" for a database it just wrote to,
and that a manual flush then opens without complaint, points at a lock or handle lifetime
inside the export step rather than at the file.

The commit-blocking half of this bead also recurred: `.beads/.br_recovery/` refilled during
the rebuild and had to be cleared by hand a third time before a commit closing a bead would
pass.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
RESOLVED UPSTREAM for the corruption half; the commit-gate half stays open here.

The corruption is beads_rust#457, "v0.5.3 (fsqlite 0.3.11) malforms migrated databases under
concurrent multi-process writes", filed 2026-08-27 by another site and confirmed by a third
the same day. Every symptom recorded on this bead appears in that report: the page-aliasing
`integrity_check` failure, the `Mutation succeeded, but automatic JSONL export failed ...
unable to open database file` warning on the write that precedes it, `issues.jsonl` intact
every time, vacuum `.bak` families left in `.br_recovery/`, and `br doctor health` reporting
healthy on a database `integrity_check` calls malformed. The named mechanism is a
vacuum-on-write self-heal replacing the file while other processes hold it open.

So the cause this bead recorded as unestablished is established, and it is not cairn's.

TWO OBSERVATIONS FROM HERE WERE NEW ENOUGH TO POST, and are recorded on that issue:

  It reproduced at far lower concurrency than the report describes -- one interactive session
  with short-lived subagents and the git hooks, against the reporter's 25-30 concurrent
  agents.

  The second event was on a database 0.5.3 had itself just built from JSONL, not on a
  migrated one. This machine's database was schema 10, which `br doctor migrate-schema plan`
  refuses outright (`available only from source schemas 13, 14, 15, and 16`), so no migration
  ever ran; the rebuild was the only path. That narrows the issue's stated "needs a migrated
  family" precondition. The one dimension where this workspace differs from a seeded one is
  payload size -- 83 comments, several over 8 KB, and both export warnings landed on exactly
  such a write. Posted as a correlation across two events, explicitly not as a claim, since no
  controlled reproduction varying only comment size was run.

ACTION TAKEN. `br` is rolled back to 0.2.22, the version the issue's own stress harness
measured clean over 408 operations where 0.5.3 malformed at 87. The documented downgrade path
worked: a 0.2.x binary refuses a 0.5.3-written database permanently, so `br init` in a scratch
directory, the empty `beads.db` copied in beside `issues.jsonl`, then import. 58 records
restored, `integrity_check` ok, `issues.jsonl` byte-identical by sha256 across a flush.
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins `BR_VERSION` to match, and CLAUDE.md carries the tell and the
recovery.

A correction to what this bead assumed: 0.2.22 is NOT a pre-FrankenSQLite release. It writes
the same `-fsqlite-ns-gate` and `-fsqlite-ns-use` sidecars. The case for it is the empirical
result in that issue, not a difference in storage engine, and this bead should not be read as
saying otherwise.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN HERE, and it is cairn's own: `br doctor` returns a nonzero exit for a
WARN-level `db.recovery_artifacts` finding, `.githooks/pre-commit` reads that exit as a failed
audit, and the message a reader gets names a score that was never computed. It blocked three
commits this session. The vendored hook is not cairn-owned, but the message a cairn commit
prints is cairn's problem to make honest. The DONE WHEN above still applies to that half.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
ANOTHER SILENT CONSEQUENCE OF THE 0.2.22 PIN, FOUND 2026-08-29: new beads got temp ids.

`br create` returned `tmpvvbh5n6it3-tlt` instead of a `cairn-` id. `.beads/config.yaml` has
had every key commented out since `br init` at 959b43f, including `issue_prefix: cairn`.
br 0.5.3 inferred the prefix regardless; 0.2.22 does not and mints a temp id.

It is silent in the way this bead is about. `br create` exits 0. `br doctor` reports
HEALTH workspace: healthy and passes all 59 checks bar the two dependency WARNs and the
`.write.lock` gitignore WARN -- none of which name the id. The bead lands in the database and
in issues.jsonl under the temp id and is indistinguishable from a real one until someone
reads it.

FIXED HERE by uncommenting `issue_prefix: cairn` in `.beads/config.yaml`, shipped with the
cairn-8jm close. Verified with a disposable probe: the create immediately before the change
minted a temp id, the one immediately after minted `cairn-00h`. Probe deleted.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED, and belongs to this bead's open half: nothing detects the condition. A
config with the prefix commented out is not a WARN, and `br doctor` is the tool that ought to
say so. Any check this bead adds for the misleading commit-block should cover this too --
same shape, a healthy-looking report over a workspace that will silently do the wrong thing.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION LANDED AT 8c1900a. THE BEAD STAYS OPEN, and what is missing is named below.

WHAT SHIPPED

scripts/beads_doctor_gate.py reads `br doctor --json`, allowlists the status and health
values observed on an intact store, and blocks everything else, so an unrecognized value
denies rather than passes. Four outcomes to .check.log: DOCTOR-CLEAR, DOCTOR-ADVISORY,
DOCTOR-BLOCKED, DOCTOR-INFRA, plus BYPASS via CAIRN_DOCTOR_GATE_OK. Wired into
.githooks/pre-commit ahead of the audit. tests/unit/test_beads_doctor_gate.py, 29 tests.

Three vendored fork sites, one more than the design named: bootstrap-audit.sh's exit-code
gate, its health-gate predicates, and inventory-beads.sh line 50, which captured doctor.json
with no `|| true` under `set -e` and killed the audit at the next step. The fork-detection
block in .githooks/pre-commit gained two markers, so a revert denies rather than silently
restoring the old behavior.

THE FINDING THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN. The plan was to relax the ok:false gate. That would have
been wrong. On a database corrupted deliberately in a disposable workspace, br 0.2.22 emits
`status: "error"` and `severity: "recoverable"` -- and the skill's health gate blocks only on

title: human_queue: an item's class and its blocker are validated independently, so they can disagree
description:
FOUND BY the fresh-eyes audit on cairn-ifd.

THE OBSERVATION. `human_queue.Item.__post_init__` (src/cairn/human_queue.py:118-135)
validates `item_class` against `CLASSES` and `blocker` against `BLOCKERS` independently.
Nothing ties the two, so a `disagreement`-class item may carry `blocker="already_settled"`,
and cairn-ifd's split keys on the blocker value alone (`blocker_is_attested` reads only
`item["blocker"]`). Such an item clears on a bare string with no attestation record.

REPRODUCED by the audit: a disagreement-class item carrying `already_settled` closed on the
string "anything".

NOT REACHABLE TODAY. `disagreement.record` hardcodes `blocker=DISAGREEMENT`, and
`disagreement.standing` reads item ids from the `disagreements` table rather than from the
class column, so no freeze is lifted this way. The two producers in `src/` that set a
blocker at all, `disagreement.py:135` and `nogo.py:219`, each set the blocker matching their
class. This is a missing invariant, not an exploit.

WHY THE SPLIT KEYS ON THE BLOCKER ANYWAY. `already_settled` is a blocker with no class of
its own, so a class-keyed split cannot express it. The fix is to add the missing invariant
rather than to re-key the split.

DONE WHEN `Item.__post_init__` refuses a blocker that is neither `already_settled` nor equal
to the item's own class, and a planted negative shows a disagreement-class item carrying a
gate blocker refused at construction.

TEST PLAN. tests/unit/test_human_queue.py gains the mismatched pair as a planted negative
beside the existing class and blocker validation cases.

title: Harness: cairn doctor accumulates run directories with no gc, and flagged backups resist removal
description:
The doctor's run artifacts accumulate under `.doctor/runs/<run-id>/` and nothing
ever removes them. Every `cairn doctor` invocation, read-only ones included, writes
a run directory, so the tree grows without bound on an agent that runs the doctor
as its first move whenever a command refuses -- which is what `robot-docs` tells it
to do.

Two properties make this more than housekeeping.

`mutate._backup` copies the source file's flags onto the backup, so a backup of the
pin or the attestation log carries `uappnd`. A run directory holding one cannot be
removed until the flag is cleared recursively. This is visible today as eight
`PytestWarning: (rm_rf) ... Directory not empty` lines in the suite, on temp trees
pytest tried to clean.

And the doctor performs no deletion by design. The gate is an AST scan scoped to
`src/cairn/doctor/`: `tests/unit/test_doctor_purity.py`. Read it before planning the
removal, because its shape is not the one "add the module to the allowlist" assumes.
`DELETE_ATTRS = {remove, unlink, rmtree, removedirs}` is refused in EVERY doctor module
with no allowlist at all, and `test_a_planted_deleter_is_caught_even_in_the_chokepoint`
pins that a delete inside `mutate.py` is caught. Only `rmdir` carries an allowlist,
`RMDIR_ALLOWED = {"mutate.py"}`, which is why `mutate.py:218`'s `target.rmdir()` —
undoing its own `mkdir` — is the one rmdir under `src/`. `WRITE_ALLOWED = {"mutate.py",
"artifacts.py"}` governs writes, not deletes. And the scan looks only inside the doctor
package: `shutil.rmtree` at `src/cairn/verifier.py:152` and `out.unlink()` at
`src/cairn/bundle.py:103` stand outside it, unrefused.

So collection cannot be a side effect of an existing path, and it cannot be bought by
adding a module to a write allowlist either. Removing a run directory needs one of two
deliberate moves, and the bead's close names which: a `DELETE_ALLOWED` set the scan does
not have today, which also moves that pinned planted-deleter expectation, or a removal
module outside `src/cairn/doctor/` that the scan is not scoped to reach.

WHAT: `cairn doctor gc --before <date> --yes` from the CLI-SURFACE of
`/world-class-doctor-mode-for-cli-tools`, which `cairn-m0-e0s.18` implemented
without it. Dangerous, gated on `--yes`, dry-run by default, listing what it would
remove and removing nothing without the flag -- the shape `cairn gc` already uses
for blobs (`src/cairn/gc.py`, `cairn-m0-e0s.13`). It must clear `uappnd` before
removing a flagged backup, and it must refuse to remove the run a `latest` symlink
points at.

The same surface also names `cairn doctor diff` and `--since=<run-id>`, neither of
which exists. They are cheap once the run index is readable and belong here rather
than in a bead of their own.

DONE WHEN: a doctor run directory older than a given date is removed by
`doctor gc --before <date> --yes` and left alone without `--yes`; a flagged backup
inside it is removed rather than refused; the run `.doctor/latest` points at is
refused with its own exit code and a message naming it; and
`tests/unit/test_doctor_purity.py` still passes, with the removal confined to one named
module and the scan's own expectations moved deliberately rather than discovered — a
`DELETE_ALLOWED` entry with the planted-deleter case retargeted, or the removal placed
outside `src/cairn/doctor/` and named where the scan's scope is stated.

Surfaced by cairn-m0-e0s.18's audit as F15, recorded there as out of scope for that
bead rather than folded into it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `cairn doctor gc --before <date>` lists the run directories it would remove
  and removes nothing; the same command with `--yes` removes them; the tree before and
  after, and both commands, pasted.
- Positive: a run directory holding a backup that carries `uappnd` — `_backup` copies the
  source file's flags onto the backup (src/cairn/doctor/mutate.py:108-113) — is removed
  rather than refused, with the flag-clearing step and the removal both shown; `cairn
  doctor diff` and `--since=<run-id>` answer from the run index, output pasted.
- Planted negative: the run `.doctor/latest` resolves to is refused with its own exit
  code and a message naming it; `--before <date>` without `--yes` leaves every candidate
  on disk, asserted by listing the tree afterwards rather than by trusting the dry-run
  banner; and `tests/unit/test_doctor_purity.py` goes red when the removal is added to a
  doctor module the scan's own sets do not name — shown once in a scratch copy with the
  failure pasted, then restored byte-identical (length + sha256 in Python, never a shell
  diff).
- No-Claim: collection bounds the doctor's own disk growth and nothing else. It is not a
  substrate GC — `cairn gc` (src/cairn/gc.py) deletes blob rows and touches no file — it
  changes no detector verdict, and it makes no claim about the eight `(rm_rf) ...
  Directory not empty` warnings beyond the ones its own runs produce.
- Test types: unit, integration, purity-scan (AST). Files:
  tests/unit/test_doctor_purity.py, tests/integration/test_doctor.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
A second measurement, stronger than the one in the description, and it inverts the gate.

Two beads closed in the same session, audited by the same hook at the same threshold:

  cairn-m0-e0s.12  760/1000   the justify module: 108 unit and integration tests, six
                              metamorphic relations at 500 examples, six named mutants
                              each killed by its own relation, a fresh-eyes test audit
                              whose thirteen findings were all applied
  cairn-qn9        970/1000   a lint-and-types cleanup with no tests of its own

The 970 is not a judgment about quality. Its scorecard reads:

  Implementation 300/300  "n/a - no code artifacts in spec"
  Docs           100/100  "n/a - no non-code artifacts in spec"
  Tests          250/250  WAIVED, Phase 4 stub mode
  Test depth     150/150  WAIVED, Phase 6 stub mode
  Cross-bead      50/50   no synthesis findings touch this bead

Phase 2 emitted its own warning: "bead cairn-qn9 produced only 1 item(s) from a
2689-char body", and spec.json in fact holds zero items. So 400 points were waived
and 400 more were awarded for having nothing to check. The bead scored highest by
being least specific.

The 760 came the other way. cairn-m0-e0s.12 named its test files, so the gatherer
had items to look for and marked four MISSING that were present; and it named ten
open downstream beads as owners for its No-Claim gaps, which the cross-bead
dimension scored as ten findings and -100, taking that dimension to 0/50. Naming a
downstream owner is required by research/SESSION-PROMPTS.md. The gate penalizes the
discipline the project mandates.

The consequence for the threshold question: raising 700 to 950 would have blocked
the well-tested bead and waved through the lighter one. The number tracks how little
the parser extracted, not how well the work was done, so no threshold on it means
what it appears to mean until the phases below are fixed.

Add to the done-when: the two beads above are re-audited after the fix and the
justify bead scores at least as high as the cleanup bead, since a threshold is only
meaningful once the ordering is right.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
RETRACTION. This bead's description and my earlier comment say the compliance audit
"mis-measures this project" and needs fixing. That framing is wrong and I am
withdrawing it. I concluded a defect in the producer from the shape of its output
without reading the producer, which is the exact inference
`absence-is-not-evidence.md` exists to stop.

What I did not check before claiming it: the skill ships
subagents/compliance-verifier.md and subagents/test-depth-auditor.md, the two the
stub banner named as not-run, and subagents/bead-spec-extractor.md, which its own
Phase 2 warning recommends for prose acceptance criteria ("LLM gets 10-49 items vs
deterministic 0-7"). It carries 43 scripts, 63 references and 23 subagents, and
scripts/_load-policy.sh resolves a project-local `audit-policy.yaml` with
precedence hardcoded < YAML < CLI. threshold, weights_by_type, weights_by_label,
project_theater_patterns, subagents and phase_4_environment are all configurable
per project without touching the vendored skill.

So the audit is not broken. We invoked its cheapest path — single-bead-audit.sh
from a git hook, which deliberately runs no subagents because a hook cannot afford
test re-runs — and never wrote a policy file.

What survives, still measured and still worth acting on:

- The hook path awards Phase 4's 250 and Phase 6's 150 without running them, so
  400 of 1000 points are unearned on that path whatever the bead contains.
- cairn-qn9 scored 970 with zero extracted spec items; cairn-m0-e0s.12, which
  carries 108 tests, six metamorphic relations and six killed mutants, scored 760.
  The ordering is inverted on the hook path.
- The cross-bead dimension took cairn-m0-e0s.12 to 0/50 for ten findings, each
  "references non-closed bead X (status=open)", which research/SESSION-PROMPTS.md
  requires a close to do.

The fix is configuration, not a fork. The threshold question is answered the same
way: it is one line in audit-policy.yaml, and it should not move until the waived
phases actually run, because raising a number over a stubbed measurement buys
confidence rather than assurance.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
The configuration path is inert on this machine, and it fails silently. Measured
2026-08-25, and it changes what this bead has to do.

  $ python3 -c "import yaml"
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'
  $ which python3
  /opt/homebrew/bin/python3          # Homebrew python@3.14, externally managed

Both readers swallow that:

- scripts/_load-policy.sh:49 runs `python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || true`
  around `import sys, yaml`, so the ImportError is discarded and the function
  emits nothing. The caller's `[ -n "${POLICY_X:-}" ]` then keeps its hardcoded
  default. Proved by sourcing it directly against a file that parses under pyyaml
  and holds `threshold: 700` at top level: POLICY_FILE resolves, THRESHOLD is
  empty.
- scripts/score-bead.py:95 wraps `import yaml` in try/except and sets
  `yaml = None`, so weights_by_type and weights_by_label are read by nothing.

So audit-policy.yaml exists, resolves, and binds nowhere. A reader would take the
file as authoritative; it is decoration until PyYAML is present. That is the
silent-fail-open shape from enforcement-over-instructions.md, in the tool we were
relying on to catch exactly that.

`audit-policy.yaml` now ships at the project root with this stated in its header,
so it does not lie about itself, and the same file is seeded into
beads_compliance_audit/, which is gitignored and had been holding an unmodified
copy of the skill's template since 2026-08-21 — that copy shadows the project-local
file, because the loader prefers the audit-dir path.

The threshold still binds, by luck rather than design: .githooks/pre-commit reaches
single-bead-audit.sh with `--threshold`, and CLI beats YAML.

WHAT
- Operator action, not an agent action: make PyYAML importable by the `python3` on
  PATH. It is Homebrew's externally-managed interpreter, so this is a deliberate
  machine-global change and belongs to whoever owns the machine.
- Then re-audit cairn-m0-e0s.12 and cairn-qn9 and check the ordering inverts back:
  the bead with 108 tests, six metamorphic relations and six killed mutants must
  outscore the cleanup with none. That is the falsifiable test for the weights.
- Only after that ordering is right does the threshold become worth moving.
- Consider reporting the silent-fail-open upstream; a skill whose job is to catch
  unearned green should not have a configuration path that fails open in silence.

DONE WHEN: `python3 -c "import yaml"` succeeds; a re-audit of both beads scores
cairn-m0-e0s.12 above cairn-qn9, with both scorecards pasted; and a deliberate edit
to weights_by_type.task provably moves a score, so the file is shown to bind rather
than assumed to.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
PROVED, by controlled substitution rather than inference, and it is not a Cairn
problem. The same condition holds for every project on this machine.

Baseline, system python3 (Homebrew python@3.14, no PyYAML):

  cairn            THRESHOLD=[]  POLICY=[]
  goddess-engine   THRESHOLD=[]

Then a shim earlier on PATH, `python3` execing `uv run --with pyyaml python`,
changing nothing else:

  cairn            THRESHOLD=[700]  POLICY=[completion-debt]
  goddess-engine   THRESHOLD=[700]

Both projects' policy files are well-formed and both bind the moment the
interpreter can parse YAML. PyYAML is the sole cause. goddess-engine has carried an
inert `.beads/audit-policy.yaml` for as long as this machine has lacked the module,
which nothing reported, because both readers swallow the ImportError.

That makes the fix worth more than one project: one install makes every
audit-policy.yaml on this machine live at once. It also raises the stakes on
reporting it upstream — a skill whose purpose is catching unearned green has a
configuration path that fails open in silence, and two projects here believed they
were configured when they were not.

The shim is not the fix and was removed after the measurement; editing PATH for a
vendored skill is a trick, not a deployment.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
FIXED at the cause, in the skill, without a machine-global install.

The three call sites that needed a YAML-capable interpreter now ask uv for one per
invocation and fall back to python3 where uv is absent:

  scripts/_load-policy.sh      python3 -           -> _policy_python -   (new helper)
  scripts/run-pass.sh:241      python3 score-bead  -> uv run --quiet --with pyyaml python
  scripts/single-bead-audit.sh:180  same

and a real audit still runs clean: single-bead-audit.sh on cairn-m0-e0s.12 exits 0

overwrite it. The change is written to survive re-application: each site is a
one-line substitution with the reason in a comment above the helper, and
/tmp/skillbak holds the originals from this session. Report it upstream; a skill
whose purpose is catching unearned green should not have a config path that fails
open in silence.

deterministic path, or stop shipping a weights section that binds nothing; and

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
STAYS OPEN. Two of the done-when items are met and pasted below, one is met only

A fixture bead closed with the word "Done." and a body naming two files that do not

775 of 1000 for having nothing to check. No threshold reaches that, because the

  cairn-qn9         0  Theater   FALSE-CLOSED   225 of 1000 weight measured
  cairn-m0-e0s.12 750  Partial                  375 of 500 measured, rescaled
  cairn-m0-e0s.16 750  Partial                  375 of 500 measured, rescaled

The fixture fails and the ordering inverts back. 500 is the highest floor the hook

It ships off, and that is the operator's call to reverse. Turning it on blocks the

NOT MET — the hook path runs the real compliance-verifier and test-depth-auditor,

Still stubbed, still awarding the tests and test_depth weights in full, which under

Leaving it off leaves this item open, and the two are one decision, not two.

ALSO MEASURED, AND FIXED HERE

score-bead.py handed a path with no spec.json reported 1000/1000 Verified, created
the directory, and wrote the scorecard into it — every dimension read its inputs as

comments.text:
THE DECISION, delegated to me and made against the whole population rather than
the four beads I had in front of me. Commit cae6829.

The switch stays off, and the reason is not caution. It is that no setting of it
separates an honest bead from a false close on this path.

WHAT WAS MEASURED

Sixteen closed beads audited individually to generate real extractions, then scored
under full_credit and under excluded at floors 0, 225, 400, 450, 475 and 500. Every
one of the sixteen measures exactly 500 of 1000 weight on the hook path, because
Phase 4 and Phase 6 are stubbed there and their tests and test_depth weights are
never measurable. cairn-qn9 measures 225.

At excluded / 450 / 600, through the real single-bead audit:

  cairn-0sc (a fixture closed with "Done.")   0  UNVERIFIABLE  hook BLOCKED the commit
  cairn-8il (same, naming no test file)       0  UNVERIFIABLE  hook BLOCKED the commit
  cairn-qn9                                   0  UNVERIFIABLE
  cairn-m0-e0s.1                            674  PASSING
  cairn-m0-e0s.12                           650  PASSING
  cairn-m0-e0s.16                           650  PASSING
  cairn-m0-e0s.2 .7 .9 .17 and the rest     750  PASSING

The gate works. The fixture that scored 975 and read Verified this morning is
refused, and the pre-commit hook blocks the commit that closes it:

  [beads-hook] Verifying 1 newly-closed bead(s) at threshold=600...
  [beads-hook] -> cairn-8il
    Score:   0 / 1000   (threshold: 600)
  [beads-hook] BLOCKED: one or more newly-closed beads failed quick audit (score < 600).

Lowering the threshold from 700 to 600 alongside is a raise, not a relaxation.
Under full_credit a bead is handed 500 free, so 700 required 200 of its 500
measured, forty per cent. Under excluded, 600 of a rescaled 1000 requires 300 of
500, sixty per cent. The bar on measured evidence goes up by half.

WHAT STOPPED IT

cairn-cue itself, audited under that same setting, scores 0 and reads UNVERIFIABLE.

                       cairn-cue          the "Done." fixture
  Implementation       n/a 250/250        n/a 250/250
  Required tests       WAIVED 300/300     WAIVED 300/300
  Test depth           WAIVED 200/200     WAIVED 200/200
  Docs                 n/a 25/25          n/a 25/25
  Anti-theater         200/200            185/200
  Cross-bead           0/25               15/25
  measured weight      225                225

Identical where the floor looks. A bead whose product is configuration and whose
body is prose is indistinguishable, to a regex extractor, from a bead with nothing
behind it. Every floor that fails the fixture fails cairn-cue and cairn-qn9 with
it, and cairn-qn9 is honest work whose only fault is prose.

So the choice was never "strict or lenient". It was "a gate that cannot fail a
false close" against "a gate that also fails honest work", and the second is not
obviously better than the first. Neither is acceptable, and the thing that makes
one of them acceptable is extraction, which this path does not do. cairn-exi owns
that choice, blocks on this bead, and carries three options with their costs.

The switch ships off, tested, with the measurement written beside it in
audit-policy.yaml so the next reader does not have to rediscover it.

STATUS OF THE DONE-WHEN LIST

  MET   a deliberate edit to weights_by_type.task moves a score
        780 -> 875 with the weights binding; 875 -> 937 -> 875 across an edit and
        its restoration, end to end through the real audit

  MET   the cross-bead dimension stops punishing a named open downstream owner
        by weight rather than by scorer change: 25 of 1000 instead of 50

  MET   a deliberately false-closed fixture scores below the threshold while
        cairn-m0-e0s.12 scores above it
        0 against 650, measured, with the hook blocking the commit -- reachable
        only with the switch on, and the switch is off for the reason above

  NOT MET, AND NOT REACHABLE HERE
        the hook path runs the real compliance-verifier and test-depth-auditor, or
        stops awarding their points. Running subagents from a git hook is what the
        skill deliberately refuses, and stopping the award is the switch. Both ends
        of that "or" now depend on cairn-exi.

This bead stays open on that last item, which is one decision with cairn-exi rather
than a separate piece of work. Closing it would be closing three quarters of a list
and calling it whole.

WHAT ELSE THIS SESSION SETTLED, all committed and all measured

  cb5fa73  weights_by_type reaches the scorer through a rubric sync run before
           rubric_sha256 is pinned; the audit dir's policy copy is refreshed from
           the project file every run rather than seeded once, so the project file
           stops being decoration; score-bead.py refuses a bead directory with no
           spec.json instead of reporting 1000/1000 Verified and creating the
           directory to hold the scorecard; .githooks/pre-commit denies when the
           skill fork is reverted, proved by hiding the sync script
  9c24f01  a red baseline this work surfaced in cairn-m0-e0s.16's own harness
  dcbe208  the unmeasured_dimensions and minimum_measured_weight keys
  cae6829  the threshold reaches the hook from the policy file; the decision above

NO-CLAIM

Nothing here measures whether any bead's work is good. It measures whether the
audit's configuration reaches the scorer and whether the scorer can return a
failing verdict for a close with nothing behind it. It can, and the project cannot
switch it on yet. The five forked call sites are in CLAUDE.md and an upstream skill
update reverts them; the pre-commit guard catches two of the five. The 650 to 750
that real beads score under the switch is still an upper bound, because the 500 of
weight it excludes was never measured rather than measured and passed.

CLOSED AT cac8ab6 WITH ALL FOUR DONE-WHEN ITEMS RE-MEASURED BY THE MAIN AGENT.
Six commits across two sessions: cb5fa73, dcbe208, cae6829, 9c24f01 (the policy file
reaching the scorer, the switch, the threshold, a red baseline), then 0c23023 (the
coherence gate) and cac8ab6 (the cross-bead attribution).

THE FOUR DONE-WHEN ITEMS

  MET  the hook path runs the real compliance-verifier and test-depth-auditor, OR
       stops awarding their points -- the second branch. The hook still runs stubs.
       It now awards them nothing and says so: the scorecard's rows for Required
       tests, Test depth and Docs read `— / —  EXCLUDED from numerator and
       denominator`.

  MET  the cross-bead dimension stops penalizing a named open downstream owner.
       cairn-cue reads `Cross-bead integration | 25 | 25 | No synthesis findings this
       bead owns; 1 ignored by policy`, against 0/25 before.

  MET  a deliberately false-closed fixture scores below the threshold while a real
       bead scores above it. Re-run by me at HEAD:
         cairn-cue   842 / 1000
         cairn-6cp     0 / 1000   UNVERIFIABLE
         cairn-qn9   842 / 1000
         cairn-m0-e0s.12  780 / 1000
       threshold 700.

The prior session's comment recorded the first item as NOT MET AND NOT REACHABLE
HERE. cairn-exi made the second branch of its "or" real, and this bead then found
that turning the switch on was necessary but not sufficient.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND, ONE OF WHICH I DID NOT ANTICIPATE

  THE SCORECARD CONTRADICTED ITS OWN ARITHMETIC. The dimension table showed Required
  tests 300/300 and Test depth 200/200 marked WAIVED, and the banner read "WAIVED
  with full credit ... an UPPER BOUND on real completion". The denominator line said
  the opposite: "scored over the 475 of 1000 weight measured (375/475), rescaled".
  The denominator was telling the truth -- 175 + 200 + 0 = 375, and 375/475 rescaled
  is 789, the reported score. So 500 points were excluded and the table said they
  were granted.

  The starker case was the fixture. cairn-6cp's rows summed to 980 while its TOTAL
  row read 0: the table and the verdict disagreed by 980 points on the one bead whose
  entire purpose is to be caught.

  Mechanism: `score-bead.py` printed `weights[key]` unconditionally on every row while
  `rescale_over_measured` had already removed that weight from both sides.

  THE CROSS-BEAD DIMENSION CHARGED A BEAD FOR BEING CITED. This is the one I did not
  name when I handed the bead over. `relevant = [f for f in findings if bead_id in
  f["beads"]]` selects every synthesis row that mentions the bead in any position.
  Six of cairn-cue's seven findings were other beads referencing IT -- cairn-0sc,
  cairn-exi, cairn-fi7, cairn-fur, cairn-l5v and cairn-us2 all name cairn-cue as the
  bead they point at. Only the seventh was its own act. The fix owns a finding by the
  row's subject:

    owned = [f for f in synthesis_findings if f.get("subject") == bead_id]

  with the invariant stated where the code is: being cited by somebody else's row is
  not a defect in this bead.

  The inversion this produced was the point. Every finding against cairn-cue read
  "references non-closed bead X (status=open)", which is exactly what
  research/SESSION-PROMPTS.md REQUIRES a close to do: name the open downstream bead
  that owns each declined finding and No-Claim gap. The honest bead scored 0/25 for
  complying; the false-close fixture, having nothing behind it and therefore no
  downstream references, scored higher. A gate that ranks a false close above an
  honest one on any dimension is inverted, and a weight reduction -- what the prior
  session applied -- caps the damage without removing the inversion.

THE SUPPRESSION IS NARROW, AND MEASURED

cairn-m0-e0s.12 keeps `15/25 -- 1 synthesis findings owned -> -10; 8 ignored by
policy`. The retained finding is a real dependency anomaly, a closed bead with an open
child. A/B against the real rubric:

  no knob:   Cross-bead 15/25 -> Score 821
  with knob: Cross-bead 25/25 -> Score 842

so the pattern suppresses the mandated shape and nothing else.

NO SIXTH FORK

All three scorer changes land in `score-bead.py` and `sync-rubric-from-policy.py`,
both already on CLAUDE.md's list of five forked call sites. `grep -n "rubric_overrides"
score-bead.py` returns exactly four knobs -- score_threshold, unmeasured_dimensions,
minimum_measured_weight, weights_by_type -- and none touches presentation or cross-bead
attribution, so configuration alone could not reach it. The new behavior is still named
in `audit-policy.yaml:110-130` rather than hardcoded, and turns off by deleting the key.

The cairn-owned half is the enforcement. `scripts/scorecard_coherence.py`, wired into
`.githooks/pre-commit`, reads the newest pass's scorecards back and denies a table that
disagrees with its own denominator. A reverted presentation fork now denies instead of
passing quietly, which is the property CLAUDE.md's fork list exists to protect.

RE-EXECUTED BY ME AT HEAD

  $ uv run python scripts/scorecard_coherence.py <the six newest scorecards>
  EXIT=0
  COHERENT ... cairn-6cp/scorecard.md
  COHERENT ... cairn-cue/scorecard.md
  COHERENT ... cairn-m0-e0s.12/scorecard.md
  COHERENT ... cairn-qn9/scorecard.md

and the same checker against a pre-fix scorecard, proving it can fail:

  $ uv run python scripts/scorecard_coherence.py \
      beads_compliance_audit/passes/2026-08-26T23-58-44Z/beads/cairn-cue/scorecard.md
  EXIT=1
  INCOHERENT: a **Denominator:** line is present but no row is marked excluded;
  denominator says 475 of measured weight; the scored rows total 1000; denominator
  says 375 measured points; the scored rows total 900; 900/1000 rescales to 900,
  not the reported 789

Handed a path with no scorecards it exits 2 NOTHING-TO-CHECK rather than passing
quietly -- confirmed by accident when I gave it an unexpanded glob.

  $ scripts/check.sh          (run alone; load average 12.24 before, 7.34 after)
  1648 passed, 9 warnings in 230.47s
  [check] all gates pass                              EXIT=0

1629 at 4dfde42 -> 1648, the 19 added.

The gate caught me, which is the best evidence it works: my first attempt at this
bead's own ARTIFACTS block claimed `scripts/scorecard_coherence.py` lines 1-170 and
the test file lines 1-200. Both were guesses. It refused, naming the real counts, 155
and 192.

NO-CLAIM

The hook path still runs stubs, and 500 of 1000 weight stays unmeasured. Nothing here
changes that; it changes the scorecard from claiming credit for it to saying so. 842
is an upper bound over the 475 that was measured.

The suppression pattern is right for this project and is not claimed to be right for
any other; it lives in audit-policy.yaml and turns off by deletion.

Three gaps, each owned by a named open bead:

  The subject-attribution change is unverified for the "Integration gaps" and
  "Contradictions" sections of synthesis.md. synthesize.py auto-detected none of
  either in this repo, so no row of those kinds exists to test against, and the
  reading that a two-bead integration gap belongs to both beads is defensible.
  Recorded on cairn-fur, which owns the audit's pattern surface.

  Only the hook path was executed. Whether run-pass.sh's parallel path -- real
  subagents, non-stub phases -- renders coherently is untested; the settling command

  Every score in this comment is subject to cairn-fi7: the anomaly scan attributes

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

Implemented by one subagent. I confirmed both defects against the real scorecards and
the real synthesis file before dispatching, re-ran all four audits at HEAD, proved the

title: M1: the missing-items corrector's `- check` line shape is unexercised by any real Phase 4
description:
Split from cairn-sf9, whose other two gaps ship without it.

Every audit-skill path this bead names — `score-bead.py`, `scripts/run-pass.sh`,
`subagents/compliance-verifier.md`, `SKILL.md` — is relative to the vendored skill at
`~/.claude/skills/beads-compliance-and-completion-verification` (CLAUDE.md's working note), never
to this repo, whose own `scripts/` holds no `run-pass.sh`. Repo paths are written from the repo
root as usual (`tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items.py`).

score-bead.py line 1283 emits `- check `<id>` (<verdict>) — <reason>` into the missing-items
section for every compliance check whose verdict is FAIL or MISSING. cairn-8jm extended
`spec_item_id_of` to that shape, so an id classifies identically whichever producer wrote its
line, and both shapes carry tests.

WHAT IS UNESTABLISHED is whether Phase 4 ever emits FAIL for an item the gatherer never
searched. Every `compliance.json` in this repo is the stub with an empty checks list, and a
scan over the 125 recorded passes finds 764 `- spec item` lines, 16 `- theater` lines and
zero `- check` lines; the first two counts rise with every new pass, so the zero is the
load-bearing figure and the one a close re-measures. The handling is therefore correct by construction and unexercised by any real
artifact.

WHY IT IS ITS OWN BEAD. The criterion needs a real Phase 4, which needs the compliance-verifier
subagent (`subagents/compliance-verifier.md`) dispatched by an agent driving the skill's phases.
`scripts/run-pass.sh` line 203 prints `Phase 4: (skipped in wrapper — Phase 4 needs subagents to
actually run tests; stubbing compliance.json + test_depth.json)` and writes `checks: []`, which is
why every recorded pass in this repo holds the stub. That driving agent is the audit skill's own
orchestrator (SKILL.md: "the user, an orchestrator, audit-policy.yaml"); it is not a Cairn
milestone deliverable, and Cairn's own orchestrator is M3 (PLAN §13), not M1. A synthetic compliance.json would
satisfy the letter of the test and none of its purpose: the whole question is what a REAL
Phase 4 emits, and a fixture written by the same person who writes the assertion answers
nothing. Fabricating one is the failure this bead exists to avoid.

DONE WHEN a real Phase 4 has run at least once under the orchestrator, and the resulting
compliance.json is either shown to contain no such row, or is used as the fixture for a test
that exercises the shape against real output.

BLOCKED ON a pass whose Phase 4 dispatches the compliance-verifier subagent instead of
`run-pass.sh`'s stub. The edge to cairn-m1-cqt holds the bead until such a pass has run; it is not
a claim that M1 builds the orchestrator this needs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a pass whose Phase 4 dispatched the compliance-verifier subagent rather than
  scripts/run-pass.sh's stub has run at least once; its compliance.json is cited by path,
  its checks list is shown non-empty, and the count of `- check` lines its missing-items
  section emitted is pasted beside a re-scan of the recorded passes run at close — over
  the 125 passes the scan behind this bead covered, 764 `- spec item`, 16 `- theater` and
  zero `- check`, the first two rising with every new pass — so the answer is a
  measurement rather than an inference.
- Positive: the outcome is recorded whichever way it lands — either the real
  compliance.json contains no `- check` row, and the close says so with the scan that

  unexercised; or it contains one, and that real line becomes the fixture for a test
  asserting `spec_item_id_of` classifies its id identically to the `- spec item` shape.
- Planted negative: a synthetic compliance.json written for this bead does not satisfy

  synthetic `- check` line already pinned at tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items.py:341

  tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items.py.
