was unfaithful and the difference came from the stub. Creating the real corpus
made it fail. It now asserts identical bytes give an identical hash anywhere and

THE TEST AUDIT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh subagent ran /optimal-tests --audit and claimed eight guards had no test.
Each claim was proved rather than believed: the guard was deleted in a scratch
copy and the suite re-run. All eight stayed green, so all eight were real. Twelve
guards now have a killing test, each verified by re-running the same deletion and
watching a test go red. The repo was restored from backup and checked
byte-identical with `shasum -a 256 -c` after every mutation.

Two audit findings were declined. Deleting the unit origin and ledger tests as
subsumed by the fuzz mutations: the fuzz asserts only that the error path matches
a regex, while those tests assert the exact path per case, so they are not a
subset. Dropping the PARI spy from the unit fuzz file because check_corpus
reaches no PARI call on any input, making it unfailable today: the spec asks for
it by name and it guards against validation later growing a PARI call. The
integration ordering proof was the weak one and now asserts run_case is never
reached rather than that three helpers went uncalled.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NO-CLAIM
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Certified is not correct beyond the corpus. Four known-answer cases, one 30-bit
seeded curve and 40 verifier draws per run do not establish that toy_curve is
correct at any other size or seed.

Cases carrying author_supplied fields are capped at CONJECTURE by justify wherever
no covering arm or cross-check exists. Case 1's P, Q and x and case 2's P and Q
are author_supplied; the seeded arm and the <=50-bit algorithm-axis cross-check
are what cover them here.

The 150-bit case has no discrete-log component: it exercises membership,
cardinality and the big-integer path only.

Case 2's Q is tagged author_supplied although the relation Q = 2P is upstream,
because the coordinates derive from a locally chosen P.

The negative control uses Q = (10,163), a generator of order 420, not the least
point outside the order-21 subgroup. That least point is (0,0), where 21*Q = Q
for a parity reason unrelated to subgroup membership.

The whole integration file skips off macOS: pinned_bundle pins through the uappnd
chflags bit. On Linux the self-test has unit coverage only. Recorded on cairn-hcl.

The gp-absent arm of exit 3 ENVIRONMENT is untested; only the missing-bundle half
is proven. Recorded on cairn-m0-e0s.18.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
No independent verifier ran. The test audit was a fresh subagent with no stake in
the code, which is better than self-review but is not independent verification;
every claim it made was re-executed here before being acted on, and its report
was treated as a claim throughout.

The four corpus cases were probed against live PARI in this session and matched
the values pinned in research/grounding/pari-sage-toy-curve-backend.md section 4.
Those upstream line references were not re-fetched from PARI or Sage; they are
taken from the grounding document as written.

cypari2 versions recorded in the env manifest. The certificate golden is valid
for that platform only.

title: M0: Tier-0 verifier subprocess (gp): membership n·Q=O then xP==Q; affirmative acceptance (rc==0 AND stdout==OK AND stderr empty); arity/field validation before spawn; explicit stack ceiling; forced crash → FAIL; gate-read instance, submitter supplies x only
description:
WHY: "No submission without a passing verifier (xP == Q) subprocess" is an invariant (CLAUDE.md). Acceptance is affirmative, never residual: gp exits 0 on fatal errors (1/0, stack overflow — PROVEN by probe) and zero-fills missing arguments, so rc==0 is not evidence of anything. The instance is gate-read: the curve, n, P, Q come from the claim statement node or dispatch record, never from the submitter, who supplies x alone — `xP == Q` on an instance the worker chose is a true statement about the wrong problem (PLAN §4).

WHAT (`src/cairn/verifier.py`, `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp`)
- `verify.gp` (shape from grounding brief §3) ships two entry points. `verify(p,a,b,n,Px,Py,Qx,Qy,x)`: `ispseudoprime(p)` → nonsingular → `ellisoncurve(E,P)` and `(E,Q)` → `ellmul(E,Q,n)==[0]` (membership FIRST — PARI's generic `elllog` can loop when no solution exists; the verifier never calls a log) → `ellmul(E,P,x)==Q`; prints exactly one line `OK` or `FAIL <reason-codes>`; `quit(0|1)`. `crash_selftest(p,a,b)`: `ellcard(ellinit([a,b],p)); print("OK"); quit(0)` — the gate's forced-backend-crash fixture, reachable only from the gate plan's crash steps (cairn-m0-e0s.11) and this bead's tests, never from `run`: on the committed 60-bit curve at the planted ceiling `8M` the real backend overflows (rc 0, EMPTY stdout, `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr — PROVEN by probe 2026-08-21), and at the bundle's `64M` it prints OK (the must-PASS control proving the entry is a live computation). `verify()` itself is NOT a crash fixture at any ceiling that starts gp: it never calls `ellcard` and prints OK on the 60-bit instance under `-s 3M`, `-s 8M` and `-s 64M` (probed 2026-08-21); below ≈ 3 MB (`-s 2M`, `-s 1M`) gp dies at startup with rc 1, stdout `### Errors on startup, exiting...` and the overflow message on stderr. The script is a gate-bundle object (kind `verifier_script`, cairn-m0-e0s.10): the driver materializes the bundle's bytes once per process to a 0444 file `verify.gp` under a per-process `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cairn-bundle-<bundle-hash>-')` directory removed at interpreter exit — never under the repo's `var/`, which `isolation_guard` (`tests/conftest.py`, cairn-m0-e0s.1) snapshots around every test — and passes that path to gp; `src/cairn/gp/verify.gp` is the bundle source and is never read at gate time.
- Driver `Verifier.run(instance: Instance, x: int) -> VerifierResult`: validates arity (exactly 9 fields), every field a non-negative int, `p > 3` (PARI's `ellinit([a,b],2)` returns `[]` and the next call dies with a fatal error at rc 0 — probed 2026-08-21; short Weierstrass is singular in characteristic 2, and the validator never lets the backend see it), `0 ≤ a, b < p`, `Px,Py,Qx,Qy < p`, `x < n`, `n` inside the Hasse interval of p (`|n − (p+1)| ≤ 2√p`) — BEFORE spawning; `Instance` reduces `a, b, Px, Py, Qx, Qy` into `[0, p)` at construction (corpus case 1's upstream `a = -3` becomes 2; cairn-m0-e0s.7) and `instance_hash` is over the reduced values; renders the nine values as decimal integer strings on ONE stdin line `verify(p,a,b,n,Px,Py,Qx,Qy,x)` (never hex, never floats); spawns `[GP_BIN,"-q","-f","-s",stack_ceiling]` loading `verify.gp` through `cairn.pari.run_gp`; backend path, stack ceiling, timeout and accept predicate come from the gate bundle (bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; injected as a config object at unit level) — the accept predicate is the structured object `{rc: 0, stdout: "OK", stderr_empty: true}` evaluated field by field (no string evaluation; the shipped bundle pins exactly that triple and cairn-m0-e0s.10 asserts it; `stdout: null` or `stderr_empty: false` is a legal, weaker predicate that leaves that field unchecked — the form cairn-m0-e0s.11's re-pinned bundle copy uses to prove the crash self-test is load-bearing — and only a missing key or a non-int `rc` is refused at construction); accepts iff `rc==0 AND stdout.strip()=="OK" AND stderr==""` (satisfiable — probed 2026-08-21: `gp -q -f -s 64M verify.gp` fed one stdin line writes 0 bytes to stderr on a good instance; `quit(1)` gives rc 1 with the FAIL line on stdout and empty stderr; the 8 MB stack overflow gives rc 0, empty stdout and `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr); everything else → FAIL with `reason ∈ {p-not-prime, singular, P-off-curve, Q-off-curve, nQ-not-O, xP-ne-Q, backend-crash, timeout, bad-arity, bad-field, submitter-named-instance}`: a stdout line starting with `FAIL ` yields its reason codes; every other non-accepting outcome is `backend-crash` (a fatal message on stderr with rc 0, the `-s 2M` startup overflow with rc 1 and `### Errors on startup, exiting...` on stdout, a killed child with rc < 0, and `OK` accompanied by any stderr bytes); a `GpTimeout` raised by `cairn.pari.run_gp` (cairn-m0-e0s.1) is `timeout`; the pre-spawn refusals `bad-arity`, `bad-field` and `submitter-named-instance` return `accepted=False` and their `gate_runs` row carries `result='refused'`; default timeout 30 s.
- Instance binding: `Instance{p,a,b,n,P,Q}` has `instance_hash = H('cairn/instance/v1' ‖ canonical instance)` (domain tag from cairn-m0-e0s.3); `run` takes an `Instance` produced by the gate run (from the claim statement node / dispatch record) and a bare `x`; a `Submission` carrying its own `(P,Q)` is refused with `reason='submitter-named-instance'` before any subprocess is spawned (a spy asserts zero spawns). The result records `instance_hash`.
- Result node: a `nodes` row of kind `verifier_result` `{instance_hash, x, accepted, reason, stdout_digest, stderr_digest, rc, wall_s}` plus a `gate_runs` row (gate='verifier', result pass|fail, instance_hash, bundle + pin hash), both written by the caller's writer (bead m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5); a verifier run is a gate run, not a skill attempt — it writes no `attempts` row and is never served from any cache (every submission re-runs the subprocess). Every verdict logs (instance_hash, accepted, reason, rc, wall_ms) at INFO and the gp argv + stdin/stdout/stderr digests at DEBUG through `cairn.log`.
TESTS (integration, real /opt/homebrew/bin/gp; `tests/integration/test_verifier.py`): corpus case 1 (p=5,n=7,P=(0,1),Q=(3,3),x=3) → OK; the committed 60-bit instance `tests/vectors/curve60_seed1.json` (cairn-m0-e0s.1) with a fixed x and Q=xP computed in-test via cypari2 → OK (≈17 ms); one-coordinate negative (Qy+1 → off-curve; and a different on-curve point → xP-ne-Q); one-scalar negative (x+1) → FAIL xP-ne-Q; wrong n → FAIL nQ-not-O; forced backend crash: `crash_selftest(p,a,b)` on the committed 60-bit curve at stack ceiling `8M` → rc 0, empty stdout, `*** ellcard: the PARI stack overflows !` on stderr → classified FAIL backend-crash, and its control at `64M` → OK; `verify(...)` on the same 60-bit instance at `3M`, `8M` and `64M` → OK (asserted every run, so the fixture's premise — only `ellcard` overflows 8 MB — is re-checked; this bead adds the `verify()`-OK-at-3M/8M/64M row to the gp-facts section of `research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` from that test's log — the one probe-5 row cairn-m0-e0s.2 leaves to the owner of `verify.gp`); startup overflow: `verify(...)` at `2M` → rc 1, stdout `### Errors on startup, exiting...`, overflow on stderr → FAIL backend-crash; a killed child (SIGKILL mid-run, rc −9) → FAIL backend-crash; a child exceeding the timeout (config `timeout_s = 0.001` on a good instance — gp cannot start in 1 ms) → FAIL timeout; p = 2 → refused pre-spawn (bad-field, zero spawns); wrong n (n + 2, still inside the Hasse interval) → FAIL nQ-not-O; missing field / extra field / negative int / x ≥ n / n outside Hasse → refused pre-spawn (spy: no spawn); `Submission(P,Q,x)` → refused pre-spawn; randomized arm: 20 draws (x, Q=xP) → OK and 20 draws x'≠x → FAIL; caplog holds one verdict record per run.

- Metamorphic relations (`tests/integration/test_verifier_properties.py`, Hypothesis, real gp, instances = the committed 60-bit vector and corpus case 2 (GF(101), `n = 89` prime), a base pair `(x, Q = xP)` computed in-test via cypari2, `max_examples=40` per relation under a local `settings` override at ≈ 17 ms per gp run; title: M0: skill runner: subprocess launch with content-addressed inputs, harness-written execution receipt (CPU/wall/RSS/scratch bytes/exit/digests/bundle hash), attempt row + statuses, cache bits, 4× wall ceiling on the trivial fixture
description:
WHY (PLAN §3, §5): the execution receipt is the harness's own record of the run, written by the writer and never by the skill; its readers are the budget ceiling, the ladder's clock and memory measurements and the provenance check. A receipt the skill writes about itself is a number from the gated party. Workers are subprocesses that return artifacts to the single writer and hold no write capability.

WHAT (`src/cairn/runner.py`)
- `launch(skill_module, skill_identity, inputs, seed, *, bundle_hash, scratch_dir, declared_expectation_s, declared_verification_s, budget_remaining, ceiling_multiplier) -> Attempt` (`skill_module` is the dotted module launched with `-m`, e.g. `cairn.skills.toy_curve`; `declared_expectation_s` for the toy-curve launch is `CostProfile.evaluate(bits).expected_wall_s` — the mean subprocess wall with interpreter start included, cairn-m0-e0s.6 — so the 4× ceiling is not tripped by process start): computes the recipe key (bead m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3); honors cache bits (`skip_cache_lookup`, `do_not_cache`, serve path of bead m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4); inserts the attempt row with status `RUNNING` (cairn-m0-e0s.4); spawns the skill as a subprocess (`[sys.executable, "-m", "cairn.skills.<name>"]`, canonical JSON in on stdin, canonical JSON out on stdout, scratch path passed as an argument; the child receives NO substrate path or handle and an environment scrubbed of `CAIRN_DB*`; the child's stdout and stderr go to files `<attempt dir>/stdout` and `<attempt dir>/stderr` outside the scratch path whose byte delta is measured — never pipes, and `communicate()` is never called, because it reaps the child through `wait()` (subprocess.py 1212/1239/2152, CPython 3.14.0 under uv; probed by cairn-m0-e0s.2 probe 7) — so `os.wait4` is the first and only reap and the stdout/stderr digests are BLAKE3 over those two files); waits with `os.wait4(proc.pid, 0)` for rusage (ru_utime, ru_stime, ru_maxrss) and takes the exit status from the status word it returns (`os.waitstatus_to_exitcode`), setting `proc.returncode` itself and never calling `proc.wait()`/`proc.poll()` afterwards — CPython's `Popen._try_wait` turns the `ChildProcessError` of an already-reaped child into status 0 (subprocess.py `_try_wait` 2019–2029, read 2026-08-21 on CPython 3.14.0 under uv — the interpreter `uv run pytest` uses; m0-stack-facts §7), which would record every crash as exit 0; `time.monotonic()` start/end; wall; bytes written under scratch (directory-size delta); exit status; stdout/stderr BLAKE3 digests; tool digests (gp sha256, cypari2/libpari versions); bundle hash. Writes the receipt node and closes the attempt row (the single RUNNING→terminal UPDATE) with status: `OK` (exit 0, well-formed output, skill status OK); `FAIL` (non-zero exit, malformed output, or skill status FAIL); `DISAGREE` (skill status DISAGREE); `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` (wall past `ceiling = multiplier × declared_expectation_s`, the `ceiling_multiplier` argument, which the caller reads from the opened bundle's `tiers.ceiling_multiplier` — 4 at M0, CONJECTURE, §5; cairn-m0-e0s.10 — the runner never opens the bundle itself: the e2e slice (cairn-m0-e0s.14) passes it from the bundle and the tests pass 4 → child killed). `startup_scan()` moves every `RUNNING` attempt with NULL `ended_at` to `INTERRUPTED` before any new launch (M0 implements the scan; M3 exercises it under crash tests); `launch` calls it first, and the same function is exposed as `uv run cairn startup-scan [--json]` — registered through cairn-m0-e0s.17 (`read_only=False, json=True, dangerous=False`: it performs only the RUNNING→INTERRUPTED transition the append-only triggers permit, and a second run finds nothing); `--json` → `{schema_version, interrupted: [attempt ids], count}`; exit 0 (also when nothing was interrupted), 3 ENVIRONMENT when `--db` cannot be opened, 5 CONFLICT on `database is locked` — the `recommended_command` the doctor names for RUNNING rows (cairn-m0-e0s.18).
- Output manifest: each artifact a blob (hash,size); the manifest node (kind `output_manifest`, `{artifacts: sorted map name → (hash,size)}` — no attempt_id inside the manifest: two attempts at one recipe must hash-equal when their artifacts do, which is what `mark_non_reproducible` and the same-manifest assertion compare; bead .4 as built, `substrate.output_manifest_hash(artifacts)`) is linked by `lineage` rows child → parent: `manifest → recipe_key` (`edge_kind='output_of'`), `manifest → each input blob` (`'input'`) and `each output blob → manifest` (`'member'`); the attempt row (`attempt_id` is not a content hash) is reached through `attempts.recipe_key` and `attempts.output_manifest_hash`, never through `lineage` — the edge set GC's reachability walks (cairn-m0-e0s.13).
- Escrow: writes the reservation columns at launch — `declared_production_cost = declared_expectation_s`, `declared_verification_cost = declared_verification_s` (the toy-curve launch passes `Evaluation.expected_core_s` and `.expected_verification_core_s`, cairn-m0-e0s.6), `reserved = declared_verification_cost`, `ceiling_multiplier`, `spent_at`/`released_at` NULL (schema-only at M0; reserve/spend/release behavior is M1).
- Logging: each launch logs (recipe key, served-from-cache | spawned, argv at DEBUG, status, wall_ms, cpu_s, rss) through `cairn.log`; a kill logs the ceiling and the elapsed wall.
TESTS (integration, `tests/integration/test_runner.py`; the launch subject is the real `toy_curve` skill, cairn-m0-e0s.6): launch toy_curve 40-bit seed 1 → attempt OK; receipt has cpu>0, wall>0, rss>0, stdout_digest == BLAKE3 of captured stdout; output manifest hash equals the skill's own manifest; second identical launch → served from cache, no new attempt; with `skip_cache_lookup` → new attempt, same manifest (Replayable double-attempt agreement); fixture skill exiting 3 → FAIL attempt, never served, and its receipt's `exit_status == 3` (a status read through Popen after the wait4 reap would be 0); fixture sleeping 2 s with declared expectation 0.2 s → killed at 0.8 s, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, never served, its receipt's `exit_status` carrying the kill signal; fixture emitting a `receipt` key in its output → ignored (receipt.cpu differs from the fake); fixture that prints its environment → no substrate path visible; fixture writing 1 MB to stderr then exiting 0 → attempt OK with no deadlock and `stderr_digest` equal to BLAKE3 of the captured file; fixture skills live in `tests/fixtures/skills/` (`exit3.py`, `sleep2.py`, `fake_receipt.py`, `print_env.py`, `stderr_1mb.py`) and are launched by module path with `tests/fixtures` on the child's `PYTHONPATH`, set by the test; `startup_scan()` on a DB with an unfinished RUNNING attempt marks it INTERRUPTED and a later `serve` ignores it, and the same fixture through `cairn startup-scan --json` reports the attempt id with exit 0 while a second run reports `count: 0`.
UNIT (`tests/unit/test_runner_status.py`, no subprocess): the status mapping table (exit, stdout well-formedness, skill status, wall vs ceiling) → exactly one of OK/FAIL/DISAGREE/BUDGET_EXCEEDED; ceiling arithmetic (`4 × 0.2 s = 0.8 s`); the environment scrub removes every `CAIRN_DB*` variable.

TEST PLAN (shapes)

DEVIATIONS AND DECISIONS, EACH DELIBERATE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Escrow is a separate table, not columns on attempts as the bead's text assumes.
   An UPDATE attempts SET reserved would hit the append-only trigger. The row goes
   in through add_escrow with spent_at and released_at NULL.

2. The ceiling and the escrow read one Evaluation object rather than three fields
   of it. All three fields are the same number today, so they agree by accident;
   PLAN section 5 line 599 requires the same declared profile, and one object makes
   that structural.

3. The divergence path is built, which the bead omits. PLAN section 3 lines 124-125
   name it the reason the receipt exists, and section 3 line 200 makes recorded
   divergences GC roots, so leaving it out would have let cairn-m0-e0s.13 collect
   the evidence.

4. replay is a parameter. The bead's signature had no way to supply the grade that
   section 3 line 116 puts in the attempt tuple.

5. budget_remaining implements the section 5 line 573 meet rule rather than sitting
   unused.

6. Re-certification aside, the runner never emits SKILL_YANKED. The status is in
   the schema and in PLAN sections 2 and 4; pre-launch refusal belongs to the tier
   gate and the in-flight case has no owner. Recorded on cairn-m1-cqt.4.

7. Ceiling enforcement is built at M0 though PLAN section 13 lines 1391-1394
   exercise it first at M1. This is a strengthening, and section 13's own closing
   rule is that a behavior no M0 test exercises is architecture rather than a slice.

8. The bead asks that the output manifest hash equal the skill's own manifest. It
   cannot: ToyCurveOutput.manifest_hash hashes that skill's OUTPUT schema, while the
   runner's manifest hashes a name-to-blob map and is generic across skills whose
   schemas it cannot decode. The checkable relation is asserted instead.

9. The wire contract (argv, stdin, stdout, env allowlist, scratch as argv[1]) is an
   M0 operator decision, not a PLAN section 2 clause; section 2 states none of it.
   Recorded on cairn-m0-e0s.16 so conformance does not cite an unwritten spec.

10. measure.launch is left alone rather than sharing a launch primitive. Its
    reaping contract is incompatible (subprocess.run then proc.returncode, which
    this runner must never do) and tests/integration/test_measure.py monkeypatches
    measure.LAUNCH_ARGV.

DEFECTS FOUND IN MY OWN WORK DURING THIS BEAD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A containment hole. _artifacts walked scratch with followlinks=False but read with
read_bytes(), which follows, so a symlink in scratch blobbed an outside file's bytes
into the substrate as the skill's artifact. A dangling symlink raised
FileNotFoundError after start_attempt and stranded the attempt at RUNNING. Only
regular files become artifacts now, and any exception after start_attempt closes the
attempt FAIL.

A grade mismatch. launch passed replay to start_attempt but not to
put_output_manifest, so an attempt launched Verifiable produced a node claiming
Replayable.

A dangling next_command. startup-scan's missing-substrate error named cairn m0-run,
which is cairn-m0-e0s.14 and unbuilt. The test now asserts the named command is in
the live registry rather than pinning a string.

Two of my own tests passed for the wrong reason. The grandchild sweep test used a
fixture that timed out, so the ceiling's kill did the work and the post-reap sweep
was never exercised. The grace test passed grace= explicitly, so mutating the
constant to zero changed nothing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THE TEST AUDIT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A fresh subagent ran /optimal-tests --audit with a 27-mutation battery whose two
controls were killed, and reported 17 survivors. Each was re-run here. Sixteen now
fail a test, verified by re-applying the same mutation and watching it go red; the
source was restored from backup and checked byte-identical with shasum -a 256 -c
after every run.

One survivor is left, honestly. Replacing the scratch delta with an absolute
measurement changes nothing, because launch creates a fresh empty scratch directory
per attempt so the baseline is zero by construction. The delta is kept because a
filesystem giving a new directory nonzero blocks would make the absolute wrong, and
allocated_bytes is tested directly against a pre-seeded directory.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NO-CLAIM
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
rusage covers the direct child plus whatever that child reaped, not the process
tree. Measured: a grandchild burning CPU appears only when the child waits for it
(0.320 s against 0.041 s). PLAN section 3 lines 120-122 specify "over the process
tree" and section 6 reads those fields for the ladder; the receipts table has no
field distinguishing the two, so an M0 row must not be read as a tree figure.
Recorded on cairn-m1-cqt.1.

peak_rss_bytes is normalized from the platform's unit (bytes on macOS, kilobytes on
Linux). The macOS unit is empirical, from a 300 MiB allocation moving the counter by
313720832; the macOS man page states no unit. The Linux branch is documented but not
executed here.

No sandbox. The environment is an allowlist and the child holds no substrate handle,
but nothing confines its filesystem or network. PLAN section 16 decision 6 puts a
container at M1.

Bytes written is a scratch-directory allocation delta, not I/O accounting. Hardlinks
double-count, APFS clones and compression misreport, a file rewritten in place a
thousand times counts once, and writes outside scratch are invisible.

Escrow behavior is M1. The reservation row is written; spend and release have no
substrate method.

Concurrent launches are untested. A second in-process writer is refused with
CONFLICT, and cross-process contention relies on SQLite's busy timeout.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

No independent verifier ran. Three fresh subagents contributed: a CPython reap
research pass, a PLAN reading, and a house-style review, plus the test audit. Each
report was treated as a claim and re-executed here before being acted on; the reap
facts were additionally already grounded by cairn-m0-e0s.2 in
tests/integration/test_grounding_subprocess.py.

FOR THE MODE B SESSION THAT DECOMPOSES THESE EIGHT. Two PLAN-named M1 deliverables
have no owner among the current children, so decomposing the placeholders as they
stand would carry the gaps forward.

Measured 2026-08-26 by scanning all eight bodies (description plus acceptance
criteria) for the terms PLAN uses.

GAP A — the tier-gate admission fixtures have a harness owner and no behavior owner

PLAN lines 1425-1433 name six: a synthetic KEEP_IN_SAMPLE table admits the 60-bit
rung of its own hypothesis key and is refused for every other Tier-2 launch; a KEEP
table is refused for a launch whose hypothesis key, method identity or
implementation revision differs from the table's; a launch of a yanked or
uncertified revision is refused whatever ticket it holds; a launch declaring Tier 1
for a production cost the boundary table assigns Tier 2 is refused; a claim
carrying both a cost model and a correctness conjecture is refused Tier 2 while
either its KEEP table or its SURVIVED record is absent; a Tier-3 request holding
KEEP and no Tier-2 node is refused.

Scanned across all eight children:

  "boundary table"   appears in none
  "uncertified"      appears in none
  "KEEP_IN_SAMPLE"   appears only in .1, and there as a ladder verdict type rather
                     than as a table the gate reads

Each child that owns fixtures says which letters it owns. None claims these six.
.3 owns the harness (tests/planted/, one test id per fixture letter and per
tier-gate item) and depends on every other child, so it assumes the behavior is
built elsewhere. .4 names one tier-gate fixture, the cumulative edge. .8 names one,
top-class routing and the Tier-3 sign-off. The remaining six are unowned.

PLAN line 1386 is explicit that these behaviors are exercised first at M1, so M0
does not close them. cairn-m0-e0s.10 built the M0 tier gate they extend.

GAP B — the operational alarms have no bead that builds them

PLAN lines 1613-1621, section 15 P4: a split-conformal anomaly flag on ladder and
self-test measurements, a one-sided bounded-mean e-process on log(measured/declared
cost), and repeated TierRefused records on one hypothesis key as a third input.

  "alarm"      appears in none of the eight
  "conformal"  appears in none
  "e-process"  appears in none

The epic's description pushes the keep-or-drop DECISION to cairn-m2-vgh, which is
correct, but nothing owns BUILDING the two monitors whose firing behavior that
decision judges. .1 produces the ladder tables and per-run costs they would read.

GAP C, weaker — decision 6's Linux container is named once and scoped nowhere

PLAN lines 1663-1665: a Linux container enters at M1 with the formalization gate
for the PROVEN gold tier, macOS fake-landrun being dev-only before that. .5 names
it in one clause with no acceptance criterion attached, and its AC is the shared
placeholder. cairn-hcl covers Linux but scopes its No-Claim to the write boundary
and says nothing about a container.

Settled by execution rather than left as a suspicion: no container spec exists in
the tree. `grep -rli landrun` outside .git returns only research prose
(research/grounding/lean-checker-protocol.md, research/KICKOFF-beads-and-M0.md,
research/PROPOSALS.md and two convergence drafts), and there is no Dockerfile.

WHAT ELSE THE SCAN SHOWED, so the decomposition session does not re-derive it

All eight carry the identical 508-character placeholder acceptance criteria — same
SHA-256 prefix 3bd8734bbc on every one. None names a single src/ or tests/ path,
and `scripts/bead-test-plan.sh` reports "names no test file; nothing to check" for
all eight. The bodies are rich on properties to preserve and on the operator
decisions that bind them, and carry no file layout, no module names and no test
plan. That is the decomposition work, and it is what this epic's own acceptance
criteria already require before any child is claimed.

The dependency shape among the eight is sound and does not need inventing:

  .2 baseline skills, also blocked by cairn-m0-e0s.16

comments.author: jwross
comments.text: MEASURED 2026-09-02 (cairn-24), two experiments on the build machine, correcting the comment above: (1) a silent 180 s per-test watchdog is the expected signature of any C call holding the GIL, so it is not evidence about the runner's scheduling (cairn-9c's correction, verified). (2) Neither pytest-timeout method interrupts an in-process libpari call: pari("for(i=1,10^9,1)") (about 36 s) under --timeout=3 fails at 35.7 s with timeout_method=signal and at 36.3 s with timeout_method=thread; both surface only after the C call returns, so a pyproject change buys nothing. (3) PARI's own alarm does bound a call in-process: pari("alarm(2, for(i=1,10^9,1))") raises cysignals.signals.AlarmInterrupt (a BaseException, not an Exception) at 2.0 s, and a 60-bit ellcard under alarm(5, ...) returns its normal value in 0.15 s. So the per-call ceiling for the self-tests is a wrap of the seam functions in src/cairn/pari.py (ellsea, ellcard, ellorder) in alarm, or a subprocess boundary. Cost of the alarm route: pari.py is in every skill's IDENTITY_SOURCES, so the change moves every implementation revision, every certificate and transcript golden, the plan's baseline revision (tests/unit/test_rho_dp.py pins it) and the bundle hash; a deliberate operator-scheduled change, not a hotfix. Neither experiment explains why the runner's libpari runs for minutes on a call that takes milliseconds here; that stays open.

title: M1: small-scale ladder (§6): pre-registered model + frozen method identity, commit-ordered instance entropy, gate-owned instance-maker + operation counter, comparison protocol + trial sizing, A/A null arm, out-of-sample rung, in-sample check, memory cap + RSS/scratch measurement, clock/wall checks, patience ceiling, per-trial replay grades, table repro record, typed verdicts
description:
Roll-up for PLAN §6 (the top anti-fabrication device); the granular children carry the work. Key properties the children hold between them: the model is pre-registered as an order of substrate records (hypothesis object precedes the gate's entropy commitment); instances are gate-made from commit-ordered entropy, never worker-chosen; the operation counter is gate-owned; the ladder verifies every trial's `xP == Q`; a REJECT whose predicate is `xP ≠ Q` or a count divergence yanks the revision and refutes no claim version; verdicts are typed {KEEP, KEEP_IN_SAMPLE, REJECT(kind), INCONCLUSIVE}; the A/A null arm and the out-of-sample rung are part of every plan; memory cap at the floor rungs with the gate's own RSS-and-scratch measurement; clock check against a per-rung reference rate the gate measures on the rung's own instances (the A/A arm at the ≤ 50-bit rungs, a gate-owned calibration run of the counted object at 60), with the plan-load bound reading the counted object's per-operation cost over the fastest implementation's (decision 12); the table's reproducibility record is the repro node `justify` reads; the Tier-1 cumulative edge is set from the measured per-run cost (decision 10, 4×, CONJECTURE). Ordering against the baseline skills (bead m1-baseline-skills) runs BOTH ways at the granular grain, so it is never a roll-up edge and lives only on the children: cairn-m1-cqt.2.1 and cairn-m1-cqt.2.2 depend on cairn-m1-cqt.1.1, whose seeded ladder-plan fields (baseline revision, refutation floor, memory cap) they replace with measured figures, while cairn-m1-cqt.1.3 depends on cairn-m1-cqt.2.1 and on the instance-maker cairn-m1-cqt.2.4, cairn-m1-cqt.1.4 on cairn-m1-cqt.2.5, and cairn-m1-cqt.1.7 on cairn-m1-cqt.2.1, whose plain rho both of its sizing arms run. Those six edges are the whole of the crossing, so a reader checks the list against the graph rather than resampling it. The M0 substrate/gate/runner shape is this roll-up's own edge to cairn-m0-e0s.
Fixture ownership: the BEHAVIORS behind fixtures (a), (b), (j), (k) and the five ladder-execution plantings belong to this bead's children; their corpus entries under tests/planted/ belong to bead C2 (cairn-m1-cqt.3.2).

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.9 (skill runner), a measurement scope this bead must not misread.

PLAN section 3 lines 120-122 specifies the receipt's CPU seconds and peak RSS as
measurements "over the process tree", and section 6 lines 768-773 and 846-853 read
exactly those fields for the ladder's memory model and clock check.

The M0 runner measures with os.wait4, which reports the direct child plus whatever
descendants that child itself reaped. Probed on this machine: a grandchild burning
1.0 s of CPU appears in the parent's wait4 result only when the direct child waits
for it (ru_utime 1.212 with the reap, 0.216 without), and ru_maxrss likewise jumps
16 MB to 51 MB. start_new_session has no effect on this either way.

So for a skill that forks and reaps its own children the two quantities coincide,
and for one that leaves orphans, or that is killed at the ceiling before it can
reap, the receipt undercounts. toy_curve is single-process, so M0 has no case where
they differ.

The receipts table carries no field distinguishing the two, so nothing in the
schema tells a reader which quantity a given row holds. Before the ladder reads
peak_rss_bytes or cpu_user_s as a process-tree figure, either the measurement has
to become a real subtree measurement (cgroups on Linux; no clean macOS equivalent)
or the receipt needs a measurement_scope field. Reading an M0 row as a tree figure
is silently wrong, not loudly wrong.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.12 (justify), which ships src/cairn/justify.py at commit 8836bb1.
Three properties of justify the ladder has to know, because the ladder is its first
real producer of ladder_table evidence.

1. The producer-standing ceiling reads the attempt's inputs from the evidence node's
   own population.param_ranges (src/cairn/justify.py, context_for), not from the
   attempt's recipe. At M0 every evidence node is synthetic and the two agree by
   construction. A real ladder_table names an attempt_id whose recipe carries the
   inputs that were actually run, and those are the inputs the rule means: a node
   declaring a wide population over a narrow run would read as covered when it is
   not. When the ladder writes real ladder_table nodes, feed context_for the recipe
   inputs reached through attempt_id and drop the population fallback.

2. justify returns a sixth typed result the bead's declared signature does not name.
   The union in the bead is Justification | CoverageViolation | LatticeViolation |
   Absent | Pending; a counterexample_hunt_record with verdict KILLED returns
   Refutation(evidence_hash), because none of the five can express "this moves the
   statement to terminal refuted with this evidence pointer" without keying the
   refutation path on a string comparison. derive_tag consumes it: it lowers the tag
   to SPECULATION, writes the downgrade row with the hunt's hash as evidence_hash,
   and calls claims.transition_status(..., "refuted"). Any new caller of justify
   must handle Refutation.

3. KEEP_IN_SAMPLE and counterexample_hunt_record are exercised by construction only
   at M0 — no ladder and no hunt exist. The KEEP_IN_SAMPLE rule is: the verdict
   justifies STRONG-EMPIRICAL only when the statement's scope.size_interval is
   contained in the node's in_sample_sizes, and justifies nothing otherwise
   (tests/integration/test_justify.py, cases keep_in_sample_covering and
   keep_in_sample_not_covering). The first real ladder run is where that rule meets
   data it did not author.

title: M1 ladder: the ladder plan as a versioned gate-bundle object with fail-closed load validation
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(2), §4 gate discipline). The ladder plan is one versioned gate-bundle
object; every tolerance, count and cap the other ladder beads read comes from it, and a
verdict is never recomputed under a later bundle. Invalid or missing gate config fails
closed (§4). The bundle store is the separate read-only SQLite file `src/cairn/bundle.py`
manages, with the pin check every gate run performs.

WHAT — the plan object's fields, its schema, and its load-time validation:

1. Fields (§6): the rung sizes (30/40/50 bits, plus the 60-bit completion rung); per-rung
   trial count (10² is a floor, not the count — the sizing bead measures and records the
   real one); the comparison protocol as one versioned object — the estimator (a CI on
   the speedup factor: baseline group-operation cost divided by claim group-operation
   cost, so a real advance is above 1; the source's median-CI form or a mean CI, named),
   the pairing (claimant and both baseline arms on the same gate-generated instance
   stream, each arm under its own gate-drawn method seeds), the CI method and its
   coverage, and the rule that every rung must pass; the tolerances of §6(3) — count
   divergence, clock, wall; the baseline skill revision (plain rho at M1, bead S1's trap
   note) — seeded here, since no `rho_dp` revision exists at this close, and replaced by
   bead S1's close with the shipped identity bundle, the same seeded-then-written split
   the refutation-floor and memory-cap fields carry below; the hold-out count m = 10 and the fit-on / hold-out split; the per-rung memory
   cap, fixed as the BSGS table for that size where the floor lives (≈ 1 GB at 50 bits,
   2³⁰ entries at 60) and absent at the 30- and 40-bit rungs, where a cap would refuse
   an honest constant-memory model that the 50-bit cap admits; the refutation-floor
   threshold per rung — the BSGS group-operation count and its memory figure at that
   size (≈ 5×10⁷ group operations under 1 GB at 50 bits, §6(4)), measured by the bsgs
   skill (bead S2) rather than asserted, and the number bead L2's floor predicate
   reads. This bead authors the field and seeds it with the §6(4) arithmetic so a
   complete plan loads; bead S2's close replaces the seeded value with its measured
   figure and records the replacement, which is where the field stops being a literal.
   The same split applies to the memory cap above; the per-trial patience ceiling (the §5 budget ceiling); the
   shape-departure tolerance; the KEEP band floor 1.01 guarding a degenerate null arm;
   and the design radius the chosen trial count targets — §6(3) names it a
   ladder-plan field recorded with the count, bead L7 measures and writes both, and
   the load-time bound in (2) reads it.

2. Load-time validation, failing closed: a plan missing any field refuses to load; and
   the §6(3) bound — the plan's clock tolerance times the counted object's recorded rate
   ratio (bead L4's bundle field: the counted object's per-operation cost over that of the
   fastest implementation on the build machine, whose per-operation cost in seconds per
   group operation bead S5 measures — the bound divides by that cost, never by a
   throughput) must stay below the KEEP band's excess over 1
   (2 × the design radius the plan's trial count targets). A plan failing the bound
   refuses to start. Neither input carries a measured value at this close — bead L4
   records the ratio once its counted object exists, and bead L7 measures the design
   radius — so this bead seeds both from the §6 arithmetic and exercises the bound
   against the seeds, each owner's close replacing its field and recording the
   replacement: the same seeded-then-written split the refutation-floor and memory-cap
   fields carry. The same bound is re-applied per rung against the measured A/A
   radius by the clock-check bead; this bead owns the load-time half only.

3. The plan's hash rides in every ladder gate-run record, so "which plan produced this
   verdict" is a checkable fact; a verdict is never recomputed under a later bundle.

DONE WHEN a well-formed plan loads and validates; each planted malformation (missing
field, bound violation) refuses with a typed reason; the plan hash appears in the
gate-run record the plan-load step itself writes. Its appearance in the gate-run record
of a ladder RUN is bead L3's assertion: L3 owns the run engine and this bead blocks L3,
so no ladder run exists at this close.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_ladder_plan.py (unit: field validation, bound check, typed
refusals); tests/integration/test_ladder_plan_bundle.py (integration: plan loads from
the bundle store, pin mismatch fails closed, hash in the gate-run record).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a complete plan object loads, validates, and its hash is recorded in the
  gate-run record the plan-load step itself writes; command and output pasted. Its
  appearance in a ladder RUN's gate-run record is bead L3's assertion — L3 owns the run
  engine and this bead blocks L3, so no ladder run exists here.
- Planted negative: a plan with a missing tolerance field, and a plan whose clock
  tolerance × rate ratio ≥ 2 × design radius, each refuse to load with a typed reason
  naming the field or the bound; both shown.
- No-Claim: a validated plan proves the configuration is coherent; it proves nothing
  about any verdict, and the per-rung re-application of the clock bound against the
  measured A/A radius is the clock-check bead's, not this one's.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_ladder_plan.py,
  tests/integration/test_ladder_plan_bundle.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.
notes:
BEAD SHORT CODES -> IDS (bead bodies name sibling beads by short code; these are the br ids): L1-L12 = cairn-m1-cqt.1.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.1.12 (ladder); S1-S5 = cairn-m1-cqt.2.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.2.5 (baseline skills); C1-C8 = cairn-m1-cqt.3.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.3.8 (planted corpus); B1-B7 = cairn-m1-cqt.4.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.4.7 (tiers, escrow, yank); F1-F8 = cairn-m1-cqt.5.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.5.8 (formalization gate); W1-W4 = cairn-m1-cqt.6.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.6.4 (workers and dispatch); H1-H4 = cairn-m1-cqt.7.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.7.4 (human queue and review); R1-R8 = cairn-m1-cqt.8.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.8.8 (epistemics); the alarms bead is cairn-m1-cqt.9. CLOSE EVIDENCE — cairn-m1-cqt.1.1 (the ladder plan as a versioned gate-bundle object with fail-closed load validation). Every bullet re-executed on the closing tree; commit SHA in the closing commit message (the evidence run below was at HEAD 6c9a555 with the closing tree uncommitted).

SHIPPED. `bundle/ladder_plan.json` lines 1-81: version 1; rungs 30/40/50 (role fit) and 60 (role hold_out), each with trials, floor_binds, memory_cap_bytes (null where the floor does not bind) and refutation_floor {group_ops, table_entries, memory_bytes}; hold_out_m 10; design_radius; the comparison protocol as one versioned object (estimator speedup_factor = baseline_group_ops / claim_group_ops in mean_ci form, pairing on a shared instance stream with gate-drawn per-arm method seeds over arms claimant / baseline / baseline_aa, ci normal at coverage 0.95, every_rung_must_pass); keep_band_floor 1.01; tolerances count_divergence 0.01 / clock 0.10 / wall 0.25; clock.rate_ratio; baseline {rho_dp, method identity rho_dp/1 {variant plain, r 32}, identity_bundle_hash, implementation_revision}; patience_ceiling {multiplier 4, basis declared_profile_mean_per_trial}; shape_departure_tolerance 0.25; provenance, one marker per owned field under the closed prefixes seeded / measured / written / policy. `src/cairn/ladderplan.py` lines 1-673: LadderPlan.load (closed field set at every level so an unknown or missing field refuses; typed LadderPlanInvalid reasons; rung rules: strictly ascending bits, exactly one hold-out rung and it is the largest, at least one fit rung, fit trials >= 100, hold-out trials == m, cap present iff floor_binds, cap == the floor's table bytes; design radius in (0, 0.5); tolerances in (0, 1); rate ratio >= 1; the clock bound clock_tolerance * rate_ratio < 2 * design_radius in Decimal on the literal digits); from_bundle (reads the `ladder_plan` object, checks patience_ceiling.multiplier against tiers.ceiling_multiplier); load_for_gate (writes the gate-run row gate='ladder_plan' plan_step='load', result pass or refused, reasons carrying 'ladder_plan:<blob hash of the canonical object>' after the refusal reason); `cairn ladder plan [--json]` (exits 2 on an invalid plan or a pin mismatch, 3 on a missing bundle or pin file, 5 on a second writer). `src/cairn/bundle.py` (ladder_plan property), `src/cairn/claims.py` (GATES), `src/cairn/schema.sql` line 274 (gate CHECK), `src/cairn/cli.py` (COMMAND_MODULES), `MAP.md` row 4, goldens gate_bundle_hash / help_ladder / help_top / capabilities, `tests/goldens/PROVENANCE.md`. Tests: `tests/unit/test_ladder_plan.py` lines 1-241 (a 63-row refusal table, the committed plan, the seeded list and its owners, the measured figures, node(), a 200-example property on the clock bound), `tests/integration/test_ladder_plan_bundle.py` lines 1-237 (load from a built and pinned bundle, refusal rows under the malformed object's own hash, the absent object, the tiers check, pin mismatch, CLI json / human / refused / second writer / missing bundle or pin / seeded none), `tests/unit/test_cli_contract.py` (DEPLOY_ARGV).

P1 a complete plan loads, validates, and its hash is in the gate-run row the load step writes
$ uv run cairn ladder plan --db $D/deploy.sqlite --bundle $D/deploy/gate-bundle.sqlite --pin $D/deploy/gate-bundle.pin --json

plan_hash == gate.digest_of('ladder_plan') == blake3(canonical bytes of the object): tests/integration/test_ladder_plan_bundle.py::test_the_committed_plan_loads_from_a_pinned_bundle_and_the_load_row_carries_the_plan_hash
$ uv run cairn ladder plan --db ... (human rendering)
rung 30 fit trials=130 floor_ops=41226 floor_bytes=497314 cap=none / rung 40 fit trials=130 floor_ops=1171749 floor_bytes=15440525 cap=none / rung 50 fit trials=130 floor_ops=44769554 floor_bytes=477370808 cap=477370808 / rung 60 hold_out trials=10 floor_ops=1840605416 floor_bytes=19625853059 cap=19625853059 / clock_bound 0.1*1=0.1<0.2432 / seeded rungs.trials,design_radius,clock.rate_ratio
$ uv run pytest tests/unit/test_ladder_plan.py tests/integration/test_ladder_plan_bundle.py -q --no-header -> 85 passed

N1 a plan missing a tolerance field (source copy without tolerances.clock)
$ uv run cairn ladder plan --db $D/missing-tolerance.sqlite --bundle $D/missing-tolerance/gate-bundle.sqlite --pin ... --json
rc=2 error: the ladder plan in bundle 6eafcdc1… is invalid (plan-missing-field:tolerances.clock); the refusal is gate run 80ea4404…
gate_runs: result refused, reasons ["plan-missing-field:tolerances.clock", "ladder_plan:7f0088d2…"] (the malformed object's own hash, not the committed plan's)
N2 a plan whose clock tolerance × rate ratio reaches 2 × design radius (tolerances.clock 0.30 at ratio 1.0)
rc=2 error: the ladder plan in bundle 6dfae0b9… is invalid (clock-bound-violated:0.3*1=0.3>=0.2432); the refusal is gate run 8fea52fc…
gate_runs: result refused, reasons ["clock-bound-violated:0.3*1=0.3>=0.2432", "ladder_plan:736a2274…"]
Every other malformation in the 63-row unit table refuses with its own typed reason; the property test draws 200 (tolerance, ratio, radius) triples and the plan refuses exactly when tolerance × ratio >= 2 × radius.

BOUND ARITHMETIC. design_radius 0.1216 = 1.96 × 0.5 × sqrt(2/130): §6(2)'s independent-arms radius at rho's sd ≈ 0.5·mean under a 95 % normal CI, at the "n ≳ 130" count §6 derives for the √2 control; both are L7's (cairn-m1-cqt.1.7) to measure on the paired stream and marked seeded. The KEEP band's excess over 1 is 2 × 0.1216 = 0.2432; the seeded clock tolerance 0.10 at the seeded ratio 1.0 (L4's field, >= 1 by L4's own assertion) sits under it. Strict inequality, Decimal, no float.

SEEDED-THEN-WRITTEN. Three fields are still literals and say so: rungs.trials and design_radius (seeded:cairn-m1-cqt.1.7) and clock.rate_ratio (seeded:cairn-m1-cqt.1.4). The refutation floor, the memory cap and the baseline revision were authored here and written in this same commit by their owners, .2.2 and .2.1, whose close comments show the rows before and after; their markers read measured: / written:. `LadderPlan.seeded_fields()` is what the run engine (L3) reads to refuse a verdict against a literal; the refusal itself is L3's.

LIMITS STATED. (1) A substrate created before 'ladder_plan' joined the gate_runs.gate CHECK refuses the row: rc=4, "IntegrityError: CHECK constraint failed: gate IN ('canon_kat', 'verifier', 'tier_gate', 'self_test', 'gate_plan', 'bundle_open')"; schema.sql runs as CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with no migration path, so a fresh substrate is the remedy and `cairn doctor` does not yet name it. (2) baseline.identity_bundle_hash covers the gp binary digest and the env manifest, so the committed object binds to this build machine; a deploy elsewhere re-authors the bundle, the property verifier.json's backend_path already has. (3) PLAN §6(3) names the tolerances without numbers; 0.01 / 0.10 / 0.25 are policy seeds marked policy:PLAN §6(3), and L4 owns their measurement. (4) The bead text names §6 mechanisms without their arithmetic; the numbers were read from PLAN §6 lines 702-914, a bead defect for the next polish pass.

TEST AUDIT + MUTATION PROOFS. scripts/mutation-check.sh, each restored byte-identical by sha256: cap == floor-table check KILLED (1 test), clock bound KILLED (4), the refusal row write KILLED (5), provenance unknown key KILLED (1), hold-out-largest KILLED (1), the schema CHECK token KILLED (8 integration tests), the .2.2 floor value KILLED (1), the .2.1 baseline revision KILLED (1). Fresh-eyes Opus review of the whole batch: REVIEW VERDICT 0 blocking, 8 non-blocking, each with a surviving mutation or a reproduction. Fixed before this close: the pin half of the ENVIRONMENT precheck, the CONFLICT branch, the strictness of the clock bound (a plan sitting exactly on 2·radius), the lower half of the CI-coverage range, the estimator numerator/denominator pins and the 'seeded none' rendering each gained the test the review specified, and all six review mutations are KILLED under mutation-check.sh; the 60-bit row is derived from one base (a 2^30-entry table at the 50-bit rung's measured ops and bytes per entry) with the rule recorded in research/grounding/m1-dlp-skill-costs.md §3; the baseline marker states that identity_bundle_hash is build-machine-local and unasserted by tests (the review's 64-zero mutation survives by design, since the value differs on CI by construction).

NO-CLAIM. Green proves the configuration is coherent and content-addressed; it proves nothing about any verdict. The per-rung re-application of the clock bound against the measured A/A radius is L4's, the floor predicate that reads these fields is L2's, and the run engine that refuses a seeded plan is L3's.

title: M1 ladder: the ladder-tested method's allow-list — counted object only, no network, no writable path but scratch, enforcement probed
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(3), §4). A ladder-tested method's allow-list is a gate-bundle template,
instantiated per dispatch and named in the dispatch record. It names: no arithmetic
backend but the gate-owned counted object and the uncounted backends the hypothesis
object declares (whose rungs are INCONCLUSIVE at best until a counted implementation
exists); no network egress; no writable path but the gate-owned scratch path; no process
spawn beyond the declared backends. A storage channel the allow-list does not name —
another writable path, network egress — is a planted-failure class the ladder's
self-test must FAIL.

WHAT

1. The template in the bundle and its per-dispatch instantiation, recorded in the
   dispatch record (bead L3 carries the record; this bead defines and enforces the
   template).

2. Enforcement, with the mechanism PROBED on this machine before it is trusted — a
   stack fact, not an assumption. Candidate arms to probe on macOS: sandbox-exec
   profiles for filesystem and network confinement of the trial subprocess; plus the
   runner's existing scratch-path and process-group machinery (src/cairn/runner.py).
   Record what each arm can and cannot confine in research/grounding/ with its tag; if
   an arm cannot be enforced pre-execution on this platform, the fallback is detection —
   scratch-path accounting, network-attempt detection — stated out loud in the grounding
   record and in the plan, never silently assumed away. The Linux container (bead F2)
   is the stronger boundary where it exists.

3. Uncounted-backend declarations: a method declaring an uncounted backend is admitted
   under the allow-list on that declaration and on nothing else, and the declaration is
   recorded where the verdict path reads it. The INCONCLUSIVE-at-best cap that
   declaration earns (§6(3)) is bead L2's verdict predicate, not this bead's: a cap is
   scored on a rung, this bead blocks L3, and no rung runs at this close.

DONE WHEN a method touching a path outside scratch, and one opening a network socket,
each fail the run with the violation named (or are provably confined, per the probed
mechanism); a method declaring an uncounted backend is admitted by the allow-list on that
declaration alone and the declaration is recorded; the per-dispatch instantiation of the
template is produced and matches the bundle template it came from. Its appearance in the
dispatch record is bead L3's assertion, and the INCONCLUSIVE cap the declaration earns is
bead L2's verdict predicate: L3 owns the record, L2 owns the verdict, and this bead blocks
L3, so neither a dispatch record nor a rung verdict exists at this close.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_ladder_allowlist.py (unit: template instantiation,
declaration handling); tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py
(integration: planted outside-write and socket-open methods fail with the violation
named; the probe's mechanism exercised for real, no mock).

ARTIFACTS:
- `src/cairn/allowlist.py`
- `bundle/allow_lists.json`
- `tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden`
- `tests/unit/test_ladder_allowlist.py`
- `tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py`
- `research/grounding/probe_method_allowlist.py`
- `research/grounding/method-allowlist-macos-sandbox.md`
- `tests/conftest.py`
- `research/grounding/framework-reexec-2026-09-08/probe_framework_reexec.py`
- `research/grounding/framework-reexec-2026-09-08/before-fix.log`
- `research/grounding/framework-reexec-2026-09-08/after-fix.log`
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: an honest method running only the arithmetic the template's counted-object
  slot names, inside the scratch path, completes, and the allow-list instantiated for it
  is asserted field-by-field against the bundle template it came from — the same
  instantiation bead L3 writes into the dispatch record; the grounding record for the
  enforcement mechanism exists with probe commands and output. The gate-owned counted
  object that slot names is bead L4's, and L4 lands after L3 which this bead blocks, so
  the slot holds a stand-in at this close and its binding to the real object is L4's
  assertion.
- Positive: a method declaring an uncounted backend in its hypothesis object is admitted
  by the allow-list on that declaration alone and the declaration is recorded where the
  verdict path reads it; the INCONCLUSIVE cap it earns is bead L2's predicate and is not
  asserted here, no rung running at this close.
- Planted negative: a method writing outside the scratch path fails with the violation
  named; a method opening a network socket fails likewise; a method spawning an
  undeclared subprocess fails; each shown live, no mock.
- No-Claim: enforcement is as strong as the probed macOS mechanism and no stronger — the
  grounding record states what is confined vs detected; the Linux container (bead F2)
  is the gold boundary, and green here claims nothing about it.
- Test types: unit, integration, probe. Files: tests/unit/test_ladder_allowlist.py,
  tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.
notes: BEAD SHORT CODES -> IDS (bead bodies name sibling beads by short code; these are the br ids): L1-L12 = cairn-m1-cqt.1.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.1.12 (ladder); S1-S5 = cairn-m1-cqt.2.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.2.5 (baseline skills); C1-C8 = cairn-m1-cqt.3.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.3.8 (planted corpus); B1-B7 = cairn-m1-cqt.4.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.4.7 (tiers, escrow, yank); F1-F8 = cairn-m1-cqt.5.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.5.8 (formalization gate); W1-W4 = cairn-m1-cqt.6.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.6.4 (workers and dispatch); H1-H4 = cairn-m1-cqt.7.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.7.4 (human queue and review); R1-R8 = cairn-m1-cqt.8.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.8.8 (epistemics); the alarms bead is cairn-m1-cqt.9. M0 ALIASES: m0-scaffold-smoke = cairn-m0-e0s.1; m0-grounding-probes = cairn-m0-e0s.2; m0-canon-hash = cairn-m0-e0s.3; m0-substrate-core = cairn-m0-e0s.4; m0-claims-schema = cairn-m0-e0s.5; m0-toy-curve-skill = cairn-m0-e0s.6; m0-skill-selftest-cert = cairn-m0-e0s.7; m0-tier0-verifier = cairn-m0-e0s.8; m0-skill-runner-receipt = cairn-m0-e0s.9; m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate = cairn-m0-e0s.10; m0-gate-plan-selftests = cairn-m0-e0s.11; m0-justify = cairn-m0-e0s.12; m0-gc-roots = cairn-m0-e0s.13; m0-e2e-slice = cairn-m0-e0s.14; m0-rho60-measure = cairn-m0-e0s.15.
close_reason: Allow-list template, its macOS sandbox-exec enforcement arm and the grounding probe. Closed on CI run 34262145902 (success) at bc0d036, after the first close on 7fa7ec5 was withdrawn on CI red. That red was two real defects: a framework-build interpreter re-execs into its app-bundle binary, which the allow-list did not admit, and the resulting denial reads `posix_spawn: <path>: Undefined error: 0` at errno 0, which detect_violation named None rather than a violation — the fail-open direction. Both reproduced locally against a framework Python before any fix (exit 0 with the defects present, exit 1 after), both fixed, both regression-tested. Evidence: 3435 passed on the runner including the eight enforcement tests that were red; 94 local tests for this bead, zero skipped; all three planted negatives confined and named with same-path positive controls; removing the sandbox wrapper makes every negative succeed, so the tests are not vacuous. No-Claim: as strong as the probed macOS mechanism and no stronger; naming is cooperative, so a method that catches EPERM is confined and unnamed; the re-exec derivation is a layout rule, not a report from the interpreter; the Linux container (bead cairn-m1-cqt.5.2) is the gold boundary and green here claims nothing about it. Commands and raw output in the close comments.

comments.text:
Closed on re-executed evidence. Every command below was run at `7fa7ec5` with the working
tree clean for all five paths this bead owns (`git status --porcelain <paths>` empty), so
the output is bound to the commit that produced it. The bead's slice landed across two
commits: `05c3289` (the module, the bundle template, the golden, both test files, the probe
and the brief) and `7fa7ec5` (the fixes the fresh-eyes audit earned).

## Positive 1 — the honest method completes and its allow-list matches the bundle template

```
$ uv run pytest --no-header -p no:randomly -v tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py
test_the_honest_method_completes_and_its_allow_list_matches_the_bundle_template PASSED [ 11%]
test_a_write_outside_the_scratch_path_is_confined_and_named PASSED [ 22%]
test_the_same_write_inside_a_permitting_writable_root_completes PASSED [ 33%]
test_a_network_socket_is_confined_and_named PASSED [ 44%]
test_an_undeclared_subprocess_is_confined_and_named PASSED [ 55%]
test_the_same_spawn_declared_as_a_backend_completes PASSED [ 66%]
test_a_declared_backend_is_admitted_on_the_declaration_alone_and_is_recorded PASSED [ 77%]
test_the_same_method_without_the_declaration_is_confined PASSED [ 88%]
test_the_profile_the_gate_wrote_is_the_one_the_allow_list_addresses PASSED [100%]
9 passed, 1476 warnings in 1.51s
```

The field-by-field assertion against the bundle template is
`tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py:81`, which compares the
instantiation to `allowlist.template(shipped)` slot by slot. The same instantiation is
what bead L3 writes into the dispatch record; this bead does not touch `src/cairn/runner.py`.

The grounding record exists with probe commands and output:
`research/grounding/method-allowlist-macos-sandbox.md`, measured table in §2.

```
$ uv run python research/grounding/probe_method_allowlist.py; echo "exit=$?"
exit=0
$ uv run python research/grounding/probe_method_allowlist.py --unresolved-scratch; echo "exit=$?"
exit=0
  "rows": [
    {"action": "arith",           "rc": 0, "stdout": "1885351238965377138CHILD_OK"},
    {"action": "scratch_write",   "rc": 0, "stdout": "CHILD_OK"},
    {"action": "declared_exec",   "rc": 0, "stdout": "CHILD_OK"},
    {"action": "outside_write",   "rc": 9, "side_effect_present": false,
     "stderr": " PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted: '.../outside/outside_write.txt'"},
    {"action": "network",         "rc": 9, "stderr": "CHILD_ERR PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted"},
    {"action": "undeclared_exec", "rc": 9, "stderr": "CHILD_ERR PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted: '/bin/echo'"}
  ],
  "sandbox_exec": "/usr/bin/sandbox-exec",
  "scratch_resolved": true,
  "uname": "Darwin 25.6.0 ... arm64"
```

The `--unresolved-scratch` arm is the second mode and it exits 0 on the same assertions:
with the scratch path left unresolved (`/var/folders/...` rather than
`/private/var/folders/...`) the profile denies the honest write too, `rc=9`, which is the
path trap §3 of the brief documents. Both modes assert confinement on all three negatives.

The counted-object slot holds a stand-in at this close. Its binding to the gate-owned
counted object is bead L4's assertion, per this bead's own acceptance criteria.

## Positive 2 — a declared uncounted backend is admitted on the declaration alone and recorded

`tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py:148`
(`test_a_declared_backend_is_admitted_on_the_declaration_alone_and_is_recorded`) — PASSED
above. The method spawns the declared backend and completes; the declaration is written
through `allowlist.record` (`src/cairn/allowlist.py:327`) and read back by
`allowlist.read` (`src/cairn/allowlist.py:333`) on the substrate the verdict path reads.
`tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py:159` is the paired control: the
same method with the declaration removed is confined.

The INCONCLUSIVE cap this declaration earns is bead L2's predicate and is not asserted
here; no rung runs at this close.

## Planted negatives — each shown live against real `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`, no mock

| Negative | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| write outside the scratch path | `tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py:95` | confined, named `outside_write` |
| network socket | `tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py:118` | confined, named `network_egress` |
| undeclared subprocess spawn | `tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py:129` | confined, named `undeclared_exec` |

Each negative asserts `out == b""`, not merely the absence of the completion marker, and
each carries a same-path positive control that runs the identical action under a
permitting allow-list and completes: `:106` for the write, `:138` for the spawn. The
controls are what separate "the clause denied it" from "the action could not run".

Non-vacuity, established by removing the enforcement rather than by reading the tests:
a scratch harness rebinding `allowlist.argv_for` to strip the `sandbox-exec` wrapper makes
all three planted negatives succeed — `rc=0`, `METHOD_COMPLETED` on stdout, the outside
file present, the undeclared binary spawned.

```
  honest          {'rc': 0, 'stdout': b'METHOD_COMPLETED', 'side_effect': None}
  outside_write   {'rc': 0, 'stdout': b'METHOD_COMPLETED', 'side_effect': True}
  network         {'rc': 0, 'stdout': b'METHOD_COMPLETED', 'side_effect': None}
  undeclared_exec {'rc': 0, 'stdout': b'spawned\nMETHOD_COMPLETED', 'side_effect': None}

EVERY PLANTED NEGATIVE SUCCEEDS WITH ENFORCEMENT REMOVED -> the tests are not vacuous
```

## Unit layer

```
$ uv run pytest -q --no-header -p no:randomly tests/unit/test_ladder_allowlist.py
75 passed, 1476 warnings in 2.65s
```

75 unit assertions plus the 9 integration runs above is 84 for the bead. Zero skipped,
zero xfailed, zero deselected.

```
```

## Fresh-eyes audit and what it moved

An independent read-only Opus pass over the tests and module returned ten findings. Each
was re-executed here before any fix; six reproduced and are fixed, with the reproduction
inverted afterward:

- `check_instantiation` accepted `writable_root="/"`, and the live run then wrote outside
  scratch at `rc=0`. Refused at `src/cairn/allowlist.py:249`.
- A substituted exec path passed `check_instantiation`. `check_binding`
  (`src/cairn/allowlist.py:280`) re-derives the allow-list from the gate-owned launch
  inputs and requires equality, so the swap is refused there.
- `sandbox-exec: execvp() of '/bin/echo' failed: Operation not permitted` was classified
  `network_egress`. Now `undeclared_exec` via `EXEC_MARKERS` (`src/cairn/allowlist.py:68`).
- A denial naming a permitted exec path returned `None`. Now `outside_write`.
- The class turned on `os.access(path, X_OK)`, i.e. on host filesystem state. The class is
  now decided from the child's own trace and quoted paths alone, so the same bytes name
  the same class on any machine (`src/cairn/allowlist.py:315`).
- `assert out != b"METHOD_COMPLETED"` is satisfied by `b"spawned\nMETHOD_COMPLETED"`.
  Every negative now asserts `out == b""`.

## No-Claim

Enforcement is as strong as the probed macOS `sandbox-exec` mechanism and no stronger.
`research/grounding/method-allowlist-macos-sandbox.md` §4 states the split: confinement is
pre-execution and independent of the method, so it holds whatever the method does; naming
the violated clause reads the child's stderr and is cooperative, so a method that catches
`EPERM` and exits 0 is confined and unnamed. The Linux container (bead F2) is the gold
boundary and green here claims nothing about it. `sandbox-exec` is deprecated by its own
man page; it is present and functional on the probed host, and `mechanism_for`
(`src/cairn/allowlist.py:175`) refuses rather than skipping when no probed mechanism is
available, so its absence is a loud red and never a silent pass. Behavior on a GitHub
`macos-latest` runner is untested locally and CI is the decider.

`check_instantiation` sees only the record and the bundle, so it cannot bind
`writable_root` or the exec paths to the launch that produced them; `check_binding` is the
gate-side check that can, and a gate admitting a launch calls that one.

comments.text:
From cairn-m1-cqt.1.5 (CobaltBridge, 2026-09-08), at CopperRidge's instruction.

The receipt fields _clock and _wall read are measured by os.wait4, which covers the direct
child plus only the descendants that child itself reaped. Measured on this host with
research/grounding/probe_receipt_scope.py, raw rows in
research/grounding/receipt-measurement-scope.md:

| arm (identical work) | cpu_user_s | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| child reaps its CPU-burning grandchild | 2.800 | 18.4 MB |
| child orphans it | 0.021 | 18.6 MB |
| the RSS arm, reaped against orphaned | | 64.0 MB against 18.5 MB |

A ceiling-killed child is worse than an undercount, it is unreproducible: four runs of
identical work returned 2.030, 0.019, 2.143 and 1.666 cpu_user_s when the grandchild
exited before the kill, against a stable 0.016 to 0.021 when it was still running.

Both predicates read that quantity and both directions are unsound:

- src/cairn/laddertable.py:430 rejects on cpu_seconds ABOVE gate_ops / reference_rate, so
  an undercount never reaches the ceiling. CPU burned in a descendant the method never
  reaps is invisible to the clock check, and the method is measured as fast. This is an
  evasion channel, not only a measurement-quality issue.
- src/cairn/laddertable.py:450 rejects on wall_seconds above cpu_seconds, so the same
  undercount inflates the ratio and returns INCONCLUSIVE(WALL) for a method that forks
  and orphans rather than one that blocks.

cairn-m1-cqt.1.5 makes the scope a measured receipt field: spawn_and_wait samples
process-group membership once per tick through proc_listpgrppids and records tree,
reaped_descendants, truncated or unsampled. The ladder-side half, a trial-row scope and a
verdict predicate refusing a figure weaker than tree, is not yet written and is the seam
these two beads meet.

No-Claim: this measures the receipt the ladder reads. It does not establish that any
existing ladder table was affected, since no real ladder run has been recorded.

      Python.framework/Versions/3.14/Resources/Python.app/Contents/MacOS/Python:
      Undefined error: 0

The runner's interpreter is a framework build: `.../bin/python3.14` is a stub that re-execs
itself into `Python.app/Contents/MacOS/Python`. `instantiate` resolves `sys.executable` and
permits that one path, so the sandbox denies the re-exec and the method never runs. The uv
CPython used locally is not a framework build and does not re-exec, which is the divergence.

Two defects, both in `src/cairn/allowlist.py`, both mine:

1. `detect_violation` cannot name this denial. `DENIED` (`src/cairn/allowlist.py:66`)
   matches only `Operation not permitted`; a denied framework re-exec presents as
   `posix_spawn: <path>: Undefined error: 0`, so the namer returns `None` — "no violation"
   for a real denial. This is the fail-open direction and it is the more serious of the
   two. Observed as `assert None == 'network_egress'` at
   `tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py:123`.

2. `exec_paths` does not admit the interpreter the allow-list was asked to run. The
   framework binary the stub re-execs into is absent from the list, so an honest method on
   a framework-build Python is confined out of existence
   (`tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py:84`).

Failing tests, all in tests/integration/test_ladder_allowlist_enforcement.py:

    test_the_honest_method_completes_and_its_allow_list_matches_the_bundle_template  :84
    test_a_write_outside_the_scratch_path_is_confined_and_named                      :102
    test_the_same_write_inside_a_permitting_writable_root_completes                  :113
    test_a_network_socket_is_confined_and_named                                      :123
    test_an_undeclared_subprocess_is_confined_and_named                              :134

    test_the_same_method_without_the_declaration_is_confined                         :168

Neither defect is a CI-only artifact: any framework-build Python reaches both. The
confinement itself behaved correctly throughout — the sandbox denied an exec that was
genuinely outside the allow-list. What failed is the naming of that denial and the
derivation of the exec paths.

title: M1 ladder: REJECT writes the right ledger kind — implementation entries yank the revision, measured entries land on the hypothesis key
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(2c), §4, §2). A REJECT's ledger kind comes from its predicate, and
getting the kind right is what keeps a tool fault from blacklisting a method (or a
method refutation from being cleared by a revision bump). A wrong answer on a
gate-generated instance is a known-answer failure the skill's corpus missed: it says
nothing about the method's cost. The REJECT verdicts this bead wires come from live
ladder runs through bead L3's engine, and the revision an `implementation` entry names
is the one L3's dispatch record carries; L3 blocks this bead, so the engine and the
record both exist at this close.

WHAT — the mapping from REJECT predicate to ledger entry and yank, wired into the
verdict path:

1. `xP ≠ Q` on any trial, or a self-reported count diverging from the gate's beyond
   tolerance → an `implementation` entry against the implementation revision the
   dispatch record names, whose retry predicate is a new certified revision; the
   revision is YANKED through the §2 machinery (bead B2) — and NO `measured` entry is
   written on the hypothesis key. This is the fixture-(b) behavior: REJECT, yank the
   revision, `implementation` entry, hypothesis key untouched.

2. The refutation floor, the memory-cap and memory-model predicates, and the in-sample
   and out-of-sample model misses → a `measured` entry on the hypothesis key, carrying
   the measured parameter points, result with CI, method identity, decision and
   caught_by — the fields the §4 reach rule and the M2 preflight read.

3. The retry predicate is written by the gate, never by the refuted party: a `measured`
   entry's is a gate-owned re-measurement under the current plan whose verdict is not
   REJECT; an `implementation` entry's is an attributed new certified revision.

4. The table records which predicate fired (bead L2's field); this bead connects
   verdict → entry writing (bead R1's record) → yank (bead B2).

DONE WHEN each REJECT predicate class writes its correct entry kind against its correct
subject; the fixture-(b) composition holds end to end (yank + implementation entry + no
measured entry on the key); the retry predicate on every written entry is gate-authored.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_ladder_reject_wiring.py (unit: predicate→kind mapping
table-driven, subject selection); tests/integration/test_ladder_reject_ledger.py
(integration: a planted xP ≠ Q run yanks the revision and leaves the hypothesis key
clean; a planted floor failure writes the measured entry with points).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a planted floor-failing run writes a `measured` entry on the hypothesis key
  carrying measured points, CI, decision, retry predicate, caught_by; entry id and
  content pasted.
- Positive: a planted xP ≠ Q run yanks the dispatched revision (visible via
  substrate.yanked) and writes an `implementation` entry against it.
- Planted negative: after the xP ≠ Q run, a query for `measured` entries on the
  hypothesis key returns none — asserted, not assumed; an entry whose retry predicate
  the refuted party attempts to supply is refused.
- No-Claim: the wiring proves kinds land on the right subjects; the preflight that READS
  these entries arrives at M2 (cairn-m2-vgh) — nothing here blocks or allows any branch
  yet.
- Test types: unit (table-driven), integration. Files:
  tests/unit/test_ladder_reject_wiring.py, tests/integration/test_ladder_reject_ledger.py.

title: M1 ladder: result-table schema, typed verdicts, the shape diagnostic, and the table's reproducibility record
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(2c), §6(5), §7). The result table is the ladder's artifact, the Tier-2
ticket under the verdict rule, and the template for a negative-results entry. `justify`
reads it as `ladder_table` evidence: verdict KEEP justifies up to STRONG-EMPIRICAL, and
KEEP_IN_SAMPLE does for a statement whose scope is the in-sample sizes
(src/cairn/justify.py already carries the covering rule; the M0 evidence was synthetic).

WHAT

1. Table schema, one row set per run: size, trials, mean and sd of group operations,
   CPU-seconds and the reference rate of §6(3), memory, success rate, fit to the
   pre-registered model, out-of-sample prediction and its band, the nonce and seeds, the
   hypothesis hash, method identity and implementation revision it ran, and the
   gate-bundle hash it ran under. Substrate storage append-only, like the other record
   tables in src/cairn/schema.sql.

2. Typed verdicts fixed in the plan: REJECT(kind) — refutation floor failed, xP ≠ Q on
   any trial, memory cap exceeded, a self-reported count diverging from the gate's
   beyond tolerance, or an in-sample or out-of-sample miss of the pre-registered model;
   the table records which predicate fired and the measured points the §4 reach rule
   needs. INCONCLUSIVE — inside the band, a count the clock cannot support, or a rung whose
   dispatched method declared an uncounted arithmetic backend in its hypothesis object:
   §6(3) caps such rungs at INCONCLUSIVE until a counted implementation exists, and the
   cap is a verdict predicate here rather than an allow-list property, because the
   allow-list admits the declaration and never scores a rung. Bead L10 admits the
   declaration and records it where this predicate reads it.
   KEEP_IN_SAMPLE — every ≤ 50-bit rung passes: floor beaten, claim CI clears the band
   on group operations, memory under cap, x recovered on every trial, model fits in
   sample. KEEP — KEEP_IN_SAMPLE plus the 60-bit completion and out-of-sample check.
   "Floor beaten" is this bead's own predicate, evaluated against the refutation-floor
   threshold the ladder plan carries (bead L1's field, measured by bead S2): a rung
   whose claim group-operation mean fails to beat that threshold is REJECT on the
   floor predicate whatever the band says, while the band arithmetic itself is bead
   L7's — this bead composes both into the verdict.

3. The sorted-distribution shape as a diagnostic column: recorded against the model's
   declared shape; a departure beyond the plan's tolerance surfaces as a human-queue
   item of class `shape_departure` and is never a verdict predicate (the defect class is
   a truncated or bimodal distribution a mean check cannot see; the class retires if by

   Replayable); its reproducibility record is the §3 policy applied per trial (every
