   recomputation of the table's statistics and verdict from the verified trial rows.
   That record is the verification component the table's launch escrows (§5), and the
   repro node §7 requires before the table justifies STRONG-EMPIRICAL.

alone; the table carries every field above; the reproducibility record recomputes the

title: M1 ladder: run engine — pre-registration order check, dispatch record, arms on a shared instance stream, per-trial verification, patience
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(0)–(2), §3). The run engine is where pre-registration becomes an order
of records rather than a statement of intent, and where every trial's inputs are
gate-owned. The dispatch record is the executable-binding §3 requires: the hypothesis
key names the method identity (interface version + canonical parameters, never the
implementation revision), while the dispatch record and every trial recipe key name the
full §2 identity bundle, so a new revision re-ladders before it spends.

WHAT

1. Refusals before any trial runs: the hypothesis object's position in the substrate's
   append-only record sequence must precede the gate's entropy commitment for the run
   (the instance-maker's nonce, bead S4) — the ladder refuses to start otherwise; a
   dispatch whose method identity differs from its hypothesis object's is refused; an
   implementation revision that is uncertified or yanked is refused (the tier gate also
   refuses it — src/cairn/tiergate.py UNCERTIFIED/YANKED — but the ladder checks its own
   dispatch, since a gate that trusts another gate's earlier answer re-checks nothing).

2. The dispatch record: hypothesis hash, method identity, implementation revision (the
   full identity bundle), the instantiated allow-list (bead L10's template), and the
   gate-bundle hash. Every trial recipe key is built from the dispatched identity.

3. Arms: claimant and both baseline arms (the A/A pair) run on the same gate-generated
   instance stream from the instance-maker, each arm under its own gate-drawn method
   seeds. The 60-bit rung runs the claimant alone (bead L9).

4. Per-trial verification: xP == Q through the Tier-0 verifier
   (src/cairn/verifier.py), the instance read from the dispatch record — never from the
   method under test (§4: a verifier run on a submitter-chosen instance is the
   easy-instance substitution).

5. Patience: a trial that hits the per-trial patience ceiling (the §5 budget ceiling,
   already enforced by src/cairn/runner.py with status BUDGET_EXCEEDED) counts as a
   failure in the success-rate column and enters the model check at the ceiling value as
   a lower bound on its cost; a rung with any failed trial is at most INCONCLUSIVE —
   never KEEP — and REJECT where the ceiling value already misses the model or the
   floor.

DONE WHEN a full ≤ 50-bit run over a toy claimant produces a table through bead L2's
schema with all arms present; each refusal in (1) fires before any subprocess spawns
(observable the way tests/unit/test_verifier_validation.py::test_pre_spawn_refusal_table
observes popen_spy == []).

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_ladder_engine.py (unit: refusal table pre-spawn, dispatch
record fields, patience accounting); tests/integration/test_ladder_run.py (integration:
a small end-to-end rung with claimant + A/A arms, per-trial verification, table
written); tests/unit/test_ladder_engine_fuzz.py (fuzz/property: refusals hold under
randomized dispatch mutations).

title: M1 ladder: gate-owned counted arithmetic object, count-divergence REJECT, and the clock and wall checks
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(3)). The operation count is the gate's measurement, never the
claimant's: every other ladder input is gate-owned, and the KEEP band is computed from
this one. A number produced by the party being gated is the hallucinated-ablation-table
failure under another name. The clock exists because the counter cannot see arithmetic
done around it.

WHAT

1. The gate-owned counted arithmetic object: the baseline group arithmetic, instrumented
   to count every addition, doubling and inversion. Compiled — because the clock bound
   below holds only while no arithmetic a method can carry is faster per operation than
   the gate's object. Record the ratio of its per-operation cost to the fastest
   implementation on the build machine (bead S5's bundle field is that fastest
   per-operation COST, in seconds per group operation — divide by it, never by its
   reciprocal) in the gate bundle. The ratio is a cost over a cost, so a
   counted object as fast as the fastest gives 1 and a slower one gives more. Assert
   here, where both numbers first exist together, that S5's fastest measured
   per-operation cost is at MOST the counted object's own per-operation cost, so the
   recorded ratio is ≥ 1 — the fastest implementation is the one that spends the fewest
   seconds per operation, and a ratio below 1 means the benchmark and the counted object
   were not measuring the same operation: bead S5 cannot assert it, because the counted object this bead builds does not exist at S5's
   close and S5 blocks this bead.

2. Count predicate: every method — claimant and baseline alike — runs against the
   counted object; a count the method reports about itself is a diagnostic column; a
   divergence between self-report and the gate's count beyond the plan's tolerance is
   REJECT (an `implementation` entry — bead L11's mapping).

3. Clock check, per trial and per rung: CPU-seconds (user + system over the process
   tree, from the execution receipt) exceeding what the counted operations would take at
   the per-rung reference rate by more than the tolerance, or wall-clock exceeding CPU
   by more than the tolerance (an idle wait on a channel the counter cannot see), marks
   the rung INCONCLUSIVE — never KEEP, never REJECT — and surfaces a human-queue item of
   class `clock_inconclusive`.

4. Reference rates: at the ≤ 50-bit rungs the reference rate is the A/A arm's measured
   rate on the rung's own instances; at the 60-bit rung, which runs no baseline arm, it
   is a gate-owned calibration run of the counted object — a fixed operation count on
   the rung's instances, never a baseline distribution — recorded in the table.

5. Effective tolerance at a rung: the smaller of the plan's value and
   2 × measured A/A radius / ratio, so a tighter band tightens the clock rather than
   opening a gap beneath it. (The load-time half of this bound is bead L1's.)

The dummy-counted-calls hole this closes: a method that computes on extracted
coordinates with its own faster arithmetic and issues dummy counted calls sits inside
the tolerance only if the ratio is unrecorded or the bound unenforced; the planted
method for it is a corpus fixture (bead C2) and must not reach KEEP.

DONE WHEN counts are gate-measured for all arms; a planted count divergence REJECTs; a
planted idle wait and a planted uncounted-arithmetic overrun each land INCONCLUSIVE with
the queue item; reference rates appear in the table at every rung including 60-bit.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_counted_object.py (unit: counting correctness against known
operation sequences, ratio recording); tests/unit/test_ladder_clock.py (unit: tolerance
arithmetic, min() rule); tests/integration/test_ladder_clock_check.py (integration:
planted divergence REJECT, planted idle-wait INCONCLUSIVE + queue item, calibration run
at the 60-bit rung recorded).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: on a small rung, the gate's count for the A/A arm matches the known operation
  count of the baseline walk within exact bookkeeping (no tolerance needed), the ratio
  field is recorded in the bundle as a cost-over-cost figure that is ≥ 1, with bead S5's
  fastest measured per-operation cost at most the counted object's own per-operation cost, and the 60-bit
  calibration-run rate lands in the table; commands and output pasted.
- Planted negative: a method self-reporting half the gate's count REJECTs with the count
  predicate named; a method sleeping mid-trial (wall > CPU beyond tolerance) lands
  INCONCLUSIVE with a `clock_inconclusive` queue item; neither reaches KEEP.
- No-Claim: green proves counting and clock predicates fire as fixed; it proves nothing
  about the compiled object's absolute speed (bead S5 measured the rates) and does not
  close the dummy-counted-calls hole by itself — the corpus fixture (C2) is the evidence
  that composition catches it.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_counted_object.py,
  tests/unit/test_ladder_clock.py, tests/integration/test_ladder_clock_check.py.

| child orphans it | 0.021 | 18.6 MB |

title: M1 ladder: execution-receipt measurement scope — a process-tree figure the ladder can trust
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §3 receipt, §6 readers; probed facts from cairn-m0-e0s.9, recorded on
cairn-m1-cqt.1's comments). PLAN specifies the receipt's CPU seconds and peak RSS as
measurements "over the process tree", and the ladder's memory and clock checks read
exactly those fields. The M0 runner measures with os.wait4, which reports the direct
child plus only the descendants that child itself reaped. Probed on this machine: a
grandchild burning 1.0 s of CPU appears in the parent's wait4 result only when the
direct child waits for it (ru_utime 1.212 with the reap, 0.216 without); ru_maxrss
likewise jumps 16 MB → 51 MB; start_new_session changes neither. So for a skill that
forks and reaps, the receipt equals the tree figure; for one that leaves orphans, or is
killed at the ceiling before it can reap, the receipt undercounts — silently, because no
schema field says which quantity a row holds.

WHAT — make the tree figure trustworthy before the ladder reads it. Two admissible
shapes; decide with evidence and record the decision:

1. A real subtree measurement. cgroups carry it on Linux; macOS has no clean equivalent
   — probe what is achievable (per-pid sampling of the process group during the run is
   the plausible macOS arm) and measure its blind window.

2. A `measurement_scope` field on the receipt, so a reader can tell a
   direct-child-only figure from a tree figure, and the ladder refuses to run a method
   whose receipt scope is weaker than the plan requires.

RECEIPT-SCHEMA COST, shared with cairn-wdg: receipt fields are hashed content, so adding
one moves every receipt hash and the goldens that carry them. cairn-wdg holds the open
decision on recording the refusing threshold in the receipt. Settle the two schema
questions together as ONE receipt change with the moved goldens named before the change,
or record explicitly why they land separately. Name cairn-wdg in the close comment.

evidence for the mechanism) or carries a scope the ladder checks; the orphan case is

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_receipt_scope.py (unit: scope field or subtree reader);
tests/integration/test_runner_tree_measurement.py (integration: reaping child vs
orphaning child vs ceiling-killed child, each receipt classified correctly).
design:
## Architecture

- Approach: derive the receipt's measurement scope from a measurement rather than accept
  it as a declaration. `spawn_and_wait` already runs a poll loop at `TICK_S = 0.005` and
  already holds the skill's process-group id (`start_new_session=True`, `pgid = proc.pid`),
  so one `proc_listpgrppids` sample per tick names the descendants that existed. The
  sampled membership plus the exit shape (reaped of its own accord, or signalled at a cap
  or yank) classifies the `os.wait4` figure the receipt carries. The ladder then refuses a
  trial whose scope is weaker than a tree figure, which closes the evasion channel probe 2
  found: CPU burned in a descendant the skill never reaps is invisible to
  `laddertable._clock`.
- Rejected alternative: a real subtree accounting figure. macOS has no cgroup equivalent,
  and probe 3 measures what a host can supply — exact group membership, not aggregated
  usage. Sampling is therefore a sound witness for the figure's scope and not a substitute
  for the figure. Also rejected: a scope supplied by the launching party, which is an
  assertion where the sampled value is a measurement.
- Scope values, three, because two do not separate the cases probe 1 distinguishes:
  `tree` (the child exited of its own accord and no group member but the leader was ever
  sampled, so there is nothing the figure can omit); `reaped_descendants` (descendants were
  sampled and the child exited of its own accord, so `wait4` carries exactly those the
  child reaped and the harness cannot establish that it reaped all of them);
  `truncated` (the child was signalled at a wall cap or a yank, or a group member outlived
  it, so the figure is an undercount of unknown size). `pari.run_gp`
  (`src/cairn/pari.py:140`) spawns and reaps, so a real gp-backed skill lands on
  `reaped_descendants` and only the ladder's own trials are held to `tree`.
- Blind window, stated because it bounds the claim: a descendant born and reaped inside one
  5 ms tick is never sampled. Sampled membership is a lower bound on the descendants that
  existed, so `reaped_descendants` and `truncated` are sound positive claims and `tree` is
  the claim the window limits. The window is measured, not assumed.
- Pattern-to-follow: `src/cairn/runner.py` `spawn_and_wait`/`Launch` for the poll loop and
  the frozen launch record; `src/cairn/substrate.py:31-45` `RECEIPT_FIELDS`/`RECEIPT` for
  the canonical field list; `src/cairn/laddertable.py:421-464` `_clock`/`_wall` for the
  verdict shape a scope refusal takes.
- Touches: `src/cairn/runner.py` (sampler, `Launch.measurement_scope`, the single receipt
  construction site at `:436-450`), `src/cairn/substrate.py` (`RECEIPT_FIELDS`),
  `src/cairn/schema.sql` (`receipts.measurement_scope`), `src/cairn/laddertable.py` (the
  scope predicate), `tests/unit/test_receipt_scope.py`,
  `tests/integration/test_runner_tree_measurement.py`.
- ADRs: none; implements PLAN section 3 receipt and section 6 readers.
- Data model impact: one additional NOT NULL hashed receipt field. Every receipt hash moves.
- Coupled decision, cairn-wdg: the pair lands as ONE receipt change carrying the scope
  field alone. `measurement_scope` is not derivable from anything the substrate already
  holds, so it must be recorded. The refusing threshold cairn-wdg asks about IS derivable
  from the recipe plus the bundle's tiers, and a recorded copy of a derivable number can
  drift from its derivation, so it stays out of the receipt and cairn-wdg records that
  verdict against this change.
- Failure modes: a forking-and-reaping skill misclassified as `truncated` and refused
  (positive control, the reaping arm must land on `reaped_descendants`); a sub-tick
  descendant missed and a `truncated` run labelled `tree` (bounded by the measured blind
  window, and the exit-shape half of the rule catches every killed run regardless of
  sampling); the ladder reading `cpu_seconds` without consulting scope (the planted
  negative — a reader that skips the scope check fails against the orphaning fixture).

## Pre-implementation research

- [R1] `os.wait4` reports the direct child plus the descendants that child reaped. An
  orphaning child undercounts CPU 2.800 s against 0.021 s and RSS 64.0 MB against 18.5 MB
  for identical work. Source: `research/grounding/probe_receipt_scope.py`, table in
  `research/grounding/receipt-measurement-scope.md` (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R2] A ceiling-killed receipt's CPU figure is not reproducible: four runs of identical
  work returned 2.030, 0.019, 2.143 and 1.666 s when the grandchild exited before the kill,
  against a stable 0.016-0.021 s when it was still running. Source: same probe, probe 2
  arm (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R3] `laddertable._clock` (`src/cairn/laddertable.py:430`) rejects on `cpu_seconds` above
  `gate_ops / reference_rate`, and `_wall` (`:450`) rejects on `wall_seconds` above
  `cpu_seconds`. An undercount both suppresses a real clock rejection and manufactures a
  spurious wall rejection. Source: both function bodies read (verified: 2026-09-08;
  Confidence: HIGH).
- [R4] `proc_listpgrppids` in `/usr/lib/libproc.dylib` returns exact process-group
  membership through ctypes, signature `(uint32, void *, int) -> int`, returning the COUNT
  of pids written and not a byte count. Cost 17.2 us per call over 2000 calls. Source:
  probe 3 arm, executed (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R5] `spawn_and_wait` spawns with `start_new_session=True` and holds `pgid = proc.pid`,
  and its poll loop already sleeps `TICK_S = 0.005`, so the group contains the skill's
  descendants alone and a per-tick sample costs 0.34 % of a tick. Source:
  `src/cairn/runner.py:30`, `:195-232`, body read (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R6] The receipt has one construction site (`src/cairn/runner.py:436-450`) and its field
  list has one home (`src/cairn/substrate.py:31-45`); the tests that build receipts derive
  them from `RECEIPT_FIELDS` rather than literal field lists
  (`tests/unit/test_substrate_predicates.py:60`, `tests/integration/test_substrate.py:423`).
  Source: bodies read (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R7] `pari.run_gp` spawns gp with `Popen` and reaps it, so gp-backed skills produce a
  `reaped_descendants` receipt and cannot satisfy a `tree` requirement. Source:
  `src/cairn/pari.py:140-145` (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R8] The goldens that move are named from an executed probe that adds the field and runs
  the suite, not from a grep. `tests/goldens/m0_run_transcript.golden` scrubs hashes to
  `[HASH]`, so a receipt-hash move need not reach it; that reading is a hypothesis the
  probe settles. Source: golden read plus the running probe (verified: 2026-09-08 for the
  scrubbing, probe pending for the list; Confidence: HIGH for the scrubbing, the list is
  recorded before any code lands).
- Delegability: STATEABLE once R8's golden list is recorded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a trial whose child reaps its grandchild and one whose child orphans it both
  produce receipts a reader classifies correctly (tree figure vs undercount), with the
  probe commands and numbers pasted.
- Planted negative: with the orphaning fixture, a reader that treats the receipt as a
  tree figure without checking scope is caught by a failing test; a ceiling-killed child
  (killed before reaping) is likewise classified, never silently read as a tree figure.
- No-Claim: this bead makes the measurement's scope explicit and checkable; it does not
  claim macOS gives a true subtree figure (the probe decides what is achievable), and
  the goldens moved by any receipt-schema change are named in the diff, not discovered.
- Test types: unit, integration, probe. Files: tests/unit/test_receipt_scope.py,
  tests/integration/test_runner_tree_measurement.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

title: M1 ladder: memory measurement, the floor-rung cap, and the memory-model check
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(2)). The harness cannot see a method's "algorithmic table" except
through what the method reports, so the quantity it can measure is the predicate and the
reported one the diagnostic, never the reverse. The cap binds where the floor lives,
because at 30 bits the BSGS table is 2¹⁵ entries and a cap there would refuse an honest
constant-memory model that the 50-bit cap admits.

WHAT

1. The measured quantity, from the execution receipt (scope per bead L5): peak RSS over
   the trial's process tree, LESS the A/A arm's peak on the same instances (at the
   60-bit rung, less the clock-calibration run's peak), PLUS the bytes written to the
   gate-owned scratch path — the only writable location on a ladder-tested method's
   allow-list (bead L10).

2. The cap: fixed in the ladder plan as the BSGS table for the size, binding at the
   rungs where the refutation floor is measured — the 50-bit rung (≈ 1 GB) and the
   60-bit completion rung (2³⁰ entries). Exceeding the cap at those rungs is REJECT
   (memory-cap predicate; a `measured` ledger entry via bead L11).

3. The memory-model check, at every rung including the small ones: the measured quantity
   must match the pre-registered memory model on the sizes measured; growth the model
   did not declare is a model miss and REJECT, never KEEP. The small rungs are carried
   by this check, not by the cap.

4. The method's self-reported table bytes: a diagnostic column only. The planted method
   that holds a BSGS-sized table in process memory while reporting zero table bytes must
   exceed the 50-bit cap on the gate's own measurement — that fixture is corpus bead
   C2's; this bead makes the measurement it relies on real.

DONE WHEN a rung's memory figure is computed from receipt + scratch accounting as in
(1); a planted over-cap method REJECTs at 50 bits and passes untouched at 30 bits under
a constant-memory model; a planted undeclared-growth method REJECTs at a small rung via
the model check.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_ladder_memory.py (unit: the subtraction-and-scratch
arithmetic, cap boundary at exactly the table size);
tests/integration/test_ladder_memory_check.py (integration: planted over-cap REJECT at
50 bits, no-cap-at-30 admit, undeclared-growth REJECT).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a small rung's memory figure equals receipt peak RSS minus the A/A arm's
  peak plus scratch bytes, shown against a method with known allocations; command and
  numbers pasted.
- Planted negative: a method allocating a BSGS-sized table at the 50-bit rung REJECTs on
  the gate's measurement whatever it self-reports; the same allocation pattern at 30
  bits under an honest constant-memory declaration is NOT refused by any cap (the model
  check is what carries the small rungs); undeclared growth at a small rung REJECTs.
- No-Claim: green proves the memory predicates fire on the gate's own measurement; it
  proves nothing about receipt trustworthiness (bead L5 owns scope) and nothing about
  scratch-path exclusivity (bead L10 owns the allow-list).
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_ladder_memory.py,
  tests/integration/test_ladder_memory_check.py.

title: M1 ladder: A/A null arm and trial-count sizing — measure the paired variance, record the count and design radius
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(2), §13 M1). The A/A null arm — the baseline run against itself in the
same harness, same trial count, same instance stream, the two arms differing only in the
method seeds the gate draws for them — sets the decision band: a speedup is KEPT only if
the whole claim CI clears 1 + 2·radius (floor 1.01 guarding a degenerate null arm). The
trial count is sized at M1 so that positive control (j) is KEPT and control (k)
INCONCLUSIVE with margin. The arithmetic that makes 10² a floor and not the count: at
rho's sd ≈ 0.5·mean, the A/A radius at 10² trials is ≈ 0.14, the band ≈ 1.28, and the √2
control's CI lower bound ≈ 1.22 — so 10² returns INCONCLUSIVE on a known-true advance.
Solving the KEEP inequality for the √2 control under independent arms gives n ≳ 130; the
paired design on a shared instance stream should need fewer, and the real number is a
measurement, not this solve.

WHAT

1. The A/A arm as a standing part of every plan run (engine bead L3 runs it; this bead
   owns its statistics): compute the A/A CI radius per rung from the two baseline arms.

2. The sizing measurement: run plain rho vs plain rho (A/A) and negation-map rho vs
   plain rho (the √2 pair) at the 30–50-bit rungs across candidate trial counts; measure
   the PAIRED variance on the shared instance stream; derive the smallest count that
   KEEPs the √2 pair with margin while the A/A pair stays INCONCLUSIVE; record the count
   and the design radius it targets in the ladder plan (bead L1's fields).

3. The recorded artifact: the sizing run's numbers (per-count radius, the √2 CI lower
   bounds) in the close comment and the derived values written into the plan.

4. The per-rung cost record §6(2) requires — "each rung's budget follows its declared
   cost profile under the chosen count (an interpreted 50-bit baseline at that count
   runs for hours, a compiled one for minutes; M1 records which)": measured wall and
   CPU seconds per ARM per RUNG at the chosen count for the interpreted baseline, and
   the whole-ladder figure they imply for one ≤ 50-bit run (three arms × the chosen
   count × three rungs). These rungs, not the 60-bit one, dominate M1 ladder cost, so
   this is decision 2's ≤ 50-bit input — bead S5 records the 60-bit half first (S5 blocks
   bead L4 and L4 blocks this bead, so S5's record always predates this number) and this
   bead completes decision 2's record with the ≤ 50-bit half — and it is also decision 10's input, which bead B7 reads as the ladder's
   per-run cost. Record wall and CPU separately and name the CORE-SECONDS figure
   (cpu_user_s + cpu_sys_s) as the one B7 multiplies, since the cumulative edge is
   metered against charges the gate carries in core seconds. If the interpreted baseline cannot run the sized ≤ 50-bit rungs inside the
   Tier-1 budget, name the compiled-baseline follow-up bead in the close comment, as
   bead S5 does for its half.

DONE WHEN the plan carries a measured trial count and design radius; the sizing evidence
shows the count is minimal-with-margin (the next smaller candidate fails one of the two
controls); the A/A radius computation is unit-tested against a synthetic distribution
with known spread; the per-arm per-rung cost at the chosen count is recorded with the
whole-ladder ≤ 50-bit figure it implies.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_ladder_sizing.py (unit: radius computation on synthetic
data, band arithmetic incl. the 1.01 floor); tests/integration/test_ladder_aa_arm.py
(integration: an A/A run at a small rung yields a radius and no verdict beyond
INCONCLUSIVE for the null claim).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: the plan's trial count and design radius are measured values with the sizing
  run's numbers pasted (per-candidate-count radius, √2-pair CI lower bounds); the
  next-smaller candidate count demonstrably fails a control.
- Positive: measured wall and CPU seconds per arm per rung at the chosen count are
  recorded with the whole-ladder ≤ 50-bit figure they imply, and named as decision 2's
  ≤ 50-bit input (bead S5 holds the 60-bit half); numbers pasted.
- Planted negative: with a synthetic degenerate null arm (radius ≈ 0), the band floors at
  1.01 rather than collapsing; an A/A claim never returns KEEP or REJECT in the
  integration run.
- No-Claim: the sizing holds for rho-shaped spread (sd ≈ 0.5·mean) on this machine's
  instances; corpus controls (j) and (k) are the proof the sized plan behaves — this
  bead records the size, it does not pre-certify the controls.
- Test types: unit, integration, measurement. Files: tests/unit/test_ladder_sizing.py,
  tests/integration/test_ladder_aa_arm.py.

title: M1 ladder: the in-sample fit on declared free parameters and the model-miss band
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(0), §6(2)). The hypothesis object declares which of the pre-registered
cost model's parameters are fixed and which the ≤ 50-bit rungs fit — the exponent and
the memory model's shape are always fixed; a constant or crossover may be left free — so
"fitted on the ≤ 50-bit rungs" names exactly the declared free parameters and nothing
else. The predicate is fixed in the plan because a model miss each implementer defines
for itself is a different ladder under one name.

WHAT

1. The fit: the declared free parameters fit by least squares on the logarithm of the
   rung means over the ≤ 50-bit rungs.

2. The in-sample check: each of those rungs' measured mean must sit inside
   1 ± 2·√(radius² + (sd_s/(mean_s·√n))²) of the fitted model's prediction at that
   size, where radius is that rung's A/A radius and n its trial count. A rung outside
   the band is an in-sample model miss — REJECT, a `measured` ledger entry (bead L11).

3. The fixture-(a) mechanism this catches, stated so the corpus bead can plant it
   exactly: a pre-registered model that fixes a parameter the measurement contradicts —
   an exponent below ½ for a method whose operations grow as √n (at exponent 0.4 the
   miss between 30 and 50 bits is ≈ 4× against a band of a few tens of percent), or a
   fixed constant below the measured one — misses in sample, while control (j)'s √n
   model with a free constant fits.

4. The claim honest about a ≥ rho cost sits INSIDE the band and is INCONCLUSIVE — its
   correct verdict; the in-sample REJECT fires on the pre-registered model's miss, not
   on being slow.

DONE WHEN the fit uses only declared free parameters; the band arithmetic matches the
formula; a planted exponent-0.4 claimant REJECTs in sample at the 30–50-bit rungs while
a √n-with-free-constant model fits.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_ladder_insample.py (unit: fit restricted to declared free
parameters, band formula against hand-computed cases, property: a model fitting all
rungs is not rejected); tests/integration/test_ladder_insample_check.py (integration:
planted exponent-0.4 REJECT, honest-slow INCONCLUSIVE).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: on synthetic rung means following √n with noise inside the band, the fit
  recovers the free constant and every rung sits in band; hand-computed band values
  match the implementation to full precision; output pasted.
- Planted negative: a model pre-registering exponent 0.4 against √n-growing measurements
  REJECTs with the in-sample predicate named and the measured points recorded; an
  attempt to fit a parameter the hypothesis object declared FIXED is refused.
- No-Claim: the in-sample check tests the declared model on the sizes measured; it
  establishes no asymptotic and never promotes — KEEP still requires the out-of-sample
  rung (bead L9) and the band checks on operations and memory.
- Test types: unit, property, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_ladder_insample.py,
  tests/integration/test_ladder_insample_check.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.

title: M1 ladder: the 60-bit completion-and-extrapolation rung
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(2b)). The 60-bit rung is the completion-and-extrapolation rung: it
exists so a clean in-sample fit that misses out of sample is REJECT, and so a method
must actually complete at the size where BSGS needs 2³⁰ table entries. A 60-bit generic
trial is ≈ 1.3×10⁹ group operations — minutes compiled, a quarter hour interpreted — so
a full 10²-trial distribution check at 60 bits is Tier-2 work by its own declared
profile, is no part of the rung, and runs only when the tier gate grants that budget.

WHAT

1. The rung runs the claimant's method alone on the m = 10 fresh hold-out instances —
   no baseline arm and no A/A arm, since the check is the claim's own fitted model
   against its own measured mean. m and the fit-on/hold-out split are ladder-plan
   fields, never worker-chosen.

2. Completion: the method must complete and recover x on all m instances (per-trial
   Tier-0 verification as everywhere).

3. The out-of-sample check: the model fitted on the ≤ 50-bit rungs (bead L8) must
   predict the measured 60-bit mean inside 1 ± 2·√(radius² + (sd₆₀/(mean₆₀·√m))²) over
   the m hold-outs. The band is widened by the rung's own sampling error because at
   m = 10 and rho's sd ≈ 0.5·mean the rung's standard error (≈ 16 %) exceeds the A/A
   radius, and a point-against-band comparison would REJECT an honest method about one
   run in five.

4. Tiering: the rung is tiered by its own declared cost profile; the KEEP_IN_SAMPLE
   table is the scoped Tier-2 ticket that admits it (tier-gate bead B5 owns the
   scoping; this bead declares the rung's profile honestly).

5. Verdict composition: KEEP = KEEP_IN_SAMPLE plus this rung's completion and
   out-of-sample pass; a clean in-sample fit that misses out of sample is REJECT
   (a `measured` entry).

DONE WHEN a claimant with an honest model passes the rung's code path end to end over the
m plan-named hold-outs at the scaled stand-in size of the TEST PLAN below; a planted
in-sample-clean/out-of-sample-missing model REJECTs; the rung's clock check uses the
calibration-run reference rate (bead L4). The real 60-bit run on 10 fresh instances is
corpus control (j)'s (bead C2, cairn-m1-cqt.3.2): the rung is admitted only on the scoped
KEEP_IN_SAMPLE Tier-2 ticket bead B5 (cairn-m1-cqt.4.5) builds, B5 does not block this
bead, and under the M0 gate a Tier-2 launch holding only the tier-0 hypothesis-object
ticket collects TIER_TWO_ABOVE (src/cairn/tiergate.py:84-85, :109-115) — so no 60-bit
rung is admissible at this close.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_ladder_oos.py (unit: band widening arithmetic, KEEP
composition rule); tests/integration/test_ladder_60bit_rung.py (integration: a scaled
stand-in rung — the real 60-bit run is quarter-hour-per-trial interpreted, so the
integration test exercises the same code path at a smaller size with plan-scaled
parameters, and the true 60-bit rung evidence lands with corpus control (j)).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: the rung code path runs claimant-only over m plan-named hold-outs, verifies
  x on each, computes the widened band from the formula, and composes KEEP only from
  KEEP_IN_SAMPLE + completion + out-of-sample pass; scaled integration run pasted.
- Planted negative: a model tuned to fit the ≤ 50-bit rungs and miss at the hold-out size
  REJECTs on the out-of-sample predicate; a rung attempted with a worker-chosen m or
  split is refused (plan fields only).
- No-Claim: the scaled integration run proves the code path, not 60-bit behavior; the
  true 60-bit evidence is corpus control (j)'s and the tier gate must grant the rung's
  budget — nothing here bypasses the KEEP_IN_SAMPLE scoped ticket.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_ladder_oos.py,
  tests/integration/test_ladder_60bit_rung.py.

title: M1 research exit: first operator-opened campaign carried to a terminal status with a rendered report
description:
M1 research exit (PLAN.md §13, M1 block): one operator-opened hypothesis on a named open subproblem is carried to a terminal status by the M1 machinery, with its ladder table or hunt record, its Skeptic record and a rendered report. The campaign's mathematical verdict is not a completion criterion; its completion and legibility are.

Background: the 2026-09-05 Astra reality check found that every existing milestone establishes engineering behavior while the project's value proposition (an independently assessable research increment) is untested by any done-when. Anthropic's 2026 zeta-bound and FLT results were each judged by named outside readers of a written artifact; cairn's egress prints tags per statement hash but no milestone requires a report a reader can assess. This bead makes the first honest research action an M1 deliverable rather than something that happens after M1.

## Architecture
- Approach: after the M1 leaves that make a single track runnable close (baseline skills, ladder run engine and its trust chain, worker dispatch, ticket lattice and escrow, router and hunt record, acceptance corpus), an operator opens one hypothesis object on a named open subproblem from HANDOFF.md, funds it through the tier gate, and lets Prover, ladder and Skeptic run it to a terminal status. The rendered report is produced by the egress renderer of §10 from substrate records only: claim statement, hypothesis key, ladder table or hunt record with its null arm, Skeptic record, calibration tag, tier spend, and a limitations section stating what the result does not show. Rejected alternative: treating M1's planted-corpus done-when as sufficient, which proves the gates catch fabrication but never that the machinery produces anything a reader can assess.
- Pattern-to-follow: tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py (end-to-end slice with real substrate and real PARI); src/cairn/repro.py for the reproduction node the report cites.
- Touches: src/cairn/egress or the renderer module named in §10; research/SESSION-PROMPTS.md (research-mode opener gains the campaign checklist); tests/e2e/ (campaign fixture); PLAN.md §13 M1 block (text landed 2026-09-05).
- ADRs: none; PLAN.md §13 is the decision record for milestone done-when clauses.
- Data model impact: none; the report reads existing node kinds. If the renderer needs a report node kind, that is a §3 schema addition and mints its own bead.
- Failure modes: (1) the campaign reaches a terminal status but the report omits the null arm or the Skeptic record, detected by the renderer refusing to render (exit 2) and the e2e fixture asserting the refusal on a planted incomplete record set; (2) the operator-opened hypothesis duplicates a settled key, detected by the ledger preflight answering AlreadySettled and the campaign fixture asserting the park; (3) the ladder's 50-bit arm exceeds the session deadline (about 93 s per rho trial times 130 trials per arm, unmeasured as a full run), detected by the ladder plan's measured duration row and the CALL_BOUND_S alarm path.

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] Reality check gap 10: no acceptance evidence that the completed machinery produces useful research; gaps 1 to 6 are owned by M1 leaves — source: ~/Knowledge/projects/cairn/reality-check-astra-2026-09-05.md (verified: 2026-09-05) (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R2] Anthropic's zeta bound (anthropic.com/research/riemann-zeta, 2026-08-10) and FLT formalization (anthropic.com/research/formalizing-fermats-last-theorem, 2026-09-04) were both accepted through a written artifact read by named outside mathematicians; the FLT technical PDF carries a limitations section — source: ~/Knowledge/research/anthropic-math-architecture-vs-cairn-2026-09-05.md (documented: 2026-09-05) (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R3] The minimum closure set for a first honest research action is cairn-m1-cqt.2 (.2.3, .2.5), .1.3 to .1.12, .6.1 to .6.4, .4.1 to .4.6, .8.2, .8.4, .3.2 to .3.8; the Lean leaves .5.* and .7.2 gate PROVEN, not a first STRONG-EMPIRICAL increment — source: same comparison note, section 4 (documented: 2026-09-05) (Confidence: MEDIUM)
- [R4] Ladder feasibility: about 93 s per 50-bit rho trial, 130 trials per arm — source: PLAN.md §6 and the grounding brief under research/grounding/ (documented: 2026-09-05) (Confidence: MEDIUM)
- Delegability: STATEABLE once R3's closure set is closed; until then NEEDS-INVESTIGATION-BEAD for the report renderer's node contract.

## Test plan
- e2e: tests/e2e/test_m1_campaign.py — a seeded campaign on a toy-curve subproblem runs Prover, ladder and Skeptic to a terminal status and the renderer emits a report whose sections are asserted against the substrate records they cite.
- e2e: tests/e2e/test_m1_campaign.py::test_incomplete_records_refuse_render — a planted record set missing the Skeptic record makes the renderer exit 2 and the campaign stay non-terminal.
- integration: tests/integration/test_ledger_preflight.py::test_campaign_on_settled_key_parks — the operator-opened hypothesis on a settled key parks with already_settled.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive observable: `uv run pytest -q tests/e2e/test_m1_campaign.py` prints `passed` for the seeded campaign and the rendered report file named in its output contains sections Claim, Hypothesis key, Ladder table (with A/A null arm) or Hunt record, Skeptic record, Calibration tag, Tier spend, Limitations.
- Planted negative: `uv run pytest -q tests/e2e/test_m1_campaign.py::test_incomplete_records_refuse_render` passes only because the renderer exits 2 on a record set missing the Skeptic record; the fixture asserts exit code 2 and the token `refused: missing skeptic_record`.
- No-Claim: a green campaign fixture proves the machinery carries a hypothesis to a terminal status and renders a legible report; it proves nothing about the mathematical value of the increment, which is not a completion criterion.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

title: M1: baseline skills rho_dp (witness certificate + gate verifier) and bsgs (refutation floor), gate-owned instance-maker, each with the §2 self-test; gmpy2 Hasse-interval BSGS as implementation axis (decision 1); compiled-baseline decision from m0-rho60-measure (decision 2); fastest-implementation clock-tolerance measurement (decision 12)

comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.16 (the section 2 conformance harness), the registration
interface the three M1 subjects need.

tests/conformance/skill_contract.py holds SUBJECTS, a tuple of SkillSubject.
Adding rho_dp, bsgs and the gate-owned instance-maker means appending three
rows and one EXPECTED_SHOULD entry each. The fields:

  name                   the matrix column label
  module                 an importable module path, launched as python -m <module>
  corpus_path            the vendored known-answer corpus, read directly by S2-04
                         and S2-05
  floor_golden           a name under tests/goldens, read as <name>.golden by S2-06
  inputs                 the stdin document; must carry bits and seed, and bits
                         must be a size the subject's COST_PROFILE declares
  out_of_range_inputs    a stdin document whose bits lie outside INDEPENDENT_RANGE
  conforming             True means every MUST FAIL is a suite failure
  certify                module_certify, which calls module.certify(sub)
  transcript             module_transcript, which calls module.transcript()
  postcondition          a callable returning (held, refused_a_planted_answer),
                         or None; S2-14 is SHOULD and does not gate
  expected_must_failures frozenset(), for a conforming subject

So a conforming M1 skill module must expose, beyond its own entry point:
INTERFACE_VERSION matching <name>/<int>, SEAM, CROSS_CHECK_AXIS in
{implementation, algorithm}, INDEPENDENT_RANGE, COST_PROFILE, IDENTITY_SOURCES,
implementation_revision(root), identity_bundle(root), run(), main(),
certify(sub) and transcript(). toy_curve is the exception that proves the rule:
its certify and transcript live in cairn.selftest, so its registry row names
toy_curve_certify and toy_curve_transcript instead.

Two clauses need care from an M1 subject:

S2-10 launches the subject through tests/fixtures/skills/harness_child.py, which
patches the module named by the subject's SEAM to return its real answer plus 2
and then calls the subject's entry. A subject whose cross-check does not route
through a single patchable module attribute cannot be checked this way, and the
seam it declares has to be the one it actually calls.

S2-11 has a source arm that greps the subject module for the token CAIRN_DB. A
skill that legitimately needs a substrate path takes it on stdin, never from the
environment.

The harness's own checks are claim-agnostic: nothing in skill_contract.py names
toy_curve, and registering a subject is the whole of the work.

All three stopped on the 10^8 op cap, never the 30-minute cap. Expected work is the
birthday bound sqrt(pi*n/2) = 1166326476 for the vector's order
n = 866004985024698433, so each wall is 1166326476 divided by the measured rate.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. The rates are STRONG-EMPIRICAL. The walls are CONJECTURE:
each assumes a rate measured over the first 10^8 ops of one walk holds for the
remaining ~1.07x10^9, and that the walk's expected length equals its birthday bound.
The 1.88x spread is attributed to machine load, which is an inference from the
declared conditions rather than an isolated measurement; an unloaded core sits at the
15 to 17 minute end.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THIS BEAD. PLAN §5 tiers the 60-bit rung by its declared cost
profile, and the Tier-1 budget is one core, minutes. Fifteen to twenty-eight minutes
is not that, on any of the three runs. The interpreted rung does not finish inside a
Tier-1 budget, which is the condition operator decision 2 named for funding a
compiled rho/BSGS baseline at M1.

That is an input, not the decision. Two things it does not settle: the gmpy2
comparison is decision 1 and remains unmeasured, so how much of the gap is
interpreter overhead rather than algorithm is unknown; and nothing here says what a
compiled implementation's rate would be, only what this one's is.

A completed 40-bit rho is available as the reference point: 474179 ops, reproducible
across all three runs, its x accepted by the real Tier-0 verifier, the planted
off-by-one refused with reason `xP-ne-Q`. Detail and commands in
`research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` §9.

title: M1 skills: rho_dp — Pollard rho with distinguished points, the §3 witness certificate, its gate-side verifier, and the negation-map variant as a method under test
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §2 skill contract, §3 witness certificate, §6 baseline). The ladder's
baseline at M1 is plain rho without the negation map (≈ 1.25√n group operations, O(1)
memory) — never BSGS. Positive control (j) of the M1 corpus submits the negation-map
variant (≈ 0.886√n, equal memory) as a claimant against that baseline and must be KEPT:
its √2 on group operations is a known answer. `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py` is the
template for the shape a Cairn skill takes — canonical JSON on stdin/stdout, an
IDENTITY_SOURCES list hashed into `implementation_revision`, a vendored corpus, a golden
certificate, a byte-equal double run through `src/cairn/selftest.py`.

WHAT

1. `src/cairn/skills/rho_dp.py`: Pollard rho with distinguished points on prime-order toy
   curves (30–60 bits). The walk definition is part of the output: the additive-walk
   multipliers (or the PRNG seed that derives them), the index function, and the
   distinguished-point predicate θ. Every nondeterminism source is pinned by an input
   seed, so a run is deterministic and the self-test's double run byte-equal.

2. The §3 witness as the skill's certificate: `{curve, n, P, Q, walk definition,
   colliding DP triples (X, a, b), (X, c, d)}`. Storing seeds in place of `(a, b)` is a
   Tier-3 storage optimization and out of scope (§3): store the triples.

3. The gate-side witness verifier as a gate-bundle object, a module distinct from the
   skill (beside `src/cairn/verifier.py`; exact placement is the implementer's), because
   the §3 owner rule grades a witness `AuditOnly` when its only verifier ships in its
   producer's own revision. The check: `aP + bQ = X = cP + dQ` for both triples, reject
   `b ≡ d (mod n)` outright — a refusal, never a silent retry — then
   `x = (a − c)(d − b)⁻¹ mod n` and `xP == Q`.

4. The negation-map variant as a method under test with its own canonical parameter in
   the method identity — NOT the ladder plan's baseline. §6 says a negation-map rho
   "once shipped as a baseline skill is the baseline from the day it lands", and control
   (j) needs plain rho as the baseline to measure the √2 against; so at M1 the variant
   ships as a claimant method and the ladder plan's baseline-revision field names plain
   rho. Promoting the variant to baseline is a deliberate later plan change, out of
   scope here. State this trap in the module docstring the plan reads.

5. The ladder plan's baseline-revision field is WRITTEN here. Bead L1 authors that field
   and seeds it, because no `rho_dp` revision exists at L1's close; this bead's close
   replaces the seed with the shipped identity bundle and records the replacement — the
   same split bead S2 carries for the plan's refutation-floor and memory-cap fields. L1
   blocks this bead, so the plan exists to write into. Without this write the plan names
   a revision nothing certified, and the ladder's baseline arms resolve to a placeholder.

6. The §2 self-test: a corpus with a per-case ledger (`pass | intentional_non_goal |
   known_gap`) and a committed pass floor; `corpus_origin` declared per case. Rho walks
   have no upstream vendored corpus, so the honest origins are `randomized_postcondition`
   (draw x, set Q = xP, run, verify the witness end to end; draw x' ≠ x and assert FAIL)
   plus `author_supplied` pinned-seed transcripts. The postcondition arm is what keeps
   the skill's results above the `author_supplied` CONJECTURE cap (§2). Golden
   certificate and byte-equal double run via the selftest machinery, following the
   toy_curve registration shape.

7. Cost profile: production ≈ 1.25√n expected group operations with sd ≈ 0.5× mean, O(1)
   memory; verification component = the witness check (a few scalar multiplications).
   Tier 1 at 30–50 bits.

8. Conformance: register as a conforming subject in the §2 contract harness under
   `tests/conformance/` (the table-driven MUST clauses cairn-m0-e0s.16 built; toy_curve
   is the first conforming subject and the registration shape to copy).

DONE WHEN the skill recovers x on fresh instances with a verifiable witness; the
self-test emits a certificate and a byte-equal double run; the witness verifier accepts
the skill's witness and refuses the planted-negative forms; the conformance harness
lists the skill as a conforming subject.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_rho_dp.py (unit: walk determinism under a pinned seed, DP
predicate, witness field completeness); tests/unit/test_rho_witness_verifier.py (unit +
property: accepts a valid witness, rejects b ≡ d, rejects a wrong x, property over
random instances); tests/integration/test_rho_dp_selftest.py (integration: corpus run,
certificate, double run, conformance registration).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: running the skill twice on one corpus case yields byte-identical transcripts
  (settled in Python with length + sha256, never shell diff), and the self-test emits a
  certificate whose hash matches the recorded golden; exact commands and output pasted.
- Positive: for a fresh 40-bit instance, the witness verifier accepts the skill's witness
  and the recovered x passes the Tier-0 verifier (`xP == Q`).
- Positive: the ladder plan's baseline-revision field carries this bead's shipped
  `rho_dp` identity bundle rather than bead L1's seed, shown by the plan row before and

- Planted negative: a witness with b ≡ d (mod n) is refused with a typed reason; a witness
  whose x fails xP == Q is refused; a corpus case whose recorded output is altered by one
  byte fails the certificate check.
- No-Claim: green proves the skill computes and certifies discrete logs on toy corpus and
  postcondition instances; it proves nothing about ladder verdicts, nothing about the
  negation-map variant's √2 (control (j) owns that measurement), and nothing at sizes the
  corpus does not cover.
- Test types: unit, integration, property. Files: tests/unit/test_rho_dp.py,
  tests/unit/test_rho_witness_verifier.py, tests/integration/test_rho_dp_selftest.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and

cannot beat that is refuted on the spot. At 60 bits the table is 2³⁰ entries — the size
at which the memory cap binds (§6(2)). The floor figures live in the ladder plan as
thresholds; this skill is the executable that makes them measured facts on this machine
rather than arithmetic, and its declared memory profile is the model shape the ladder's
memory check reads. §6's two-threshold rationale: BSGS is the right floor (a method that
cannot beat a table lookup at 50 bits is not an advance) and the wrong acceptance bar (a
method at 4.9×10⁷ ops and 900 MB would "beat BSGS" while losing to plain rho on both
axes) — the acceptance bar belongs to rho (bead S1).

WHAT

1. `src/cairn/skills/bsgs.py`: deterministic baby-step giant-step DLP on prime-order toy
   curves. Deterministic end to end, so its replay grade is Replayable and it needs no
   witness.

2. Declared memory profile as part of the typed cost profile: table entries ≈ √n, bytes
   per entry stated and measured, growth shape declared. The skill reports its own table
   bytes in its output — a self-report the ladder treats as a diagnostic column only; the
   gate's own RSS measurement is the predicate (§6(2)).

3. §2 self-test: corpus with per-case ledger and committed floor; origins — a
   `randomized_postcondition` arm (draw x, set Q = xP, assert recovery) plus
   `author_supplied` pinned cases; golden certificate; byte-equal double run.

4. Cost profile: production ≈ 1.5√n group operations, memory ≈ √n table entries;
   verification component = a Tier-0/1 re-run under the §3 Replayable policy. Tier 1 at
   30–50 bits.

5. Conformance registration in `tests/conformance/` as for rho_dp.

6. The ladder plan's floor and cap fields become measured facts here. Measure the BSGS
   group-operation count and the table's memory footprint at the 30-, 40- and 50-bit
   rungs on this machine, and write them into the ladder plan's refutation-floor
   threshold and per-rung memory-cap fields (bead L1 authors those fields and seeds them
   with the §6(4) arithmetic), replacing the seeded values and recording the replacement.
   The 60-bit cap is 2³⁰ × the measured bytes per entry, recorded as an extrapolation
   from the measured per-entry figure rather than a run at 60 bits. Without this write
   the plan ships the arithmetic as a literal and no bead's close disagrees with it —
   the shape cairn-xpk records.

30–50 bits matches the declared profile; the self-test certificate and double run hold;
and the ladder plan's refutation-floor and memory-cap fields carry this bead's measured
figures rather than bead L1's seeded §6(4) arithmetic.

title: M1 skills: gmpy2 Hasse-interval BSGS as the second implementation axis for the toy-curve order (decision 1)
description:
CONTEXT (operator decision 1, PLAN §16; §2 axis rule). M0 ships PARI-only arithmetic
with the BSGS-vs-SEA algorithm-axis cross-check on the toy-curve order, valid through 50
bits. Decision 1 adds the implementation axis at M1: a gmpy2 Hasse-interval BSGS as a
second implementation for the toy-curve order. The §2 axis rule is why gmpy2: two builds
of one library are one implementation (`gp` and `cypari2` both wrap libpari), so the
second implementation must touch no libpari code anywhere on its path; gmpy2 wraps GMP.
Decision 1's phrase "from the session script" (research/KICKOFF-beads-and-M0.md:31,
research/convergence/r1/ledger-r1.md:100) names a council-session artifact absent from
this tree — no file under src/ or research/ carries gmpy2 code — so the phrase is
provenance and never a file to open; the algorithm is specified in full below.

WHAT

1. An order computation for toy curves by BSGS over the Hasse interval
   [p+1−2√p, p+1+2√p], using gmpy2 integers and its own elliptic-curve point arithmetic
   (short Weierstrass over F_p, affine or Jacobian — implementer's choice, libpari-free).
   Placement suggestion: `src/cairn/skills/order_bsgs_gmpy2.py`.

2. Wire it as toy_curve's implementation-axis cross-check: declared axis
   `implementation`, with a declared input range over which the axis is independent —
   the bit range where the Hasse-interval BSGS is affordable, MEASURED (time per curve
   at each size, ≥ 50 curves per size), never assumed. Outside the range the skill
   declares no cross-check and results cap accordingly (§2).

3. Disagreement handling per §2: on an order mismatch the run returns status DISAGREE
   (never OK, so never cached), writes both transcripts and digests to a substrate node,
   and the caller parks or refutes; a silent retry with a third tool is forbidden.

COST WARNING. `src/cairn/pari.py` and `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py` are members of
toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES: any edit bumps `implementation_revision` and reseeds the
transcript and certificate goldens (CLAUDE.md working note). Plan the wiring to minimize
edits to those files; when a golden reseeds, read the diff before committing it.

DEPENDENCY NOTE. `uv add gmpy2` — pyproject pins PyPI ([[tool.uv.index]]) because the
global uv config points at a corporate Artifactory that times out off-network; the pin
already covers this. gmpy2 exposes its version via importlib.metadata if needed, as
cypari2 does.

DONE WHEN the cross-check agrees with PARI's order on ≥ 50 random curves per size across
the declared range; a planted wrong order yields DISAGREE with both transcripts
recorded; the declared range carries its measurement.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_order_bsgs_gmpy2.py (unit + property: order recovery on
known curves, Hasse-interval bounds, libpari-free import graph);
tests/integration/test_toy_curve_cross_check.py (integration: agreement run, planted
DISAGREE, substrate node with both transcripts).

title: M1 skills: gate-owned instance-maker — nonce lifecycle, commit-ordered seed derivation, do_not_cache
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §6(1), §3 cache bits, §7 hunt). The ladder generates its own instances
from a gate-owned maker whose entropy the worker never sees before committing its
method. The counterexample hunt (§7) freezes its sampler under the same entropy rule, so
this derivation is shared machinery: the hunt bead consumes it. The documented exploit
class this exists against is overfitting a fixed instance an evaluator reuses.

WHAT — a gate-owned instance-maker (placement suggestion `src/cairn/instances.py`):

1. Nonce lifecycle: draw a fresh nonce at the start of each ladder run, AFTER the
   hypothesis object is recorded and never derived from it; never reuse a nonce across
   runs of the same hypothesis object — a rung re-run after INCONCLUSIVE sees fresh
   instances, because the first run's table published its seeds. A reuse attempt for the
   same object is refused.

2. Seed derivation: seed of trial i at size s is H(nonce ‖ hypothesis hash ‖ s ‖ i)
   under a canonical, typed, domain-separated encoding with its own domain tag and a
   known-answer test vector — the §3 key-construction rules, built on the existing
   `src/cairn/canon.py` / `src/cairn/keys.py` BLAKE3 machinery.

3. Instance generation: a fresh random prime-order curve and random (P, Q) per trial by
   calling the certified toy_curve skill with the derived seed.

4. Cache bits: the maker's interface declares its output non-memoizable, so its nodes
   carry `do_not_cache` and the cache's serve path refuses them (§3;
   `substrate.attempt_eligible` and `serve_sql` already read the bit).

5. Withholding: the nonce sits outside every worker allow-list until the run completes;
   nonce and seeds are then recorded in the result table so every trial replays.

6. The §2 self-test and golden certificate, as for the other two baseline skills —
   PLAN §13 M1 names rho_dp, bsgs AND the gate-owned instance-maker as each shipping
   it: a vendored known-answer corpus with a per-case ledger (`pass |
   intentional_non_goal | known_gap`), a committed pass floor, a declared
   `corpus_origin` per case (the derivation vectors of (2) are a
   `randomized_postcondition` arm — draw a nonce, derive, re-derive, assert equality
   and assert a flipped input diverges — plus `author_supplied` pinned vectors), a
   certificate hashing the canonical transcript, and a byte-equal double run through
   src/cairn/selftest.py. The maker is a launched revision like any other and
   src/cairn/tiergate.py refuses an UNCERTIFIED revision whatever ticket it holds
   (bead B6), so a maker with no recorded certificate cannot start a ladder run at
   all. Register it under tests/conformance/ as a conforming subject the way beads S1
   and S2 register theirs.

7. A declared cost profile with production and verification components, in the typed
   interface, as §5 requires of every skill the tier gate reads.

DONE WHEN the same (nonce, hypothesis hash, s, i) reproduce the same instance
byte-for-byte; different nonces give different instances; the derivation matches its
known-answer vector; the maker's substrate writes carry do_not_cache and are refused by
the serve path; the self-test emits a certificate matching its golden and a
byte-equal double run, and the maker appears as a conforming subject.

RELATED PLANTED CLASS (owned elsewhere): a worker-supplied instance list is the
planted-failure fixture the ladder's own self-test must FAIL — the ladder self-test bead
plants it; this bead's negatives are the reuse refusal and the vector mismatch.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_instance_maker.py (unit: derivation known-answer vector,
determinism, nonce-reuse refusal); tests/integration/test_instance_maker_substrate.py
(integration: do_not_cache on the node, serve path refuses, nonce withheld until
completion then present in the table); tests/integration/test_instance_maker_selftest.py
(integration: corpus run, certificate against the golden, byte-equal double run,
conformance registration).
acceptance_criteria:

- Positive: a maker node in the substrate carries do_not_cache and the cache serve path

title: M1 skills: decisions 2 and 12 — compiled-baseline funding decision and the clock-tolerance reference rate, measured and recorded
description:
CONTEXT (operator decisions 2 and 12, PLAN §16; §6(3)). Two M1-bound operator decisions
are measurements on this machine, and both feed the ladder plan.

Decision 2: a compiled rho/BSGS baseline is funded only if the interpreted 60-bit rung
cannot finish inside the Tier-1 budget. The input is the measured 60-bit rho row that
cairn-m0-e0s.15 recorded (one 60-bit rho with cypari2; §6's prior: ≈ 1.3×10⁹ group ops,
minutes compiled, a quarter hour interpreted).

Decision 12: the fastest arithmetic implementation for the clock-tolerance check is
measured — gmpy2 vs cypari2 vs a C reference — and recorded in the gate bundle. §6(3)
consumes it: the clock check bounds uncounted arithmetic only while no arithmetic a
method can carry is faster per operation than the gate's counted object, so the plan
validation requires clock-tolerance × ratio < the KEEP band's excess over 1 (2·radius),
where ratio is the counted object's per-operation COST over the per-operation COST of
the fastest implementation measured here — a cost over a cost, equal to 1 when the two
are equally fast and above 1 when the counted object is slower, never a cost divided by
a rate. Bead L4 computes and records the ratio once the counted object exists; bead L1
validates the bound at plan load. This bead produces the fastest measured per-operation
COST that the ratio's denominator reads. The bundle field is named and stored as a
per-operation cost in SECONDS PER GROUP OPERATION, never as a throughput in operations
per second: the two are reciprocals, and beads L1 and L4 divide by this field directly,
so a throughput stored here silently inverts the bound the plan validates.

WHAT

1. Decision 2 record: read cairn-m0-e0s.15's close evidence; state the comparison basis
   explicitly (the 60-bit rung is m = 10 hold-out completion trials, §6(2b), so the
   comparison is 10 × the measured per-trial cost against the Tier-1 ceiling the gate
   bundle's boundary table carries — `max_core_s` for tier 1 in bundle/tiers.json, 3600
   core seconds as shipped — which is readable at this close, while the ladder plan's own
   per-rung budget field is bead L1's and is not read here); record the funding decision
   with the numbers. The 60-bit rung
   is one of two inputs: §6(2) also prices the ≤ 50-bit rungs at the sized trial count
   across three arms (an interpreted 50-bit baseline at that count runs for hours, a
   compiled one for minutes), which is the larger figure and the one bead L7 measures
   and records. The funding trigger covers both rungs; L7 is blocked on bead L4 and
   L4 is blocked on this bead, so L7's number is always absent at this close: the record
   names the 60-bit half and says which half it stands on, and bead L7 completes it with
   the ≤ 50-bit half at L7's own close. If either rung cannot finish inside the
   budget, open the compiled-baseline follow-up bead at close — do not fold that work
   into this bead.

2. Decision 12 measurement: a micro-benchmark of per-group-operation cost (point add,
   double) for gmpy2, cypari2, and a small C reference on the build machine, with trial
   count and spread recorded; write the fastest per-operation COST (seconds per group
   operation) and the full comparison into the gate bundle as the field the ladder plan
   validation reads, and the raw run into
   research/grounding/ with its tag.

DONE WHEN both records exist — the decision with its inputs and basis, the per-operation
cost with its spread — and the bundle field is readable by the plan-validation path.

NO-CLAIM SCOPE NOTE: rates measured here are facts about this build machine at this
date. The ladder re-measures per-rung reference rates on its own instances at run time
(§6(3)); this bead sets the plan-load bound only.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_clock_reference_rate.py (unit: the bundle field exists, has
the declared shape, and carries its per-arm spread; an absent or malformed field fails).
The sanity bound that the fastest measured per-operation cost is at MOST the counted
object's own per-operation cost — the inequality that makes the recorded ratio ≥ 1 — is
NOT assertable in this bead: the counted object is bead L4's and L4 is blocked
on this bead, so no counted-object rate exists at this close. L4 asserts it where it
records the ratio.

- Positive: the decision-2 record exists with the m0 row's numbers, the rung budget, and

- Positive: the decision-12 benchmark ran on this machine with ≥ 10³ operations per

  and raw output pasted, grounding file path cited.

- No-Claim: the recorded per-operation costs are build-machine facts at measurement time; they promote

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
Carried forward from cairn-m0-e0s.11 (commit 4a4bb69), re-homed here because it
was first written into cairn-m0-e0s.14's comments and that bead has since closed.
This bead builds the planted fixture corpus and exercises the tier gate, so it is
the one that will make the branch below reachable.

The gate plan's two tier-gate steps use a fixture skill_identity_hash that no
substrate certifies. tiergate.predicate_reasons adds UNCERTIFIED whenever
sub.certified(identity) is false, so both fixture launches always collect at least
one reason and the gate never admits them.

Two consequences.

The tier gate collects every applicable reason rather than short-circuiting, so a
planted reason arrives alongside UNCERTIFIED. The gate plan's steps check
membership (tier-two-above in reasons, ticket-absent in reasons), never equality.
A step or fixture written against the whole reason tuple breaks the first time an
unrelated predicate fires.

gateplan._run_waiver's ticket-present branch is defensive and unreachable today: it
fires only if the gate mints a ticket for the waiver hypothesis, which requires an
admission, which UNCERTIFIED prevents. It is asserted by no test, and that is
stated rather than papered over. A planted corpus that certifies a fixture identity
makes that branch live, and it needs a test before it is trusted.

Pinned by tests/integration/test_gateplan.py::test_a_recorded_waiver_hypothesis_removes_ticket_absent_and_fails_the_waiver_step,
which reaches the neighboring branch by pre-recording the hypothesis object.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
FROM cairn-m0-e0s.15: two refusal branches this bead's fixture corpus can reach.

`rho60_report` in `src/cairn/measure.py` raises BACKEND on three conditions. One is
covered by a real test: a 40-bit walk stopped by `--cap-minutes` before it solves,
reachable with no fault injection at all (`cairn measure rho60 --cap-minutes 0.0001`
exits 4 naming the op count).

The other two have no user-reachable trigger at fixed bits and no test:

  - the Tier-0 verifier refuses the 40-bit x that the walk recovered
  - the 60-bit instance's order differs from the recorded RHO60_ORDER

Reaching either needs a planted subject rather than a mock, which is what this bead
builds. A planted instance whose recorded order disagrees with its curve, and a
planted verifier subject that refuses a correct x, would each land on one of them.

Recorded rather than left silent: the M0 close states plainly that these two carry no
test, so a later reader does not mistake the green suite for coverage of them.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
MOVED HERE FROM cairn-fur, which does not own it: a planted subject the skill-contract
harness has no fixture for.

cairn-oij (commit 58a1438) gave S2-12 an in-range arm that plants the declared seam and
requires the reported cross-check result to move. Three subject shapes now have a real
fixture: one that cross-checks (toy_curve, PASS), one that hardcodes its in-range result
(nonconforming, FAIL), and one whose axis is not in the allowed set (witness, FAIL at the
first arm).

A fourth shape has none: a subject that DECLARES a seam and never calls it on the
in-range path. The arm would report the constant-result FAIL for it, because a result
that does not move is a result that does not move regardless of why. That is the
intended verdict, but it is inference from reading the code rather than a measurement,
and it is the shape closest to a real mistake -- a skill whose cross-check is wired to
the wrong call site looks conforming everywhere else.

It belongs on this bead because this bead builds the planted fixture corpus, and that is
exactly what settling it needs: take the nonconforming fixture, give it a real comparison
against a seam it declares but does not use on the in-range path, and assert S2-12 FAILs
with the constant-result reason rather than the no-seam one. The distinction between
those two reasons is what a reader of the matrix would act on.

Recorded on cairn-fur first, under a framing of that bead as owning "the harness's
pattern surface" that was too wide. It would have been lost when cairn-fur closed.

title: M1 corpus: the tests/planted/ harness — planting registry, cold-cache enforcement, escape counting, the epic rollup
description:
CONTEXT (the M1 epic's done-when). The corpus is the measurement of false accepts AND
the must-PASS controls that keep a gate that rejects everything from passing the bar:
≥ 30 plantings, every fixture caught under a cold cache (skip_cache_lookup),
INCONCLUSIVE counting as an escape, no matched true advance rejected, ≥ 4 positive
controls PASS. No fixture may be satisfied by a mock standing in for the gate it tests
(tests/unit/test_no_mocks_in_integration.py is the existing no-mock discipline).

WHAT — the tests/planted/ harness the fixture-family beads (C2–C7) plug into:

1. Layout and registry: one test id per planted artifact, its family being the fixture
   letter (a)–(m), the tier-gate/escrow/yank/ladder-execution item or the canary it
   belongs to; each entry is registered with that family, its expected verdict class
   (must-FAIL / must-PASS), its EXPECTED VERDICT — the exact outcome the gate must
   produce — and its owning behavior bead. The class
   alone is not enough: a control's correct outcome can be the very verdict the escape
   rule reads as an escape (control (k)'s is INCONCLUSIVE), and a control that returns
   KEEP is the ladder minting a false advance from its own null arm. Entries are per planted artifact, never per fixture letter — a letter with two planted Solutions registers two entries, a control with three arms registers three — so the ≥ 30 and ≥ 4 bars are computed at planting grain and carry the margin the finer count gives them; the EXPECTED VERDICT field forces that grain, since a letter whose arms expect different outcomes (control (l)'s PROVEN and its two below-PROVEN arms) has no single expected verdict to register. The registry is data a test reads, so the counts below are computed, not
   asserted by hand.

2. The epic-level rollup test: total plantings ≥ 30; positive controls ≥ 4; zero
   escapes (a must-FAIL fixture whose run lands INCONCLUSIVE or passes IS the escape);
   zero controls whose observed verdict differs from the registered expected verdict, so
   control (k) returning KEEP or REJECT fails the rollup rather than counting as a
   control that was not rejected. This is the single test whose green means the
   epic's done-when bar, and it fails loudly listing every escape by fixture id.

3. Cold-cache enforcement: every fixture run sets skip_cache_lookup and the harness
   asserts the attempt was fresh (not served), so a cached pass can never satisfy a
   planting.

4. No-mock discipline extended to tests/planted/. The existing check is a
   text-pattern scan and not an AST parse: `scan_for_mocks` matches `MOCK_PATTERNS`
   (`unittest.mock`, `MagicMock`, `mocker.patch`) as substrings over `SCANNED_DIRS`
   (tests/_checks.py:3-4), which names tests/integration, tests/e2e and
   tests/conformance and not tests/planted — so extending it is an edit to that file,
   and tests/unit/test_no_mocks_in_integration.py:7,11 is the caller.

DONE WHEN the harness runs with the registry populated by this bead's own harness-owned
self-check family — one must-FAIL entry, one must-PASS control entry whose registered
expected verdict is INCONCLUSIVE (control (k)'s shape), and one deliberately
mis-registered entry (must-FAIL marked must-PASS) — the rollup math is computed from the
registry, and the mis-registered entry is caught by the rollup as an escape. The
self-check family registers under its own `self_check` family name and the rollup's
corpus counts — the ≥ 30 plantings and the ≥ 4 positive controls — exclude it by that
name, so the harness's own entries can never stand in for a corpus fixture. Beads C2-C7
carry the real families and register them into this same rollup as they land; every one
of them is blocked by this bead, so none of their entries exists at this close, and the
self-check family is what keeps the rollup's own mechanics observable here. Bead C8's
carried-forward planted subjects belong to none of the families this registry enumerates
and register none, so they never count toward the ≥ 30 plantings or the ≥ 4 controls;
they sit under the same harness and share its no-mock discipline and nothing else.

TEST PLAN — tests/planted/conftest.py, tests/planted/test_corpus_rollup.py (the rollup
+ registry mechanics; the corpus family files arrive with C2–C7, and C8's
carried-forward subject files sit beside them registering no family).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: the rollup computes plantings, controls, and escapes from the registry, and
  the harness's own self-check family reports through it; run pasted.
- Planted negative: a fixture registered must-FAIL whose gate run passes is listed as an
  escape by id; a control whose observed verdict differs from its registered expected
  verdict is listed by id (shown on the self-check control entry, registered
  expected-verdict INCONCLUSIVE and driven to KEEP — control (k)'s own entry is bead
  C2's); a fixture run that was served from cache fails the cold-cache assertion;
  a mock introduced under tests/planted/ is caught by the no-mock check.
- Planted negative: a `self_check` entry counted toward the ≥ 30 plantings or the ≥ 4
  positive controls fails a test — the exclusion is asserted, not assumed.
- No-Claim: the harness measures the corpus; its own `self_check` family exercises the
  rollup's mechanics and is no corpus planting — with C2-C8 absent the corpus count is
  zero and the rollup reports the shortfall by name, never a vacuous green. The ≥ 30 and
  ≥ 4 bars are gated on a registry `corpus_complete` flag that bead C7's close flips (a
  strict xfail keyed on the same flag is the other shape), because `pyproject.toml` sets
  `testpaths = ["tests"]` and scripts/check.sh:70 runs `pytest` over it while the hook's
  `--fast` path skips tests (scripts/check.sh:61-62): an unconditionally failing rollup
  is green on every hook and red in CI from this close until C7's.
- Test types: integration harness. Files: tests/planted/conftest.py,
  tests/planted/test_corpus_rollup.py, tests/_checks.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

1. a synthetic KEEP_IN_SAMPLE table admits the 60-bit rung of its own hypothesis key
   and is refused for every other Tier-2 launch (bead B5);
2. a KEEP table is refused for a launch whose hypothesis key, method identity or
   implementation revision differs from the table's (bead B5);
3. a launch of a yanked revision, and of an uncertified revision, is refused whatever
   ticket it holds (bead B6);
4. a launch declaring Tier 1 for a production cost the boundary table assigns Tier 2 is
   refused (bead B6);
5. a claim carrying both a cost model and a correctness conjecture is refused Tier 2
   while either its KEEP table or its SURVIVED record is absent (bead B5);
6. a Tier-3 request holding KEEP and no Tier-2 node is refused (bead B5);
7. a branch on the Tier-1 ticket whose worker launches would carry its hypothesis key's
   charge past the Tier-1 cumulative edge is refused at the crossing launch while a
   second ladder run on the same key is admitted (bead B7);
8. a claim whose hypothesis object names the target family with a cost model below the
   generic bound is routed to the router's top class and holds no Tier-3 ticket without
   the §10 sign-off (bead R2).

ALSO, the carried-forward waiver branch, asserted by no test. gateplan._run_waiver
reaches its ticket-present branch (src/cairn/gateplan.py:409-410) only when the tier
gate's decision carries TICKET_ABSENT AND a `tickets` row already exists for the waiver
hypothesis key. Certification is irrelevant to it: gateplan.py:407 branches on
TICKET_ABSENT alone, and under the M0 gate the two preconditions exclude each other —
TICKET_ABSENT fires exactly when no hypothesis object is recorded for the key
(tiergate.predicate_reasons), while TierGate._mint writes a ticket row only when one IS
recorded, and hypothesis_objects is append-only so a recorded object never goes away.
So certifying a fixture identity does not reach the branch, and the planting has to
produce the pair itself: either a directly seeded `tickets` row for a key whose
hypothesis object is absent, or an M1 state under bead B5's lattice in which a key
already carrying a minted ticket is still refused TICKET_ABSENT (B5 adds the §8
presence check and the §7 pre-filters to the Tier-1 ticket, so that state is expected
to exist — confirm it against B5's implemented lattice, and seed the row where it does
not). Membership-not-equality discipline applies to every reason assertion (the gate
collects all applicable reasons).

exercised, cold, no mock.
