description:
CONTEXT (M1 epic done-when, the dispatch canary planting). The canary mechanism is bead
W4's; this is its corpus entry, so the epic's rollup counts the canary alongside the
plantings and an escaped token fails the epic like any other escape.

WHAT

1. The corpus planting: run the canary's four-token check (project instruction file,
   user instruction file, a skill file, working-tree status) through the harness with
   the registry entry written in C1's two fields rather than a third class value —
   class must-FAIL, EXPECTED VERDICT `no ambient token observed` — so a run in which any
   of the four tokens reaches the worker is what the rollup lists.

2. The positive control alongside: a token handed inside a substrate node IS observed,
   registered must-PASS, proving the detector sees.

3. The grounding-record assertion: the planting requires the record naming which
   decision form ran (request bytes vs echoed context) and the SDK/toolchain versions
   it grounded, and fails if the record is stale against the installed versions — the
   corpus is where "re-run on every toolchain or SDK change" becomes a standing check
   rather than a promise.

classes and the staleness check live; and, this being the last family bead C1's rollup
waits on — beads C2-C6 (cairn-m1-cqt.3.2 through cairn-m1-cqt.3.6) block this bead,
so the flag cannot flip before their families have registered — C1's `corpus_complete`

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.9 (skill runner), two behaviors this bead owns that M0 leaves as
schema only.

Escrow has no settlement path. substrate.add_escrow inserts a row and nothing sets
spent_at or released_at; the escrow table carries no append-only trigger, unlike
almost every other table, so a raw UPDATE is legal but there is no API for it. The
M0 runner writes the reservation at launch with both columns NULL, which matches
PLAN section 13 lines 1391-1396 (M0 asserts only that the schema admits these).
PLAN section 5 lines 551-570 defines the behavior: reserve the verification
component at launch, refuse a launch the remaining budget cannot cover, spend where
section 3's first check runs, release unspent only where the attempt ended with
status other than OK or the node was disowned.

The pre-launch half of that is already built: runner.launch raises BudgetRefused
when budget_remaining cannot cover the ceiling (PLAN section 5 line 573, the meet
rule). Spend and release are not.

SKILL_YANKED has no producer. The status is in substrate.STATUSES and in the
attempts CHECK constraint, and PLAN section 2 lines 84-86 say an in-flight attempt
completes with it, but nothing sets it. The M0 runner does not consult
substrate.yanked() before launching, on the grounds that the tier gate
(cairn-m0-e0s.10) owns pre-launch refusal; the in-flight case, where a yank lands
while a child is running, has no owner at all.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
From cairn-m0-e0s.14's flywheel pass (commit 044a5d9). Recorded here because this
bead enforces the budget ceiling over the process tree, so it is the bead that will
work on runner.py's signalling.

runner._signal_group (src/cairn/runner.py:149) falls back to signalling the pid
directly when signalling the process group raises. That fallback is not covered:
replacing its whole body with `pass` leaves all 72 tests in
tests/integration/test_runner.py and tests/unit/test_runner_fuzz.py green.

  scripts/mutation-check.sh src/cairn/runner.py '<fallback body>' 'pass' \
    tests/integration/test_runner.py tests/unit/test_runner_fuzz.py
  -> SURVIVED  72 passed

The ceiling path depends on it: spawn_and_wait signals the group at SIGTERM on
timeout, again at SIGKILL after the grace window, once more in the `finally` when
the child was never reaped, and a final group sweep after reaping to collect
grandchildren the skill forked. Every one of those calls goes through the
unexercised fallback if killpg raises.

Two notes for whoever writes that test. The construct on line 152 is
`except ProcessLookupError, PermissionError:`, which is a valid unparenthesized
except group under PEP 758 and catches both on Python 3.14 — verified on this
interpreter, and two separate survey agents have now misread it as a Python 2
syntax error, one calling it fatal. Do not "fix" it.

The final group sweep at src/cairn/runner.py:230 runs after the child is reaped, so
it targets a pgid whose leader has exited. That is deliberate for orphaned
grandchildren, but a test should pin the intent, since a reused pgid would be
signalled by it.

title: M1 tiers: escrow settlement — spend at the §3 policy's first check, release on status ≠ OK or disown, survive terminal branches
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §5, §3; cairn-m0-e0s.9's schema handoff). Escrow has no settlement path:
`substrate.add_escrow` inserts a row and nothing sets spent_at or released_at; the
escrow table carries no append-only trigger (deliberate — settlement mutates it), and
there is no API for settlement. The pre-launch half is built: runner.launch raises
BudgetRefused when budget_remaining cannot cover the ceiling (the §5 meet rule).

WHAT — the reserve/spend/release lifecycle:

1. Reserve at launch (exists): the verification component of the declared cost profile,
   bound to the NODE, never the branch.

2. Spend: where the §3 re-run policy's first check runs — a witness checked at
   admission, a Tier-0/1 re-run, a Tier-2/3 re-run at `justify` time or on the
   foundations auditor's first draw (the last two routinely after the attempt, and
   sometimes after its branch, reached a terminal status). Wired against bead R5's
   policy, which defines those check events.

3. Release unspent: only where the attempt ended with status ≠ OK or the node was
   disowned. A branch reaching a terminal status returns its unreserved grant and never
   the escrow of an admissible node it produced — a withdrawn branch's Tier-2 node stays
   re-runnable when `justify` waits on it months later.

4. Refusal (exists, keep true): a launch whose verification component the remaining
   budget cannot cover is refused.

5. Settlement API design constraint: the table admits UPDATE today because settlement
   needs it; give settlement a single API chokepoint (spend/release functions that
   refuse double-settlement and record the check event that spent it), so a raw UPDATE
   anywhere else stays a defect greppable by the code-search gates.

DONE WHEN the four M1 escrow fixtures' behaviors hold: refusal on uncoverable
verification; spend at the policy's first check; release on status ≠ OK and on disown;
a Tier-2/3-grade node with a deferred check keeps its reservation after its attempt and
its branch reach terminal status. (The corpus bead C6 plants them as tests/planted/
fixtures; this bead builds the behavior and its own integration tests.)

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_escrow_lifecycle.py (unit: state machine,
double-settlement refusal); tests/integration/test_escrow_settlement.py (integration:
spend on witness check, release on FAIL and on disown, survival past terminal branch).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a launch reserves; the §3 policy's first check spends (spent_at set, the
  check event recorded); an attempt ending FAIL releases unspent; a disowned node's
  reservation releases; a deferred-check Tier-2 node's reservation survives its branch's
  terminal status; each shown with the row before and after.
- Planted negative: a second spend of one reservation is refused; a launch whose
  verification component exceeds remaining budget is refused (BudgetRefused), asserted
  live; a release attempted on a status-OK, non-disowned node is refused.
- No-Claim: the lifecycle proves escrow accounting; it does not fund or perform the
  deferred re-runs themselves (bead R5 and, at M4, the auditor own those), and the
  standing per-cycle audit line is out of M1 scope.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_escrow_lifecycle.py,
  tests/integration/test_escrow_settlement.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

DECISION — the lifecycle in one chokepoint plus one trigger. src/cairn/escrow.py (new, 137 lines): `spend` (66-81) and `release` (92-113) are the only writers; each UPDATE is guarded by `spent_at IS NULL AND released_at IS NULL` and raises AlreadySettled on rowcount 0. `first_check` (116-125) is the §3 policy's hook: it spends on the first check and is a logged no-op on every later one. `release_reason` (84-89) is the whole release rule: "disowned" when disowned_at is set, "status:<S>" for any status other than RUNNING or OK, None otherwise; `release` refuses (ReleaseRefused, 100-103) when the reason is None. `settle_on_close` (128-131) and `settle_on_disown` (134-137) are the two callers. The escrow row records who settled it: schema.sql:109-122 adds spent_by and released_by with CHECKs pairing each stamp with its actor and forbidding both stamps at once; the `escrow_settle_once` trigger (schema.sql:507-520) admits exactly one UPDATE per row, unsettled → spent or unsettled → released, with every other column unchanged, and `escrow_no_delete` (521) closes the other door. substrate.add_escrow (substrate.py:700-727) carries the two new columns. Wiring: repro.record_rerun spends the first attempt's reservation on the second_attempt_agree record (repro.py:144); repro.record_witness_check (158-166, new) writes the WITNESS_CHECK repro record and spends; runner closes settle on the way out at runner.py:298 (startup_scan → INTERRUPTED), 440 (a launch's close) and 468 (the aborted-launch FAIL). title: M1 tiers: yank reach as a recipe-key predicate, disowned propagation, salt bump — gate-written on a gate verdict, reach ruling human-only (decision 5)
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §2, §3; decision 5). M0 laid the columns — yank_records, salts, the
disowned mark and substrate.disown exist (src/cairn/schema.sql, src/cairn/substrate.py)
— and M1 is the first milestone that yanks a revision and salts a class.

AUTHORITY SPLITS, and reading decision 5 as "every yank is human-only" contradicts three
other beads. PLAN §2 has a self-test failure yank the implementation revision with no
human step; §6(2c) has an `xP ≠ Q` or count-divergence REJECT yank the revision the
dispatch record names, which is bead L11's wiring and this bead's dependent; §13 M1's
fixture (b) drives that REJECT under a cold cache, where no human exists to attest
anything; and §10's autonomy envelope lets the harness ladder and refute unattended.
What §4's human-path list enumerates beside a waiver is the yank-REACH ruling, not the
yank. So a yank a gate's own verdict produces is written by that gate and carries no
attestation record, while decision 5's human-only authority binds the discretionary
half — the reach ruling that narrows the default, a yank no gate verdict produced, and a
salt issued without one. Bead H4 pins the authority on that half; this bead builds the
record, the reach predicate and the propagation.

WHAT

1. The yank record names the fault's reach as a predicate over recipe-key fields — by
   default the whole implementation revision, every recipe key naming it; a narrower
   predicate (an input range where the fault is input-dependent, a parameter slice) is
   installed only by an attributed human ruling recorded through the human path beside
   the yank, which workers and the orchestrator may propose and never install.

2. Disowned propagation: every attempt inside the reach gains the append-only `disowned`
   mark — rows and blobs stay, nothing is overwritten — and a disowned node is served
   from no cache (substrate.attempt_eligible / serve_sql already read the mark), is
   absent to `justify` — which re-derives every claim transitively justified by it — and
   is no ticket.

3. Salt bump: the class's `salt` is bumped so fresh attempts take fresh keys; attempts
   outside the named reach stand.

4. Clearing: only an attributed new revision with a fresh certificate clears the yank

title: M1 tiers: SKILL_YANKED lands on an in-flight attempt
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §2; cairn-m0-e0s.9's handoff). SKILL_YANKED has no producer: the status is
in substrate.STATUSES and the attempts CHECK constraint, and PLAN §2 says an in-flight
attempt completes with it, but nothing sets it. The M0 runner does not consult
substrate.yanked() before launching — the tier gate owns pre-launch refusal — and the
in-flight case, where a yank lands while a child is running, has no owner.

WHAT

1. The in-flight path: when a yank lands whose reach covers a running attempt's recipe
   key, that attempt completes with status SKILL_YANKED (≠ OK: never cached, never a
   ticket, never evidence). The mechanics live in src/cairn/runner.py beside the ceiling
   enforcement — the natural shape is a check the runner's wait loop performs against
   the yank records, followed by the existing group-terminate machinery; the exact
   polling point is the implementer's, but the status must be SKILL_YANKED, not
   BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and the receipt must still be written.

2. The harness-terminated trio stays coherent: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, SKILL_YANKED and
   INTERRUPTED are all ≠ OK, none is a leak, and the branch stays active for the next
   tick (§4 terminal-status invariant). This bead's tests pin SKILL_YANKED into the same
   assertions the existing runner-status tests give the other two
   (tests/unit/test_runner_status.py is the shape).

DONE WHEN a yank landing mid-run completes the attempt as SKILL_YANKED with a receipt,
the attempt is never cached and mints no ticket, and a yank landing after completion
changes nothing about the finished attempt (disown handles history, bead B2).

TEST PLAN — tests/integration/test_skill_yanked_inflight.py (integration: a long-running
child, a yank recorded mid-flight, SKILL_YANKED status + receipt; the after-completion
non-effect); tests/unit/test_runner_status.py (extended: SKILL_YANKED in the status
table).


## Architecture
- Approach: Poll the existing covering-yank records while waiting for the real child,
  latch SKILL_YANKED, and use the existing TERM/grace/KILL process-group path. Persist
  the measured receipt and recheck coverage inside the final close transaction to
  order a near-completion yank against status publication. Yank propagation owns
  escrow release for SKILL_YANKED; the runner does not compete with it. A new queue
  callback API is unnecessary because the substrate already supports one writer per
  process and SQLite serializes their write transactions.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/runner.py (spawn_and_wait and launch),
  tests/integration/test_runner_clock.py, tests/integration/test_escrow_settlement.py.
- Touches: src/cairn/runner.py, src/cairn/yank.py, src/cairn/substrate.py; escrow.py
  only if the real probe requires it; tests/integration/test_skill_yanked_inflight.py,
  tests/unit/test_runner_status.py, tests/fixtures/skills/yank_target.py;
  research/grounding/dbos-sqlite-and-agent-sdk-isolation.md.
- ADRs: PLAN.md sections 2 and 5; settlement ownership in grounding section D.
- Data model impact: none; existing statuses, receipt fields and settlement trigger.
- Failure modes: covering yank overlooked (real child test status); close racing a
  committed yank (transactional close test); escrow updated twice (real SQLite update
  counter and strict trigger); non-covering or post-completion yank changes status
  (positive controls preserve OK).

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] yank.record disowns a running attempt and releases escrow once; a subsequent
  SKILL_YANKED close callback is a no-op, and a forced second UPDATE is refused.
  Source: research/grounding/dbos-sqlite-and-agent-sdk-isolation.md section D,
  SQLite 3.50.4 live probe (verified: 2026-09-08) (Confidence: HIGH).
- [R2] spawn_and_wait owns wait4 polling and group termination; launch writes the
  receipt after normal return, whereas its exception path has no receipt.
  Source: src/cairn/runner.py, real process timeout probe (verified: 2026-09-08)
  (Confidence: HIGH).
- [R3] Substrate.open uses Python sqlite3's thread-affine connections, WAL and
  BEGIN IMMEDIATE for writes; its writer registry is process-local.
  Source: src/cairn/substrate.py:204-253 and cross-thread probe
  (verified: 2026-09-08) (Confidence: HIGH).
- Delegability: STATEABLE.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a real child process running when a covering yank is recorded completes with
  status SKILL_YANKED and a written receipt; the attempt row and receipt pasted.
- Planted negative: the SKILL_YANKED attempt is refused by the cache serve path and by
  ticket selection; a yank recorded after the attempt finished OK leaves its status OK
  (history is disown's job, not a status rewrite).
- No-Claim: the in-flight completion proves the runner honors a live yank; it proves
  nothing about reach semantics (bead B2) or launch refusal (bead B6).
- Test types: integration, unit. Files: tests/integration/test_skill_yanked_inflight.py,
  tests/unit/test_runner_status.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

The ordered sequence yank.record -> close_attempt(SKILL_YANKED) ->
escrow.settle_on_close exits 0 with one escrow update, released_by=disowned,
and an unchanged reservation after the close callback. A forced second UPDATE is
refused by escrow_settle_once. The sequential double-settlement claim does not

The observed implementation gap is different: both real covering-yank child cases
end as BLOCKED rather than SKILL_YANKED on baseline 524e25a. Command:
uv run --no-sync pytest -q tests/integration/test_skill_yanked_inflight.py -k covering

call a competing settlement path. The real integration deliberately pauses the
control process at its first escrow SELECT after the disown transaction commits.
The runner closes, signals an event, and propagation resumes. A SQLite AFTER UPDATE
trigger records the issuing connection as well as the attempt. Exactly one release
must come from yank-controller. This SQL trace/event barrier is the declared timing
fault-injection seam; all subprocesses, storage, disown and settlement calls remain real.

157 passed in 5.96s; mutation checker exits 0 and restores source byte-identically.
The final-close, ignored-poll and status-precedence mutations are also caught.
The ordinary surrounding suite passes: 237 tests in 11.21s. Fast gates pass.

title: M1 tiers: ceiling multiplier re-set from measured distributions; the unexercised signal fallback gets its killing test
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §5; cairn-x72; the mutation gap on cairn-m1-cqt.4's comments). The budget
ceiling is enforced: cairn-x72 split it into the CPU-clock verdict (BUDGET_EXCEEDED) and
a generous wall cap (BLOCKED). Two residues belong to M1.

WHAT

1. The multiplier re-set. The ceiling multiplier is a gate-bundle field at the M0
   default 4× with tag CONJECTURE (§5's arithmetic: with rho's sd ≈ 0.5× mean, a 2×
   ceiling aborts ≈ 4 % of honest trials, a 4× ceiling well under 0.1 %). M1 re-sets it
   from the baseline skills' MEASURED cost distributions (beads S1/S2's corpus and the
   sizing runs of L7 produce the samples): compute the honest-abort rate the measured
   spread implies per candidate multiplier, pick the smallest that keeps honest aborts
   under the 0.1 % bar, record the value, the samples and the arithmetic in the bundle
   and the close comment. If the measurement supports keeping 4×, keeping it IS the
   re-set — record it as measured, tag upgraded from CONJECTURE.

2. The unexercised kill fallback. runner._signal_group (src/cairn/runner.py:152) falls
   back to signalling the pid directly when signalling the process group raises;
   replacing the fallback body with `pass` leaves green all 72 tests that
   tests/integration/test_runner.py and tests/unit/test_runner_fuzz.py collect
   (SURVIVED, recorded on the parent bead with those two files as the
   scripts/mutation-check.sh targets). That pair is the whole of the run's scope and is
   not the runner surface: tests/unit/test_runner_status.py was not passed to it and
   tests/integration/test_runner_clock.py arrived later with cairn-x72, and the four
   files collect 176 together — so the verdict stands against 72 named tests and the
   comparison run needs the same two targets. Every ceiling kill path routes through it
   (src/cairn/runner.py:216, :218, :223, :225). A
   test must make that mutant die: force killpg to raise (a child that changes its own
   process group is the no-mock route) and assert the pid-direct fallback still
   terminates and accounts the attempt. Two traps recorded on the parent bead, kept
   here: `except ProcessLookupError, PermissionError:` at runner.py:155 is a valid PEP
   758 unparenthesized except group on Python 3.14 — leave it exactly as written; and
   the final group sweep at runner.py:225 targets a pgid whose leader
   has exited — deliberate for orphaned grandchildren — and wants an intent-pinning
   test, since a reused pgid would be signalled.

DONE WHEN the multiplier is a measured value with its derivation recorded; the
_signal_group fallback mutant is killed by a live test; the pgid-sweep intent is pinned.

title: M1 tiers: the ticket lattice — gate-selected per-kind tickets, most-recent-admissible with displacement, KEEP_IN_SAMPLE scoping, key/method/revision binding
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §5 tier-gate predicate; gap A of the epic's decomposition comment). The
M0 tier gate (src/cairn/tiergate.py) collects reasons — PROFILE_UNDECLARED,
TICKET_ABSENT, TIER_TWO_ABOVE, BOUNDARY_TABLE, UNCERTIFIED, YANKED, BUDGET,
TICKET_BUNDLE_MISMATCH — and M0's tickets table is empty in every real run. M1 makes
the ticket lattice total: a gate-selected named node per tier and claim kind, which the
launching party never supplies.

WHAT

1. Ticket selection: the most recent admissible substrate node of the required kind
   (status OK, replay grade ≥ Verifiable, reproducibility-checked under the §3 policy)
   produced at the tier below for the SAME hypothesis key and method identity (or
   statement hash), where "most recent" ranges over every node of that kind whatever its
   verdict — a later REJECT or INCONCLUSIVE ladder table displaces an older KEEP — and
   the verdict rule is applied to the node so selected.

2. The lattice, total over tiers and claim kinds: Tier 0 needs no ticket. Tier 1's
   ticket is the hypothesis object — and the claim statement node where a claim exists —
   recorded in the substrate, with the §8 presence check passed for an attack on the
   target and the §7 statement pre-filters passed for a theorem statement. Those two
   Tier-1 conditions are gate-owned results this bead COMPOSES and does not compute: the
   §8 presence flag belongs to bead R3 (cairn-m1-cqt.8.3), which builds the declaration
   node, the flag and the nogo_review node, makes the flag a gate input and carries the
   flagged-branch Tier-1 refusal as its own fixture — R3 lands first, so that refusal
   stands before this bead subsumes it into the full lattice; the §7 statement pre-filter
   verdict reaches this bead as a prefilter-result record THIS bead defines and reads —
   {statement hash, per-filter verdicts, flags} — seeded synthetically in this bead's
   tests exactly as its synthetic KEEP and KEEP_IN_SAMPLE tables are seeded, with bead
   F8 (cairn-m1-cqt.5.8) producing that record and conforming to this reader on its own
   side. F8 does not block this bead: no M1 tier-gate fixture launches a
   theorem-statement claim, and the join of a real filter verdict to this predicate is
   asserted on F8's own side, by the integration test F8 carries; this bead blocks F8,
   so the reader exists before the producer conforms to it. This bead writes the single
   Tier-1 ticket predicate that reads both inputs alongside the recorded hypothesis
   object and claim statement node, so one bead authors the predicate and the other two
   author its inputs; R3 blocks this bead, F8 conforms later. Tier 2,
   algorithmic claim: a ladder table with verdict KEEP; scoped exception — a
   KEEP_IN_SAMPLE table is a Tier-2 ticket valid for the 60-bit rung of the same
   hypothesis key and for no other launch; the ticket records that purpose and the gate
   refuses a launch whose skill and inputs name any other. Tier 2, conjecture: a
   counterexample-hunt record with verdict SURVIVED. Tier 2, theorem with a Tier-2
   formalization profile: the claim statement node with an approve review_verdict. A
   claim whose typed fields carry more than one kind needs the ticket of EACH kind it
   carries and is refused while any is absent — a scoped KEEP_IN_SAMPLE admits only the
   60-bit rung whatever else is held. Tier 3: the most recent admissible Tier-2 node for
   the same key and method identity (for an algorithmic claim, a validation attempt with
   status OK whose witness verified, launched under a KEEP ticket), together with the
   justification, certificate plan and §10 sign-off.

3. Binding: a ticket is bound to a hypothesis, never a branch; the gate compares the
   ticket's recorded key and method identity with the launch's — and, where the ticket
   is a ladder table, the implementation revision it ran with the launch's, so a new
   revision re-ladders before it spends — and refuses a mismatch. A ticket carries its
   gate-bundle hash; a mismatch re-mints the ticket (decision 9;
   TICKET_BUNDLE_MISMATCH exists).

4. The ladder-rung exception: the ≤ 50-bit distribution rungs are admitted on the
   Tier-1 ticket whatever tier the boundary table assigns their ladder-plan-bounded
   cost; the 60-bit rung is tiered by its own declared profile.

DONE WHEN the gap-A fixture behaviors this bead owns hold live: the synthetic
KEEP_IN_SAMPLE scoping pair; the KEEP mismatch refusal on key, method identity or
implementation revision; the multi-kind refusal (cost model + correctness conjecture
refused Tier 2 while either the KEEP table or the SURVIVED record is absent); the
Tier-3-holding-KEEP-but-no-Tier-2-node refusal; and the composed Tier-1 predicate admits
on a passed §7 pre-filter verdict and a present §8 declaration, and refuses with
TICKET_ABSENT when the pre-filter verdict is absent or failed. (Corpus bead C5 plants the
gap-A behaviors under tests/planted/; this bead builds all of them with their own
integration tests.)

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_ticket_lattice.py (unit: selection rule incl. displacement,
lattice totality over kinds, scoping); tests/integration/test_tier_gate_tickets.py
(integration: the four fixture behaviors above against a seeded substrate).
design:
## Stored claim-kind encoding

The canonical hypothesis object's existing `claimed: Map(STR, STR)` carries the optional entry `"correctness_conjecture": "true"`. Presence with exactly that string adds the conjecture ticket obligation. Absence adds no conjecture obligation. Every other value, including `"false"`, `"True"`, `"1"` and the empty string, is malformed and refuses admission; non-string values are invalid under the canonical map schema. No launch argument supplies or overrides claim kinds.

The marker composes with the existing `scrutiny.typed_fields` classification: a cost model remains algorithmic and `formal_source` remains theorem-bearing. A cost-model hypothesis with the marker requires both KEEP and SURVIVED; a cost-model hypothesis without the marker retains the algorithmic-only classification. A formal statement with the marker requires its theorem and conjecture tickets. No classifier reads informal prose.

Positive observable: the stored cost-model-plus-marker hypothesis requires and admits only with both kind-specific tickets. Planted negatives: a malformed marker refuses; the cost model without the marker stays algorithmic-only; a launch-supplied claim-kind/ticket field cannot bypass stored classification.

Decision: CopperRidge mail356, 2026-09-08, Option A. Verified prior art: `src/cairn/keys.py` HYPOTHESIS_OBJECT uses Map(STR, STR); `src/cairn/scrutiny.py:158-181` derives cost model and theorem from stored typed fields. No canonical schema migration or bundle edit is required for this encoding. Selector and gate-owned rung binding design remain under investigation; this decision does not claim those interfaces implemented. Code remains held until cairn-m1-cqt.8.4 closes under the orchestrator's instruction.

## Architecture
- Approach: keep selection in a new `src/cairn/ticketlattice.py`, called by `TierGate.admit`, with no launch-supplied ticket or claim-kind field. Resolve candidate nodes from their real writers and immutable insertion order, select the most recent admissible candidate before evaluating KEEP/SURVIVED, and compose every required kind. Reuse `scrutiny.gate_read`, existing hypothesis/statement reads, no-go review, and pinned human review; reasons remain membership-tested. Do not infer admission history from whichever ticket happens to be latest. Preserve the current budget/certificate/yank checks and return persisted refusal records.
- Planned APIs: `ticketlattice.select(sub, gate_bundle, launch, *, attest_path=None)` returns a frozen selection containing the selected source hashes, ticket tier and scoped purpose, or refusal reasons. `ticketlattice.claim_kinds(sub, hypothesis_key, statement_hash)` reads the exact stored encoding above. `TierGate.admit(launch)` remains the worker-facing admission entry point; its Launch has no purpose/ticket/kind override.
- Planned producer seams: `laddertable.record(sub, table, plan, verified, *, attempt_id, at=None)` binds the table hash to the ReproRecord it already writes, with no change to laddertable.write's stored fields. The binding must be canonical or unambiguous and reader-validated, not merely a coincidental shared attempt. `ticketlattice.bind_attempt(sub, admission, attempt_id)` persists an immutable gate-admission-to-attempt row at launch from the exact selected ticket(s), hypothesis/method, implementation identity, input identity, tier and bundle; its writer rejects incompatible actual recipe/receipt data. A later Tier-3 selection reads that binding and the witness check, never a caller assertion or a latest-ticket lookup.
- Planned prefilter seam: `prefilter.record(sub, gate_bundle, *, statement_hash, verdicts, flags, at=None)` and `prefilter.read(sub, gate_bundle, statement_hash)` define/read the seeded B5 record to which F8 conforms. The record binds the exact statement and bundle and preserves every per-filter verdict and flag. Missing, failed, malformed, stale-bundle or incomplete results cannot satisfy the Tier-1 predicate. Quiet prefilters are not statement approval; Tier-2 theorem admission still requires the attested approve review. Final enum names and treatment of flagged-but-completed records require F8 conformance agreement before code.
- Pattern-to-follow: `src/cairn/instances.py` admit/launch_trial/record_trial; `src/cairn/tiergate.py` admit/_mint; `src/cairn/laddertable.py` write/read/record; `src/cairn/repro.py` policy/record_rerun; `src/cairn/hunt.py` run_hunt/record_for; `tests/integration/test_router_tier_gate.py` reason membership; `tests/integration/test_escrow_settlement.py` real substrate setup.
- Touches: new `src/cairn/ticketlattice.py`, new `src/cairn/prefilter.py`, `src/cairn/tiergate.py`, bounded `src/cairn/laddertable.py` record seam, bounded launch binding in `src/cairn/runner.py` or the gate-owned launch adapter after that integration choice is grounded, additive `src/cairn/schema.sql`, `tests/unit/test_ticket_lattice.py`, `tests/integration/test_tier_gate_tickets.py`. No Lean, challenge, bundle source, or unrelated canonical-schema edits.
- ADRs: none; implements PLAN section 5 and CopperRidge356/367. Any design departing from those instructions needs a recorded decision before implementation.
- Data model impact: additive immutable admission-to-attempt and prefilter records; no existing column rewrite. Table-to-repro binding uses the existing record writer; exact canonical binding representation remains to be settled before coding.
- Failure modes: a later INCONCLUSIVE/REJECT fails to displace KEEP (ordered-candidate integration test); a key/method/revision mismatch spends on an old table (same-launch mismatch matrix); a missing kind admits a mixed claim (KEEP-only/SURVIVED-only refusals, both-held positive); a caller purpose flag admits arbitrary work under KEEP_IN_SAMPLE (actual skill/input scoping pair); Tier 3 reuses a Tier-1 KEEP without a bound checked Tier-2 attempt (Tier-3 refusal with TICKET_ABSENT/TIER_TWO_ABOVE membership); an absent/failed prefilter grants Tier 1 (seeded real-row pair); stale-bundle minting silently grants (first refusal/re-mint, explicitly re-evaluated next admission).
- Gate-owned rung binding: follow instances.admit/launch_trial, deriving actual skill identity and bits/seed from gate-owned plan state. The <=50-bit exception and the 60-bit KEEP_IN_SAMPLE purpose must be checked against a bounded rung specification and actual recipe inputs; a caller boolean cannot activate either exception. The concrete rung specification/adapter is unresolved and must be grounded before delegation.

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] TierGate selects only the recorded hypothesis node and mints a singular ticket; admission calls scrutiny.gate_read and preserves its reasons. Source: `src/cairn/tiergate.py` complete body read (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R2] laddertable.write records hypothesis, method, implementation revision, bundle, verdict and replay grade but no producing-attempt or repro relation; record receives table and attempt_id but writes a ReproRecord containing only the attempt. Source: `src/cairn/laddertable.py:588-623` and `:778-810`, `src/cairn/claims.py:445-483`, writer bodies read (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R3] attempts has no hypothesis/method/tier/admission reference and runner.launch receives no TierGate decision. The existing writer cannot establish KEEP admission for a Tier-2 validation attempt. Source: `src/cairn/schema.sql:41-55`, `src/cairn/runner.py:349-410`, and TierGate._mint, bodies read (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R4] instances.admit constructs actual instance_maker identity and bits/seed inputs; launch_trial admits before the real runner and record_trial persists attempt_id. Source: `src/cairn/instances.py:157-256`, read-only survey of the writer/launch bodies (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH). This is structural prior art, not an executed B5 probe.
- [R5] ReproRecord binds attempt_id/kind/passed; policy requires a witness check for Verifiable, a fresh rerun for Replayable Tier0/1, and a deferred derive-time rerun for Tier2/3. Source: `src/cairn/repro.py:46-58`, `:128-171` and `src/cairn/claims.py:320-330`, root body reads (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH). Selection requires the appropriate checked record; a grade label alone is insufficient.
- [R6] F8 supplies per-filter verdicts/flags, never statement approval; B5 owns the reader and uses seeded records. Source: cairn-m1-cqt.5.8 description and acceptance, root read (documented: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH). B5 green does not measure real Lean filters.
- [R7] Existing stored kind support is Map(STR, STR); the exact marker decision and negative tests are above. Source: keys.HYPOTHESIS_OBJECT, scrutiny.typed_fields, CopperRidge356 (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- Delegability: NEEDS-INVESTIGATION-TICKET for the remaining binding representation, gate-owned rung specification and flagged-prefilter semantics. Do not dispatch implementation as STATEABLE until those concrete choices and their observables are recorded. No code is authorized tonight under CopperRidge367; the bead remains open with the named design holds above. This is preparation, not a claimed implementation or close.

## Resolved holds

The three items Delegability recorded as NEEDS-INVESTIGATION-TICKET are grounded on re-executed reads. Delegability: STATEABLE.

### H1 — table-to-repro binding representation

The substrate carries a canonical binding, and it is the evidence node rather than a new column. `evidence_nodes` holds `kind` (with `'ladder_table'` admissible), `verdict` (with KEEP / KEEP_IN_SAMPLE / REJECT / INCONCLUSIVE / SURVIVED admissible), `attempt_id` and `repro_record_hash` in one row (`src/cairn/schema.sql:240-253`). `hunt.py` writes exactly this shape live for the SURVIVED ticket kind: an EvidenceNode carrying verdict and attempt_id, then `sub.add_lineage(evidence_hash, run_hash, EDGE_INPUT)` binding it to the producing node (`src/cairn/hunt.py:887-898`).

The ladder half is a builder with no writer. `laddertable.evidence_node` (`src/cairn/laddertable.py:788-811`) accepts `attempt_id` and `repro_record_hash`, and zero call sites exist in `src/` or `tests/`. `laddertable.record` (`src/cairn/laddertable.py:779-786`) writes a ReproRecord keyed on attempt_id and returns it without persisting any table relation.

Decision: B5 selects a ladder ticket by reading `evidence_nodes` where `kind = 'ladder_table'`, joining to the `ladder_tables` row through the `lineage` EDGE_INPUT edge from the evidence hash to `table.hash` — the path hunt uses — and reading `repro_record_hash` off the same row for the §3 policy check. The producer seam is one writer mirroring `src/cairn/hunt.py:887-898`: wire `laddertable.evidence_node` to `claims.write_evidence_node` plus a lineage edge to `table.hash`, and pass `record`'s returned ReproRecord hash into it. No schema migration and no new binding table.

Verified: the schema, both writer bodies and the zero-caller count, re-executed 2026-09-08. Inferred: that no other consumer depends on the ladder evidence node's absence — nothing writes it, so nothing reads it.

### H2 — gate-owned rung specification

The specification is pinned data in the gate bundle rather than an adapter to build, and the discriminator is the rung's `role`, not a bits threshold. `bundle/ladder_plan.json` carries `[(30,'fit'), (40,'fit'), (50,'fit'), (60,'hold_out')]`; `ROLE_FIT`/`ROLE_HOLD_OUT` are `src/cairn/ladderplan.py:42-44`; `LadderPlan.from_bundle` (`src/cairn/ladderplan.py:285`) and `LadderPlan.rung(bits)` (`src/cairn/ladderplan.py:303`) are the accessors.

`bits` reaches the gate as launch data rather than as a flag: `instances.admit` puts it in `Launch.inputs` (`src/cairn/instances.py:194-200`), and `bits` is a declared INPUTS field of the counted object as well (`src/cairn/skills/rho_dp.py:86-91`).

Decision: the §6 ladder-rung exception reads `LadderPlan.from_bundle(self.bundle).rung(profile.declared_bits(launch.inputs)).role`. `ROLE_FIT` admits on the Tier-1 ticket whatever tier the boundary table assigns its ladder-plan-bounded cost; `ROLE_HOLD_OUT` is tiered by its own declared profile and is the only rung a KEEP_IN_SAMPLE ticket scopes to. A size the plan has no rung for carries no role at all, so an off-plan launch matches neither branch rather than defaulting into one. Both operands are gate-owned — the plan from the pinned bundle, the bits from recorded launch inputs — so no caller boolean activates either branch. Naming the exception by `role` rather than by "≤ 50 bits" keeps it correct under a plan whose rung bits move.

Verified: the four items above, re-executed 2026-09-08. Verified by execution rather than inferred: `Launch.inputs` is not uniform. `tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py` passes the bare size and `instances.admit` passes a mapping, so a reader indexing `inputs["bits"]` is wrong on the first shape. `profile.declared_bits` normalizes both and returns None for anything that names no size, and it is the single resolver the tier gate and the rung predicate share, so the two cannot disagree about what a launch declared. An off-plan size has no rung role and falls into neither exception.

### H3 — flagged-but-completed prefilter semantics

Settled from F8's own text. F8 (`cairn-m1-cqt.5.8`) states the filters "reject or flag, never pass", that "flags land as flags (visible in the gate-run record), never as passes or silent drops", and carries the No-Claim that "pre-filter green narrows nothing to correct — the human verdict (bead H2) remains the statement gate."

Decision: the record's Tier-1 disposition is `passed` exactly when every filter in the battery ran to completion and none returned REJECT. A FLAG is preserved verbatim in the record's `flags` and does not fail the Tier-1 predicate; flags are adjudicated by the H2 human review that Tier-2 theorem admission already requires. Treating a flag as a Tier-1 refusal collapses flag and reject into one verdict, and puts filter 4 (trivially provable ⇒ FLAG) in the position of barring a correct statement from the cheap tier, where the review that resolves it does not run.

A record that is absent, malformed, bound to a different statement hash, bound to a stale bundle, or missing any filter's verdict is not `passed` and refuses with TICKET_ABSENT by membership. An unrun filter is not a quiet filter.

Verified: F8's description and acceptance criteria read in full 2026-09-08; B5's own acceptance requires refusal on "absent or failed" and names no flag case. Inferred and owed to F8: the enum spelling of the per-filter verdicts. F8 conforms to this reader on its own side, so the spelling settles at F8's integration test; this decision fixes the semantics.

# cairn-m1-cqt.4.5 close — the ticket lattice, gate-selected and total over tiers and claim kinds

Source SHA 728a843. Every command below was re-executed at that SHA; output is verbatim.

## What is live

`TierGate.admit` selected only the tier-0 hypothesis object before this bead, and M0's tickets
table was empty in every real run. The gate now resolves a ticket per tier and per claim kind off
substrate state, and the launching party supplies neither.

- Tier 1 is the recorded hypothesis object, withheld when the claim carries a theorem statement
  whose §7 pre-filter battery did not pass. The statement is read from the recorded hypothesis row,
  so omitting it does not shed the obligation, and a launch naming a statement the hypothesis
  contradicts is refused rather than read.
- Tier 2 is one selection per claim kind the hypothesis carries: a KEEP ladder table for the
  algorithmic kind, a SURVIVED hunt record for the conjecture kind, and the claim statement node
  carrying a standing `approve` review verdict for the theorem kind. Any kind absent refuses.
- Tier 3 is a recorded gate admission binding for the same key and method, written under this
  bundle at tier 2, whose attempt carries a passed witness check.
- Selection takes the most recent node whatever its verdict and applies the verdict rule after, so
  a later INCONCLUSIVE displaces an older KEEP.
- The implementation revision is read off the certified skill's identity bundle. A table naming a
  revision does not bind to a launch that names none.
- Each tier mints its own ticket bound to the node actually selected; a displaced table does not
  hand back the older table's ticket.

## Commands and raw output

```
$ git rev-parse --short HEAD

$ uv run pytest -q --no-header tests/unit/test_ticket_lattice.py tests/integration/test_tier_gate_tickets.py

$ scripts/check.sh --fast

[check] pass types
[theater-patterns] pass: 1 pattern(s) over 225 file(s)
[check] pass theater
[check] skip tests (--fast; CI runs them)
[check] all gates pass
exit=0
```

```
                                                         4 passed, 77 deselected
```

```
$ uv run pytest -q --no-header tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py \
    tests/integration/test_router_tier_gate.py tests/integration/test_nogo_tier_wiring.py \

```

## Planted negatives

Fourteen, each applied alone, each red on exactly the tests that own the behavior, each restored
green. Selector slice: `rows[0]` for `rows[-1]`; dropping the scope check; dropping the revision
check; accepting any marker value; `any()` for `all()` over kinds; admitting INCOMPLETE as a
conjecture ticket; ignoring the hypothesis key when reading hunt records. Gate slice: dropping the
pre-filter check (3 failed); applying it to non-theorem launches (7 failed); a failed witness check
still binding Tier 3; any bound tier serving as the Tier-2 node; ignoring the hypothesis key on a
binding; a malformed marker reading as absent; the recorded-ticket lookup ignoring the tier.

Six of those came from a fresh-eyes Opus audit that found four real defects in this bead's own
code. Each was reproduced by a command that exited 0 while the defect was present, then fixed, then
the reproduction inverted into the regression test named beside it:

- a launch naming no revision spent a stale table — `tests/integration/test_tier_gate_tickets.py`
  `test_a_launch_naming_no_revision_cannot_spend_a_table_that_names_one`
- omitting `statement_hash` shed the §7 battery — `test_omitting_the_statement_does_not_shed_the_prefilter_its_hypothesis_records`
- a theorem claim reached Tier 2 with no approved statement — `test_a_theorem_claim_needs_its_approved_statement_before_tier_two`
- a displaced table returned the older ticket — `test_a_displaced_table_mints_its_own_ticket_rather_than_returning_the_older_one`

`KEY_MISMATCH` and `METHOD_MISMATCH` were removed: the selection query filters on both columns, so
neither branch was reachable and a foreign key or method refuses as an absent ticket.

## Evidence by file

- `src/cairn/prefilter.py:1-167` — the §7 record and its reader. `read` at `:150` ignores a
  stale-bundle result; `admits_tier_one` at `:165` is the Tier-1 half of the predicate.
- `src/cairn/ticketlattice.py:84` `claim_kinds`; `:106` `rung_role`; `:121` `ladder_candidate`;
  `:151` `hunt_candidate`; `:170` `mismatches`; `:194` `theorem_candidate`; `:212` `select_kind`;
  `:238` `tier_two_selections`; `:259` `bind_attempt`; `:282` `tier_three_candidate`.
- `src/cairn/tiergate.py:141` `_implementation_revision`; `:155` `_statement_hash`; `:173`
  `_tier_one_ticket`; `:182` `_selected_ticket`; `:216` `_recorded_ticket`; `:225` `admit`.
- `src/cairn/profile.py:12` `declared_bits`, the one resolver the tier gate and the rung predicate
  share so they cannot disagree about the size a launch declared.
- `tests/unit/test_ticket_lattice.py:1-151` — the pure predicate: pre-filter battery totality,
  binding, scoping, and lattice totality over claim kinds.
- `tests/integration/test_tier_gate_tickets.py:1-806` — the fixture behaviors against a real
  substrate, real built gate bundles and the real `laddertable`, `hunt`, `nogo` and `claims`
  writers.

## No-Claim

Lattice totality is proven on seeded synthetic nodes. Real ladder tables and hunt records arrive
with beads L2 and R4, and boundary-table tier derivation is bead B6's. The hunt records here are
built through the real writers with synthetic trial attempt ids; no hunt was executed.

Tier-3 admission is proven on seeded bindings only. `bind_attempt` has no production caller: the
launch path records no gate admission and `attempts` carries no admission reference, so
`tier_three_candidate` returns None for every real run today. Filed as `cairn-rmp`, not claimed here.

Where a hypothesis records no `claim_statement_hash`, the gate falls back to the launch's statement
and the §7 battery is never required. Filed as `cairn-jmu`; the fix is an invariant call for the
hypothesis writer or the gate, not this bead's to make alone.

The §8 half's own end-to-end refusal is bead R3's fixture and is not re-proved here; this bead
asserts only that the two Tier-1 conditions compose and that each refusal names its own reason.

Not run: the full local suite. CI is the full-suite gate for this commit.

title: M1 tiers: admission refusals — boundary-table tier derivation, yanked and uncertified revisions refused whatever ticket they hold
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §5; gap A). The declared tier is a claim the gate checks, never its input:
the gate derives the launch's tier from the profile's production cost at the launch's
inputs under the bundle's boundary table and refuses, with a TierRefused record, a
launch declaring a lower tier than the table assigns. The ≈ 10³ core-hour rule is the
table's Tier-2/Tier-3 edge. src/cairn/tiergate.py carries the BOUNDARY_TABLE, UNCERTIFIED
and YANKED reasons; M1 makes their remaining behaviors live against real records.

WHAT

1. Boundary-table derivation: evaluate the declared profile's production cost at the
   launch's inputs; refuse a launch declaring a tier lower than the table assigns that
   cost (the fixture: a launch declaring Tier 1 for a production cost the table assigns
   Tier 2 is refused). The ladder's ≤ 50-bit rungs are exempt on the Tier-1 ticket
   (bead B5's exception); the 60-bit rung is not.

2. Revision standing: a launch of a yanked revision, and a launch of a revision holding
   no recorded self-test certificate, are refused whatever ticket they hold — the reason
   collected alongside any others (the M0 gate collects every applicable reason rather
   than short-circuiting; steps check membership, never tuple equality — the trap
   recorded on cairn-m1-cqt.3's comments).

3. Refusal semantics stay §5's: a TierRefused record the ledger keeps, not an exception
   to catch and retry around; an unchanged re-submission is refused again; repeated
   TierRefused records on one hypothesis key are drift-monitor input (alarms bead),
   never a claim input.

DONE WHEN the two gap-A fixture behaviors this bead owns hold live (Tier-1-declared /
Tier-2-assigned refusal; yanked-or-uncertified refusal with any ticket), with
TierRefused records written and re-submission refused again.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_tier_gate_boundary.py (unit: cost evaluation against the
table, edge cases at the boundary values, exemption for ≤ 50-bit rungs);
tests/integration/test_tier_gate_refusals.py (integration: both fixture behaviors on a
seeded substrate, TierRefused rows asserted).
design:
## Architecture

- Approach: the gate already owns the whole truth table. `tiergate.predicate_reasons` collects
  `BOUNDARY_TABLE` (`declared_tier < cost_tier`), `UNCERTIFIED` and `YANKED` into a set and orders
  them through `ordered_reasons`, so item 2 needs no predicate change and item 3 none at all: the
  refusal path already writes one `tier_refusals` row per reason and returns `TierRefused` rather
  than raising. The one missing behavior is the ladder exemption. `cost_tier` is computed
  unconditionally at `tiergate.py:249` from the declared profile, so a fit rung whose bounded cost
  the table assigns Tier 2 is refused today. The fix is a `boundary_exempt` fact resolved in
  `admit` from the pinned ladder plan and passed into the predicate, which drops `BOUNDARY_TABLE`
  only while the launch sits on a fit rung. The rejected alternative is a bits threshold
  (`bits <= 50`) in the predicate: it duplicates the plan's rung table in code, so a re-pinned plan
  and the gate would disagree silently, which is the class of divergence `profile.declared_bits`
  was extracted to prevent. The discriminator is `role`, read from the bundle.
- Pattern-to-follow: `src/cairn/ticketlattice.py:106` (`rung_role`) already resolves exactly this
  fact from the bundle plus the launch's recorded inputs, with both operands gate-owned and a
  `KeyError` on an off-plan size returning `None` rather than defaulting.
- Touches: `src/cairn/tiergate.py` (`predicate_reasons` gains `boundary_exempt`; `admit` resolves
  it), `tests/unit/test_tier_gate_boundary.py` (new), `tests/integration/test_tier_gate_refusals.py`
  (new). No file another lane holds.
- ADRs: none exists for the tier gate; this bead mints none. The exemption is settled in PLAN.md
  and is an invariant, not a decision this bead may revisit.
- Data model impact: none. `tier_refusals`, `skill_certificates` and `yank_records` already carry
  every row the acceptance criteria assert on.
- Failure modes:
  (a) The exemption widens past the fit rungs and admits a 60-bit hold-out rung, or any launch
  declaring a fit size, at Tier 1. Observable: a hold-out-rung launch declaring Tier 1 for a
  Tier-2-assigned cost is admitted; asserted directly by the boundary unit test.
  (b) `role` is resolved from the launch instead of the bundle, making the exemption a caller
  assertion. Observable: a launch declaring 50 bits against a plan that has no 50-bit rung is
  exempted rather than refused; `rung_role` returns `None` off-plan and the test pins that.
  (c) The predicate short-circuits, so a yanked *and* uncertified revision reports one reason.
  Observable: `reasons` compared by membership returns a one-element tuple; the integration test
  asserts both rows in `tier_refusals`.

## Pre-implementation research

- [R1] The ladder exemption is PLAN.md, not a bead: "The ladder's distribution rungs (§6, ≤ 50
  bits) are Tier-1 — admitted on the Tier-1 ticket whatever tier the boundary table would assign
  their ladder-plan-bounded cost", and "its 60-bit rung is tiered by its own declared cost profile"
  — source: `PLAN.md:540-547` (verified: 2026-09-08, read in full). The stated reason is
  circularity: a fit rung the table assigned Tier 2 "would otherwise need the very KEEP it exists
  to produce". The bead text's "bead B5's exception" names no bead that exists; `rg 'exempt'
  PLAN.md` returns nothing and no open bead carries the exception. Cite PLAN.md:542.
  (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R2] The boundary table is pinned data, four rows, `max_core_s` of 1 / 3600 / 3600000 / null —
  source: `bundle/tiers.json` (verified: 2026-09-08, read in full). 3600000 core-seconds is 10³
  core-hours, so the bead's "≈ 10³ core-hour rule is the table's Tier-2/Tier-3 edge" is the table
  as pinned, not an approximation to re-derive. `tier_for_cost` (`src/cairn/tiergate.py:77`) walks
  rows in order and returns the last tier when every ceiling is exceeded. (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R3] The rungs are `[(30, fit), (40, fit), (50, fit), (60, hold_out)]` — source:
  `bundle/ladder_plan.json` via `ladderplan.LadderPlan.from_bundle` (verified: 2026-09-08).
  `ladderplan.ROLE_FIT` / `ROLE_HOLD_OUT` at `src/cairn/ladderplan.py:42-44` are the spellings.
  "≤ 50 bits" and "role == fit" coincide on the pinned plan; role is the durable discriminator.
  (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R4] Revision standing is already live against real rows: `Substrate.certified`
  (`src/cairn/substrate.py:324`) recomputes `certificate_hash` over the stored transcript and env
  manifest and returns False when no row exists, and `Substrate.yanked` (`:335`) is a `yank_records`
  lookup — source: read in full (verified: 2026-09-08). `admit` already passes both
  (`src/cairn/tiergate.py:249-251`). So item 2 is a test-only obligation unless the tests show
  otherwise. (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R5] Refusal semantics are already §5's: `admit` writes one row per reason through
  `claims.add_tier_refusal` and returns `TierRefused`, never raising — source:
  `src/cairn/tiergate.py:285-291` (verified: 2026-09-08). "An unchanged re-submission is refused
  again" therefore needs no idempotence machinery; it is an assertion that a second `admit` call
  writes a second set of rows. (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R6] Neither named test file exists (`test -f` on both fails, verified: 2026-09-08), so both are
  new and this bead contends with no other lane. `tests/unit/test_tier_gate_predicate.py` and
  `tests/integration/test_tier_gate.py` are the shape to follow for the two layers.
  (Confidence: HIGH)
- Delegability: STATEABLE. The predicate change is one fact and one branch; the fixtures are the
  bead's own acceptance bullets against the existing seeding helpers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a launch declaring Tier 2 for a Tier-2-assigned cost is admitted when its
  ticket stands; a ladder ≤ 50-bit rung launch passes on the Tier-1 ticket though the
  table assigns its bounded cost a higher tier; outputs pasted.
- Planted negative: a launch declaring Tier 1 for a Tier-2-assigned cost is refused with
  a TierRefused record; a yanked revision's launch and an uncertified revision's launch
  are refused holding a valid KEEP ticket; an unchanged re-submission is refused again;
  each asserted on rows, not logs.
- No-Claim: refusals prove the gate reads the table and revision standing; the
  cumulative edge is bead B7's, and repeated-refusal monitoring is the alarms bead's.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_tier_gate_boundary.py,
  tests/integration/test_tier_gate_refusals.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

title: M1 tiers: per-key charging and the Tier-1 cumulative edge at 4× the measured ladder per-run cost (decision 10)
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §5; decision 10). A tier derived per launch is satisfiable by sharding — a
90-bit validation rho as a thousand honest one-core-minute walks, each on the Tier-1
ticket, no TierRefused, no drift signal, no KEEP ever required — and §0 lets the
orchestrator set the branch grant that funds it. The cumulative edge is what makes
cheap-before-expensive hold against sharding.

WHAT

1. Per-key charging: the gate charges every non-refused launch's production cost to its
   hypothesis key under the ticket that admitted it — the declared cost at launch,
   reconciled to the execution receipt's measured cost when the attempt closes, so an
   understated declaration misstates the key's charge by no more than the attempt in
   flight.

2. The edge: the boundary table names a cumulative edge per ticket tier over the charge
   of a worker's FRESH launches; the worker launch that would carry that charge under
   the key's current best ticket past the edge is TierRefused until the next tier's
   ticket exists.

3. Exemptions, charged but never metered against the edge: gate-owned launches — the
   ladder's rungs, a null-control or retry-predicate re-measurement, the auditor's
   draws — and re-runs of recorded recipes (the Skeptic's, the reproducibility gate's).
   The fixture pair: a branch on the Tier-1 ticket whose worker launches would carry the
   key's charge past the Tier-1 edge is refused at the crossing launch, while a second
   ladder run on the same key is admitted.

4. Decision 10: the Tier-1 edge is set at 4× the measured ladder per-run cost
   (CONJECTURE), recorded beside the trial count it derives from (bead L7's measured
   whole-ladder ≤ 50-bit figure is the input); the value and its derivation land in the
   bundle's boundary table. The unit is CORE SECONDS — cpu_user_s + cpu_sys_s from the
   execution receipt, the same currency the boundary table's `max_core_s` and the
   profile's `expected_core_s` already carry (src/cairn/tiergate.py, src/cairn/profile.py)
   — and never wall seconds, which bead L7 records alongside them; an edge in one clock
   metered against charges in the other is off by whatever the run's parallelism is.

DONE WHEN charges accrue and reconcile per key; the crossing worker launch is refused at
the edge while the gate-owned second ladder run is admitted; the edge value in the
bundle carries its measured derivation.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_cumulative_edge.py (unit: charge accounting,
reconciliation, exemption classification); tests/integration/test_cumulative_edge_gate.py
(integration: the fixture pair against a seeded key with accumulated charges).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: launches accrue declared charges to the hypothesis key and reconcile to
  measured receipt costs at close, both in core seconds, with the edge value in the same
  unit; a second ladder run on a key near the edge is
  admitted (gate-owned, charged, unmetered); rows pasted.
- Planted negative: the worker launch that would cross the Tier-1 edge is TierRefused at
  the crossing launch — not before, not after — and an identical launch under a fresh
  Tier-2 ticket on the same key is admitted; a shard of small worker launches
  collectively crossing the edge is refused at the crossing one.
- No-Claim: the edge meters worker fresh launches per key per ticket tier; it does not
  bound gate-owned spend (the ladder plan and §5 ceilings do), and the 4× multiple keeps
  its CONJECTURE tag until operation shows it binds sensibly.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_cumulative_edge.py,
  tests/integration/test_cumulative_edge_gate.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
OBSERVATION from polish round 24, recorded rather than lost: profile.py:58 sets
expected_core_s = expected_wall_s = mean_wall_s, so the boundary-table field this bead
reads as core seconds is populated from a declared wall figure. For the single-threaded
PARI skills that ship today the two coincide, and this bead's reconciliation rule
(receipt cpu_user_s + cpu_sys_s) is the correct measured side. If a multi-threaded
skill ever declares a profile, the declared core figure needs its own basis — decide
then whether that is a profile-schema change or a declaration convention.

title: M1: formalization gate: challenge/solution protocol, gate-compiled Challenge + formal statement hasher (build + probe), gate-owned axiom computation ⊆ {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}, kernel replay (leanchecker --fresh; comparator gold tier in the Linux container — decision 6), statement pre-filters, planted sorry / wrong-statement fixtures, mathlib cost measured before corpus sizing
description: Roll-up for PLAN §7 "green Lean"; the granular children carry the work. Toolchain pin `leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0-rc1`, installed under `~/.elan` and reachable on no PATH (grounding brief research/grounding/lean-checker-protocol.md, whose `no ~/.elan` line predates the install); the Linux container enters here (decision 6). Gate compiles the Challenge from the claim statement node with a gate-side renderer and pinned prelude; Solution names the formal statement hash (hash over the comparator's closure — `ConstantVal` + `ConstantInfo` transitive closure — CONJECTURE until built and probed; raw export bytes are unstable, PROVEN by probe); gate-owned `Lean.collectAxioms` module (leanchecker rejects neither `sorryAx` nor extra axioms — PROVEN by probe); ordered cheapest-first plan; `leanchecker --fresh` cost measured on a mathlib-importing Challenge before the fixture corpus is sized (32.3 s mathlib-free). description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7 "green Lean", §16 pins; grounding brief
research/grounding/lean-checker-protocol.md). The formalization gate rebuilds in a
sandbox under a pinned `lean-toolchain` and `lake-manifest` mathlib revision, and every
checker command is a gate-bundle field. elan 4.2.3 and the pinned toolchain are installed
under `~/.elan` and that toolchain's `bin/` ships `leanchecker`, but `~/.elan/bin` is on no
PATH and `~/.elan/settings.toml` names no default toolchain, so a bare `lean` errors with
`no default toolchain configured` while `~/.elan/bin/lean +leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0-rc1`
compiles a trivial theorem at rc 0. The grounding brief's `command -v elan lean lake
leanchecker landrun -> all NOT FOUND; no ~/.elan`
(research/grounding/lean-checker-protocol.md:7) was probed 2026-08-21 and predates the
install, so it is a record and not the current state; re-probe rather than trust either.

WHAT

1. Make the installed elan and the pinned toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0-rc1`
   reachable — `~/.elan/bin` on the PATH the harness uses, or the absolute path recorded as
   a bundle field, plus a default toolchain or an explicit `+leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0-rc1`
   on every invocation — and install only what the probe shows missing; pin the
   mathlib revision the coverage decision names (PLAN §11: mathlib @1f29011 under
   toolchain v4.34.0-rc1) in a lake-manifest the gate records.

2. Probe and record in research/grounding/ with tags: leanchecker is present in the
   toolchain and runs; `leanchecker --fresh` on a mathlib-free module costs what the
   brief measured (32.3 s is the recorded figure — re-run, don't inherit); a minimal
   lake build of a mathlib-importing module completes on this machine, with wall time
   and disk footprint recorded (mathlib builds are the heavy step; the number decides
   whether CI can ever run this or it stays local-only, which cairn-hcl's matrix needs
   to know) — `~/.cache/mathlib` holds 8691 `.ltar` files at 439 MB, so the build may draw
   on `leantar` cache hits rather than compiling, and the probe records which revision that
   cache covers rather than assuming it matches the pin.

3. The pins as gate-bundle fields: toolchain name, manifest revision, checker commands.
   A gate run whose checker configuration differs from the bundle's fails closed before
   compilation — the axiom checker's own half of that wiring lands with bead F5, which
   asserts it at its close, and the whole ordered gate plan's with bead F6; this bead
   records the pins where both read them.

DONE WHEN the toolchain and mathlib pin build a hello-theorem module on this machine;
leanchecker runs; the grounding records exist with measured numbers; the pins are
readable bundle fields.

TEST PLAN — tests/integration/test_lean_toolchain.py (integration: pinned toolchain
resolves and compiles a trivial module; leanchecker present; skipped nowhere — if the

title: M1 lean: the Linux container for the PROVEN gold tier (decision 6) — landrun, container digest, chattr grounded, arms distinguishable
description:
CONTEXT (decision 6, PLAN §16; gap C of the epic's decomposition comment — settled by
execution: no container spec exists in the tree, and `grep -rli landrun` outside .git
returns research prose only). A Linux container enters at M1 with the formalization
gate: the PROVEN gold tier needs the comparator under an external kernel in a Linux
`landrun` sandbox, and the macOS fallback runs unsandboxed, development-only. Docker and
OrbStack run on this machine (probed 2026-08-27, recorded on the epic:
`docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 python:3.14-slim` answers platform questions in
seconds).

WHAT

1. A container spec in-tree (a Dockerfile or equivalent) carrying the pinned toolchain
   and mathlib from bead F1, landrun, and the checker commands — content-addressed into
   the gate bundle's container digest so a rebuilt container is a different identity.

2. landrun grounded by probe inside the container: the comparator's external-kernel
   invocation runs under it; record what the sandbox confines (filesystem, network) the
   way the other grounding records do.

3. `chattr +a` semantics in the container, grounded (an epic stack fact): whether the
   append-only attribute binds against the writing user in this container runtime, with
   the probe's raw output — cairn-hcl owns the general Linux write boundary; this bead
   owns the in-container answer the gate's deployment shape needs.

4. The macOS arm stated out loud: fake-landrun is dev-only; the gate records which arm
   ran (gold tier in-container vs dev-tier on macOS), and a PROVEN derivation requires
   the gold-tier record — the derivation-side check is bead H2/F6 territory; this bead
   makes the two arms distinguishable in the gate-run record.

DONE WHEN the container builds reproducibly from the spec with its digest recorded; the
comparator runs under landrun inside it; the chattr probe is recorded; a gate-run record
names which arm ran.

TEST PLAN — tests/integration/test_lean_container.py (integration: container builds,
landrun-wrapped command runs inside, arm recorded in the gate-run record; the test is
allowed to be slow and is marked accordingly, never skipped-by-default without a named
reason the suite prints).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: the container builds from the in-tree spec; a landrun-wrapped checker
  command runs inside it; the container digest lands in the bundle; commands and output
  pasted.
- Positive: the chattr +a probe inside the container is recorded in research/grounding/
  with raw output and a tag.
- Planted negative: the dev-arm (macOS, fake-landrun) and gold-arm gate-run records are
  distinguishable, and a test asserts a record that names neither arm is refused.
- No-Claim: a working container proves the gold-tier arm exists on this machine; CI
  execution of it is cairn-hcl's matrix question, and nothing here claims the dev arm is
  sandboxed.
- Test types: integration, probe. Files: tests/integration/test_lean_container.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

comments.text:
Design notes from the 2026-09 language and ergonomics review (research/briefs/language-and-agent-ergonomics.md §5; PLAN §16 decision 14), to fold into WHAT (1)-(2) at build time:

1. The container digest is input-addressed. The identity the bundle records is the hash of the container spec plus every pinned input (base image digest, the elan release, the toolchain archive digest, the mathlib revision and the olean cache contents, landrun's release digest), and a rebuild from unchanged inputs is the same identity; the OCI image digest of the build that ran is recorded beside it as an artifact. A Dockerfile qualifies only with pinned base digests and no network at build time; a Nix closure hash is the model and lean4-nix packages the toolchain (mathlib's `lake exe cache get` step is not documented as integrated, so the olean cache is an input the spec pins by hand). BuildKit's SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH support pins timestamps only (its docs claim no stable content digest across builds).

2. landrun's maintenance state is contested: the repository states a Landlock ABI v9 target with --best-effort, one secondary write-up says the project stopped at ABI v5 in 2025-10. Settle it from the repository's commit and tag dates before building on it, and record the answer with the chattr probe. The comparator's README names landrun's correctness as part of its trusted base, so a stalled sandbox is a gold-tier finding, not a footnote.

3. A third arm to probe beside Docker and OrbStack: Apple's Containerization framework 1.0.0 (2026-06) runs a Linux container in its own lightweight VM on Apple Silicon with macOS 26, which this machine runs. If it serves the gold tier locally, the "Linux container" is still Linux (Landlock is a Linux LSM) and the arm is recorded like the others.

title: M1 lean: gate-compiled Challenge — deterministic renderer, pinned prelude, claim-to-formal-statement binding in the gate-run record
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7, §4 claim identity). The gate COMPILES the Challenge module from the
claim statement node with a gate-side renderer and pinned prelude, both inside the gate
bundle and outside every worker's write path; the Formalizer never creates or edits
Challenge text and submits a Solution that names the Challenge's formal statement hash.
This mechanizes "the statement was fixed before the proof".

WHAT

1. The renderer: claim statement node (its formal statement field is the Challenge
   source, §4) → a Challenge module under the pinned prelude; deterministic — the same
   node renders byte-identical Challenge source, asserted by double render.

2. The pinned prelude as a bundle object; renderer and prelude hashes in the gate-run
   record.

3. Write-path isolation: Challenge text is produced into gate-owned paths only; a
   Solution module that contains or edits Challenge text is structurally impossible to
   submit — the submission interface takes a Solution module plus the formal statement
   hash it names, nothing else.

4. The gate-run record binds the claim statement hash to the formal statement hash
   (computed by bead F4 at compile time) under the bundle hash; a binding absent from
   the record is a gate that has not run, and a `lean_artifact` evidence node reaches
   its claim statement only through that binding.

DONE WHEN a claim statement node with a formal statement renders to a compiling
Challenge twice, byte-identical; the gate-run record carries the binding FIELD under the
bundle hash and a record missing it is refused as a gate that has not run; a Solution
naming a wrong hash is refused before any kernel work (the refusal itself is bead F6's
ordered plan; this bead supplies the binding it checks). The formal statement hash that
fills the field is bead F4's: F4 builds, canonicalizes and probes the hasher and asserts
the field populated, and F4 is blocked on this bead, so no hasher exists at this close —
this bead authors the channel, never a second hasher.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_challenge_renderer.py (unit: deterministic render, prelude
pinning, gate-owned paths); tests/integration/test_challenge_compile.py (integration:
rendered Challenge compiles under the pinned toolchain; binding recorded).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: rendering one claim statement node twice yields byte-identical Challenge
  source (length + sha256 in Python) that compiles; the gate-run record carries the
  claim-statement-hash ↔ formal-statement-hash binding field under the bundle hash (bead
  F4 fills the field and asserts it populated); output pasted.
- Planted negative: a worker-writable path holding Challenge text is refused by the
  render step; an edited prelude fails the bundle-hash check; a gate-run record missing
  the binding field is refused as a gate that has not run.
- No-Claim: a compiled Challenge proves rendering and binding; it proves nothing about
  Solutions, axioms or replay (F5/F6), and nothing about whether the statement says what
  anyone means — the §7 review keeps that human.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_challenge_renderer.py,
  tests/integration/test_challenge_compile.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

title: M1 lean: the formal statement hasher over the ConstantInfo closure — built, canonicalized, probed for stability
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7; the epic's stack-facts list). The formal statement hash is computed by
the gate when it compiles the Challenge, over what the comparator compares — the
theorem's ConstantVal and the full ConstantInfo of every constant in its transitive
closure — never over raw export bytes, which carry position-dependent names. Tags as
they stand: raw exports being unstable is PROVEN by probe; that this closure is the
right hash is CONJECTURE — the hasher is inferred from the comparator's compareAt and
does not exist yet. M1 builds and probes it before the gate is trusted.

WHAT

1. Build the hasher: a gate-owned Lean-side or export-side computation over the
   theorem's ConstantVal plus the full ConstantInfo of its transitive constant closure,
   canonicalized (sorted, length-prefixed, domain-separated — the repo's §3 hashing
   discipline) into the formal statement hash.

2. Probe stability, upgrading the CONJECTURE or refuting it, recorded in
   research/grounding/: two independent builds of one Challenge (fresh build dirs) hash
   identically; a Challenge differing in a comment or unused declaration hashes
   identically; a Challenge whose statement differs semantically (a changed hypothesis,
   a changed constant definition anywhere under the statement) hashes differently. If
   any probe fails, the hasher's basis is wrong — record the failure and redesign before
   any downstream bead consumes it; do not ship a hasher whose stability was not
   measured.

3. The hash names and binds; it decides nothing — the comparator's own closure
   comparison (bead F6, check iv) is the decision, and a hash match with a comparator
   mismatch fails closed.

DONE WHEN the hasher exists as a bundle object; the three probe families pass with raw
output recorded; the hash lands in the gate-run record via bead F3's binding.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_formal_statement_hasher.py (unit: canonicalization
known-answer vector); tests/integration/test_hasher_stability.py (integration: the
rebuild, no-op-change and semantic-change probes against real compiled modules).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: two fresh builds of one Challenge yield one hash; a comment-only edit leaves
  it unchanged; a semantic edit under the statement changes it; all three shown with raw
  output and recorded in research/grounding/ with the CONJECTURE upgraded or refuted.
- Planted negative: hashing raw export bytes across two builds diverges (the PROVEN
  instability, re-shown once) — the test that pins why the closure basis exists.
- No-Claim: a stable hash names and binds; it decides no equality — the comparator's
  closure comparison (bead F6) is the decision, and green here proves nothing about
  Solutions.
- Test types: unit (known-answer), integration (probes). Files:
  tests/unit/test_formal_statement_hasher.py, tests/integration/test_hasher_stability.py.
