title: M1 lean: gate-owned axiom computation ⊆ {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7 check iii; epic stack facts). leanchecker rejects neither `sorryAx` nor
extra axioms — PROVEN by probe — so the axiom set must be computed by the gate itself,
never read from output the Solution's own compilation emits (an axiom list emitted by
the Solution's build is a count reported by the party being gated).

WHAT

1. A gate-owned module in the bundle that imports the Solution and runs
   `Lean.collectAxioms` over the Challenge's theorem names, and requires the result
   ⊆ {`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`}.

2. What the allow-list rejects, stated for the fixture authors: `sorryAx` (the sorry
   escape), the per-computation axioms of `decide +native` / `bv_decide` — the probe on
   the pinned toolchain records `decide +native` → `[t._native.decide.ax_1_1]`
   (research/grounding/lean-checker-protocol.md:43), a per-theorem generated name, so a
   fixture matches that `._native.decide.ax_` shape and not a fixed axiom name — and any
   custom axiom.

3. Configuration discipline: the permitted-axiom set, the checker command and its
   external kernels are gate-bundle fields, never per-run literals; a run whose checker
   configuration differs from the bundle's fails closed before compilation.

4. Re-probe on this machine and record: leanchecker accepting a sorryAx-carrying module
   (the fact this design rests on), so the grounding record carries the run rather than
   the brief's memory. At the gold tier the comparator's own axiom check runs too (bead
   F6); this bead is the ordinary path.

DONE WHEN the gate-owned computation reports exactly the axioms of planted modules —
clean, sorry-carrying, native-decide-carrying, custom-axiom-carrying — and the gate
refuses the three dirty ones; configuration comes from the bundle and a mismatch fails
closed.

TEST PLAN — tests/integration/test_axiom_computation.py (integration: the four planted
modules against the real toolchain; bundle-config mismatch fails closed; the leanchecker
re-probe recorded).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a clean Solution's computed axiom set is inside the allow-list and the gate
  proceeds; the computation names axioms per theorem from the gate-owned module, not
  from Solution build output; run pasted.
- Planted negative: a sorryAx module, a native-decide module and a custom-axiom module
  are each refused with the offending axiom named; leanchecker alone accepting the

- Test types: integration, probe. Files: tests/integration/test_axiom_computation.py.

title: M1 lean: kernel replay, closure comparison, and the ordered cheapest-first gate plan with its planted self-tests
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7 checks i–iv and the ordered plan; §4 ordered scopes). The gate: (i)
rebuild in a sandbox under the pinned toolchain and manifest; (ii) kernel-replay with
`leanchecker --fresh` (the checker inside the toolchain; comparator with an external
kernel at the gold tier, under landrun in the Linux container — bead F2); (iii) the
axiom computation (bead F5); (iv) the Challenge and Solution theorem statements
identical over the statement's transitive constant closure, so a redefined constant
anywhere under the statement fails. "No error messages" or an empty sorries list is
never a PROVEN criterion — both have leaked sorry/admit in published systems.

WHAT

1. The ordered, cheapest-first gate plan (the §4 declarative-plan shape,
   src/cairn/gateplan.py): the pin and formal-statement-hash check → the statement
   pre-filters (bead F8) → the Tier-≥2 review verdict where required (§5) → the sandbox
   build → the axiom computation → the kernel replay → the closure comparison. An
   earlier failure blocks the later steps and records why, so a sorry-shaped Solution
   never reaches --fresh.

2. A Solution naming any formal statement hash but the Challenge's fails closed before
   kernel replay.

3. The closure comparison as the decision (check iv): comparator-based equality over the
   transitive constant closure; a hash match with a comparator mismatch fails closed.
   Gold tier runs the comparator with an external kernel in the container; the ordinary
   path runs in-toolchain; the gate-run record names the arm (bead F2's
   distinguishability).

4. Gate self-test per §4 discipline, in the bundle and ahead of the gate: a planted
   sorry-Solution must FAIL at the axiom step without reaching --fresh; a planted
   wrong-statement Solution (strictly weaker theorem) must FAIL the closure comparison;
   an exact-match Solution must PASS. These are the gate-side behaviors corpus fixtures
   (c) and (d) plant under tests/planted/ later.

DONE WHEN the ordered plan runs a real Solution end to end; each planted failure stops
at its named step with later steps blocked; the gold arm replays inside the container.

TEST PLAN — tests/integration/test_formalization_gate.py (integration: full pass on an
exact-match pair; sorry stops before --fresh; weaker-statement fails closure comparison;
wrong-hash fails first; step order asserted from the plan record).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: an exact-match Challenge/Solution pair passes all ordered steps with the
  step sequence visible in the plan record, on both arms where available (ordinary
  in-toolchain; gold in-container); run pasted.
- Planted negative: the sorry-Solution fails at the axiom step and --fresh never runs
  (asserted from the plan record, not inferred); the strictly-weaker Solution fails the
  closure comparison; a Solution naming a stale formal statement hash fails before any
  build; a run under an edited checker command fails closed before compilation.
- No-Claim: a green gate run proves the artifact proves the compiled statement under the
  allowed axioms; PROVEN still requires the human review_verdict on the same statement
  hash (bead H2), and statement meaning stays a human question.
- Test types: integration (real toolchain, no mock). Files:
  tests/integration/test_formalization_gate.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

Adopted from the lean-proof-mastery fit brief (Source: research/briefs/skills-fit-lean-proof-mastery.md (cairn-lnz) §4.)
- P-6b Input fingerprint on the dev arm (row 13): on `dev-macos-fake-landrun` the gate takes a sha256 fingerprint over `lean/Challenge/`, `lean/lakefile.toml`, `lean/lake-manifest.json`, `lean/lean-toolchain` and the Solution file ahead of the sandbox build and again after kernel replay; a mismatch fails closed at the step where it is observed and the plan record names the changed path. Planted: a Solution whose build step rewrites a Challenge file is refused with that path named; pasted. On the gold arm the same fingerprint runs and its equality is pasted as the second witness beside landrun's read-only mounts.
- P-6c Timeout is its own step outcome (row 15): the plan record's step-outcome vocabulary distinguishes `timeout` from `fail`; a planted slow Solution run under a reduced `lean.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S` stops at `timeout` with later steps blocked, and the record line pasted shows `timeout`, never `fail`.
- P-6d Kernel-replay failure planted (row 22): a Solution module adapted from lean4's `tests/pkg/leanchecker/LeanCheckerTests/AddFalse.lean` at commit `3447a668` (Apache-2.0, attribution in the fixture file), which adds an unchecked `false : False` through `Environment.addDeclCore` with `doCheck := false`, passes the axiom step and fails at `leanchecker --fresh`; it runs in the same test as the exact-match positive, so the negative is attributed to the forgery and not to the environment; both verdict lines and the step at which each stopped pasted. A second fixture from the same family (`ReplaceAxiom.lean` or `AddFalseConstructor.lean`) is added if its failure lands at a different step; otherwise the grounding row says why one suffices. Precondition the bullet rests on, undecided in any bead and absent from `src/cairn/` (no Solution build path exists; `challenge.py` renders the Challenge only): the Solution module is compiled so its elaborator commands run, and `import Lean` is admissible in a Solution. title: M1 lean: statement pre-filters — vacuity, ∃-trap linters with pinned limitations, stubs, bounded prove/disprove, blind round-trip diff
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7 statement-level review). Verified-but-wrong-statement is more dangerous
than an open gap. The mechanical pre-filters reject or flag, never pass: they are the
cheap first line, and the human verdict remains the gate (bead H2).

WHAT — the pre-filter battery, each a typed check with reject/flag semantics:

1. Vacuity: attempt to derive `False` from the hypotheses; certified vacuous ⇒ REJECT.

2. Linters for the `∃ x, P x → Q` trap: the plain form is caught; the
   binder-predicate and conjunction-nested forms pass silently. The linter the
   limitation is measured on is formal-conjectures' `ExistsImplicationLinter`
   (research/grounding/lean-statement-linters-vacuity.md:12), vendored as four files
   onto v4.34.0-rc1 with two one-line import edits and probed there
   (lean-statement-linters-vacuity.md:16, STRONG-EMPIRICAL): `∃ n > 0, n ≠ 1 → False`
   is silent, the binder predicate elaborating to `∃ n, n > 0 ∧ (… → …)`, and
   `∃ n, (n ≠ 0 → False) ∧ True` is silent likewise, while `(∃ n, n ≠ 0 → False) → True`
   warns twice. A different linter is a different limitation, so a close that builds its
   own re-measures rather than inheriting these two forms. The limitation is the item
   the Skeptic's checklist carries (bead W2's template), stated in the linter's own docs
   so nobody reads linter-green as trap-free.

3. Stubs and new axioms: declarations that are stubs, and any axiom introduction, flag.

4. A bounded prove/disprove attempt with a weak prover: trivially provable or trivially
   disprovable ⇒ FLAG (a trivial statement is not necessarily wrong, so this flags).

5. A blind round-trip informalization diffed against the source claim: divergence ⇒
   FLAG. Blind = the informalizer sees the formal statement only, never the source
   claim's prose.

6. Wiring: the pre-filters run in the gate plan ahead of the sandbox build (bead F6's
   order — F6 wires that position and asserts it from the plan record; this bead blocks
   F6, so no plan carrying a sandbox-build step exists at this close), and the filters emit the prefilter-result record bead B5
   (cairn-m1-cqt.4.5) defines and reads for a theorem statement's Tier-1 ticket — this
   bead conforms to B5's reader, its integration test asserting that a produced record
   admits through B5's predicate; B5 seeds synthetic records and does not wait on this
   bead; B5 blocks this bead, so the reader this test admits through exists here.

DONE WHEN each filter fires on a planted statement of its class and stays quiet on a
clean one; flags land as flags (visible in the gate-run record), never as passes or
silent drops; the documented linter limitation is itself pinned by a test showing the
nested form passing — a limitation asserted out loud rather than discovered later; and
a prefilter-result record these filters produce admits a theorem-statement launch through
bead B5's Tier-1 ticket predicate, the join B5 leaves to this bead because B5 proves its
own half on seeded synthetic records.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_statement_prefilters.py (unit: each filter against planted
positive and clean statements; the nested-form pass pinned);
tests/integration/test_prefilters_in_gate.py (integration: flags in the record, and a
produced prefilter-result record admitting through bead B5's Tier-1 ticket predicate;
the pre-filters' position ahead of the sandbox build is bead F6's assertion, F6 landing
after this bead).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: each filter fires on its planted class (vacuous hypotheses, plain ∃-trap,
  stub, new axiom, trivially provable, round-trip divergence) and stays quiet on a clean
  statement; flags visible in the gate-run record; runs pasted.
- Positive: a prefilter-result record these filters produce — {statement hash, per-filter
  verdicts, flags} as bead B5 (cairn-m1-cqt.4.5) defines it — admits a theorem-statement
  launch through B5's Tier-1 ticket predicate, while the same record recorded failed is
  refused with TICKET_ABSENT present by membership (never tuple equality), so the join is
  asserted on a produced record rather than on B5's seeded synthetic one; rows pasted.
- Planted negative: the binder-predicate and conjunction-nested ∃-trap forms PASS the
  linters — pinned by a test, so the limitation is a measured fact the Skeptic checklist
  carries, not a surprise.
- No-Claim: pre-filter green narrows nothing to correct — the filters reject or flag,
  never approve; the human verdict (bead H2) remains the statement gate.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_statement_prefilters.py,
  tests/integration/test_prefilters_in_gate.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

Adopted from the lean-proof-mastery fit brief (Source: research/briefs/skills-fit-lean-proof-mastery.md (cairn-lnz) §4.)
- P-8a Coverage matrix across pre-filters and the Skeptic's checklist (row 23): one table with a row per statement-level failure class the lane names (vacuous hypotheses; the `∃ x, P x → Q` trap in plain, binder-predicate and conjunction-nested forms; stub; new axiom; trivially provable; trivially disprovable; round-trip divergence; quantifier drift; quantifier-order confusion; domain drift; statement weakening; hidden placeholder; tautology), each assigned to the pre-filter that fires, the Skeptic checklist item that carries it (`.6.2`), or an explicit uncovered row with its reason. title: M1 lean: first library items (Finite W.Point over a finite field, Hasse bound, DLP definition) as Challenge fixtures
description:
First formalized-library items authored as M1 Challenge fixtures (PLAN.md §11 and §13 M1): Finite W.Point over a finite field, the Hasse bound, and a DLP definition (exists k, k smul P = Q), written under the §7 Challenge/Solution protocol so the M4 library imports them instead of starting empty.

Background: PLAN.md §11 names these as the first library items absent upstream in mathlib at the pinned revision, and the 2026-09-05 comparison with Anthropic's FLT formalization found that reuse of existing formal scaffolding (106 files adapted from Imperial FLT and flt-regular) is what made an 11-day run possible. cairn-m1-cqt.5.7 already needs a mathlib-importing Challenge to measure gate cost; the DLP definition is small enough to be that probe, so the two beads share one artifact.

## Architecture
- Approach: author each item as a Challenge under the §7 protocol (statement, formal statement hash over the ConstantInfo closure, gate-owned axiom check, kernel replay) with a Solution that proves it against mathlib at the pinned revision, so the item passes the same gate any PROVEN claim passes and lands in the library by the ordinary intake path. Order: DLP definition first (it doubles as the .5.7 cost probe), then Finite W.Point over a finite field, then the Hasse bound (which may need to be stated as an axiom-free import of an existing mathlib result if one lands upstream before this bead runs; check the pinned revision first). Rejected alternative: a hand-written Lean file outside the protocol, which the library could not import without re-proving and which the statement hasher never sees.
- Pattern-to-follow: bundle/challenge_prelude.lean (the gate-compiled prelude) and src/cairn/challenge.py (the Challenge renderer hashed into the gate bundle).
- Touches: lean/ (three Challenge and Solution pairs), src/cairn/challenge.py only if a new statement shape is needed, tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden if challenge.py or the prelude moves (regenerate in the same attributed commit per AGENTS.md), PLAN.md §11 and §13 (text landed 2026-09-05).
- ADRs: none; PLAN.md §11 coverage decision (mathlib @1f29011, toolchain v4.34.0-rc1) is the record.
- Data model impact: none.
- Failure modes: (1) the Hasse bound proof exceeds the gate's measured cost budget, detected by the .5.7 cost table and the gate plan's per-item duration row; (2) a statement pre-filter (.5.8) flags the DLP definition as vacuous because the existential is trivially satisfiable on a degenerate instance, detected by the pre-filter's linter output on the fixture and answered by stating the definition over the cyclic subgroup generated by P; (3) an edit to challenge.py moves the gate bundle hash and every deployed pin, detected by tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden failing until regenerated.

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] PLAN.md §11 names Finite W.Point over a finite field, the Hasse bound, a DLP definition, Groebner bases and summation polynomials as first library items absent upstream — source: PLAN.md:1284-1290 (verified: 2026-09-05) (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R2] Anthropic's FLT formalization adapted 106 files from Imperial FLT and flt-regular; Buzzard names that reuse as the reason 11 days was possible — source: ~/Knowledge/raw/anthropic-math-2026-fermat.md (documented: 2026-09-05) (Confidence: HIGH)
- [R3] cairn-m1-cqt.5.7 requires a mathlib-importing Challenge to size the fixture corpus, so the DLP definition item can serve as that probe — source: br show cairn-m1-cqt.5.7 (verified: 2026-09-05) (Confidence: MEDIUM)
- [R4] mathlib at the pinned revision has Weierstrass curves, the proved affine group law, division polynomials and finite fields, but not the three items above — source: PLAN.md §11 coverage decision (documented: 2026-09-05; re-verify against the pinned revision before authoring) (Confidence: MEDIUM)
- Delegability: STATEABLE after cairn-m1-cqt.5.4 (hasher) and .5.8 (pre-filters) close.

## Test plan
- integration: tests/integration/test_challenge_gate.py::test_library_items_pass_gate — each of the three Challenge and Solution pairs passes hasher, axiom check and kernel replay under the gate plan.
- unit: tests/unit/test_challenge_prefilters.py::test_dlp_definition_not_vacuous — the DLP definition survives the vacuity and exists-trap linters.
- conformance: tests/conformance/test_gate_bundle_golden.py — the gate bundle hash golden matches after any prelude or renderer change.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive observable: `uv run pytest -q tests/integration/test_challenge_gate.py::test_library_items_pass_gate` prints `passed` and the gate log names three Challenge hashes with axiom set within {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}.
- Planted negative: `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_challenge_prefilters.py::test_dlp_definition_not_vacuous` passes only because the pre-filter accepts the subgroup-scoped definition and rejects a planted degenerate variant with the token `vacuity:exists-trap`.
- No-Claim: a green gate run proves the three items are formally stated, hashed and kernel-replayed against the pinned mathlib; it proves nothing about their usefulness to a later PROVEN claim.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

Adopted from the lean-proof-mastery fit brief (Source: research/briefs/skills-fit-lean-proof-mastery.md (cairn-lnz) §4.)
- P-9a Falsifier ahead of the Solution (row 4): each item's Challenge statement gets a degenerate-instance probe under the pinned mathlib ahead of any Solution attempt, as an `example` or `#eval` in a scratch module: the DLP definition on the trivial subgroup and with `P = 0`, the finiteness statement over the smallest field the definition admits, the Hasse bound at `q = 2` and `q = 3`; a probe that refutes the statement sends the item back to statement authoring, never to the Solution. Probe files and their output pasted.
- P-9b The three-statement triple (row 5): for each item, the close pastes the source locator (PLAN §11 line), the normalized statement with every normalization named, and the elaborated type from `set_option pp.all true in #check @<Target>` at the pinned toolchain; a normalization with no stated reason is a defect. The triple lands in the grounding row for the item.
- P-9c No partial item, and the six-field record for one that stalls (row 10): an item that reaches no green gate run leaves the bead open and records, in the grounding row: the exact statement attempted, the first unsupported step, the witness or diagnostic, the checked survivors (lemmas that compiled), the scope of the attempt (toolchain, mathlib revision, wall time, route), and the reopening condition. The record pasted where it applies; otherwise the close says no item stalled.
- P-9d Axioms per item, transitively (row 2): each Solution's transitive axiom set is the gate's F5 output, pasted per theorem name, beside a `#print axioms` run by the author as a separate line marked author-check; the two agree or the disagreement is the finding.
- P-9e Library facts at the pin (row 27): every mathlib declaration a Solution uses is cited at file:line at mathlib `1f29011`, and the claim that an item is absent upstream is shown by a failing `#check` or an empty `grep` over the pinned checkout, pasted; a declaration found upstream turns that item into an import with its own statement match, recorded in PLAN §11's coverage line.

title: M1 workers: the dispatch path and its record — handed-node hashes, role-template hash, allow-list, request-bytes hash
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §4 workers; §1). Every worker is a fresh-context agent dispatched by the
harness as its own top-level query, never composed by a parent model. Its prompt is
exactly the handed substrate nodes plus its pinned role template. The dispatch SDK's
isolation is grounded against the installed version in
research/grounding/dbos-sqlite-and-agent-sdk-isolation.md.

WHAT

1. Construct the worker invocation from handed nodes and the pinned role template:
   no settings sources, skill files, working-tree snapshot, parent conversation,
   continuation, or arbitrary extra prose. Record the observed SDK options with
   their calibration tag; W4 owns the standing isolation canary.
2. Write an append-only substrate dispatch record before the SDK call, carrying the
   ordered handed-node hashes, role-template hash, tool allow-list, SDK/CLI versions,
   bundle identity, prompt-bytes digest, and provider request-bytes digest where the
   SDK exposes provider bytes. Otherwise record the explicit unavailability reason.
   Never label a constructed prompt digest as a provider request digest.
3. The public dispatch API accepts node IDs and a role name, with no argument for
   injecting gate internals or extra prose. W2's pinned role-template store is the
   only prose source outside the handed nodes.
4. Resolve each handed node by its content address and refuse a content/hash mismatch.
   Handed nodes and subproblem text are mutable worker prompts; the role template is
   immutable gate-bundle configuration.

TEST PLAN

- tests/unit/test_dispatch_record.py: record fields, hash validation, API surface,
  refusals, SDK initialization validation, immutable records.
- tests/integration/test_worker_dispatch.py: offline integration of real SQLite,
  pinned bundle, record persistence, and the installed SDK's command construction.
  No SDK-boundary mock and no credential-dependent pytest skip.
- Mandatory manual live close gate:
  `uv run python tests/integration/test_worker_dispatch.py`.
  This entry point executes the real top-level SDK query and checks the persisted
  record, fresh sessions, emitted allow-list, and cancellation. Its raw output and
  substrate artifact path are required close evidence, bound to the source SHA.
  CI runs the offline tests; provider availability and a paid credential are not CI
  dependencies. The live gate is re-executed before this bead closes.
- tests/fixtures/worker_dispatch.py owns shared test construction; unit and integration
  test modules do not import each other.

## Architecture
- Approach: The harness resolves all context before calling the SDK. A pinned
  worker_roles object provides the role template, tools, model, and execution bounds.
  Dispatch and terminal-result records are separate append-only rows, so an absent
  result is an unfinished dispatch rather than a fabricated success. Offline CI checks
  deterministic construction; a real authenticated SDK run is mandatory close evidence.
  A paid provider call in every CI run adds availability and credential dependencies
  without improving deterministic contract coverage.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/claims.py (write_gate_run), src/cairn/bundle.py (GateBundle).
- Touches: src/cairn/dispatch.py, src/cairn/worker.py, src/cairn/schema.sql (additive),
  named tests and fixture, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, SDK isolation grounding brief.
- ADRs: PLAN.md §4 worker dispatch contract; test execution split authorized by the

title: M1 workers: the Skeptic's scoped read-only substrate handle and tool allow-list
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7 independent skeptic). The Skeptic sees only the statement, never the
Prover's reasoning — if it reads the proof it just agrees; independence is the whole
value. Isolation is by construction at both layers: context (bead W1's dispatch) and
capability (this bead).

WHAT

1. The scoped read-only substrate handle: scoped to the statement node's closure and
   filtered by evidence kind — the statement, plus the recipes and certificates of
   repro_node, ladder_table and counterexample_hunt_record evidence (a re-run needs
   those); for lean_artifact evidence the Challenge's formal statement hash and the
   gate-run verdict ONLY — never the Solution blob or its recipe inputs, the checker
   re-run being the gate's job; never the Prover's transcript or proof text. The formal
   statement hash is the gate-run binding field bead F3 (cairn-m1-cqt.5.3) authors and
   bead F4 (cairn-m1-cqt.5.4) fills; neither blocks this bead and no line under src/,
   tests/ or src/cairn/schema.sql carries one, so the lean_artifact projection is
   asserted against a seeded evidence node and a seeded binding, the way bead B5 seeds
   bead F8's prefilter record. No M1 fixture dispatches a Skeptic against a real Lean
   artifact, so the join to a gate-produced binding is outside M1.

2. The tool allow-list: counterexample search tools only, no general file read, no
   shell; both handle scope and allow-list are gate-bundle config, and the dispatch
   record names the allow-list it ran under, so a widened one is visible in the ledger.

3. Re-runs set skip_cache_lookup (§3): a Skeptic re-run of any experiment records a
   fresh attempt, never a cache read. The §3 concurrency contract holds: the handle is
   read-only; a worker returns artifacts to the single writer and holds no substrate
   write capability.

DONE WHEN a Skeptic dispatch can read exactly the filtered closure and nothing else —
probed by attempting each forbidden read through the handle (Prover transcript, Solution
blob, an unrelated statement's nodes) and observing refusal; its experiment re-runs
appear as fresh attempts with skip_cache_lookup set.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_skeptic_handle.py (unit: filter rules per evidence kind,
read-only enforcement); tests/integration/test_skeptic_isolation.py (integration: a
live-shaped dispatch whose handle refuses the forbidden reads; fresh-attempt semantics
on re-run).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: through the Skeptic handle, the statement node, a ladder table's recipe and
  a repro certificate are readable; for a lean_artifact only the formal statement hash
  and verdict come back, both read from the seeded binding of WHAT (1) since no gate run
  produces one at this close; reads shown.
- Planted negative: the Solution blob, the Prover transcript, an unrelated statement's
  closure and any write are each refused through the handle; a re-run served from cache
  instead of a fresh attempt fails the test.
- No-Claim: capability isolation proves what the handle can reach; context isolation is
  the dispatch canary's claim (bead W4), and nothing here measures what the model was
  told; the lean_artifact projection is proven on a seeded binding, never on one a
  formalization gate run produced.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_skeptic_handle.py,
  tests/integration/test_skeptic_isolation.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.
notes: BEAD SHORT CODES -> IDS (bead bodies name sibling beads by short code; these are the br ids): L1-L12 = cairn-m1-cqt.1.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.1.12 (ladder); S1-S5 = cairn-m1-cqt.2.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.2.5 (baseline skills); C1-C8 = cairn-m1-cqt.3.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.3.8 (planted corpus); B1-B7 = cairn-m1-cqt.4.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.4.7 (tiers, escrow, yank); F1-F8 = cairn-m1-cqt.5.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.5.8 (formalization gate); W1-W4 = cairn-m1-cqt.6.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.6.4 (workers and dispatch); H1-H4 = cairn-m1-cqt.7.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.7.4 (human queue and review); R1-R8 = cairn-m1-cqt.8.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.8.8 (epistemics); the alarms bead is cairn-m1-cqt.9. comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
## Architecture
- Approach: construct a frozen, typed projection before dispatch. The worker handle contains only serialized allowed records and no Substrate connection. Evidence selection starts at the exact statement hash, never general lineage traversal. A pinned skeptic_scope object can narrow the supported evidence kinds; it cannot widen the compiled maximum. MCP tools expose scoped reads and structured rerun requests, never arbitrary paths, SQL, modules, prompts, or options. The single writer executes an admitted rerun with skip_cache_lookup forced true; worker code receives no write handle.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/dispatch.py _prepare; src/cairn/claims.py evidence_for; src/cairn/repro.py rerun_launch_kwargs and record_rerun.
- Touches: src/cairn/skeptic.py, src/cairn/worker.py, minimal coordinated src/cairn/dispatch.py seam, tests/unit/test_skeptic_handle.py, tests/integration/test_skeptic_isolation.py, additive grounding. Any gate-bundle source edit requires coordination with CopperRidge and its owner.
- ADRs: none; this implements the bead's scoped-handle and single-writer contract.
- Data model impact: none planned. The seeded Lean binding uses an explicit evidence-to-gate-run input edge, checked against the statement and bundle, and returns only formal_statement_hash and result.
- Failure modes: arbitrary graph traversal leaks forbidden records (negative read tests); an allowed_tools-only configuration exposes unlisted tools (installed SDK initialization/tool-list probe); a rerun uses cache (fresh attempt and skip_cache_lookup assertions).

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] EvidenceNode stores attempt_id and repro_record_hash; attempts name recipes; recipe identities name certificates. Source: src/cairn/claims.py and src/cairn/substrate.py (verified: 2026-09-08 by file reads; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R2] The existing repro gate rejects same-attempt, different-recipe and cache-served reruns. Source: src/cairn/repro.py:115-156 (verified: 2026-09-08 by root file read; Confidence: HIGH). The survey's two selected tests passed; root will reexecute any test used for close evidence.
- [R3] SDK tools=[] disables built-ins; allowed_tools grants permission rather than limiting availability. Source: Context7 /anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python, README and types.py (documented: 2026-09-08). Installed 0.2.152 MCP behavior is under an initialization-only probe before worker code changes; documentation alone is not probe evidence.
- Delegability: the filtered snapshot is STATEABLE; worker MCP connection and rerun integration remain root-owned pending the installed-version probe and peer dispatch seam.

## Criterion to assertion

## Mocks, monkeypatching, patching

`grep -nE "mock|Mock|monkeypatch|patch\(|stub|fake|dummy"` over both scoped test files
returns two hits, both the seeded data value `arm="dev-macos-fake-landrun"` — a gate-run
field, not a test double. **There are no mocks, no monkeypatching and no patching of
production code in either file.** The MCP server, the SQLite substrate, the gate bundle
(built from the real `bundle/` tree with `shutil.copytree`) and the child replay are all
real. The only stand-in anywhere is `lambda _: None` for `clear_flags` inside
`live_check`, which is not on any pytest path.

Nothing here hides a real path; the paths not exercised offline are the provider-facing
ones (F1, F3), and the file is explicit that the live command owns them.

## RULE 2

No weakening found. The scoped source contains no calibration-tag, ladder, verifier or
"proven" logic that it could relax; it is a read projection plus a refusal set.

- `_lean_projection` cannot manufacture a proof: it requires exactly one gate-run input
  edge, a gate run matching both the scoped statement and the pinned bundle hash on the
  node *and* the ledger row, and a non-empty `formal_statement_hash`; it then returns the
  seeded hash and the gate's own `result`. It stamps nothing.
- Reruns are writer-owned and forced fresh (`skip_cache_lookup=True`), and refuse a
  disowned, inadmissible or yank-covered source, so a Skeptic cannot recycle a cached
  attempt into new evidence.
- The scope can only narrow `MAX_EVIDENCE_KINDS`, never extend it (`set(kinds) <= MAX…`),
  and `snapshot` takes no scope override (pinned by a signature assertion).
- F8 records that the projection hides the gate `arm`, so dev-arm and gold-arm verdicts
  are indistinguishable to the Skeptic. This matches the stated criterion; it is raised
  as an epistemics observation for the criterion's owner, not as a rule violation.

The grounding brief's §E is consistently labeled (`VERIFIED-PROBE`, `Documented`,
`STRONG-EMPIRICAL`) and closes with an explicit `CONJECTURE` scope-limit paragraph that
disclaims rerun scheduling and ambient-context leakage, deferring the latter to `.6.4`.
Every §E stack claim names an executed probe with a root command and a raw-output path.
Three of them check out against the artifacts still present on this machine: the live log
contains `CAIRN_SCOPED_READ_810`, `"total_cost_usd": 0.008751`, session
`0dc41084-1d62-474a-a915-c5cb4ffa2532`, exactly the three `mcp__cairn_skeptic__*` tool
names and `"status": "connected"`. Nothing in §E is an unlabeled stack assertion. Two
durability caveats: the artifacts live under `/private/tmp/`, so the citations decay with
the machine's temp roots, and the recorded source hashes carry the F10 delta.

## No-Claim — what this audit did not verify

- **No provider call was made.** `live_check`, the named W3 close command, was not run.
  Every §E `STRONG-EMPIRICAL` claim about model-facing tool availability, the child's
  actual read execution and the reported costs is taken from the recorded artifacts, not
  re-executed. Model-facing behavior is unverified by me.
- I did not verify that `worker._execute` delivers the scoped server to a real child.
  F1 is a statement about test coverage, established by a surviving mutant, not a claim
  that the production path is broken. `_validate_init` would raise on that drift at
  runtime, which I read but did not exercise against a live init.
- I ran only the five named test files, not `scripts/check.sh`, ruff, ty, codespell,
  `theater-patterns.sh` or the full pytest suite. Cross-file regressions from the audited
  code are outside what I measured.
- I did not construct a mutant for "the worker gains a Substrate handle"; that is not a
  one-string edit, so the criterion is marked a partial gap on inspection only.
- F9 is a read of the projection path and the `RECIPE` schema, not an executed
  reproduction. F8's harm is not demonstrated; only the mechanism is.
- I did not assess whether the four should-fix gaps are worth closing given cost; the
  three worker-envelope ones (F1, F2, F3) all sit behind a second, tested refusal.
- Other sessions hold uncommitted edits to `.beads/issues.jsonl`, `src/cairn/justify.py`,
  `src/cairn/schema.sql` and three untracked `disagreement` files. I did not read, run or
  reason about them, and any interaction between them and this audit is unmeasured.

## Tree cleanliness

`git diff --stat 42ad2a0` over the seven scoped paths produces no output. `shasum -a 256 -c`
against the pre-mutation digest list reports OK for all seven:


`git status --short` shows the same four modified and three untracked entries that were
present at session start, all owned by other sessions. Nothing was staged, stashed,
committed or deleted, and no history-rewriting or path-discarding git command was run.

title: M1 workers: the dispatch canary — planted tokens, decision forms, re-grounding on toolchain change, failure yanks the path
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §4, §13 M1 dispatch canary). That a dispatched worker's context holds
nothing but the nodes it is handed — no settings source, no skill file, no working-tree
snapshot — is a stack fact the canary grounds before the dispatch path is trusted, and
re-grounds on every toolchain or SDK change. The canary is decided on the emitted
request bytes where they are observable and on the worker's echoed context otherwise; an
echo that omits a planted token is a regression signal and not a proof, and the
grounding record names which form ran.

WHAT

1. The plantings: a distinct token in each settings source — the project-level
   instruction file, the user-level instruction file, a skill file, and the working
   tree's status (an uncommitted file whose name carries the token).

2. The assertion: after a dispatch through bead W1's path, every planted token is
   absent — from the emitted request bytes where the SDK exposes them (the observable
   form), else from the worker's echoed context (the fallback form; the worker's role
   for the canary run is "echo your entire context verbatim").

3. The grounding record: which form ran, the SDK and toolchain versions probed, raw
   evidence; re-run required on every toolchain or SDK change — wire the version pin
   into the check so a changed version with a stale canary record REFUSES dispatches
   (the §2 shape: an uncertified revision is a yanked one that was never tested).

4. Failure semantics: a canary failure yanks the dispatch path as a failed self-test
   yanks a skill revision — dispatches refuse until a fresh canary passes on the new
   toolchain.

DONE WHEN the canary runs green on the current SDK with the record naming its form; a
planted token deliberately injected into the dispatch (a positive control — hand the
token in a handed node) IS found, proving the detector can see; a stale canary record
against a bumped SDK version refuses dispatches.

TEST PLAN — tests/integration/test_dispatch_canary.py (integration: the four plantings,
both decision forms exercised where available, the positive control, the stale-record
refusal). The corpus-side planting entry is bead C7's; this bead is the mechanism and
its gate wiring.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a canary run finds all four planted tokens absent under the strongest
  available decision form, with the grounding record naming the form and versions; the
  positive control (token handed in a node) IS detected; raw evidence pasted.
- Planted negative: with the SDK version pin bumped and no fresh canary record, a
  dispatch is refused naming the stale canary; a simulated canary failure (the positive
  control treated as ambient) yanks the path — dispatches refuse until re-grounded.
- No-Claim: absence under the echo form is a regression signal, not proof of isolation —
  the record says which form ran, and only the request-bytes form is an observable
  boundary; nothing here claims the model provider adds no context server-side.
- Test types: integration, probe. Files: tests/integration/test_dispatch_canary.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.
notes: BEAD SHORT CODES -> IDS (bead bodies name sibling beads by short code; these are the br ids): L1-L12 = cairn-m1-cqt.1.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.1.12 (ladder); S1-S5 = cairn-m1-cqt.2.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.2.5 (baseline skills); C1-C8 = cairn-m1-cqt.3.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.3.8 (planted corpus); B1-B7 = cairn-m1-cqt.4.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.4.7 (tiers, escrow, yank); F1-F8 = cairn-m1-cqt.5.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.5.8 (formalization gate); W1-W4 = cairn-m1-cqt.6.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.6.4 (workers and dispatch); H1-H4 = cairn-m1-cqt.7.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.7.4 (human queue and review); R1-R8 = cairn-m1-cqt.8.1 through cairn-m1-cqt.8.8 (epistemics); the alarms bead is cairn-m1-cqt.9. comments.text:
Session B grounding and interface facts (2026-09-07):

- `dispatch.run(sub, gate_bundle, *, role, node_ids)` accepts no extra prose, SDK
  options, tool overrides, settings, or caller-supplied templates. The pinned
  `worker_roles` object maps a role name to exactly `template`, `tools`, `model`,
  `max_turns`, and `timeout_s`. W2 owns the production role templates.
- The verified path uses one fresh ClaudeSDKClient instance per dispatch, one
  top-level query, bare mode, skills disabled, no session persistence, no settings
  sources, and an empty temporary working directory. SDK 0.2.152, CLI 2.1.259.
- The tool registry is empty. Bare mode reported no tools when WebSearch was
  requested. W3 owns the scoped MCP connection and its live probe; accepting a
  nonempty allow-list without observing it in initialization is not supported.
- `prompt_bytes_hash` hashes the exact serialized handed-node envelope;
  `role_template_hash` hashes the custom system prompt separately. The provider
  HTTP request bytes are not exposed by the public SDK interface. The record
  carries null request_bytes_hash and its explicit unavailability reason.
- CI is offline. The mandatory paid-provider close command is
  `uv run python tests/integration/test_worker_dispatch.py`, which requires an
  existing API-key source in bare mode. W4 owns repeated ambient-context leakage
  checks, SDK/CLI changes, and the canary's execution policy. SDK initialization
  metadata and an exact echo are not proof that every injected instruction is absent.

title: M1: human queue as a typed object + closing rule + acknowledgment record; review_verdict through the human path; PROVEN derivation (lean_artifact + approve on the same statement hash); §7 disagreement protocol; decisions 3 (Tier-2 needs open operator session until M3), 4 (Reframer drafts, human ratifies), 5 (the discretionary half of yanks/salt human-only; a gate-verdict yank is the gate's own write)
description: Roll-up for PLAN §10 (human loop) and §7 (statement-level review, disagreement protocol); the granular children carry the work. The human queue is a typed object with fifteen classes (statement_review, nogo_review, waiver_request, yank_ruling, revision_admission, expert_signoff, disagreement, near_dup_review, supersedes_refuted_review, null_control_pending, clock_inconclusive, shape_departure, leaked, cost_drift, audit_shortfall) and a closing rule one of whose paths is an attributed `acknowledgment` record through the human path; every human-attested node enters through the attestation file (bead m0-gate-bundle-pin-tier-gate) as the operator's own OS user; `review_verdict` names one statement hash and does not transfer to a superseding version; a disagreement is recorded with both artifacts' hashes, classified, routed, and the tag stays at its pre-dispute level. Owns fixture (l)'s verdict half, the Tier-2 human-session rule (decision 3), claim-statement authorship (decision 4) and the authority on the DISCRETIONARY half of yanks and salt (decision 5) — a reach ruling that narrows the default, a yank no gate verdict produced, a salt issued after no recorded yank — while a yank a gate's own verdict produces is that gate's write and carries no attestation record (cairn-m1-cqt.4.2). title: M1 human: the queue as a typed object — fifteen classes, blockers, the exhaustive closing rule, the acknowledgment record
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §10). The human queue is a typed substrate object, not a phrase. Depth and
age are drift-monitor inputs and strategy inputs, never gate inputs, and the closing
rule is what keeps them from being edited down.

WHAT

1. The item type: class ∈ {statement_review, nogo_review, waiver_request, yank_ruling,
   revision_admission, expert_signoff, disagreement, near_dup_review,
   supersedes_refuted_review, null_control_pending, clock_inconclusive, shape_departure,
   leaked, cost_drift, audit_shortfall}, the branch or statement hash it blocks and the
   blocker that holds it, and its enqueue time. Schema addition to
   src/cairn/schema.sql with append-only discipline for the item's identity; closure is
   a recorded event, not a row rewrite.

2. The closing rule, exhaustive: an item closes by a human-path record (§4 attestation
   file, src/cairn/attest.py), by its blocker clearing, or — for an item that holds no
   blocker (leaked, clock_inconclusive, shape_departure, cost_drift, audit_shortfall) —
   when the branch, rung or audit cycle it names reaches a terminal status, re-runs or
   next meets its target, or by an attributed `acknowledgment` record through the human
   path naming the item. It closes by NO other path.

3. The `acknowledgment` record as a human-path kind (an operator-attested record like a
   review_verdict, digest + offset discipline per §4).

4. Readers: depth and age queryable (the orchestrator may prefer branches needing no
   human input — strategy, never a reason to lower scrutiny); enqueue APIs for the
   producers other beads wire (clock_inconclusive from L4, shape_departure from L2,
   cost_drift from the alarms bead).

DONE WHEN items enqueue with class and blocker; each closing path closes; no other
mutation closes; an acknowledgment enters only through the attestation file and closes
only the item it names.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_human_queue.py (unit: class set, closing-rule state
machine, refusal of out-of-rule closure); tests/integration/test_human_queue_paths.py
(integration: close via attestation record, via blocker clear, via terminal status;
acknowledgment digest discipline).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: an item of each closing family closes by its lawful path (attestation
  record, blocker clear, terminal status, acknowledgment) with rows shown before and
  after.
- Planted negative: a direct status write to an open item is refused; an acknowledgment
  record whose digest matches no attestation entry leaves the item open (absent-unless-
  digest-matches, the §4 reader rule); depth and age cannot decrease except through a
  lawful close, asserted over a scripted sequence.
- No-Claim: the queue is bookkeeping the gates and humans read; green proves closure
  discipline, not that any producer enqueues correctly (the producing beads own their

title: M1 human: the disagreement protocol — recorded with both hashes, classified, routed, tag frozen at pre-dispute level
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7 disagreement protocol; §10 panel rule). A Prover/Skeptic or panel
disagreement is never resolved by vote; it is recorded with both artifacts' hashes,
classified, routed to an owner, and the claim's tag stays at its pre-dispute level until
resolved.

WHAT

1. The disagreement record: both artifacts' hashes, a classification ∈ {statement error,
   proof gap, harness bug, out-of-scope, inconclusive}, the routed owner (the human for
   statement errors — a `disagreement` human-queue item, bead H1), and the statement
   hash in dispute.

2. Tag freeze: while a disagreement stands on a statement hash, `justify` derivations
   for that hash hold at the pre-dispute level — implemented as a gate input the
   derivation reads, not as advice; resolution (the record's closure through the queue's
   lawful paths) releases the freeze.

3. DISAGREE-status kinship: a skill cross-check DISAGREE (§2) and a worker-level
   disagreement are different records — the first is an attempt status the caller parks
   or refutes on, the second is this typed record; the bead documents the boundary so
   neither absorbs the other's cases.

DONE WHEN recording a disagreement freezes the tag at its pre-dispute level (a
would-be-upgrading justify run holds), the queue item routes by classification, and
resolution releases the freeze with the history showing freeze and release.

title: M1 human: decisions 3, 4, 5 enforced — the Tier-2 operator-session knob, Reframer drafts with human ratification, the discretionary half of yanks and salt human-only
description:
CONTEXT (operator decisions 3, 4, 5; PLAN §16, §10, §4). Three human-authority rules
bind M1 and each needs an enforcement point, not a memo.

WHAT

1. Decision 3 — Tier-2 spend requires an open operator session until M3. §10 makes this
   an operator knob in the gate bundle. Implement: the knob as a bundle field (default
   ON until M3); an operator-session signal the tier gate can read whose shape follows
   the §4 boundary — operator-attested, not orchestrator-writable; the natural form is a
   session record through the attestation path with an expiry, and the tier gate refuses
   a Tier-2 admission while no unexpired session stands (a TierRefused reason of its
   own). Session liveness semantics (duration, renewal) are the implementer's, recorded
   in the bundle.

2. Decision 4 — the Reframer drafts claim-statement nodes; a human ratifies through the
   human path. Enforcement: a claim statement node authored by a worker context enters
   as a draft; the tier gate treats an unratified statement as absent for any ticket
   that requires a claim statement node; ratification is an attestation-path record
   binding the statement hash.

3. Decision 5 — the DISCRETIONARY half of yanking and salt issuance is human-only, like
   waivers. The half that is not: a yank a gate's own verdict produces — a §2 self-test
   failure, a §6(2c) `xP ≠ Q` or count-divergence REJECT — is that gate's own write and
   carries no attestation record, because §4's human-path list enumerates a yank-REACH
   ruling and not a yank, and because M1's fixture (b) drives that REJECT under a cold
   cache where no human exists to attest anything (bead B2 carries the split; §10's
   autonomy envelope is why it has to hold). Bead B2 builds the record, the reach
   predicate and the propagation; this bead pins the authority on the discretionary
   half: a reach-narrowing ruling, a yank naming no gate verdict, and a salt bump
   following no recorded yank accept only attestation-backed records, and a worker- or
   orchestrator-shaped write of one is refused (the same absent-unless-digest-matches
   reader rule as review_verdicts).

DONE WHEN each rule has a live refusal: Tier-2 admission without a session; a ticket
built on an unratified statement; a reach-narrowing ruling, a yank naming no gate
verdict, or a salt bump following no recorded yank, each without attestation — while a
yank a gate verdict produced stands with none.

title: M1 epistemics: the proportional-scrutiny router — a bundle predicate over typed fields, monotone class requests, the Tier-3 sign-off rule
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7 proportional scrutiny). "A run announcing it broke ECDLP has produced
evidence it erred" is a routing rule, not a sentence in a worker prompt: the router's
classes are a predicate in the gate bundle over the TYPED fields of the hypothesis
object and claim statement node (target family, claimed property or cost model, scope)
and the §8 flag, never over prose. A scrutiny class carried by prompt text fails under
§1's pressure; carried by a bundle predicate over typed fields, it fails closed.

WHAT

1. The class predicate as a bundle object: input = the typed fields + the §8 flag
   (bead R3's presence check); output = a scrutiny class. The top class — a claim whose
   scope names the target family and whose claimed property is a solve below the
   generic bound, by any method — requires ladder KEEP where the claim is algorithmic,
   the formalization gate and statement review where it is a theorem, reproducibility,
   and the §10 expert sign-off; the tier gate issues no Tier-3 ticket without all of
   them.

2. Monotonicity: the orchestrator may request a class and can never lower one — the
   router's assignment is a floor, and the request path accepts only upward requests.

3. The tier-gate read: the gate judges launches against the scrutiny class the router
   assigned (§5's three gate-owned objects) — wire the class into the gate's inputs so
   the gap-A fixture "a claim naming the target family with a sub-generic cost model is
   routed to the top class and holds no Tier-3 ticket without the §10 sign-off" holds
   live (corpus bead C5 plants it).

4. The §10 expert sign-off as a human-path record kind, owned here because this bead's
   criteria are the only ones that read a recorded sign-off and no other M1 bead writes
   one: src/cairn/attest.py ships `KINDS = ("review_verdict", "waiver")`, so the sign-off
   is a third kind — a canonical record the operator appends to the attestation file,
   mirrored as a substrate row carrying the record's digest and file offset, read under
   §4's absent-unless-the-digest-matches rule. That is the shape bead R3 gives
   `nogo_review` and bead H1 gives `acknowledgment`. A sign-off names the one statement
   hash it signs and does not transfer to a superseding version. Scope: the gate's READ of
   the record is this bead's; the `expert_signoff` human-queue class and the enqueue a
   refusal makes are bead H1's, and this bead neither builds nor asserts them.

DONE WHEN classification is a pure function of typed fields + flag; the top-class rule
fires on a planted target-family sub-generic-bound claim; a lowering request is
refused; the tier gate refuses Tier 3 without the sign-off for a top-class claim.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_scrutiny_router.py (unit: predicate over typed fields,
monotone requests, no prose input anywhere in the signature);
tests/integration/test_router_tier_gate.py (integration: top-class claim end to end to
the Tier-3 refusal).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a claim naming the target family with a cost model below the generic bound
  classifies to the top class; a tightened-bound claim classifies lower; classification
  reads typed fields only (signature pinned by a test); runs pasted.
- Planted negative: an orchestrator-shaped request to lower a class is refused; a
  top-class claim's Tier-3 request without the expert sign-off is refused at the tier
  gate with THIS bead's own sign-off-absent reason present BY MEMBERSHIP, never tuple
  equality — the shipped gate already refuses every Tier-3 launch on TICKET_ABSENT and
  TIER_TWO_ABOVE alone (src/cairn/tiergate.py:82-85, whose only ticket kind is the
  tier-0 hypothesis object), so a refusal carrying only those two is the M0 gate
  answering and proves nothing this bead wired, and the assertion fails on it; the
  same launch with the sign-off recorded no longer carries that reason; prose fields
  are unreachable by the predicate (no text argument exists).
- Planted negative: a sign-off row whose digest matches no record at its file offset is
  absent to the gate, so the top-class Tier-3 refusal still carries this bead's
  sign-off-absent reason; a sign-off naming a different statement hash leaves it carried
  likewise — both asserted on rows, so "recorded" means attested and not merely written.
- No-Claim: routing assigns scrutiny; it grants nothing — the obligations it names are
  discharged by the gates that own them, and accept_for_tiering (bead R3) satisfies
  none of the top class's obligations.

title: M1 epistemics: the no-go presence check and the nogo_review node — flag consumers wired into router and tier gate
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §8). Any proposed attack on the target must state how it evades all three
no-gos — (1) Shoup √n: must exploit named curve-specific structure, not generic ops;
(2) isogeny invariance: order and embedding degree are invariant, walking cannot help;
(3) prime-field index-calculus obstruction: no efficient point decomposition over prime
fields, Weil-descent/GHS/summation-polynomial methods need F_{q^n}, n>1 — or be flagged
almost-certainly-broken. The gate is mechanical in the PRESENCE dimension only; the
content of a declared evasion is reviewed by the Skeptic and the human, never by this
gate.

WHAT

1. The declaration: a content-addressed node the branch points at, outside the
   hypothesis key (its words are prose). A missing or empty declaration is an automatic
   flag.

2. The flag's consumers, wired: the router (bead R2) routes a flagged attack to the top
   scrutiny class; the tier gate grants a flagged branch no Tier-1 ticket while the
   declaration is absent (the §5 presence check) and no ticket above Tier 1 until a
   nogo_review records accept_for_tiering. This bead computes the flag, makes it a gate
   input and owns the flagged-branch refusal's fixture; bead B5 (cairn-m1-cqt.4.5) is the
   single author of the Tier-1 ticket predicate and reads this flag as one of its two
   composed inputs, the §7 pre-filter verdict (bead F8) being the other. This bead blocks
   B5, so the flag exists before the predicate that reads it is written.

3. The nogo_review node: {hypothesis hash, declaration hash, reviewer, verdict ∈
   {accept_for_tiering, reject, needs_revision}, gate-bundle hash, time, supersedes?},
   immutable, written only through the §4 human path as a review_verdict is; absence is
   the flag. accept_for_tiering restores ordinary ticket eligibility ONLY — it is no
   claim tag and satisfies none of the top scrutiny class's obligations.

DONE WHEN a target-attack branch without a declaration holds no Tier-1 ticket; with a
declaration but no review, nothing above Tier 1; with accept_for_tiering, ordinary
eligibility returns; a nogo_review outside the attestation path is invisible to readers.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_nogo_presence.py (unit: presence predicate, flag
computation, node shape); tests/integration/test_nogo_tier_wiring.py (integration: the
three eligibility states against the tier gate; attestation digest discipline on the
node).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a target-attack branch with a declaration and an attested accept_for_tiering
  regains ordinary ticket eligibility — at Tier 1 as an admission, and above Tier 1 as
  the disappearance of this bead's own no-review reason rather than as an admission,
  since bead B5's ticket lattice lands after this bead and the M0 gate still answers
  TIER_TWO_ABOVE on every Tier-2 launch; the review node's digest matches its
  attestation record; rows pasted.
- Planted negative: the same branch with no declaration is refused a Tier-1 ticket — a
  refusal the M0 gate does not make on its own, since a Tier-1 launch holding a recorded
  hypothesis object is admitted there, so the Tier-1 half stands unaided; with a
  declaration and no review, the launch above Tier 1 carries THIS bead's own no-review
  reason present BY MEMBERSHIP, never tuple equality — TIER_TWO_ABOVE alone is the M0
  gate answering, the only ticket kind until bead B5 being the tier-0 hypothesis object
  (src/cairn/tiergate.py:84-85, :109-115), and the assertion fails on it; an
  accept_for_tiering offered as satisfying a top-class obligation changes nothing there;
  a nogo_review row with no matching attestation digest is absent to readers.
- No-Claim: presence is the only mechanical dimension — nothing here judges whether an
  evasion argument is sound; that stays with the Skeptic's notes and the human.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_nogo_presence.py,
  tests/integration/test_nogo_tier_wiring.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

title: M1 epistemics: the counterexample-hunt record — frozen sampler, SURVIVED/KILLED/INCOMPLETE semantics, KILLED writes the ledger and refutes
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7 strong law of small numbers). A small-case pattern is a conjecture
until it survives larger cases plus a deliberate counterexample hunt. The algorithmic
ticket has a table shape the gate can read; the conjecture ticket needs one too, or the
tier gate reads an orchestrator's prose.

WHAT

1. The counterexample-hunt record, a substrate node: {statement hash, sampling
   distribution D (content-addressed), pre-registered budget (trial count, family
   bounds), the gate's entropy commitment and seeds (the §6 instance-maker rule — bead
   S4's derivation, hunt-domain-tagged), per-trial outcomes, any counterexample with its
   verifier status, verdict ∈ {SURVIVED, KILLED, INCOMPLETE}}.

2. The frozen sampler: the hunt samples from the DECLARED D exactly — the sampler is
   frozen against the declared distribution the way the ladder freezes method identity;
   a hunt run whose sampler disagrees with D is refused before any trial.

3. Verdict semantics: SURVIVED under the declared budget = the Tier-2 ticket for a
   conjecture (bead B5's lattice reads it). KILLED — by a counterexample that passed
   its verifier — writes the §4 ledger entry (bead R1) and moves the claim version to
   terminal `refuted` (justify's Refutation path exists in src/cairn/justify.py; wire
   the hunt into it). INCOMPLETE — the §5 ceiling stopped the hunt before its declared
   trial count, status BUDGET_EXCEEDED — is no ticket. Without this node the
   conjecture's tag ceiling is CONJECTURE.

DONE WHEN a hunt runs against a planted-false small-case conjecture and KILLs it with a
verified counterexample (fixture (e)'s behavior; the corpus entry is bead C4's); a
planted-true conjecture SURVIVEs its declared budget and mints ticket standing; a
ceiling-stopped hunt lands INCOMPLETE with no ticket.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_hunt_record.py (unit: record fields, verdict rules, frozen-
sampler refusal); tests/integration/test_counterexample_hunt.py (integration: KILLED
with verifier-passed counterexample + ledger entry + refuted transition; SURVIVED path;
INCOMPLETE path).
design:
## Architecture
- Approach: a dedicated hunt module owns a canonical distribution, preregistered trial/family budget, domain-separated entropy seeds, ordered trial records, and the SURVIVED/KILLED/INCOMPLETE decision. The coordinator binds its sampler to the hypothesis distribution before execution, derives outcomes from real trial execution and counterexample verification, persists the full record, and exposes its evidence through the existing claims/ledger/justify interfaces. A caller-supplied verdict is rejected as an authority boundary. Generic evidence rows alone are insufficient because they cannot preserve the sampling and verification transcript. The initial sampler is gate-owned uniform integer sampling over declared finite parameter bounds; the record explicitly states that distribution, and other distribution kinds must have their own implementation before admission.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/instances.py; src/cairn/claims.py; src/cairn/ledger.py; tests/integration/test_ledger_entry_writers.py
- Touches: src/cairn/hunt.py, src/cairn/justify.py only where the real record needs joining, tests/unit/test_hunt_record.py, tests/integration/test_counterexample_hunt.py. Any shared schema addition requires coordination before editing.
- ADRs: PLAN.md section 7 strong law of small numbers; no new ADR.
- Data model impact: canonical hunt plan/distribution/run nodes and lineage using existing node storage; a typed evidence envelope for existing consumers. No table migration planned.
- Execution boundary: executor and verifier are trusted harness adapters, each returning a real runner.Attempt whose stored recipe, receipt, manifest and output are reread. The plan pins their identities; recipes bind the sampled-input blob and seed, and output binds the plan, statement, trial, point and executor output where applicable. Detached result objects, caller-supplied verification booleans, cached attempts and mismatched bindings refuse. Tests use real subprocess adapters with independently checked arithmetic, not fabricated attempt rows. This is not authentication of arbitrary caller-supplied gate configuration.
- Failure modes: sampler mismatch before a trial executes (named refusal and zero trial invocations); a failed counterexample verifier incorrectly killing a claim (record verdict and statement status); a ceiling-stopped run supplying standing (INCOMPLETE record plus BUDGET_EXCEEDED attempt and absent standing).

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] instances.py:82-154 implements a committed nonce lifecycle with one nonce per run and publication after execution; its ladder seed needs a separate hunt domain. Source read 2026-09-08 (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R2] claims.py:63-76 and :445-469 persist only the generic evidence envelope, so the full hunt transcript needs a separately hashed node linked to it. Source read 2026-09-08 (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH).
- [R3] ledger.py:211-263 already accepts measured KILLED hunt evidence and derives its retry predicate; justify.py:404-463 drives terminal refuted from Refutation. Source reads plus uv run pytest -q tests/integration/test_ledger_entry_writers.py::test_a_killed_shaped_entry_lands_as_measured_on_the_hunt_record tests/unit/test_justify_rules.py: 75 passed, 973 warnings, 21.57s. Raw output /tmp/cairn-session-a.vgwPnp/hunt-prior-art.log (verified: 2026-09-08; Confidence: HIGH). This verifies seeded prior art, not a real hunt.
- [R4] The full coordinator, frozen sampler and complete transcript have not been executed; they are the implementation deliverable, not established stack facts (documented: bead .8.4 acceptance; Confidence: HIGH).
- Delegability: STATEABLE. Exact positive and planted negatives remain the bead acceptance criteria; finite-distribution survival is never a theorem about the family.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a planted-false conjecture's hunt returns KILLED with a verifier-passed
  counterexample, the ledger entry written and the claim version at terminal refuted; a
  planted-true conjecture SURVIVEs its declared budget; both runs pasted.
- Planted negative: a hunt whose sampler draws outside the declared D is refused before
  any trial; an INCOMPLETE hunt mints no ticket standing; a counterexample failing its
  verifier does not KILL.
- No-Claim: SURVIVED is ticket standing under the declared budget and D — evidence about
  D, never about the family; the P1 quantitative floor is bead R8's separate decision.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_hunt_record.py,
  tests/integration/test_counterexample_hunt.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.

title: M1 epistemics: the reproducibility gate's re-run policy by grade and tier, and the Verifiable owner rule
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §3 reproducibility gate, §13 M1). Admission re-runs the recipe (or
re-checks the witness) and compares bitwise; on divergence the second copy is kept,
rooted, as evidence of non-reproducibility and the node is marked inadmissible. The
policy is fixed by grade and tier and budgeted before launch. An unconditional re-run
doubles the cost of exactly what the tier system rations; the cap keeps a cheaper
policy from becoming a silent promotion.

WHAT

1. The policy, fixed by grade and tier: Verifiable ⇒ the witness is always checked;
   Replayable at Tier 0/1 ⇒ always re-run; Replayable at Tier 2/3 ⇒ re-run at the
   moment `justify` would derive a class above CONJECTURE from the node (the derivation
   WAITS on it), otherwise sampled later with the claim's tag capped at CONJECTURE
   meanwhile (the auditor arrives at M4; before it, the deferred re-run stands until
   justify draws it).

2. Divergence semantics: for a Replayable recipe, two successful non-disowned attempts
   with different output manifests mark the recipe non-reproducible and inadmissible,
   both attempts kept and rooted; every reproducibility-gate re-run sets
   skip_cache_lookup (fresh attempt, never overwrite).

3. The Verifiable owner rule: Verifiable is assigned only where the verifier is a
   gate-bundle object or a certified skill whose §2 identity bundle differs from the
   witness producer's and whose self-test carries a must-FAIL witness; a witness whose
   only verifier ships in its producer's own revision is graded AuditOnly — and
   AuditOnly is inadmissible as evidence. Grades only weaken (grade_history exists in
   the schema).

4. Escrow wiring: the policy's first check is where bead B1's spend fires; the deferred
   Tier-2/3 case is why reservations survive terminal branches.

DONE WHEN each grade × tier cell behaves per the table; a planted divergence marks
non-reproducible with both attempts rooted (fixture (i)'s behavior); the owner rule
grades a producer-verified witness AuditOnly (fixture (m)'s third clause); the deferred
re-run fires exactly when justify derives.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_repro_policy.py (unit: the grade × tier decision table, the
owner rule); tests/integration/test_repro_gate.py (integration: divergence handling,
deferred-derivation trigger, skip_cache_lookup on re-runs). The spend the policy's
first check fires is bead B1's assertion — B1 owns escrow settlement and this bead
blocks B1, so at this close `substrate.add_escrow` still inserts a row nothing sets
`spent_at` on and there is no settlement API to observe.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a Verifiable node's witness is checked at admission; a Tier-1 Replayable
  re-runs immediately; a Tier-2 Replayable's re-run fires when justify derives above
  CONJECTURE and the derivation waits on it; runs pasted.
- Planted negative: a planted second attempt with a different manifest marks the recipe
  non-reproducible and inadmissible with both attempts rooted; a witness whose only
  verifier ships in its producer's revision grades AuditOnly and justifies nothing; a
  re-run served from cache fails the test.
- No-Claim: the policy proves when checks fire; sampling cadence and the audit line are
  M4's auditor — before it, deferred nodes wait capped at CONJECTURE, and nothing here
  claims that gap is covered.
- Test types: unit (decision table), integration. Files: tests/unit/test_repro_policy.py,
  tests/integration/test_repro_gate.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

title: M1 epistemics: the transitive justified_by query and the downgrade re-derivation walk (fixture h)
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7; fixture (h)). The foundations auditor's core query is transitive: no
claim, of any class, may carry a justified_by edge at any depth to a strictly weaker
premise, and a failed re-verification downgrades the node AND re-derives every claim
transitively justified by it. The auditor's sampling cadence arrives at M4; the QUERY
and the re-derivation walk are M1's, because fixture (h) exercises them and the yank
path (bead B2) already needs the walk.

WHAT

1. The transitive query over the justified_by DAG: given a claim version, walk its
   justification closure and report any edge at any depth whose premise class is
   strictly weaker than the class the dependent claim carries — the lattice violation
   fixture (h) plants (a PROVEN claim with a weaker premise in its transitive closure).

2. The re-derivation walk: on a node's downgrade (failed re-verification, disown), every
   claim transitively justified by it re-derives through justify; tags move only by the
   append-only tag-history discipline with evidence pointers.

3. Shared machinery: bead B2's yank propagation and bead R5's divergence handling both
   trigger the same walk — one implementation, three callers.

DONE WHEN the query finds a planted deep weak premise (three hops down) and reports the
path; a downgrade re-derives the closure with tag history showing evidence-bearing
transitions; no false positive on a chain of equal-or-stronger premises.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_justified_by_query.py (unit: lattice comparison, path
reporting, property over random DAGs — no weaker-premise chain escapes, no clean chain
flagged); tests/integration/test_transitive_rederivation.py (integration: downgrade →
closure re-derivation with history).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a planted PROVEN claim resting on a CONJECTURE premise three hops down is
  found with its path named; a downgrade of a mid-DAG node re-derives every dependent
  claim; runs pasted.
- Planted negative: a clean closure (equal-or-stronger premises throughout) yields no
  finding under the property test's generated cases; a re-derivation that would move a
  tag without an evidence pointer is refused by the tag-history discipline.
- No-Claim: the query and walk prove structure; sampling cadence, strata and the
  spot-check bound are the M4 auditor's — nothing here schedules audits.
- Test types: unit, property, integration. Files:
  tests/unit/test_justified_by_query.py, tests/integration/test_transitive_rederivation.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

title: M1 epistemics: justify's cost-model scoping and producer-standing ceiling live on real evidence; context reads recipe inputs through attempt_id
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §7 kind map; §2 producer standing; fixtures (f), (g), (m);
cairn-m0-e0s.12's handoff on cairn-m1-cqt.1's comments). src/cairn/justify.py ships the
rules against synthetic evidence; M1 is where they meet real producers, and where one
recorded correction lands.

WHAT

1. Cost-model scoping, live: a statement whose typed fields carry a cost model takes
   STRONG-EMPIRICAL from a ladder_table produced by a ladder gate run and from NO other
   kind — a statistical or repro_node offered for it returns the CONJECTURE ceiling
   (fixture (m)'s second clause), because a cost measured by the party claiming it is
   the §6(3) failure. Fixture (f): a claim seeking STRONG-EMPIRICAL with no repro node
   is capped. Fixture (g): statistical evidence offered for PROVEN returns a lattice
   violation.

2. Producer-standing ceiling, live: where the producer is a certified skill rather than
   a gate-bundle object or gate run, a revision whose self-test record carries no
   STRONG-EMPIRICAL basis covering the attempt's inputs — every corpus origin
   author_supplied, no randomized-postcondition arm, no cross-check whose declared
   independent range contains them — caps the node at CONJECTURE (fixture (m)'s
   author_supplied clause).

3. The recorded correction (from the m0-justify handoff): context_for reads the
   attempt's inputs from the evidence node's own population.param_ranges; at M0 the two
   agree by construction. A real ladder_table names an attempt_id whose recipe carries
   the inputs actually run, and those are the inputs the rule means — a node declaring
   a wide population over a narrow run would read as covered when it is not. Feed
   context_for the recipe inputs reached through attempt_id and drop the population
   fallback for nodes that carry one.

4. Callers handle the sixth result: justify returns Refutation(evidence_hash) beyond
   the five-way union its M0 bead declared; every M1 caller added by these beads
   handles it (the hunt bead R4 produces it).

DONE WHEN fixtures (f), (g) and (m)'s justify clauses hold against REAL evidence nodes
(a real table, a real self-test record); the context_for change reads recipe inputs
with the wide-population case caught by a test.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_justify_cost_scoping.py (unit: kind-map rules per fixture
clause); tests/integration/test_justify_live_producers.py (integration: real table and
self-test records through justify; the wide-population-narrow-run case).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: a real ladder_table with its repro record justifies STRONG-EMPIRICAL for a
  covered cost-model statement; the recipe-inputs path resolves context through
  attempt_id; runs pasted.
- Planted negative: a statistical node offered for the same cost-model statement returns
  the CONJECTURE ceiling; statistical-for-PROVEN returns a lattice violation; an
  author_supplied-only producer's node caps at CONJECTURE; a node declaring a wide
  population over a narrow real run is caught as not covering.
- No-Claim: kind-map scoping proves what evidence can justify; it neither runs the
  ladder nor reviews statements, and fixture entries under tests/planted/ are corpus
  bead C4's.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_justify_cost_scoping.py,
