title: M1 epistemics: the §15 P1 small-numbers floor — e-process built minimally, decided on planted-false conjectures, adopt-or-drop recorded
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §15 P1; §13 M1's closing item). Whether the small-numbers gate gains a
pre-registered quantitative floor is DECIDED at M1 with planted-false conjectures. The
candidate: a betting e-process on sampled instances — the Experimentalist declares a
sampling distribution D over the family, ε, α and a seed before sampling (all hashed
into the claim, so a new D is a new claim and the orchestrator cannot tune D toward
clean cases), accumulating E_t = ∏(1 − λ_t(X_t − ε)) with λ_t ∈ [0, 1/(1−ε)] against
H₀ "P fails with probability ≥ ε under D"; Tier-2 spend on PROVING the conjecture would
require E ≥ 1/α. It is about D, never the family; it never promotes a tag; log₁₀E is a
numeric attribute, not a sub-grade.

WHAT

1. A minimal implementation sufficient to run the experiment (the e-process
   accumulator, the pre-registration hashing, the wealth threshold).

2. The experiment: on planted-false conjectures at honest ε — hundreds to thousands of
   clean cases — measure whether the floor ever changes a decision the counterexample hunt
   would not already make. Bead R4 ships one such conjecture (the fixture (e) behavior);
   this bead authors the rest against R4's hunt machinery and its declared-D freezing, so
   the ≥ 3 below has a named author rather than a corpus R4 does not carry.

3. The decision, recorded with the runs: adopt (the floor becomes a bundle-configured
   resource gate before Tier-2 spend, never a tag promoter, never in the orchestrator's
   reward) or drop (record the evidence it never bound; the implementation stays as an
   experiment artifact, unwired). The §7 statistical-monitor invariant binds either
   way: block or alarm, never promote — an adopted floor that could promote is a
   gate-layer change review must refuse.

DONE WHEN the experiment ran on ≥ 3 planted-false conjectures with honest ε; the
decision is recorded with numbers; if adopted, the wiring carries a planted test that a
passing E can never move a tag; if dropped, the record names what never bound.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_small_numbers_floor.py (unit: e-process arithmetic, wealth
bound, λ range, pre-registration hashing; the never-promotes planted test in either
outcome).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: the e-process accumulates correctly on hand-checkable sequences; the
  experiment's runs on planted-false conjectures exist with ε, α, seeds and outcomes
  pasted; the adopt-or-drop decision is recorded with its evidence.
- Planted negative: a passing E offered as tag evidence moves nothing (the
  never-promotes test); a D re-declared after sampling hashes to a different claim.
- No-Claim: the decision is about whether the floor BINDS at honest ε on the planted
  set; adoption would gate Tier-2 spend only, and dropping refutes usefulness on this
  evidence, not validity.
- Test types: unit, experiment. Files: tests/unit/test_small_numbers_floor.py.

title: M1 alarms: the §15 P4 drift monitors — split-conformal flag and the measured-versus-declared e-process, wired to cost_drift, moving nothing
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §15 P4; gap B of the epic's decomposition comment — no bead builds the
monitors whose firing behavior M2's keep-or-drop decision judges). The alarms are
strategy-layer drift monitors, never enforcement: the per-run budget ceiling is
enforcement; these watch. A fired alarm is a human-queue item of class cost_drift and a
strategy input the orchestrator's tick may read to park with budget_preempt; it moves no
tag, ticket or scrutiny class. Their inputs exist from M1: the ladder's tables, the
self-test records, the receipts, tier_refusals.

WHAT — both monitors and their wiring (one module; the keep-or-drop decision is
cairn-m2-vgh's, judged on whether either fires on anything the ladder or the ceiling
misses):

1. The split-conformal anomaly flag on ladder and self-test measurements: an
   order-statistic threshold over a calibration split, returning +∞ when the sample is
   too small for the requested coverage — never clamping. A measurement beyond the
   threshold flags.

2. The one-sided bounded-mean e-process on log(measured/declared cost), read from the
   execution receipts' measured-versus-declared ratio (the §5 reconciliation, bead B7,
   makes the ratio a recorded fact); wealth crossing its threshold flags.

3. The third input: repeated TierRefused records on one hypothesis key (the
   tier_refusals table), a count-based input to the same flag surface.

4. Wiring: a fired alarm enqueues cost_drift (bead H1) with the branch or key it names.
   The §7 invariant, planted as a test: no alarm state reaches any tag, ticket or
   scrutiny input — the monitors' outputs are readable by the queue and the strategy
   layer alone.

DONE WHEN each monitor fires on a planted drift (a receipt stream whose measured costs
run hot against declared; a measurement far outside the calibration distribution; a
refusal burst on one key) and enqueues cost_drift; the too-small-sample case returns +∞
and fires nothing; the never-moves-anything invariant is a test.

TEST PLAN — tests/unit/test_conformal_flag.py (unit: order-statistic threshold, +∞ on
small samples); tests/unit/test_cost_eprocess.py (unit: e-process arithmetic on planted
streams); tests/integration/test_alarms_queue.py (integration: fired → cost_drift item;
invariant test that alarms reach no gate input).
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: each of the three inputs, planted with drift, fires its flag and enqueues a
  cost_drift item naming the branch or key; runs pasted.
- Planted negative: a calibration sample below the coverage's minimum returns +∞ and
  never fires; a fired alarm changes no tag, no ticket standing and no scrutiny class —
  asserted by the invariant test, not by absence of code.
- No-Claim: fired-or-quiet behavior on planted streams is all M1 proves; whether the
  monitors catch anything real that the ladder and ceiling miss is M2's keep-or-drop
  question (cairn-m2-vgh), and a monitor that never does is dropped there.
- Test types: unit, integration. Files: tests/unit/test_conformal_flag.py,
  tests/unit/test_cost_eprocess.py, tests/integration/test_alarms_queue.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and

title: M2 — memory: dead-end ledger preflight (refuted-by-hypothesis-key vs parked) + Formalizer worker + statement-review workflow + hash-chained log with head checkpoint
description:
SCOPE (PLAN §13 M2): Dead-end ledger (refuted-by-hypothesis-key vs parked) + the Formalizer worker + the statement-review workflow (the formalization gate and the pre-filters it submits to are M1's). Decompose into child beads when M1 closes; nothing here is pre-decomposed. Operator decision 7: §15 P5 (conformal surprise per claim class as an extra scrutiny trigger — a claimed effect in the top-α of its class's historical claims raises scrutiny and can never lower it, never promotes a tag and never enters the orchestrator's reward) is decided here, at its decide-by milestone: whether it adds anything beyond "bigger claim ⇒ more scrutiny". §15 P4 (operational alarms: the split-conformal anomaly flag on ladder and self-test measurements, the bounded-mean e-process on `log(measured/declared cost)`, repeated `TierRefused` records as a third input — strategy-layer drift monitors that move no tag, ticket or scrutiny class; described in the M1 epic cairn-m1-cqt) has decide-by M1–M2 and its keep-or-drop decision is recorded here by M2 close: an alarm that never fires on anything the ladder or the ceiling misses is dropped.

DONE WHEN: a parked branch auto-revives on blocker-clear; a refuted hypothesis key is `Blocked` unaided; a proposal whose declared region contains a measured REFUTED point for the same method and cost model is `Blocked` though its key is fresh; a `supersedes` edge into a REFUTED version with an unmet retry predicate parks with `supersedes_refuted_review` until the attributed difference statement is recorded; a refutation without a null arm parks the proposal with `null_control_pending`, the blocker clears when the re-measurement lands, and the preflight then answers `Allowed` — with the table as the evidence that met the retry predicate — when the re-measurement did not REJECT and `Blocked` when it did; a proposal differing from a `measured` REFUTED entry only in implementation revision is `Blocked`, while one differing from an `implementation` entry by a certified new revision is `Allowed`; a new branch opened on a key a promoted branch holds — or whose claim statement stands at STRONG-EMPIRICAL after the branch that earned it withdrew — or on a sub-region of such a holder's region with the same method identity and cost model, parks with `already_settled` until a superseding object with its difference statement is recorded; a log truncated to an earlier valid prefix fails startup verification against the checkpoint — also when the truncated log has been re-extended and its forked head appended to the checkpoint, since every older checkpointed head must remain a prefix head (§3) — and an unreachable checkpoint blocks promotion; a worker that returns with a claim it opened still open yields a `Leaked` record while a harness-terminated attempt yields none; and a green Lean artifact with no `review_verdict` stays below PROVEN while the statement-review workflow routes it to the human queue.

ADDS: the ledger preflight (`Allowed | Blocked | RequiresNullControl | AlreadySettled`) with its measured-point reach, `supersedes_refuted_review`, `null_control_pending` and `already_settled` parks with the null-control resolution rule, the hash-chained log (`chain = H(domain ‖ prior_chain ‖ canonical_record)`) and its head checkpoint (a file beside the gate-bundle pin carrying the append-only flag — M0 grounded what that flag refuses; the second OS user arrives at M3 per decision 8), the terminal-status invariant, the statement-review workflow routing green artifacts to the human queue and recording `review_verdict` nodes through the human path, and the near-duplicate advisory (64-bit SimHash over hypothesis text; advisory only) routed to the human or to a `near_dup_review` park (Librarian routing arrives at M4).
acceptance_criteria:
- Every done-when clause maps to a named test run at close; the preflight answers are typed and never default to Allowed.
- Planted negative (epic level): a log truncated to an earlier valid prefix (and the re-extended, forked-head variant) must fail startup verification; a preflight on a refuted hypothesis key must not answer `Allowed`; a green Lean artifact without a `review_verdict` must stay below PROVEN; a worker returning with an open claim must yield a `Leaked` record — any of these passing silently fails the epic.
- No-Claim: ledger teeth are proven on synthetic and M1-generated entries; the orchestrator that would walk the tree is M3.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
FROM cairn-m0-e0s.13 (GC roots + reachability), a property M2 has to know.

`src/cairn/gc.py` roots liveness in the `roots` table, whose CHECK constraint
(`src/cairn/schema.sql:24-28`) admits four kinds only: recipe, ledger_row,
certificate, divergence. `reachable()` walks `lineage` undirected from those rows,
and every blob with no path to one of them is collectable.

M2's hash-chained log and its checkpoints are therefore NOT roots. A blob whose only
reference is a log entry or a checkpoint is collectable today, and `cairn gc --yes`
will delete it. This is the No-Claim line .13 closed under, not an oversight in it.

M2 has to do two things when it lands: add its root kind(s) to the `roots` CHECK
constraint, and insert a roots row as it writes each log checkpoint. The lineage
edges from a checkpoint to the blobs it covers must exist too, since reachability
reads `lineage` and nothing else.

Verified at cairn-m0-e0s.13's close commit: a blob reachable from a rooted node
survives collection and an unrooted one does not, mutation-proved by
`scripts/mutation-check.sh src/cairn/gc.py "    return set(blobs) - reachable(roots, edges)" "    return set(blobs)" tests/integration/test_gc.py tests/unit/test_gc_properties.py tests/unit/test_gc_reachability.py`
-> KILLED by 15 test(s).

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
Design note from cairn-lnz (skills fit for /lean-proof-mastery-with-epistemic-humility, v6, skill_hash sha256:1b027976b6694978c4fc2cd6b48f84602fcf40f41921674224afb7b8991f7ef5). Source: research/briefs/skills-fit-lean-proof-mastery.md §6, rows 10 and 25 of §3. Decomposition still waits for M1 close; these are inputs to it, each tagged INFERRED.

1. Dead-end ledger entry shape. An entry carries six fields: the exact rejected claim (the claim statement hash), the first unsupported step, the witness or diagnostic (a hash of the artifact), the checked survivors (lemma names with their own axiom sets), the scope of the attempt (toolchain, mathlib revision, wall time, route), and the reopening condition. `refuted` versus `parked` is a disposition over that record, not a replacement for it. A ledger preflight that answers "this dead end was walked" without the reopening condition cannot say whether it is worth re-walking.

2. Typed statement-change proposal. The Formalizer's submission gains `proposed_statement_change`: a new informal statement plus the reason, routed to the human queue as a `statement_review` item and never applied by the worker. A Solution proving `H -> T` for a new premise `H` is a different statement and fails the gate's closure comparison; it is submitted against a new claim statement node carrying `H`, and the record links the two. The worker may propose a change and never adopt one silently.

3. How the skill reaches the Formalizer without entering the tree. The Prover role template for the Formalizer names the skill by name, version and skill_hash as the discipline the worker runs under; the harness loads the skill from the operator's machine at dispatch, and the dispatch record (W1) pins the loaded file's sha256 beside the template hash. The skill's text is proprietary and stays outside the tree and the gate bundle; the ledger fact is which version ran. The trade: a file outside the bundle is not pinned by the bundle hash, so the dispatch record is its only pin. Operator decision at M2.

4. Skeptic checklist items P-62a (independence axes) and P-62b (four statement-audit items) are M1 work on cairn-m1-cqt.6.2; the Formalizer inherits them unchanged.

title: M3 — orchestrator: branch tree + bandit + info-per-dollar allocation + structured self-redesign (data, not gates); crash-safe ticks; second OS user for the process (decision 8)
description:
SCOPE (PLAN §13 M3): Branch tree + bandit + info-per-dollar allocation + structured self-redesign (data, not gates). Decompose when M2 closes. The orchestrator may rewrite the branch tree, funding and prompts — never the gates, calibration taxonomy, ladder, verifier, no-go checklist, or what counts as proven (CLAUDE.md). Operator decision 8: the separate OS user for the orchestrator process arrives here (the pin and attestation file then bind by ownership, not only by mode); decision 3: Tier-2 spend no longer requires an open operator session once the orchestrator exists — revisit then.

DONE WHEN: on ≥ 20 seeded runs each containing a stalled branch — gate-outcome yield over the last `k` ticks indistinguishable from zero — it is force-parked with blocker `low_yield_pivot` within `m` ticks unaided, with `k` and `m` pinned in the M3 test plan; no REFUTED row and no terminal `withdrawn` status is written by the orchestrator's path in any run; the parked branch auto-revives when its pinned predicate clears; a crash mid-tick resumes without double-applying a completed step (§15 P3), every attempt in flight at the crash standing at `INTERRUPTED` on restart — never OK, never a leak; on seeded runs holding one branch whose hypothesis is the known true advance of control (j) and one whose hypothesis is fixture (a)'s method, the orchestrator's own dispatch carries the first to KEEP and a STRONG-EMPIRICAL tag through `justify` and the second to a measured REFUTED entry, unaided — the motion half of the bar; on seeded runs where one branch family pre-registers `k` junk cost models or jittered regions on one method, that family does not out-earn control (j)'s branch under the allocation surrogate (a cheap REJECT at the 30-bit rung is a gate outcome, and a surrogate that pays for it per cost would teach REJECT farming). Decides the allocation mechanics and crash-safe tick shape (§15 P3, P6) against that bar, including whether a bandit earns its place at all.
acceptance_criteria:
- ≥20 seeded runs with the named outcomes; `k`, `m` pinned in the test plan; the orchestrator's path writes no REFUTED row and no withdrawn status in any run (asserted by query).
- Planted negative (epic level): a seeded run whose stalled branch is not parked with `low_yield_pivot` within `m` ticks fails; a crash mid-tick that double-applies a step or leaves an in-flight attempt at any status but `INTERRUPTED` fails; a junk-cost-model family out-earning control (j) under the surrogate fails — any of these fails the epic.
- No-Claim: seeded synthetic runs; the allocation surrogate is gate-outcome reward per measured cost until M3 decides otherwise.

title: The review-verdict reader re-derives a row's digest from its fields, as the acknowledgment and nogo_review readers do
description:
CONTEXT. Three readers decide whether a human-path row counts. `human_queue._acknowledgment_row_matches` (src/cairn/human_queue.py) rebuilds the acknowledgment from the row's fields and compares its digest to the row's stored digest before consulting the attestation file; `nogo.row_visible` (src/cairn/nogo.py, bead cairn-m1-cqt.8.3) re-derives a nogo_review's digest from the row's fields and requires the attestation record at its offset to be that digest. `claims.visible_review_verdicts` (src/cairn/claims.py, `verdict_matches_file`) passes the row's STORED `record_digest` to `attest.attestation_record_matches`, so a review_verdicts row whose fields were tampered while its stored digest and offset still name a real record in the file is visible: justify.context_for reads `approved` from it, and human_queue's `_attestation_binding` compares a closure's digest against the same stored column.

WHAT. Make the review-verdict reader re-derive: rebuild `claims.ReviewVerdict` from the row's fields (statement_hash, reviewer, verdict, checklist_template_hash, gate_bundle_hash, at, supersedes, file_offset), require the rebuilt `record_digest` to equal the stored one and to be the record at the row's offset; a row failing either is absent to `visible_review_verdicts`, to `justify.context_for` (`approved`) and to `_attestation_binding`. Mirror nogo.row_visible's shape so the three readers read alike; a shared helper in attest.py is acceptable if it takes the rebuilt digest, not the row.

TEST PLAN. tests/unit/test_claims_visible_verdicts.py (unit: an honest row is visible; a row whose stored digest names a real record but whose fields differ is invisible; a row whose stored digest disagrees with its fields is invisible even when the file holds the fields' record); tests/integration/test_justify.py gains one case: an approved lean_artifact whose verdict row was forged derives Pending, not PROVEN. Planted negative shown by mutation on a scratch copy: removing the re-derivation makes the forged-row test pass its old way.

NO-CLAIM. Green proves the reader derives its verdict from the row's fields and the file; it does not prove the file itself is trustworthy, which is the operator's write boundary.

## Architecture
- Approach: change the predicate, not the storage; one rebuilt-digest check in `claims.visible_review_verdicts` and in `human_queue._attestation_binding`, following `nogo.row_visible`. Rejected: dropping the stored column, since the closure binding and the queue's closure rows key on it.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/nogo.py (`row_visible`, `_review_of`, `mirrored`)
- Touches: src/cairn/claims.py, src/cairn/human_queue.py, tests/unit/test_claims_visible_verdicts.py, tests/integration/test_justify.py
- ADRs: none
- Data model impact: none

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
CLOSED 2026-08-27.

DONE WHEN, clause by clause.

  the migration lands            159 PTH findings -> 0
  PTH in the select list         pyproject.toml line 48
  scripts/check.sh stays green   1838 passed, exit 0
  the write-boundary tests pass  tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py 36 passed

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD TEXT.

The bead says 95 findings across 20 files. Measured at HEAD before touching anything: 159
across 48, the growth being the doctor module and files added since the bead was written.

The bead does not mention RE-CERTIFICATION, and it was required. `src/cairn/pari.py:60`
carried a PTH113 finding, and `pari.py` is in `toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES`, which
`implementation_revision()` hashes byte-for-byte. One `os.path.isfile` call therefore moves
the skill identity. Excluding it was the alternative and was refused: a permanent per-file
lint exemption for one trivial call is not what cairn-fur's standard for exemptions allows.

THE RE-CERTIFICATION, AND WHAT MOVED.

  implementation_revision  ae2b15b0...2419 -> c2d3ec90...7ece
  skill_identity_hash      be2c3574...6a89 -> ecf24823...ad1b

Two goldens moved of 23. `toy_curve_certificate.golden`: one field, `implementation_revision`.
`toy_curve_selftest_transcript.golden`: one record of six.

The transcript's changed record, decoded from its hex rather than read from a summary:

  CHANGED  P  [644105449,676417329] -> [316664663,739552369]
  CHANGED  a  487328381 -> 854200561
  CHANGED  b  284663071 -> 744592367
  CHANGED  n  827952809 -> 998221457
  CHANGED  p  827990353 -> 998256443
  same     bits 30 | cross_check "agree" | outcome "pass" | status "OK"

Records 0-3, the vendored corpus cases, and record 5, the verifier arm at 20/20, are
byte-identical. The five that moved are the drawn curve, and `selftest.run_once` seeds it
with `blake3(implementation_revision || "selftest-seed")`, so they are a direct function of
the identity. Nothing moved that does not depend on it: no verdict, clause result, ledger
entry, count, floor or cost number.

THE NEW CURVE IS VALID, NOT MERELY DIFFERENT. Checked arithmetically rather than assumed:
p = 998256443 is prime; 4a^3 + 27b^2 is nonzero mod p, so the curve is non-singular;
P = (316664663, 739552369) satisfies the curve equation; n = 998221457 is prime and lies in
the Hasse interval [998193252, 998319636]; nP is the identity; and (n-1)P = -P, so P has
exact order n rather than a proper divisor. Since n is prime and is the only multiple of n
in an interval of width about 126000, the group has prime order n. A reseed that produced a
degenerate curve while every test still passed was the worst outcome available here, and
nothing in the suite checks it, so it was checked by hand.

The goldens were regenerated, not hand-edited: `implementation_revision()` recomputed from
the tree yields the value present in the new certificate golden and absent from HEAD's.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND, AND WHAT CHANGED BECAUSE OF IT.

No BLOCKING and no MAJOR: a differential over every migrated os/pathlib pair, against modes
0644/0444/0000, flags UF_APPEND and UF_IMMUTABLE, dangling symlinks, missing paths and
missing parents, comparing exception TYPE and errno, found zero semantic mismatches. The
`pytest.raises(PermissionError)` on the 0444 + append-only pin did not become vacuous.

Two MINOR findings, both real, both fixed.

  `scripts/` sat in the format gate and not the lint gate, so the rule this bead exists to
  enable did not gate it. A probe file with `os.path.join` under `scripts/` passed at exit 0.
  That directory now holds `closing_commit.py`, `audit_attribution.py`, `gate_marker.py` and
  `mutation_verdict.py` -- the logic deciding whether a commit is allowed -- so it is linted
  like the code it gates. `gate lint` reads `src tests scripts`, and the twelve pre-existing
  errors that surfaced were each dispositioned rather than blanket-ignored: two UP017 and one
  FURB167 autofixed, one PERF401 rewritten, five S607 given a `scripts/**` per-file ignore
  because `git`, `br` and `uv` come from PATH by design and `src/` must keep the rule, and
  three EXE001 resolved by removing decorative shebangs from files every call site invokes
  through `uv run python`.

  The two `# noqa: PTH100` exemptions carried a justification nothing bound. Swapping them to
  `Path.resolve()` left 122 tests green. The premise needed correcting first: pytest's
  `tmp_path` is already `/private/var/...` on this machine, so a bare `tmp_path` db cannot
  distinguish `abspath` from `resolve`, which is why the mutation survived. The property is
  now bound by a symlink alias the test builds itself, observed through a delegating spy that
  records and calls through, with two-sided assertions. Both mutations are KILLED.

THE EXEMPTIONS THAT REMAIN, and why. Two sites keep `os.path.abspath`, verified by execution
rather than recalled:

  '/var/tmp/x.db'  abspath -> /var/tmp/x.db   resolve -> /private/var/tmp/x.db
  'a/../b.db'      abspath -> .../b.db        absolute -> .../a/../b.db

`Path.resolve()` follows the symlink and `Path.absolute()` does not normalize `..`, so
neither is a drop-in. Both sites derive a sibling directory of the substrate db, and
resolving would move the tree off the db's own directory.

NO-CLAIM

CI IS NOT GREEN ON THIS TIP AND CANNOT BE. The account's Actions tier is exhausted until
2026-09-01; a dispatched job returns "The job was not started because recent account payments
have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased" in four seconds with no steps. This
project's rule is that the ship is done when CI is green on the pushed commit, and that
condition is unmet. Every gate here ran on one macOS machine only.

Green does not prove that no `Path` method raises a different exception TYPE than its `os`
counterpart on a path form this suite never constructs: a null byte, a path over PATH_MAX, a
filesystem returning ELOOP. The write-boundary matrix covers the states this repo builds.
Settled by a property test parametrizing those forms across each migrated call pair,
asserting identical exception type and errno. Not built.

The identity moved for a lint fix. That is content addressing working, and it is not free:
any cached artifact keyed on the old `skill_identity_hash` is now a miss, and any record
outside this repo that quotes the old value is stale.

`tests/integration/test_gate_bundle.py:232` uses a bare `pytest.raises(PermissionError)` with
no `match=`. Pre-existing, not introduced here, and the surrounding content-unchanged and
no-sibling assertions carry the contract, so it was left alone rather than churned.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Three Opus subagents: an implementer, an auditor sharing none of
its context, and a fixer. The operator decoded the transcript golden's hex, confirmed which
fields moved and which did not, executed the abspath comparison, re-ran the write-boundary
and PTH100 mutations, and took the full gate. That is a separation of hats within one
session, not verification by another party.

title: Harness: lift the br 0.2.22 pin now that beads_rust#457 is fixed in 0.5.7
description:
`br` was rolled back to 0.2.22 on 2026-08-28 after `beads.db` corrupted twice in two hours
under 0.5.3. That was beads_rust#457, and cairn's confirmation is posted in the thread.

THE ISSUE IS CLOSED. v0.5.7 published 2026-08-29; the issue closed and was last updated
2026-08-31. Two independent A/B confirmations in the thread, each varying only the binary:

  0.5.3  ext4    malformed after write 2, 14 recovery artifacts
  0.5.7  ext4    30/30 integrity_check ok across three runs, two families, 0 artifacts
  0.5.3  tmpfs   malformed after write 1
  0.5.7  tmpfs   10/10 ok, 0 artifacts

The fix covers the SERIAL single-mutation trigger, not only the concurrent case the issue
title names. That matters here: cairn's corruption arrived from sequential single-agent
writes, which is the trigger the fix was measured against.

WHAT THE PIN COSTS TODAY
- `br create` mints `tmp...` ids unless `issue_prefix` is set explicitly; 0.5.3 inferred it.
  Worked around in `.beads/config.yaml`, but the workaround is only needed on 0.2.22.
- `br doctor health` reports healthy on a database `integrity_check` calls malformed.
- The pin is carried in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as `BR_VERSION` and in CLAUDE.md.

WHAT TO WATCH ON THE WAY UP, and it is not the corruption
0.5.x added semantic verification on import and REFUSES a JSONL payload it considers
malformed. In the issue thread it rejected four real defects in another project's exporter
output that 0.5.3 had imported without complaint: malformed dependency prefixes, edges to
dropped records, cross-store references, and dependency timestamps lacking sub-second
precision. cairn's `issues.jsonl` has been written by 0.2.22 throughout and has never been
put through that check. A refused import is the likely first failure, and it is a finding
about our data rather than about the binary.

Also: a 0.2.x binary refuses a 0.5.x-written database permanently, so the downgrade path is
`br init` in a scratch directory, the empty `beads.db` copied in beside `issues.jsonl`, then
import. That path is proven -- it is how the rollback was done.

DONE WHEN
- `br` upgraded, `BR_VERSION` in ci.yml moved to match, and CLAUDE.md's pin note replaced by
  whatever is true after.
- `issues.jsonl` round-trips: imported by the new binary and re-exported byte-identical,
  settled by sha256 in Python rather than by shell `diff`.
- If import is refused, every defect it names is recorded here with whether it is a real
  defect in our data or a false positive.
- The `issue_prefix` workaround re-tested: confirm whether an id is still minted correctly.
- `br doctor` on the upgraded store, with its output compared against the widened predicates
  in `scripts/beads_doctor_gate.py`, since those were established by observation on 0.2.22
  and a new binary may emit statuses the gate has never seen. The gate denies on anything
  unrecognized, so a vocabulary change surfaces as a blocked commit rather than silently.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
CLOSED. br is 0.5.7 and every risk this bead named was measured rather than assumed.

THE FEARED FAILURE DID NOT HAPPEN

This bead predicted that 0.5.x's semantic import verification would be the first failure, since
`issues.jsonl` has been written by 0.2.22 throughout and had never faced that check. It passed:

  br sync --import-only    66 issues processed, 66 created, 0 rejections
  PRAGMA integrity_check   ok
  round-trip               833675 bytes, sha256 6e5b202fc3ad3866, BYTE-IDENTICAL

The round-trip was settled in Python by length and digest, not by shell `diff`.

The write path, which is what forced the rollback, was probed on the real store: `br create`
minted `cairn-yzs` rather than a `tmp...` id, and `integrity_check` stayed ok. The probe was
deleted; it leaves a tombstone row in `issues.jsonl`, which is the ninth.

`scripts/beads_doctor_gate.py` accepts the new binary's vocabulary with no change: 55 `ok`,
1 `warn`, `workspace_health: healthy`, verdict advisory, no unrecognized status. That gate's
allowlist was established by observation on 0.2.22 and denies anything it has not seen, so this
is the case where it would have blocked every commit. It did not.

scripts/check.sh: 1958 passed, all gates pass, exit 0, under 0.5.7.

TWO THINGS THIS BEAD DID NOT PREDICT

The release asset renamed. The 0.5 line publishes `beads_rust-<version>-darwin_<arch>.tar.gz`;
the 0.2 line published `br-`. A version bump that left the asset name alone would have 404'd
the install step. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` carries both changes, and its install block was
executed verbatim: asset resolved, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK, `br 0.5.7`.

`br list --json` returns an object, `{"issues": [...], "total", "limit", "offset", "has_more"}`,
where 0.2.22 returned a bare array. A caller indexing it like an array gets a dict key and no
error. Nothing under `scripts/`, `tests/` or `.githooks/` parses it, so no gate broke, but
CLAUDE.md documented the array shape and would have taught an agent to write the bug.
`br show --json` still returns an array. `ISSUE_NOT_FOUND` is unchanged, which is the code
`scripts/br_lookup.py` allowlists, though its exit code moved from 6 to 3 and the classifier
keys on the code.

A TRAP FOUND BY ACCIDENT, AND RECORDED

A second bead store sits at `~/.beads` at schema 10. br walks upward for a workspace, so a
command run while the repo's `.beads` is absent binds to that one and reports
"Schema version mismatch: expected 17, found 10" -- an error about a database nobody meant to
touch, which for several minutes read as damage to ours. The repo database is schema 17 with
66 issues and `br doctor migrate-schema plan` reports no migration needed.

This also bears on `cairn-368`: its CI recipe moves `.beads` aside before `br init`. A runner
has no home store so the recipe is sound there, but the same commands on a developer machine
bind to `~/.beads` in the window between the move and the restore.

NO-CLAIM

The upgrade is verified on macOS arm64 only; the Linux arm is untested and `cairn-hcl` owns it.
The corruption fix itself is NOT independently confirmed here -- no stress run was performed on
this machine. The evidence for it is the two A/B confirmations in beads_rust#457 plus one clean
write probe, which is not a measurement of the 408-operation harness that justified the
rollback. Concurrent multi-process writes, the condition the issue title names, were not
exercised: every command in this session was sequential and single-agent. The pre-upgrade store
and the 0.2.22 binary are preserved for rollback. `br doctor` still exits 1 for any WARN, so
`scripts/beads_doctor_gate.py` remains the gate rather than the exit code. Whether 0.5.7 emits
doctor statuses beyond the two observed is unestablished; the allowlist denies on anything new,
so a vocabulary change surfaces as a blocked commit rather than a silent pass.

title: Harness: the suite hung on a macOS CI runner with no output for 45 minutes
description:
The suite hung on a GitHub macos-latest runner and produced no output for 45 minutes.

Run 32888575222, commit a71e3a0, cancelled by the job's own timeout-minutes: 45.
The gate trace ends:

  19:16:10 [check] pass format
  19:16:10 [check] pass lint
  19:16:10 [check] pass spelling
  19:16:11 [check] pass types
  20:01:17 ##[error]The operation was canceled.

So `uv run pytest -q` ran for 45 minutes and emitted nothing. What makes this a
finding rather than a slow runner:

- The same commit passes locally: 1353 passed in 377.39 s, exit 0.
- The same job on the same runner type two commits earlier (run 32887773951,
  commit 32f8743) finished pytest in 318.53 s with 1351 passed and 2 failures.
- The only change between them widened two numeric bounds in
  tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py's BUSY_ROWS table. A bound cannot
  cause a hang; the assertion it guards runs after the worker thread is joined.

OBSERVATION, not a conclusion: I have not established what blocked. The candidates
worth checking first are the tests that spawn subprocesses and wait
(tests/integration/test_runner.py, tests/e2e/), and the two busy-timeout rows whose
worker.join() has no timeout, so a second writer that never returns hangs the suite
rather than failing it. Nothing here says which, and a single occurrence may be the
runner rather than the code.

WHAT
- Give pytest its own deadline in CI so it dies with a traceback naming the test
  rather than being killed by the job, which reports nothing. Note that macOS ships

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
FROM cairn-m0-e0s.18: two subprocess waits this bead's deadline work should cover,
and one test that can go red for a reason that is not a defect.

`tests/integration/test_doctor.py` spawns real child interpreters in two places: the
concurrency test (two `cairn doctor --fix` children racing for the lock) and the
crash test (a child SIGKILLed between backup and apply). Both called
`communicate()` with no timeout when they landed. The audit flagged it against this
bead, and both now pass `timeout=60`, so a wedged child fails as a test rather than
as a job cancellation. That is the shape this bead asks for, applied to the two new
waits.

The second item is not fixed and wants a decision here rather than in the doctor.

The concurrency test is inherently racy. It asserts that one child exits 0 or 2 and
the other exits 5, which holds only if the second child reaches the lock while the
first still holds it. The lock is taken before detection, which makes the window
wide, but it is a window: if the first child finishes before the second acquires,
the assertion fails. That is a flaky RED, never a flaky green -- it cannot pass
while the lock is broken -- so it is honest, and the mutation proving it
(`LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` to `LOCK_SH | LOCK_NB`) is KILLED by 2 tests.

Every construction available from the test side alone either makes both children
lose, which is vacuous, or leaves the same window. Closing it needs an env-gated
hold seam inside `mutate.Lock.acquire`, in the shape of the existing
`CAIRN_DOCTOR_CRASH_AFTER_BACKUP` hook. Adding a production sleep hook for a test
was declined rather than done quietly.

So the open question belongs with this bead's deadline work: is a test that can go
red on scheduler luck acceptable in CI, or does it earn the fourth seam? A retry
would be the wrong answer -- it would mask a genuinely broken lock.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
FROM cairn-exi's session, 2026-08-26: a load-sensitive wall-clock ceiling, measured.

Not the hang this bead describes -- that signature is no output for 45 minutes, and
what happened here was slow-but-progressing output under saturation. Recorded because
the mechanism is the one this bead has to reason about, and because it is now measured
rather than hypothesized.

WHAT HAPPENED. `scripts/check.sh` ran while several subagents were each running full
pytest suites. Load average reached 131. The suite reached 46 percent, emitted nothing
for 16 minutes, and was killed at a 600-second tool timeout. A clean reproduction of
the same commit then finished in 771 seconds against a normal 240 -- four times slower,
never stalled.

THE THREE FAILURES UNDER LOAD, all in tests/integration/test_runner.py:

  test_a_real_forty_bit_launch_records_a_receipt_with_live_measurements
  test_the_manifest_carries_the_skill_s_own_output_bytes
  test_a_second_identical_launch_is_served_from_cache

each on the same assertion:

  assert attempt.status == "OK" and not attempt.served_from_cache
  AssertionError: assert ('BUDGET_EXCEEDED' == 'OK')

The runner enforces a ceiling of `ceiling_multiplier: 4` -- four times the cost
profile's predicted wall for a 40-bit launch (tests/integration/test_runner.py:35-45).
A real PARI launch exceeds it under contention.

  loaded   (load avg 131)  3 failed, 1626 passed in 771.50s
  quiet    (load avg 13)   49 passed in 8.74s   -- the whole file, exit 0

WHY IT BELONGS HERE. A GitHub-hosted runner is shared and its load is not observable
from inside the job. A ceiling calibrated against an idle machine converts contention
into a red suite that reads as a code defect, and the failure names a budget rather
than a scheduler, so the next reader chases the runner instead of the load. That is the
same class of misattribution this bead exists to stop: the transcript has to say what
actually happened.

Two things for whoever takes this bead. A per-test deadline that dies with a traceback
naming the test would have turned the 16-minute silence into a named failure in
seconds, which is already this bead's first WHAT item; and it should decide whether
`ceiling_multiplier` is the right instrument at all, since a multiplier over a
predicted wall measures the machine as much as the skill. Raising it buys green at the
cost of the budget meaning anything.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
Three of the four items are settled; the fourth is a decision for the operator.

ITEM 1 (check.sh streams) — CONFIRMED STILL TRUE. `scripts/check.sh` lines 40-56: `gate()`
runs `"$@"` directly with no capture, and appends RUN/PASS/FAIL to `.check.log` around it.
A stall now leaves a `RUN <gate>` line with no matching PASS.

ITEM 2 (pytest's own deadline) — DONE, commit 1e16fc3. pytest-timeout pinned at 2.4.0, with
`timeout = 180` and `timeout_method = "thread"` in `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, so CI and a
local run enforce the same deadline and no coreutils `timeout` is involved.

  (`tests/conformance/test_skill_contract.py::test_clause[toy_curve-S2-01]` setup, from
  `--durations=25` over 1648 passing tests in 232.44 s). The worst contention factor this
  project has measured is 4x, putting a contended worst case near 33 s. The longest chain of
  inner subprocess bounds inside one test is 120 s -- the two 60 s `communicate()` calls in
  the doctor concurrency test -- so 180 s keeps the inner, more specific bound firing first,
  and stays 15x below the job's 45-minute ceiling.

  `thread` over `signal`: signal delivery cannot interrupt a blocked C call holding the GIL
  and cannot reach a hang in a worker thread. Both candidate hangs take exactly that shape --
  a SQLite busy wait, a flock, an `os.wait4` with no timeout parameter.

  Observed against a test that sleeps for an hour, with the deadline dropped to 8 s:

    +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ Timeout +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
      File ".../tests/unit/test_deadline_demo.py", line 5, in
        test_a_test_that_blocks_past_the_deadline_is_named_in_the_output
        time.sleep(3600)

  A hang in a fixture is covered by the same budget: the same instrument against a wedged
  fixture names `File "/tmp/dl/test_setup_hang.py", line 8, in wedged`.

ITEM 3 (the unbounded worker join) — FIXED, commit 2fc25cb, and it carried a second defect.
`tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py:114` joins with the row's own declared ceiling
plus 25 s, and a worker still alive after it is an assertion naming the `busy_timeout` that
did not return. The thread is now a daemon, because a join timeout alone does not help: the
first attempt at the mutation never terminated at all, since pytest waited at interpreter
shutdown on three sleeping non-daemon threads after the assertions had already fired.

  scripts/mutation-check.sh tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py \
    'b.execute("insert into t values (2)")' 'time.sleep(3600)' \
    tests/integration/test_grounding_sqlite.py
  KILLED  by 3 test(s): 3 failed, 6 passed, 8 warnings in 87.54s

  AssertionError: the second writer with busy_timeout=0 ms never returned within 25.1 s

ITEM 4 (the sweep) — DONE, commit 1e16fc3. Bounded at 60 s: `communicate()` and `wait()` in
`tests/integration/test_grounding_subprocess.py`, the gp version probe in
`tests/integration/test_grounding_gp.py`, the CLI child in
`tests/integration/test_cli_streams.py`, the eight validator children in
`tests/unit/test_bead_artifact_block.py`, the script child in
`tests/unit/test_scorecard_coherence.py`. Two waits stay unbounded with a reason: `os.wait4`
has no timeout parameter in Python, so the calls in `test_grounding_subprocess.py` and
`test_runner.py` rely on the per-test deadline and each reaps a child that runs `sys.exit(3)`
or `pass`; and `child.wait()` in `tests/fixtures/skills/forks_a_grandchild.py` runs inside a
skill the runner spawns under `ceiling_s` plus grace and a SIGKILL, so the runner bounds it
and a timeout there would change what the fixture models.

`scripts/bead_artifact_block.py` calls `git cat-file` and `br show` with no timeout. That is
the commit gate, not the suite, so it is outside this bead's WHAT and is left alone rather
than changed unasked.

SECOND HALF OF DONE WHEN — CONFIRMED. `gh api` on the three runs after the incident:
32895819844 (2bdbda8), 32896614987 (5faab01), 32898412001 (5ce45fe), all `success`, all on
commits `git merge-base --is-ancestor a71e3a0` confirms are descendants of a71e3a0. Their
`Gates` step, which is the whole of `scripts/check.sh`, took 245 s, 259 s and 266 s
respectively -- the same order as the 318 s and 298 s baselines the bead already records, not
a run that scraped in under the ceiling. Raw job logs for all three now return 404, so the
pytest line itself is no longer recoverable; the step duration is the bound that survives.

THE OPERATOR'S OPEN QUESTION, now measured rather than worried about. Over 25 back-to-back
trials of the doctor concurrency scenario, reading `lock_taken` / `lock_released` /
`lock_held` timestamps out of both children's JSON stderr:

  hold_ms     min 58.66   median 66.20   max 124.37
  arrival_ms  min -0.19   median  1.12   max  11.17
  outcomes    25 of 25 gave (0, 5)

`arrival_ms` is how far after the winner took the lock the loser reached it. The window is the
hold; the risk is the arrival exceeding it. Worst observed pairing is a 58.66 ms hold against
an 11.17 ms arrival, so the loser would have to be 5.3x later than its own worst observed
offset to miss. The median margin is 65 ms. Both children pay the same interpreter startup,
which is why they converge within a millisecond, and contention slows both together rather
than staggering them.

Recommendation, and it is a recommendation only: leave the seam out. A production sleep hook
inside `mutate.Lock.acquire` buys a margin that is already 5x on the worst of 25 trials, and
it is the kind of hook that outlives its reason. Stated limit: n=25 on one machine at load
average ~6, not on a GitHub runner, and I have no way to measure the arrival spread under
runner contention from here.

THE DEADLINE COSTS NOTHING. `scripts/check.sh` run alone, both times on this machine:

  before  fefd33e   1648 passed in 232.44 s   exit 0   load average 5.68 at the end
  after   1e16fc3   1648 passed in 232.15 s   exit 0   load average 6.51 at the end

Commits: 2fc25cb, 1e16fc3. Not closed: the first DONE WHEN clause is demonstrated locally,
not yet observed on a runner, and nothing here has been pushed.

  05:14:26Z [check] pass theater

  other way was the one uploading none.

  `timeout-minutes` raised 15 -> 30. Fifteen was set on the reasoning that a green run
  takes five minutes and three times that is headroom. This run measured a slow runner
  at fifteen-plus, so that reasoning was right on the numbers and wrong on the variance.

suite runs 1702 tests in about 230 s on a quiet machine; CI's own green runs sit at
245-300 s. This run was at least 3.5x that with no per-test outlier.

contention alone produces exactly this profile -- 1648 tests at 771 s against a normal

passed 49/49 once quiet. A shared runner is not observable from inside the job.

something that kills pytest a few minutes before the job ceiling and dumps every

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
CLOSED 2026-08-27 at the commit this comment ships with.

THE SHAPE THE SECOND HANG HAD, and why the shipped instrument did not catch it.

The reopen note asked for a session-level deadline: something that kills pytest before the
job ceiling and dumps every thread's stack, so a uniformly slow run leaves a profile rather
than a silence. That is built. It took two instruments rather than one, and the reason is
the finding worth carrying forward.

WHAT WAS BUILT

  tests/_session_deadline.py arms two independent watchdogs from pytest_configure, both
  writing to an os.dup of the real stderr taken before pytest's fd capture redirects fd 2.

  PRIMARY: a private daemon thread waiting on a threading.Event. On expiry it prints a
  Timeout (H:MM:SS)! banner, calls faulthandler.dump_traceback(all_threads=True) and exits
  124. Deadline from CAIRN_SESSION_DEADLINE, default 1500 s.

  BACKSTOP: faulthandler.dump_traceback_later at deadline + 15 s, exit code 1, which
  faulthandler fixes and does not let a caller change. pyproject.toml blocks pytest's
  bundled faulthandler plugin so nothing can cancel it.

  A malformed or non-positive value raises pytest.UsageError at configure time and runs zero
  tests, rather than falling back to no deadline. The one way to run unbounded is
  CAIRN_SESSION_DEADLINE_SKIP='<reason>', which prints its reason to stderr.

  scripts/check.sh adds --durations=25 and logs the armed deadline and both exit codes to
  .check.log, so a reader who tails the log after a hang can tell the instrument was on.

THE TWO HOLES, EACH REPRODUCED

An independent audit found the first and the operator reproduced the second. Neither
instrument alone is sufficient, and each covers exactly the other's gap.

  A single-instrument thread watchdog is STARVED by a GIL-holding C call. Child body
  re.match(r"(a+)+$", "a" * 40 + "b") under a 4 s deadline: alive at 30 s, killed by an
  external SIGKILL at exit 137, zero Timeout banners.

  A single-instrument faulthandler timer is CANCELLED by the first test failure. pytest's
  bundled plugin registers pytest_exception_interact as tryfirst and calls
  cancel_dump_traceback_later unconditionally; runner.py fires it on every reported failure
  and every collection error. Child whose first test fails and whose second sleeps 3600,
  under a 4 s deadline: alive at 20 s, SIGKILL, exit 137, zero banners.

  So the instrument evaporated in exactly the case it exists for: a long session that is
  both slow and failing.

BOTH REPRODUCTIONS RE-RUN AT THIS COMMIT, by the operator

  GIL-STALL        EXIT=1   wall=19s  banners=1   (4 s deadline + 15 s backstop grace)
  FAIL-THEN-HANG   EXIT=124 wall=5s   banners=1   (thread, at its own deadline)

  The GIL profile names the frame: re/__init__.py line 167 in match. The fail-then-hang

33041862321 is unestablished and is not established here. The bead's DONE WHEN asked for

title: Harness: S2-12 passes a skill that hardcodes its in-range cross-check result
description:
The section 2 conformance harness (cairn-m0-e0s.16) extracts S2-12 as: axis in
{implementation, algorithm}, independent_range an interval record over the input
fields, result == untested outside that range, and the certificate's
selftest_summary.cross_check block carrying only axis and independent_range.

A subject satisfies all four while performing no cross-check at all. It declares
an axis, declares a range, reports untested outside it, and hardcodes a string
inside it. tests/fixtures/skills/nonconforming.py is exactly that shape and
scores PASS on S2-12.

What catches such a subject is S2-10, which plants a disagreement at the declared
seam through the real runner and requires the status to move to DISAGREE. The
nonconforming fixture fails S2-10 for that reason. So the harness as a whole is
not fooled; S2-12 alone is.

The gap is that the two clauses interlock without saying so. A skill that
declares no seam, or declares one it does not call, fails S2-10 and passes S2-12,
and a reader of the matrix cannot tell from the S2-12 column whether a
cross-check exists.

The change: give S2-12 an in-range arm that requires the reported result to move
when the declared seam is planted, and let a constant string fail. The verdict
reasons then say which of the two clauses carries the evidence.

Cost of doing it inside cairn-m0-e0s.16 rather than here: the bead specifies the
nonconforming fixture must fail exactly S2-01, S2-04, S2-10 and S2-11. The
stronger arm adds S2-12 to that set, which is a change to that bead's acceptance
criteria rather than a fix inside them.

Evidence, at commit 1fe8d6c:

  uv run python <scratch>/dump.py

  nonconforming
  S2-10 MUST   FAIL  a planted disagreement at cairn.pari.ellsea still returned OK
  S2-12 MUST   PASS  axis algorithm, range {'bits': [0, 50]}, untested outside it
                     and in the ledger

Recorded in tests/conformance/COVERAGE.md under "What these checks do not decide".

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
CLOSED AT 0e56023. Two commits: 58a1438 (the in-range arm), 0e56023 (the record on
cairn-m0-e0s.16, whose acceptance this changes).

THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED AND INVERTED

S2-12 extracted four conditions -- an axis in {implementation, algorithm}, an
independent_range interval, `untested` outside that range, and the certificate's
cross_check block carrying only axis and range. A subject satisfies all four while
performing no cross-check at all: declare an axis, declare a range, report untested
outside it, and hardcode a string inside it. `tests/fixtures/skills/nonconforming.py`
is exactly that shape.

  before   S2-12 MUST  PASS  axis algorithm, range {'bits': [0, 50]}, untested
                             outside it and in the ledger
  after    S2-12 MUST  FAIL  in range the cross-check reports 'agree' whether or not
                             cairn.pari.ellsea is planted, so it compares nothing and
                             S2-12 carries no evidence that a cross-check exists

THE THREE-SUBJECT MATRIX, re-executed by me at HEAD through scripts/check.sh

  clause         nonconforming  toy_curve      witness
  S2-10 MUST     FAIL           PASS           FAIL
  S2-11 MUST     FAIL           PASS           PASS
  S2-12 MUST     FAIL           PASS           FAIL
  nonconforming MUST score 7/12   (was 8/12)
  toy_curve MUST score 12/12      (unchanged)
  witness MUST score 3/12         (unchanged)

Exactly one cell moves. `toy_curve` performs a real cross-check and still scores
12/12, which is the half that matters: the arm passes a conforming subject rather
than failing everything. `witness` fails S2-12 at the first arm on
`cross_check.axis 'vibes' is not one of ['implementation', 'algorithm']`, so the new
arm is never reached and its score is untouched.

  $ scripts/check.sh          (run alone; load 7.93 before)
  1648 passed, 8 warnings in 227.70s
  [check] all gates pass                              EXIT=0

Unchanged at 1648: the arm lives inside an existing clause and adds no test.

ONE MECHANISM, TWO CLAUSES

S2-10's planting was reusable as-is. It launches `skills.harness_child` with
CAIRN_HARNESS_SUBJECT and CAIRN_HARNESS_MODE=seam, and the child monkeypatches
`subject.SEAM` to `real(...) + 2` before delegating; the only per-clause difference
is the recipe salt. It is extracted verbatim into
`_launch_with_planted_seam(subject, ctx, salt)` and `_declared_seam(module)`, and
S2-10 now calls the helper. Two clauses, one implementation, no second planting path
to drift.

THE VERDICT REASONS NOW CARRY THE EVIDENCE

That was the bead's actual purpose: a reader of the S2-12 column could not tell
whether a cross-check existed, because S2-10 was silently carrying that weight.

  toy_curve PASS   ...untested outside it and in the ledger; in range 'agree' moves
                   to 'disagree' when cairn.pari.ellsea is planted, so S2-12 itself
                   carries the evidence that a comparison runs
  no seam   FAIL   the subject declares no seam, so its in-range result answers to
                   no second opinion

PROVED ABLE TO FAIL

  `if planted == inside:` -> `if False and planted == inside:`
      KILLED by 2 test(s): 2 failed, 47 passed
  `_launch_with_planted_seam(...)` -> `_launch(...)`  (the plant removed)
      KILLED by 2 test(s): 2 failed, 47 passed

The second is the one that matters. With the plant removed, `toy_curve` itself fails
S2-12, so its PASS is carried by observed movement rather than by an arm that cannot
fail.

NO GOLDEN MOVED

`matrix()` is a `pytest_terminal_summary` section, not a golden, and the MUST-failure
set lives in code (`expected_must_failures`) rather than in a captured file. The four
`*_floor.golden` files are read by S2-05 and S2-06, which this arm does not touch.
`toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES` is untouched, so no transcript or certificate golden
reseeded.

A CLOSED BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE CHANGES, AND IS SAID SO

`cairn-m0-e0s.16` is closed, and its acceptance says the nonconforming fixture fails
exactly S2-01, S2-04, S2-10 and S2-11. That set is now five. The bead is not reopened
or edited; a comment on it records the change so a later reader of its close evidence
is not misled.

ONE DISAGREEMENT WITH MY OWN DIRECTION, AND IT WAS RIGHT

I asked for the COVERAGE.md matrix row for S2-12 to gain the new arm. The clause
table's third column is a verbatim PLAN §2 quote, and
`test_clause_table.py::test_coverage_table_matches_clauses` binds only id, level and
check-function name. Editing the quote would have misattributed the arm to PLAN. The
arm is documented instead under "Where a check reads more than the sentence", beside
S2-10's and S2-11's extra arms, and the quoted row is intact. Settled by
`uv run pytest tests/conformance/test_clause_table.py -q`, green.

NO-CLAIM

This proves S2-12 no longer passes a subject whose in-range result cannot move. It
does not prove the arm is right for a subject that declares a SEAM and never calls it
on the in-range path: no such fixture exists, and the arm would report the
constant-result FAIL for it, which is the intended verdict but is inference rather
than measurement. Recorded on cairn-fur, which owns the harness's pattern surface.

The arm adds two launches per subject to S2-12. The conformance module runs 53 passed
in 8.94 s after the change; the before figure was not timed, so no claim is made about
its cost.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED

Implemented by one subagent. I re-ran the full suite at HEAD and read the printed
matrix myself, read the arm and both verdict reasons in the source, and confirmed the
one-cell movement and that toy_curve holds at 12/12. I did not re-run the two
mutations. That is a separation of hats within one session, not independent
verification by another party.

title: Harness: CI has no br, so the artifact-block gate and the pre-commit hook are tested only where they already work
description:
CI installs pari and nothing else, so `br` is absent on the runner. The
artifact-block gate refuses without it -- correctly, since reporting a block as
valid without reading the body would be a silent fail-open -- and the consequence
is that the gate's happy path is never exercised anywhere but a developer machine.

Measured 2026-08-27 at commit 4ec8697: 22 of the 23 tests in
`tests/unit/test_bead_artifact_block.py` pass with `br` off PATH, because they
drive validation over a body file. The twenty-third drives the gate by bead id and
therefore needs `br show`. Its oracle was corrected to assert the parity deny by
its reason rather than by an exit code with two causes, which is right on its own
terms, but it does not restore the coverage: on CI nothing reads a real bead body
through the gate.

The same holds for `.githooks/pre-commit` as a whole. It runs `bead-test-plan.sh`,
`bead-artifact-block.sh` and the compliance audit, every one of which shells out to
`br`, and none of them runs on the runner. The hook is tested only where it is
already known to work.

WHAT: give CI a real `br`. It is `beads_rust` on crates.io (0.5.1 published; 0.2.10
is what this machine has, so pin deliberately rather than taking latest). A
`cargo install` compiles a 10 MB binary and will dominate the job unless the
resulting binary is cached on the cargo bin path across runs, so the cache is part
of the work rather than an optimization.

Do NOT satisfy this with a stand-in `br` that returns canned JSON. The thing under
test is the gate reading a real bead, and a fake `br` would make the test pass
while proving nothing -- the same fail-open shape the gate itself refuses.

DONE WHEN: `test_a_matching_extractor_regex_does_not_deny` exercises a real `br
show` on the runner; a CI run's log shows the artifact-block gate reading a bead
body and passing; and the added install does not lengthen the job by more than a
minute on a warm cache, measured across three runs.

Surfaced by the first push of the M0 straggler session: 43 commits, all green
locally, one red on the runner for exactly this reason.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
SECOND HALF OF THE SAME GAP: the compliance skill is absent on CI too, so the
extractor-parity cross-check never runs there.

Observed in run 33037689499 (commit 98333ee, green):

  PARITY-UNKNOWN artifact-block: the compliance skill is not installed;
                 the extractor regex was not compared

repeated on every invocation the suite makes. `scripts/bead_artifact_block.py:281-289`
prints that to stderr and CONTINUES.

The warn-rather-deny choice is deliberate and, on its own terms, right. The two
missing-infra cases are not the same:

  br absent            DENY (exit 3). The gate cannot do its job at all -- reporting a
                       block as valid without reading the body is a silent fail-open.
  skill absent         WARN. The gate can still do its job; it loses one auxiliary
                       cross-check. Denying would make the gate unrunnable on every
                       machine that does not vendor the skill, CI included.

What it costs: the parity check exists to catch drift between this repo's copy of
`PATH_HINT_RE` and the vendored extractor's. An upstream skill update that changes
that regex would make cairn accept blocks the audit cannot read -- the appearance of
a gate with none of its effect. On CI that drift is undetectable, so the protection
is a developer-machine-only property, and the log line is its only trace.

This is the same root cause as this bead's `br` half: the runner carries neither, so
`.githooks/pre-commit` and everything it invokes are exercised only where they are
already known to work. Whatever gives CI a real `br` should give it the vendored skill
as well, and the DONE WHEN should require a CI log showing `PASS artifact-block <id>`
rather than `PARITY-UNKNOWN`.

Same prohibition as the br half: do not satisfy this with a stub skill carrying a
copy of the regex. That would compare cairn's regex against a fixture cairn also
controls, which is a check that cannot fail.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
A second surface for this bead's thesis, found while closing cairn-fi7.

The pre-commit and post-commit hooks grew real decision logic: a closing-commit resolver
whose git failures must DENY, an attribution corrector whose exit code the hook gates on,
and a gate-coverage record that decides whether post-commit is allowed to push. The Python
holding those decisions is covered at 94-98 percent.

The bash that calls it is covered at zero, and not by oversight: `tests/conftest.py`'s
`isolation_guard` refuses a subprocess whose argv0 is not `sys.executable` or the gp
binary, so no test in this suite can spawn `bash` to exercise a hook. The uncovered call
sites are `record_gate`, the coverage `check`, the `CLOSING_RC` branches and the
`ATTRIBUTION-DENY` case.

That is the same shape this bead already names for CI: the gate is exercised only where it
already works. Whatever answer this bead reaches for running the hooks where `br` and the
compliance skill are absent should also say how the hook shell gets exercised anywhere.

cairn-rof carries the other half, the record attesting to a parent rather than to the
staged tree.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
CLOSED 2026-08-27. All three DONE-WHEN clauses are settled on real runner evidence, taken
before the account's Actions tier ran out.

DONE WHEN, clause by clause.

1. `test_a_matching_extractor_regex_does_not_deny` EXERCISES A REAL `br show` ON THE RUNNER.

   The runner installs the published darwin binary for the version pinned in
   `BR_VERSION`, checked against the sha256 published beside it, cached on the cargo bin
   path and keyed on the version.

   The test's prior oracle was two negative assertions -- "no longer matches" not in stderr,
   "DENY artifact-block parity" not in the log -- and both hold VACUOUSLY when the gate exits
   3 for want of `br`, which is exactly what CI did. It now requires exit 0, the
   `pass cairn-exi (closed):` line on stdout, and `PASS artifact-block cairn-exi` in
   `.check.log`. None of those can be produced by a run that never read a bead.

   Mutation proof that the new oracle gates, explicit single target:

     scripts/mutation-check.sh scripts/bead_artifact_block.py \
       'if shutil.which("br") is None:' 'if shutil.which("br") is not None:' \
       tests/unit/test_bead_artifact_block.py
     KILLED  by 2 test(s): 2 failed, 24 passed

   Under the prior oracle the same mutation SURVIVED.

2. A CI RUN'S LOG SHOWS THE GATE READING A BEAD BODY AND PASSING.

   Run 33104091974, commit 6e876e7, macos-latest, green. From the step that cats
   `.check.log`:

     2026-08-27T18:38:22Z PASS artifact-block cairn-exi
     2026-08-27T18:38:22Z BYPASS artifact-block cairn-exi: proving the bypass is logged
     2026-08-27T18:38:22Z DENY artifact-block infra: br not on PATH

   and from the step before it: `br 0.5.3`.

   Both arms are exercised there: the gate reads a real bead and passes, and the
   absent-`br` deny still fires, asserted by its reason rather than by an exit code with two
   causes. The gate is no longer tested only where it already worked.

3. THE INSTALL COSTS UNDER A MINUTE ON A WARM CACHE, ACROSS THREE RUNS.

   Step timings, `Restore br` + `Install br` + the version print:

     33104091974  cold   1s + 1s + 0s = 2s   (Install br ran)
     33105687625  warm   2s + 0s + 0s = 2s   (Install br SKIPPED, cache hit)
     33105703637  warm   3s + 0s + 0s = 3s   (Install br SKIPPED, cache hit)

   Three seconds against a sixty-second budget. The skipped step in runs two and three also
   settles the implementer's UNVERIFIED note about whether `actions/cache` v6.1.0's
   `cache-hit` output behaves as assumed on this runner: it does.

THE PROHIBITION WAS HONORED. No stub `br`, no canned JSON, no stub compliance skill, no
skip and no platform conditional. The gate reads the real `cairn-exi` out of the real
`.beads/issues.jsonl` that `br` imports. `scripts/theater-patterns.sh` passes.

A DEVIATION FROM THE BEAD TEXT, ON EVIDENCE. The bead specifies `cargo install beads_rust`.
That route does not hold on a stable toolchain, and both lines fail differently:

  0.2.10  a dependency is gated behind a nightly-only feature (`#![feature(portable_simd)]`)
  0.5.3   declares a rustc floor of 1.95/1.96, above the 1.94 available

Either failure would be a red run about Rust rather than about cairn. The published release
binary is the route taken, and the version swap was proven safe rather than assumed:
`br show <id> --json` is byte-identical between 0.2.10 and 0.5.3 on this repository's beads,
compared by sha256 under a pristine HOME in a fresh clone.

Checkout takes full history, because the gate resolves every commit an ARTIFACTS block
names and a depth-1 clone reads all five of cairn-exi's as absent.

SUITE: 1835 passed at the pwj commit, exit 0. 1836 at the tip after the cost caps.

NO-CLAIM

CI IS NOT GREEN ON THE TIP, AND CANNOT BE. The account's Actions tier is exhausted and
refreshes on 2026-09-01; a job dispatched after that point returns "The job was not started
because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased"
in four seconds with no steps. This project's standing rule is that the ship is done when CI
is green on the PUSHED commit, and that condition is unmet for every close after run
33104091974. The evidence above comes from runs that completed before the tier ran out; the
first session after the refresh re-verifies the accumulated tip.

This does not establish that the compliance skill runs in CI. It does not: the skill lives
under a home directory the runner does not have, so `.check.log` still carries
`PARITY-UNKNOWN artifact-block: the compliance skill is not installed; the extractor regex
was not compared` on every CI run. That half of this bead's thesis is untouched, and the
extractor-parity check remains exercised only on a developer machine.

The bash in `.githooks/pre-commit` and `.githooks/post-commit` still has no test, because
`tests/conftest.py`'s `isolation_guard` refuses a `bash` subprocess. The Python those hooks
call is covered at 94-98 percent; the shell calling it is at zero. cairn-rof carries that
gap, and a comment on this bead records it.

Nothing here measures whether a cold cache would still be cheap if the release asset moved
or the download were rate-limited. The install is one `curl` against a GitHub release, and
it has been exercised exactly once.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. One Opus subagent implemented it. The operator re-ran the
mutation on the new oracle, both `br` paths locally, confirmed all five commits cairn-exi
names resolve, read the CI log lines quoted above out of the run itself, and read the diff.
That is a separation of hats within one session, not verification by another party.

title: Harness: drive ty to zero warnings and delete the override table
description:
Drive ty to zero warnings, then delete the override table in pyproject.toml.

ty 0.0.74 is a gate in scripts/check.sh, run with --exit-zero-on-warning: an error
blocks, a warning does not. 46 warnings stand, every one of them scoped to a named
file in [[tool.ty.overrides]]. That table is debt, not design, and this bead empties
it. Proved the gate is real, not decorative: `return value + 1` on a str-annotated
parameter exits 1 in src/cairn/exits.py, which is not on the list, and exits 0 in
src/cairn/runner.py, which is. The cost of every line in that table is exactly that.

The four families, with what each needs:

1. invalid-argument-type, 34 hits (src/cairn/attest.py, tests/factories.py,
   tests/integration/{test_grounding_fs,test_tier_gate,test_toy_curve}.py). All are
   `SomeDataclass(**{**fields, ...})`, where the dict's value type widens to a union
   and every field is reported against it. No checker narrows this. The fix is to
   stop routing typed constructors through an untyped dict: build the dataclass with
   named arguments, or give the dict a TypedDict.

2. unsupported-operator, 10 hits (src/cairn/runner.py, src/cairn/verifier.py,
   tests/integration/test_verifier_properties.py, tests/unit/test_canon_properties.py).
   Two shapes. Guards the checker cannot read — `timed_out and elapsed >=
   terminated_at + grace`, where terminated_at is None until a timeout, and
   `_is_int(self.p) and self.p >= 1`, a custom predicate that narrows nothing. Both
   are correct today and both become checkable with an assert or an isinstance. The
   rest is PARI Gen arithmetic; cypari2 ships no stubs, so a stub package or an
   explicit int() at the boundary is what closes it.

3. not-iterable, 1 hit (src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py:306). transcripts is built only
   on the DISAGREE path and read only there, an invariant the checker cannot see.
   Note the cost before touching this one: toy_curve.py is in IDENTITY_SOURCES, so any
   edit bumps implementation_revision and the transcript and certificate goldens must
   be regenerated with their diffs read.

4. no-matching-overload, 1 hit (src/cairn/runner.py:245): round(x, n) with x untyped.

Done when: `uv run ty check src tests` reports zero diagnostics and exits 0 without
--exit-zero-on-warning; the [[tool.ty.overrides]] blocks are gone from pyproject.toml;
scripts/check.sh runs ty without the flag; and a planted type error in any file under
src or tests exits 1.

description:

plus the HEAD it gated against, post-commit reads that record once, unlinks it, and
denies the push when a closed bead is not covered or the parent does not match.

ONE HOLE REMAINS, stated when it shipped. If pre-commit runs and the commit is then
aborted, the record survives. A later `--no-verify` commit on the SAME parent closing
the SAME beads is vouched for by that surviving record, and the push proceeds.

than to a parent and a bead list. `git write-tree` gives that hash and is safe to call
from a hook.

and `.githooks/post-commit` has no test: the `record_gate` and `check` call sites, the
`CLOSING_RC` branches and the `ATTRIBUTION-DENY` case are shell, and `tests/conftest.py`
refuses a bash subprocess, so no test in this suite can reach them. The Python each hook
calls is covered at 94-98 percent; the shell that calls it is covered at zero. cairn-pwj
owns the CI half of that problem and carries a comment pointing here.

- The record attests to the staged tree, and a test shows an aborted-then-`--no-verify`
  commit on the same parent is denied rather than vouched for.
