comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
CLOSED. Both halves shipped: the record attests to a tree, and the hook shell has a test tier.

PART 1 -- THE HOLE, EXECUTED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED

The stated hole was that an aborted commit leaves the gate record behind, and a later
`--no-verify` commit on the same parent closing the same beads is vouched for by it. Run
against the unfixed code in a scratch repo with a bare origin, the failing-first output shows
origin receiving TWO commits -- the ungated tree was pushed:

  assert scratch.origin_shas() == [scratch.git("rev-parse", "HEAD^").stdout.strip()]
  E  Left contains one more item: 'f75f1463eeb06954b75b7466ec8b3516fa8f48d1'

`scripts/gate_marker.py` now carries `tree` beside `parent` and `gated`; `.githooks/pre-commit`
supplies `git write-tree`, `.githooks/post-commit` supplies `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`, and a
record with no `tree` key denies a commit that has one, so a stale record fails closed rather
than passing on a missing field.

VERIFIED BY THE SESSION, not only by the implementer. Neutering the tree comparison alone --
`if recorded_tree != tree:` made unreachable, nothing else touched -- turns three tests red:

  test_an_abandoned_gate_run_does_not_vouch_for_a_later_no_verify_commit
  test_a_record_written_over_a_different_tree_vouches_for_nothing
  test_a_record_carrying_no_tree_vouches_for_no_commit_that_has_one

File restored byte-identical afterwards, verified by length and sha256 in Python.

PART 2 -- THE DECISION ON HOW HOOK SHELL GETS EXERCISED

`tests/conftest.py`'s autouse `isolation_guard` allow-lists only the interpreter and `gp` as
`argv0` and fails any test that mutates the repo tree, so no test in the existing tiers can
reach `record_gate`, the `CLOSING_RC` branches or `ATTRIBUTION-DENY`. That guard is not the
problem and was not weakened: roughly 1900 tests depend on it being absolute, and it is
byte-unchanged.

DECIDED: a separate tier, `tests/hook_contract/`, with its own conftest shadowing the guard by
name. Each test builds a `git init` repo plus a bare origin under `tmp_path`, copies in the
real `.githooks/` and the scripts the hooks call, sets `core.hooksPath`, and drives real
`git commit`. 40 tests. Where the scratch repo cannot satisfy a gate honestly the test takes
that gate's own named, logged bypass; no hook was edited to make a test pass.

That the tier is load-bearing rather than decorative was shown by making `record_gate` a no-op:
7 of 12 selected tests go red, including the record, the post-commit consume, the abandoned-run
and the amend cases.

WHAT REMAINS UNEXERCISED, named rather than summarized as "none":

  .githooks/pre-commit:40-42   the GATE-RECORD-FAILED arm -- reachable only by stubbing
                               gate_marker.py, which would test the stub
  .githooks/pre-commit:95-96   the $HOME/.claude and $HOME/.codex skill fallbacks; the scratch
                               repo always resolves the first candidate or none
  pre-commit:18-19,
  post-commit:19-20            the `cd "$ROOT" ||` failure arms, structurally unreachable
                               because a hook only runs from inside a worktree

Also: what each stubbed script DECIDES is not covered here. This tier proves the shell reads an
exit code correctly; the Python that produces it is covered in `tests/unit`.

A DEFECT THE SESSION CAUGHT THAT THE IMPLEMENTER'S OWN NO-CLAIM PREDICTED. It recorded that it
had not run `ty check`. It had not, and two `no-matching-overload` errors were sitting in
`tests/hook_contract/conftest.py` at the two `subprocess.run` calls. Fixed by annotating
`env: dict[str, str]`; both cleared.

scripts/check.sh: 2006 passed, all gates pass, exit 0.

NO-CLAIM

This tier has never run in CI. It needs git, uv and a warm uv cache, and the fixture points
`UV_CACHE_DIR` and `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR` at the real HOME while moving HOME to `tmp_path`.
That it works on a runner is inference until a CI run says so, and it adds roughly 68 seconds
to the suite.

The `ATTRIBUTION-DENY` case, the `CLOSING_RC` nonzero branches, the doctor-gate deny and the
`MISSING_RC` arms are driven by replacing the called script inside the scratch repo with one
that exits the code under test. The bash branch genuinely executes; the exit code is
manufactured. The compliance skill in the scratch repo is a five-file stand-in carrying only
the markers the hook greps for.

The implementer reported a pre-existing failure in
`tests/integration/test_session_deadline.py::test_f` when running `tests/unit tests/integration`
as a pair, and showed it reproduces with this tier removed. It does NOT appear in
`scripts/check.sh`, which passed 2006 with zero failures, so the condition is scoped to that
narrower invocation and is not diagnosed here.

Whether the index `git write-tree` hashes is always the one the commit is built from is taken
from reading pre-commit end to end plus the abandoned-run test observing the two agree; no case
was constructed where a gate mutates the index between the two.

title: Harness: three unexercised paths in the missing-items corrector
description:
Three gaps left open by cairn-8jm, all in scripts/audit_missing_items.py, none of which
that bead's acceptance criteria reached.

1. THE `- check` LINE SHAPE IS A PARSE GAP OF UNESTABLISHED FREQUENCY.

score-bead.py:1241 emits `- check \`<id>\` (<verdict>) — <reason>` into the same section for
every compliance check with verdict FAIL or MISSING. cairn-8jm extended spec_item_id_of to
both shapes, so a given id classifies identically whichever producer wrote its line, and both
shapes are tested. What is unestablished is whether Phase 4 ever emits FAIL for an item the
gatherer never searched: every compliance.json in this repo is the stub with an empty checks
list, and a scan of all recorded passes finds 710 `- spec item` lines, 241 `- theater` lines
and zero `- check` lines. So the handling is correct by construction and unexercised by any
real artifact.

DONE WHEN a real Phase 4 has run at least once under the orchestrator and the resulting
compliance.json is either shown to contain no such row, or is used as the fixture for a test
that exercises the shape against real output.

2. ONLY ONE UNREADABLE-INPUT PATH HAS A NAMED OUTCOME.

EXIT_UNREADABLE_SPEC covers json.JSONDecodeError from spec.json. An unreadable scorecard.md,
a permissions error on either file, and a spec.json that parses to a non-dict all raise
uncaught. The direction is safe -- a traceback exits nonzero and the hook denies -- but it is
not one of the three named outcomes, and the enforcement discipline this project follows asks
for a distinct log line per outcome so an agent can confirm which path fired. This is the
same defect class cairn-8jm fixed for the missing heading, one layer out.

DONE WHEN each unreadable-input path has its own verdict, exit code and .check.log line, with
a test per path.

3. THE FROZEN GATHERER EXCERPT CANNOT DETECT A LAUNDERED REGENERATION.

tests/fixtures/compliance_skill/ holds a point-in-time cut of gather-evidence.sh with the
source digest, and tests/integration/test_audit_missing_items_drift.py compares the live file
against it. Someone who edits the vendored gatherer AND regenerates the fixture in one step
passes both the hermetic assertions and the live comparison. Only the GATHERER_* constants
failing to match the new excerpt would catch it, and a regeneration that preserves the
structures those constants name would slip through entirely.

DONE WHEN either the fixture's digest is pinned somewhere a regeneration cannot silently
rewrite, or the classifier's constants are derived from the excerpt at import time so a
structural change cannot leave them stale.

TEST PLAN

- tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items.py — one test per newly named unreadable-input outcome,
  each asserting the exit code, the verdict on stdout and the .check.log line.
- tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items_gatherer.py — the laundered-regeneration guard, run
  hermetically so it holds on a machine with no vendored skill.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
CLOSED on parts 2 and 3. Part 1 is SPLIT OUT to cairn-eaj, not silently dropped.

WHY PART 1 IS NOT HERE. Its criterion is that a real Phase 4 has run under the orchestrator,
which arrives with M1. The whole question is what a REAL Phase 4 emits for an item the gatherer
never searched, and a fixture written by the same hand that writes the assertion answers
nothing -- it would be the very "correct by construction, unexercised by any real artifact"
condition this bead was opened to name. cairn-eaj carries it, blocked on the orchestrator.

PART 2 -- each unreadable-input path has its own verdict, exit code and log line.

Three paths raised uncaught before: an unreadable scorecard.md, a permissions error on
spec.json, and a spec.json parsing to a non-dict. Each observed failing first:

  scorecard.md   PermissionError at audit_missing_items.py:286
  spec.json      PermissionError at audit_missing_items.py:288
  non-dict spec  AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' at :144

Now EXIT_UNREADABLE_SCORECARD 5, EXIT_UNREADABLE_SPEC_FILE 6, EXIT_SPEC_NOT_AN_OBJECT 7, each
with its own .check.log line, registered ahead of no-section and debt-from-nothing so a
structural failure outranks the verdict. The spec-file test also asserts the older
`DENY missing-items unreadable-spec:` line is ABSENT, so the two spec paths cannot collapse
into one. Each reverted separately turns exactly one test red.

PART 3 -- the pinned digest, and why the other option was refused.

The bead offered two resolutions. Deriving the GATHERER_* constants from the excerpt at import
time was REJECTED with a reason worth recording: a launder that preserves the structures
regenerates an excerpt the derived constants agree with, so derivation follows the launder
silently and closes staleness rather than the hole. It would also make
scripts/audit_missing_items.py, which .githooks/pre-commit runs, import from tests/fixtures/.

So the digests are pinned as literals in reviewed source at
tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items_gatherer.py:30-33. The excerpt and its metadata are cut in
one step, so the recorded digest cannot witness its own cut; a literal in a test file is not
reached by the regeneration step.

THE ATTACK, RUN BY THE SESSION RATHER THAN ONLY BY THE IMPLEMENTER. A structure-preserving
comment edit inside the excerpt, every case arm, for-header, the `!= "primary"` guard and the
single expected_path_hints reader untouched, with the metadata digest and byte count
regenerated as an honest developer would:

  honest tree                        10 passed
  laundered + metadata regenerated    3 failed
      test_the_frozen_excerpt_is_the_bytes_this_file_pins
      test_the_fixture_metadata_agrees_with_the_digests_this_file_pins
      test_expected_path_hints_reaches_the_code_artifacts_loop_only
  restored                           10 passed

Both files restored byte-identical, verified by length and sha256 in Python.

DOES IT CRY WOLF. Not on a legitimate upstream update, which trips the existing live-comparison
drift test instead. It fires on the re-cut that follows, which is the moment a human is already
re-reading the three loops, and the assertion names the required response. One deliberate edit
per legitimate re-cut is the price, and it is charged at the point of review.

scripts/check.sh: 1963 passed, all gates pass, exit 0.

NO-CLAIM

The new .githooks/pre-commit case arms for exit codes 5, 6 and 7 are UNTESTED. tests/conftest.py
refuses a bash subprocess, so no test reaches them; their correctness rests on reading the file
and a `bash -n` parse. The classifier's exit codes are tested; the hook's reaction to them is
not. The .check.log line format is asserted by substring against a temp log rather than against
a real pre-commit invocation.

The laundered `source_sha256` was fabricated rather than produced by editing the real vendored
gatherer, so the honest-re-cut case is modeled and not observed end to end. No real upstream
skill update was simulated. The implementer reported the Bash sandbox intermittently denying
getcwd and repo writes, and three of its commands ran with the sandbox disabled; the files it
touched were verified restored by digest, but the cause of that denial is unestablished.

Exit codes 5, 6 and 7 were checked against their one in-repo consumer by grep; tooling outside
this repository that reads them was not surveyed.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
`MAP.md` is pinned by `tests/unit/test_map.py`, which reads six registries out of the code (`cli.registered()`, `claims.EVIDENCE_KINDS`, `claims.REPRO_KINDS`, `claims.GATES`, `claims.TAGS`, `bundle.source_objects`) and asserts each name appears as an exact backticked token in the map.

Two defects were found by demonstration rather than inspection, and both are fixed.

The first version's regex matched a name inside a longer code span, so dropping `justify` from MAP.md left the test green: RED_EXIT=0, "12 passed". Rewritten to exact-token matching. Re-demonstrated: RED_EXIT=1, `AssertionError: MAP.md names no command for: justify`, "2 failed, 11 passed"; restored, "13 passed". `test_a_name_appearing_only_inside_a_longer_code_span_does_not_count` pins the distinction.

The fresh-eyes audit then found the planted negative dropped `names[0]` only, 1 of 15 commands and 1 of 18 bundle objects. Parametrized over every name in every registry. Planting an underscore special-case in `absent()`: 26 failed, 34 passed. Restored: green.

Stated limit, not overstated: the span set is registry-blind, so a name held by two registries is satisfied by one span (`verifier`, `gate_plan` and `ladder_plan` are in both `claims.GATES` and the bundle objects), and a name in any row satisfies the check regardless of which layer documents it. The bead asks for verbatim presence in MAP.md, which is what this delivers. It is not "the map and the registry cannot disagree".

`MAP.md` line 29 gained `scrutiny`, `lean_statement_hasher` (`lean/Cairn/StatementHash.lean`) and `lean_axiom_checker` (`lean/Cairn/Axioms.lean`); paths verified against `lean.STATEMENT_HASHER_PATH` and `lean.AXIOM_PATH`. Applying `absent()` to `git show HEAD:MAP.md` confirms those three were genuinely missing, so the edit was necessary and the test is not decorative.

title: cairn status --json: one read-only call rendering the whole state and the admissible commands
description:
CONTEXT (PLAN §12 recorded results; research/briefs/language-and-agent-ergonomics.md §3-4). An agent driving Cairn reads state from `doctor`, `bundle show`, `capabilities`, `gate`, `justify` and `br` separately and reassembles it in its own context on every turn. Restate's introspection surface (invocations list/describe plus a SQL view over the journal) is the bar; the CLI meets it without a companion binary.

WHAT. `cairn status --json` (read-only, registered like every other command, dry-run semantics irrelevant) renders in one document: the gate bundle hash and pin match; each gate-plan step's last verdict; the skill revisions with their certificate state (certified, uncertified, yanked, with the yank reach); tier budgets remaining per the bundle's tiers object; claim statements by status and calibration tag with counts; the last N gate runs (N a flag, default 10) with gate, result and reasons; the human queue depth when the queue exists (H1); and an `affordances` list naming the commands that are admissible from this state, each with the exit code it would return on a dry run. Missing subsystems (not yet built) appear as `absent`, never as zero counts, so an absence is not read as an empty population. Wall time under two seconds on the M0 substrate; the document scrubs to a golden.

DONE WHEN the golden exists, the command answers under two seconds on a populated substrate, and a substrate with a tampered bundle row makes `status` report `pin_match: false` and the bundle-open refusal among the affordances.

TEST PLAN — tests/integration/test_status.py (integration: populated substrate, golden with scrub(); planted negative: tampered bundle); tests/unit/test_status_render.py (unit: absent vs empty distinction, affordance list).
acceptance_criteria: The golden exists; under two seconds on a populated substrate; a tampered bundle row yields pin_match false and the bundle-open refusal among the affordances; absent subsystems render as absent, never as zero counts.

title: scripts/check.sh --unit: a unit tier of the suite under one minute with a measured slow marker
description:
CONTEXT (scripts/check.sh; research/briefs/language-and-agent-ergonomics.md §4). `check.sh --fast` runs format, lint, spelling, types and theater in seconds; the full suite runs about fifteen minutes and CI bills it at ten times wall clock. Between them there is no tier, so an agent either skips the suite or pays fifteen minutes per edit, and a 15-minute verdict is one the agent runs rarely and batches around.

WHAT. `scripts/check.sh --unit` runs the fast gates plus `uv run pytest tests/unit -q -m "not slow"` with `--durations=10`, and writes RUN/PASS/FAIL lines to .check.log like every gate. title: Harness: four doctor detector findings are unreachable without a mock, and d_kat has no vectors seam
description:
Four of `cairn doctor`'s detector findings cannot be reached by any test, because
the thing they detect cannot be made to fail without a mock, and the doctor's tests
take no mocks.

After cairn-m0-e0s.18's audit pass the doctor sits at 97 percent line coverage
(`cairn.doctor` 798 statements, 24 uncovered) with 28 fixtures. Every remaining
detector gap is one of these:

  detectors.py:158  D-pari-inprocess/stack
  detectors.py:172  D-pari-inprocess/ellcard
  detectors.py:185  D-pari-inprocess/libpari-version
  detectors.py:480  D-kat/mismatch

The first three need cypari2 itself to misreport: a failed 64 MB allocatemem, an
`ellcard` on corpus-1 returning something other than 7, or a `pari.version()` that
is not 2.17.x. Reaching them needs either a mock of `pari.pari` / `pari.pari_versions`
or a second libpari build on the machine to point cypari2 at.

The fourth is closer. `d_kat` calls `kat.run()` with no argument, so its vectors come
from the repo-wide `kat.DEFAULT_VECTORS`. There is no way to hand it a corrupt vector
file, and corrupting the repo's own is not an option -- though not because a guard
would stop it. `GUARDED_DIRS = (".doctor", "deploy", "var")` (tests/conftest.py:19) is the
whole of what `_snapshot` walks (tests/conftest.py:32-42), so `tests/vectors/` is
unwatched: `VECTORS` and `GOLDENS` (tests/conftest.py:20-21) are read paths for the
golden harness and `load_vector` and are snapshotted nowhere. A test that rewrote
`canon_kat.json` in place and failed to restore it would poison every later test in
the session and leave the checkout dirty with nothing raising, which is why the seam
below is the fix and an in-place rewrite-and-restore is not.

WHAT: give `d_kat` its vectors through the doctor's `Context` rather than reading a
module global, so a fixture can point it at a deliberately corrupt vector file under
`tmp_path` and `D-kat/mismatch` becomes reachable with no mock at all. The doctor declares no seam today: nothing under `src/cairn/doctor/`
names one, and `pari.GP_BIN` is a module global (src/cairn/pari.py:11) that the
detectors read (src/cairn/doctor/detectors.py:85) and the gp fixtures repoint with
`monkeypatch.setattr(pari, "GP_BIN", ...)` (tests/integration/test_doctor.py:509), which
is how they drive real `/bin/sh` scripts. The `Context` field is therefore the doctor's
first declared seam, and the place that enumerates both is this bead's to create.

The three cypari2 findings are a different problem and may not be worth solving. A
second libpari on the machine is real work for three refusal branches. Decide
deliberately: either declare a fourth seam for `pari.pari_versions` and say so where
the other seams are declared, or record that these three are unreachable by design
and stop counting them as a gap.

DONE WHEN: `D-kat/mismatch` has a fixture that corrupts a vector file under `tmp_path`
and asserts the finding, with no mock; and the three `D-pari-inprocess` findings either
have fixtures or a recorded decision that they stay unreachable, with the reason.

Surfaced by cairn-m0-e0s.18's audit as F11. The 28 fixtures that bead does ship cover
every other declared finding.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: `d_kat` takes its vector path from the doctor's `Context`
  (src/cairn/doctor/detectors.py:59) instead of `kat.run()`'s import-time default
  (src/cairn/doctor/detectors.py:477 against src/cairn/kat.py:7,23), and a fixture
  pointing it at a deliberately corrupt vector file under `tmp_path` raises
  `D-kat/mismatch` with no mock anywhere in the path; the command, the finding and the
  fixture's directory name pasted.
- Positive: the seams a doctor fixture may repoint are enumerated in one named place
  under `src/cairn/doctor/`, which declares none today, so a reader enumerates them
  rather than discovering them; the inventory names the new vectors seam and the
  pre-existing `pari.GP_BIN` module global (src/cairn/pari.py:11) the detectors read
  (src/cairn/doctor/detectors.py:85) and the gp fixtures repoint with
  `monkeypatch.setattr` to drive real `/bin/sh` scripts
  (tests/integration/test_doctor.py:501-509); the inventory pasted.
- Positive: the three `D-pari-inprocess` findings
  (src/cairn/doctor/detectors.py:158, 172, 185) are settled either way and the ruling is
  recorded — a declared fourth seam for `pari.pari` / `pari.pari_versions` with fixtures
  that reach all three, or a written decision that they stay unreachable, with the reason

- Planted negative: with an uncorrupted vector file the finding does not fire, so the

title: Harness: a refused attempt's receipt does not record the threshold that refused it
description:
cairn-x72 split the budget ceiling into two: the verdict reads CPU time and refuses with
BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and a generous wall cap catches a stuck child and refuses with BLOCKED.

The receipt records cpu_user_s, cpu_sys_s and wall_s. It does not record ceiling_s or
wall_cap_s. So a reader holding a refused attempt's receipt can see what the attempt spent
but not what it was allowed to spend, and cannot tell from the receipt alone whether the
refusal was correct.

The kill log line names wall_cap_s, so the information exists in the run log. A receipt is
the durable artifact and the log is not.

WHY THIS WAS NOT DONE IN cairn-x72: receipt fields are hashed content. Adding one moves
every receipt hash and the goldens that carry them, which is a different change with a
different blast radius from re-pointing a clock.

THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME SCHEMA QUESTION is cairn-m1-cqt.1.5, which asks whether the receipt
carries a `measurement_scope` field so a reader can tell a direct-child figure from a
process-tree one. Both add a hashed receipt field and both move the same goldens, so they are one
receipt change or two golden reseeds. cairn-m1-cqt.1.5 settles the pair; this bead's decision is
recorded against that change, or the reason the two land separately is recorded here.

DONE WHEN
- A decision, recorded, on whether the threshold belongs in the receipt at all, given that
  the recipe plus tiers.json already determine it and a receipt that repeats a derivable
  number can drift from it.
- If it goes in: the goldens that move are named before the change, not discovered during it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: the decision is recorded either way, with its reasoning and its inputs — the
  receipts table today carries cpu_user_s, cpu_sys_s and wall_s and no ceiling_s or
  wall_cap_s (src/cairn/schema.sql:57-71), while the kill log line does name wall_cap_s
  (src/cairn/runner.py:254), so the reader of a refused attempt's receipt cannot tell
  from the receipt alone what the attempt was allowed to spend; the record says whether
  that is worth a hashed field given the recipe plus bundle/tiers.json already determine
  the threshold.
- Positive: the decision is recorded against cairn-m1-cqt.1.5's receipt-schema change, or
  the reason the two land separately is recorded here — one of the two, never neither,
  since both add a hashed receipt field and both move the same goldens.
- Planted negative, if the field goes in: every golden the change moves is NAMED before
  the change and the list is pasted; a golden that moves and was not named fails a test,
  shown once by omitting one name in a scratch copy, output pasted, then restored
  byte-identical (length + sha256 in Python, never a shell diff). A recorded threshold
  that disagrees with the recipe-plus-tiers.json derivation for the same attempt likewise
  fails, so the repeated number cannot drift from the derivable one in silence.
- No-Claim: this settles what a refused attempt's receipt records and nothing about
  whether either refusal is correct; the CPU-versus-wall split itself is cairn-x72's,
  already closed, and is not re-opened.
- Test types: unit, integration, golden. Files: tests/unit/test_runner_status.py,
  tests/integration/test_runner.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.

  KEEP, WITH A KNOWN OVERLAP -- "Choosing what to work on next". Its `bv` caveats now also live
    in CLAUDE.md's working notes. The duplication is deliberate: CLAUDE.md is loaded always and
    this file is pasted once, so a reader of either is covered. Recorded so the next pass does
    not "discover" it as drift.
  KEEP -- Modes A, B, C, D.
  KEEP AS-IS -- Mode E, which is marked NOT AVAILABLE YET and gates itself on M1.
  MOVE, EVENTUALLY -- "How subproblems get chosen (PLAN section 10)". It restates PLAN section
    10 for a mode that cannot run yet. It moves when Mode E becomes available, not before,
    because moving it now costs a redirect for no reader.

Nothing is tagged DELETE. The previous pass already removed what the gates enforce.

WHY A DOCUMENT AND NOT A SKILL

A skill's advantage is conditional loading by name. This file is already selectively loaded by
the only mechanism that matters: a human pastes ONE mode at session start, not the whole file.
The skill form would add indirection without changing what reaches the context.

It carries no machinery to hold. The bead itself records that it has no `references/` of its
own and points at three scripts wired on 2026-08-25. A skill without machinery is a document
with an extra lookup step.

And "skill" is already overloaded in this project in three senses that CLAUDE.md has to spell
out: a Cairn skill (deterministic Python, content-addressed), a worker role template, and a
Claude Code skill. A fourth thing called a skill costs more in confusion than the loader saves.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS. A mode acquiring real machinery -- a script that runs the mode rather
than describing it -- at which point the machinery wants a home and a skill is the right one.

NO-CLAIM

The section tags are a judgment over the file's headings and its first 92 lines, which were
read this session; Modes A through E were tagged from their headings and this session's use of
Mode A, not from a line-by-line reading of all 336 lines. No benchmark was run, so the claim
that a benchmark would change no decision is an argument rather than a measurement. The file
was not edited: the "MOVE, EVENTUALLY" tag is recorded for a future pass rather than acted on,
so this close leaves the document byte-identical to how it was found.

title: Test harness: the local session deadline default (1500 s) sits inside 80 s of an idle full run; raise it to 3000 s with CI kept at 900, and register the harness hook modules through pytest_plugins
description:
CONTEXT. tests/_session_deadline.py arms a session-wide deadline (DEFAULT_SECONDS = 1500, overridden by CAIRN_SESSION_DEADLINE; CI sets 900) that dumps every thread and exits 124. On this Mac the full suite takes 1424 s idle (2026-09-02, 2576 tests), 1483 s idle (2026-09-02, 2585 tests) and 2053 s under load average 6-9 from sibling sessions (2026-09-03, 2666 tests): the default sits inside 80 s of an idle run and a loaded run dies at 27 percent with the main thread in ordinary test code (measured 2026-09-02: `Timeout (0:25:00)!` with the main thread in tests/integration/test_session_deadline.py::test_a3 inside communicate). Every close this week ran the full suite under `CAIRN_SESSION_DEADLINE=3000` by hand. The suite grows with every bead, so the margin only shrinks. Unrelated but in the same harness file family: tests/conftest.py registers the two harness modules by importing their hook functions with `# noqa: F401`, which the compliance audit's theater scan flags as an ignore-list line on every close that touches it.

WHAT. Raise the local default so a loaded machine cannot kill a healthy run: DEFAULT_SECONDS = 3000 in tests/_session_deadline.py, the BACKSTOP_GRACE unchanged, the check.sh DEADLINE banner reading the same value, and CI unchanged at 900 through ci.yml (the runner finishes in 590-616 s; the runner's ceiling is timeout-minutes 20, so the 900 s deadline stays under it with the backstop's 15 s). State the arithmetic in the module: the default is the idle full-run time times two, rounded, and is revisited when an idle run passes half of it. Register the harness modules in tests/conftest.py through `pytest_plugins = ["pytester", "_session_deadline", "_libpari_stall"]` in place of the two `# noqa: F401` imports, so the wiring is a declaration rather than an unused-import exemption; tests/unit/test_libpari_stall_hook.py::test_the_hook_is_registered_in_this_session already proves the libpari hook is registered and the deadline suite proves the deadline hooks are.

TEST PLAN. tests/unit/test_check_gate_instruments.py:70 already pins the check.sh DEADLINE banner to DEFAULT_SECONDS and :84 the armed seconds, so the banner literal and the constant cannot drift once both move; add `assert DEFAULT_SECONDS == 3000` beside the existing `> 4 * 230` bound at tests/integration/test_session_deadline.py:272; the child tests keep their explicit 4 s deadlines. tests/unit/test_libpari_stall_hook.py::test_the_hook_is_registered_in_this_session and the deadline suite's configure tests cover the pytest_plugins registration. Planted negative: with the conftest registration deleted on a scratch copy, the registration test fails; with the banner literal changed on a scratch copy, the pinning test fails.

NO-CLAIM. A longer default proves nothing about the suite's speed; a run that needs it is slow, and the durations list at the end of the run says where.

- Approach: one constant, one banner literal, one pinning test; the CI value stays in ci.yml so the runner's tighter bound is explicit there. Rejected: deriving the default from the core count or the load average, which makes a kill depend on the machine's state and is exactly the unreproducible failure the deadline exists to make legible.
- Pattern-to-follow: tests/_session_deadline.py (resolve_seconds, the explicit env override and the usage error), scripts/check.sh line 68 (the banner), tests/unit/test_check_gate_instruments.py lines 70 and 84 (the banner and the armed seconds pinned to the constant), tests/conftest.py line 16 (pytest_plugins already carries "pytester")

title: Harness: the tier budget ceiling reads wall time, so a busy CI runner reads as a refused gate
description:
`runner.status_for` refuses an attempt when `wall_s > ceiling_s`, and the ceiling is
`ceiling_multiplier * expected_wall_s`: 4 from `bundle/tiers.json` times 0.1338 from
`src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py:32`, so 0.5352 seconds of WALL time for the 40-bit toy curve.

That number was measured on a developer machine. A shared CI runner does not honor it, and
the refusal it produces reads as a gate finding rather than as a slow neighbor.

OBSERVED 2026-08-27, run 33105687625, commit 4005439, macos-latest:

  ceiling_s  0.5352
  wall_s     0.600659   <- refused
  cpu_s      0.235461   <- less than half the ceiling

The attempt used 0.235 s of CPU to spend 0.601 s of wall. That ratio IS the contention, and
the receipt already records both numbers. The gate reads the one that measures the machine.

The same commit is green locally at 1835 passed in 270 s on a quiet machine, and the two CI
runs on it failed DIFFERENTLY -- one BUDGET_EXCEEDED at 388 s, one wedged until the session
deadline fired at 25 minutes naming `tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py::test_the_derivation_`.
Different failures on one unchanged commit is the signature of contention, not of a defect.

Prior instance, recorded in a previous session: a load spike produced three BUDGET_EXCEEDED
failures on tests that then passed 49/49 on a quiet machine.

WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY A NUMBER TO RAISE

The budget ceiling is a real tier control, and PLAN section 5 states Tier-1 as "one core,
minutes". A gate that refuses genuinely runaway work is doing its job, and widening the
multiplier until CI stops complaining would retire the control rather than fix it. The
defect is the CLOCK, not the threshold: wall time on a shared runner measures the runner.

Note `src/cairn/skills/toy_curve.py` is in `IDENTITY_SOURCES`, so editing the profile
constant reseeds the randomized arm and moves the transcript and certificate goldens. A fix
that lives in `runner.py` and `bundle/tiers.json` costs nothing there; a fix that edits the
profile is a re-certification.

DONE WHEN
- A decision, recorded, on which clock the ceiling reads. CPU time is already on the
  receipt and is the honest measure of the work; wall time measures the work plus whoever
  else is on the box.
- Whatever clock is chosen, a test that fails while the defect is present: an attempt whose
  CPU is inside the ceiling and whose wall is outside must not be refused, and one whose
  CPU is genuinely outside must still be refused.
- If wall time is kept for any reason, that reason is written down along with what CI is
  expected to do on a slow runner, so the next red run is diagnosable rather than puzzling.

comments.author: jwross
comments.text:
CLOSED. The clock decision is recorded below, and the defect was reproduced on this machine
before anything was changed.

THE REPRODUCTION, WHICH THIS BEAD PREDICTED

A full suite run on 2026-08-31 under machine load returned 17 failures; re-run in isolation,
12 still failed. The errors are this bead verbatim:

  AssertionError: assert ('BUDGET_EXCEEDED' == 'OK')
  AssertionError: assert -15 == 0                      SIGTERM, the launch loop's own kill
  parsed=ParsedOutput(well_formed=False, status=None, reason='stdout is empty')

The suite had been red for the reason this bead names. It was not flakiness: the ceiling is a
fixed 0.5352 s of wall, so a loaded box blows it deterministically.

THE DECISION, WHICH CLOCK THE CEILING READS

The verdict reads CPU time, user plus system. A separate and much larger wall cap remains as
a liveness net, and it carries its own status.

  ceiling_s   4 x 0.1338 = 0.5352 s, unchanged in arithmetic, now compared against
              cpu_user_s + cpu_sys_s rather than wall_s
  wall_cap_s  max(wall_cap_multiplier x ceiling_s, ceiling_s + wall_cap_floor_s)
              = 120.5352 s for the toy curve, from bundle/tiers.json

Both are needed. CPU is the honest measure of the work, and wall measures the work plus
whoever else is on the box. But a child that is genuinely stuck burns no CPU, so a pure CPU
budget alone never fires on the case that most needs a timeout. Two ceilings, and critically
two statuses: BUDGET_EXCEEDED for work that is too expensive, BLOCKED for work that is stuck.
A single status over two causes is the conflation this project has now been bitten by three
times.

WHAT CI DOES ON A SLOW RUNNER NOW. The observed CI datum from run 33105687625 -- wall
0.600659, cpu 0.235461, ceiling 0.5352 -- reads OK: cpu is inside the ceiling and wall is far
inside the cap. A runner would have to be roughly 225 times slower in wall than in CPU before
the net fires, and the status would then read BLOCKED, so a future red run says stuck rather
than over budget. The tier control is not widened. BUDGET_EXCEEDED now requires real CPU,
which contention does not manufacture.

Precedence when both fire: BUDGET_EXCEEDED wins. That was the implementer's judgment, not an
instruction, and it is pinned by a test so it can be flipped deliberately rather than drifting.

A SECOND SITE OF THE SAME DEFECT, FOUND AND FIXED

Eight of the twelve failures went green on the runner change alone. The other four were a
different instance of the same shape: the grace-window and group-sweep tests hard-code their
own wall constants, 0.2 s, measured on a quiet box. A CPython interpreter cannot boot and
install a SIGTERM handler in 0.2 s on a loaded machine, so SIGTERM arrived before the handler
existed and the fixture's whole point never ran. Raised to a named HANDLER_INSTALLS_WITHIN_S
of 3.0 against fixtures that loop for 30 s. No assertion was weakened to buy it: exit_status
== -9, the grandchild existence check and sigterm_seen == "term" all still hold.

VERIFICATION, RE-EXECUTED BY THE SESSION

The four new clock tests were observed failing against the unfixed code before the fix.
The 12 isolation failures: 81 passed, 0 failed, no survivors.
scripts/check.sh: 1937 passed, all gates pass, exit 0.
No re-certification: implementation_revision is unchanged and zero files in
toy_curve.IDENTITY_SOURCES were modified, verified by execution.
tests/goldens/gate_bundle_hash.golden moved because bundle/tiers.json is one of its hashed
sources; it is the only golden that moved.
Each half reverted separately leaves the new tests red, so neither half is untested.

NO-CLAIM

The fix was verified at load 5, not at the load 15-25 that produced the failure, so the green
is weaker evidence than the red it replaces. The 120 s wall-cap floor is adopted from the
design, not measured; no test exercises the cap at its shipped value, only at an injected
1.0 s, and that the same code path fires at 120.5 s is arithmetic inference over unit-tested
code. schema.sql uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so a substrate created before this change
keeps the old CHECK and will raise on a BLOCKED close; fresh substrates are unaffected.
BUDGET_EXCEEDED was grepped for in Python files only, so prose or JSON elsewhere enumerating
runner statuses may now be incomplete. test_a_slower_tick_still_stops_the_child still uses a
0.2 s cap and belongs to the same family as the four constants raised here if it ever flakes.
The receipt records what an attempt spent but not the threshold it was allowed to spend, so a
refused attempt is diagnosable from the kill log rather than from the receipt alone; that is
owned by cairn-wdg, opened for it.

title: Harness: CI runs on macos-latest and bills at 10x, which is what exhausted the quota
description:
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` line 24 is `runs-on: macos-latest`. GitHub bills macOS runners at
10x the Linux rate, so a run whose wall time is 8 minutes costs 80 of the 2000 free minutes.

MEASURED 2026-09-01 from `gh run list`, summing each run's created-to-updated interval:

  30 runs listed              216 wall minutes    2161 billed at 10x
  3 runs on 2026-09-01         14.6 wall minutes   146 billed at 10x

The quota exhaustion on 2026-08-27 was 23 runs spending about 2020 of 2000. On ubuntu-latest
the same 216 wall minutes bill 216, and the quota is never reached.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE CHANGE

`toy_curve.identity_bundle()` hashes tool digests and the container digest into
`implementation_revision`, and the certificate and transcript goldens bind to it. If cypari2
or PARI digests differently on Linux, the goldens move, and that is a re-certification rather
than a configuration edit. The question is empirical and one run answers it.

`research/grounding/m0-stack-facts.md` records the stack probes; `cairn-hcl`, deferred to M1,
already states the gold tier needs Linux, so a Linux runner moves toward that rather than away.

WHAT ELSE SPENDS MINUTES

`.githooks/post-commit` pushes every bead-closing commit, so three beads closed in ten minutes
produced three runs. `cancel-in-progress` is on for main and did kill one of them, which is
the mechanism working, but a batched close would not have started them. Closing several beads
in one commit costs one run.

DONE WHEN
- A decision, recorded, on the runner, with the golden movement measured rather than predicted.
- If the goldens move: named before the change, with whether the movement is a real identity
  change or an artifact of the build.
- If macos-latest is kept, the reason is written down along with the per-run cost, so the next
  quota exhaustion is a known price rather than a surprise.
- A decision on whether every bead-closing commit still pushes, or whether a session batches.
close_reason: duplicate: cairn-hcl owns the runner matrix and measured the Linux blockers first

title: M1: cost_tag is a literal compared to itself, so the slice's cost tagging is unchecked
description:
Found while verifying the M0 epic's *Done when* clause 7, which requires the four slice nodes
to be "hashed, self-tested, cost-tagged substrate nodes".

Two of the three hold solidly. The four hashes are distinct and content-addressed, and node B's
was rebuilt independently from canon and matched byte for byte. `selftest_ref` is not merely
truthy: it equals the exact certificate hash `cairn selftest toy-curve` emitted, and the slice's
own abort path refuses the run outright when that certificate is absent —
`raise SliceRefused(REASON_UNCERTIFIED, NEXT_CERTIFY)` at `src/cairn/m0.py:237`, whose reason
string is `uncertified-revision` (`src/cairn/m0.py:24`). `uncertified_skill` names something
else entirely, the doctor fixture directory `tests/doctor_fixtures/uncertified_skill/`, which is
not on this path.

THE THIRD IS AN ASSERTION COMPARING A LITERAL TO A LITERAL.

`cost_tag` is the bare string "tier0", hardcoded at all four `SliceNode(...)` construction
sites in `src/cairn/m0.py:396-399`, and again at line 314 inside node A's canonical encoding.
The e2e assertion is `all(node["cost_tag"] == "tier0" for node in nodes)`.

Nothing derives the tag from the tier gate's admitted decision, so the test compares a constant
to the same constant. It would catch the field being removed or renamed. It cannot catch the
tag being WRONG, because there is no independent source it could disagree with.

WHY IT IS NOT WRONG TODAY, and why that is not the same as being checked. A 40-bit toy curve
IS tier 0, so the literal is correct. And tier-0 launches mint no ticket -- the `tickets` table
is empty after a run, confirmed by execution -- so there is currently nothing to derive from.
The tag is right by construction and unverified by measurement, which is the same shape this
project has now found in a gate five times.

WHY IT BELONGS TO M1 RATHER THAN TO M0, and what the independent source actually is. It is not
a ticket. A tier-0 launch never carries one: `TierGate._selected_ticket` returns None whenever
`declared_tier == 0` (`src/cairn/tiergate.py:109-111`), and PLAN §5 fixes that — "Tier 0 needs no
ticket" — so no M1 bead can give these four launches a ticket to read. The source M1 does create
is the tier the gate DERIVES from the bundle's boundary table. `TierGate.admit` computes it today
(`tier_for_cost(self.boundary_table, evaluation.expected_core_s)`, `src/cairn/tiergate.py:138`)
and records it nowhere — `Admitted` carries `ticket_tier`, not the derived tier
(`src/cairn/tiergate.py:44-50`), and the gate-run row carries neither — which is why there is
currently nothing to derive from. Bead `cairn-m1-cqt.4.6` is where that derivation becomes a
checked gate decision rather than a side computation: it refuses a launch declaring a tier below
the one the boundary table assigns its production cost, so the tier a launch is admitted under is
a quantity the gate stands behind. `cairn-m1-cqt.4.5` supplies the ticket lattice it sits in.

What 4.6 does not hand over is a column. No table holds the derived tier: `gate_runs` carries
`result` and `reasons` (`src/cairn/schema.sql:272-283`), `tier_refusals` carries `declared_tier`
and `ticket_tier` (`src/cairn/schema.sql:296-303`), and 4.6's own criteria are refusals — while
these four launches are admitted Tier-0 launches that write no refusal row at all. Surfacing the
derived tier on the admission is therefore this bead's own first move, never something 4.6
delivers. Deriving the tag before 4.6 would produce a second literal, not a check.

DONE WHEN
- `cost_tag` is read from the admitted tier decision rather than written as a literal, and a
  test fails when a node's tag disagrees with the tier its launch was admitted under.
- Or, if the tag is genuinely a property of the launch request rather than of the admission, a
  recorded decision saying so, with the reason the e2e assertion is allowed to compare a
  constant to itself.

A SECOND, SMALLER OBSERVATION FROM THE SAME PASS, recorded here rather than in its own bead
because it is the same file. `src/cairn/m0.py:222` reports `spawned = result.rc is not None`.
That is an inference about whether a subprocess ran, and it is unfaithful on the timeout path,
where a real spawn also yields `rc = None`. The M0 clause about refusing a submitter-named
(P, Q) BEFORE the subprocess spawns is verified by
`tests/unit/test_verifier_validation.py::test_pre_spawn_refusal_table`, which observes
`popen_spy == []` directly, so the clause itself is sound. The e2e field is reporting, not the
gate, and it would mislead a reader of a timed-out run.
acceptance_criteria:
- Positive: every slice node's `cost_tag` is read from the tier decision that admitted its
  launch rather than written as the literal at src/cairn/m0.py:314 and :396-399; the node
  rows and the admission they were read from are pasted side by side, so the two are
  visibly different sources.
- Planted negative: a node whose tag disagrees with the tier its launch was admitted
  under fails a test — forced once in a scratch copy with the failure pasted, then
  restored byte-identical (length + sha256 in Python, never a shell diff). The existing
  assertion at tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py:124 must be the one that goes red, since
  comparing a constant to the same constant is the defect this bead exists to remove.
- Positive: src/cairn/m0.py:222 reports `spawned` from the spawn rather than inferring it
  from `result.rc is not None`, which is also None on the timeout path; a timed-out run's
  gate-run record is pasted showing the corrected field.
- Alternative, recorded rather than skipped: if the tag is genuinely a property of the
  launch request and not of the admission, the close records that decision with the
  reason the e2e assertion may compare a constant to itself, and names what would have to
  exist for it to become a measurement — a decision, never a silent keep.
- No-Claim: deriving the tag proves the slice record agrees with the admission that
  produced it. It re-opens nothing about the pre-spawn refusal clause, which stays proven
  by tests/unit/test_verifier_validation.py::test_pre_spawn_refusal_table observing
  `popen_spy == []` directly.
- Test types: unit, e2e. Files: tests/e2e/test_m0_slice.py,
  tests/unit/test_verifier_validation.py.
- Done when: every bullet above has been re-executed at close, with the exact command and
  its raw output pasted in the close comment and bound to the commit SHA that produced
  it; a bullet without pasted output is not done.
- Evidence cites file:line for each touched source and test file in the close comment.

title: M1 tiers: yank.record as one substrate transaction (yank row, salt row, disowns, escrow releases, re-derivation)
description:
yank.record (src/cairn/yank.py) writes the yank row, the salt row, one disowned mark and one escrow release per covered attempt, then re-derives every resting claim, each through its own Substrate call and transaction (sub._tx() is not nestable). A crash between them leaves a yank row with no salt bump, or disowned attempts whose escrow still stands. Surfaced as an unverified observation by the fresh-eyes Opus review of the cairn-m1-cqt.4.2 close (comment on that bead). Deliverable: one transaction around the whole propagation, with a test that injects a failure after the first write and asserts nothing landed.

## Architecture
- Approach: a Substrate.transaction() context that the existing add_/disown/escrow writers join when one is open, so yank.record wraps its five steps in it; the alternative of a compensating undo is refused by the append-only triggers.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/yank.py record() and src/cairn/substrate.py _tx()
- Touches: src/cairn/substrate.py, src/cairn/yank.py, src/cairn/escrow.py, tests/integration/test_yank_propagation.py
- ADRs: none
- Data model impact: none
- Failure modes: a nested transaction error (observable: SubstrateError in the injected-failure test); a partial yank (observable: yank row present with current_salt None in the same test)

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] sub._tx() is not nestable and every writer opens its own — source: src/cairn/substrate.py (verified: 2026-09-05 by reading the callers in yank.record) (Confidence: HIGH)
- Delegability: STATEABLE

comments.text:
In-flight yank ownership contract from cairn-m1-cqt.4.3, source checkpoint
02ef57ebeb0d992a9fbac403997b55df8c9941f4:

Yank propagation owns escrow release when the runner closes SKILL_YANKED. The
runner skips settle_on_close for that status, including when propagation pauses
after disown commits and before the escrow read. The integration test
tests/integration/test_skill_yanked_inflight.py records the actual settling
connection with a SQLite trigger and requires exactly one update by the yank
controller. Restoring the runner's competing callback is caught by that test.

The ordered callbacks already avoided a duplicate update through their standing
checks; that sequential bug was not reproduced. Multi-step yank.record crash
atomicity is not established by .4.3 and remains owned here. Preserve the single
release owner and strict escrow_settle_once trigger when making the propagation
transaction/recovery path atomic. Grounding section D records the actual probe.

title: M1 substrate: canon.decode refuses non-canonical bytes (duplicate map keys, unsorted or repeated set members, non-NFC strings)
description:
canon.decode (src/cairn/canon.py) refuses trailing bytes, truncation, wrong tags, non-minimal ints and negative zero, and accepts three shapes the encoder never produces: a map with a repeated key (last wins), a set out of order or with a repeated member, and a non-NFC string; encode(decode(b)) != b for such input and the two byte strings content-address differently. Verified mechanism with no reachable premise today: both decode callers (yank.recipe_fields, scrutiny._hypothesis_fields) read canonical bytes canon.encode wrote. Surfaced by the fresh-eyes Opus review of the cairn-m1-cqt.8.2 close. Deliverable: the three refusals in decode_at with a unit test per shape in tests/unit/test_canon_decode.py.

## Architecture
- Approach: compare the decoded key count with len(out) in _Map.decode_at, check sorted-and-unique element bytes in _Set.decode_at, and check unicodedata.is_normalized("NFC", s) in _Str.decode_at; the alternative of re-encoding and comparing bytes costs a second pass over every node read.
- Pattern-to-follow: src/cairn/canon.py decode_int_body (the existing minimality refusal)
- Touches: src/cairn/canon.py, tests/unit/test_canon_decode.py
- ADRs: none
- Data model impact: none
- Failure modes: a refusal on bytes a writer legitimately produced (observable: the round-trip tests over keys.RECIPE and keys.HYPOTHESIS_OBJECT in tests/unit/test_canon_decode.py)

## Pre-implementation research
- [R1] the only decode callers read node canonical bytes written by canon.encode — source: src/cairn/yank.py recipe_fields, src/cairn/scrutiny.py _hypothesis_fields (verified: 2026-09-05 by the review's caller trace) (Confidence: HIGH)
- Delegability: STATEABLE

title: Harness: three unexercised paths in the missing-items corrector
description:
Three gaps left open by cairn-8jm, all in scripts/audit_missing_items.py, none of which
that bead's acceptance criteria reached.

1. THE `- check` LINE SHAPE IS A PARSE GAP OF UNESTABLISHED FREQUENCY.

score-bead.py:1241 emits `- check \`<id>\` (<verdict>) — <reason>` into the same section for
every compliance check with verdict FAIL or MISSING. cairn-8jm extended spec_item_id_of to
both shapes, so a given id classifies identically whichever producer wrote its line, and both
shapes are tested. What is unestablished is whether Phase 4 ever emits FAIL for an item the
gatherer never searched: every compliance.json in this repo is the stub with an empty checks
list, and a scan of all recorded passes finds 710 `- spec item` lines, 241 `- theater` lines
and zero `- check` lines. So the handling is correct by construction and unexercised by any
real artifact.

DONE WHEN a real Phase 4 has run at least once under the orchestrator and the resulting
compliance.json is either shown to contain no such row, or is used as the fixture for a test
that exercises the shape against real output.

2. ONLY ONE UNREADABLE-INPUT PATH HAS A NAMED OUTCOME.

EXIT_UNREADABLE_SPEC covers json.JSONDecodeError from spec.json. An unreadable scorecard.md,
a permissions error on either file, and a spec.json that parses to a non-dict all raise
uncaught. The direction is safe -- a traceback exits nonzero and the hook denies -- but it is
not one of the three named outcomes, and the enforcement discipline this project follows asks
for a distinct log line per outcome so an agent can confirm which path fired. This is the
same defect class cairn-8jm fixed for the missing heading, one layer out.

DONE WHEN each unreadable-input path has its own verdict, exit code and .check.log line, with
a test per path.

3. THE FROZEN GATHERER EXCERPT CANNOT DETECT A LAUNDERED REGENERATION.

tests/fixtures/compliance_skill/ holds a point-in-time cut of gather-evidence.sh with the
source digest, and tests/integration/test_audit_missing_items_drift.py compares the live file
against it. Someone who edits the vendored gatherer AND regenerates the fixture in one step
passes both the hermetic assertions and the live comparison. Only the GATHERER_* constants
failing to match the new excerpt would catch it, and a regeneration that preserves the
structures those constants name would slip through entirely.

DONE WHEN either the fixture's digest is pinned somewhere a regeneration cannot silently
rewrite, or the classifier's constants are derived from the excerpt at import time so a
structural change cannot leave them stale.

TEST PLAN

- tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items.py — one test per newly named unreadable-input outcome,
  each asserting the exit code, the verdict on stdout and the .check.log line.
- tests/unit/test_audit_missing_items_gatherer.py — the laundered-regeneration guard, run
  hermetically so it holds on a machine with no vendored skill.
